author: ikaevus
body:
Part of #545, stacked on #693. Reconstruct an independently signed Ed25519 removal decision from the existing locked SQL admission facts. Bind deployment, actor/session, restart consent, exact account/node/Agent generation, baseline/candidate/job, nonce, and original expiry. A valid SQL approval without the independent proof cannot pass this check. Tests cover the exact signature, wrong key, every changed field, session revocation, and absence of executable rows.

The trusted signer and verifier key must live outside runtime database authority. This is a rehearsal; no signer, task writer, consumption record, route or production wiring is added. The eventual transaction must verify proof and consume approval atomically with the scoped job.

The #693 systemd/Reality job passed. Its dispatch race shard exhausted 120 seconds, so split that exact selection without dropping tests or changing watchdogs. The matrix remains under the existing aggregate Agent gate. Local compile/vet and selection coverage checked; the SQL integration test requires the disposable CI PostgreSQL service.

author: sahil1
body:
## The problem

Home (the `home` trial) read like a feed dump on a real morning with two computers:

- **Coming up · today** was a column of Chief of Staff's to-dos, most with no date, so not "today" at all, and the same tasks showed twice ("Gary: make the introduction he offered (not done yet)", "Them: set up the face-to-face meeting in New York", "Parvinder: present the AWS paper…", all on one computer).
- **Ready to look at · 29** was a stack of big cards, each an agent's whole last message cut mid-word ("…Still pending on your list, fr"), the project said twice ("GIT GIT", "roadmap roadmap"), Reply / Clear / Open on every card, and work from days ago mixed in with this morning's.
- Everything had the same weight, so there was nothing to scan.

**Why the tasks were doubled:** the task list itself had them twice. A meeting's action items handed to Chief of Staff a second time (`POST /api/meetings/:id/chief` with none left unsent sends all of them again) adds a second copy of each task with a new number. Home showed every line of the list. It now shows one row per task, matched on the words. The test scene builds this exact case: the same meeting is handed on twice on Desk.

## What changed

**Server (`server/home.js`, one line in `server/index.js`)**
- `tidy()` keeps one row per thing. The same task twice on a list, or on two computers, is one row: the one waiting on you wins, then the one Chief of Staff is working on, then this computer's, then the newest. A cloud agent seen from both computers is one row. Agents with the same name on two computers stay as two rows. It runs on each computer's own list and again in `/api/home` over every computer's list, so tasks from a remote computer on an older Bridge AI are also merged.
- `dueOf()` reads the day a task names ("by Friday", "tomorrow", "on 12 Nov", "2026-11-20", "next Thursday", "end of week"), counted from the day the task was added. Chief of Staff's tasks have no due date of their own, and a meeting's action items often say when. Only English words are read; any other task has no day, and it goes in the undated group.
- A date-only `added`/`done` value is treated as local midnight, not UTC midnight (before, a task added today showed as "Nov 4").

**Home (`src/components/NeedsHome.jsx`, `needshome.css`)**
- **Waiting on You**: the inbox's answer-in-place cards, two across on a computer.
- **Ready to Look At**: short rows in a quiet list. Each row has the name, the project once (only when it differs from the name), a PR tag, a line or two that ends at a word, and the computer and time on the right. Newest first. Only the last day's six newest show, with **Show all N** for the rest of that day. **Older than a day · N** is folded away, with **Clear all**, which asks once more. On a computer, Pull request / Clear / Open appear while the pointer or keyboard focus is on a row. Clicking a row opens the whole message with Reply, Pull request, Clear and Open. Rows you've opened go lighter, and **Clear read · N** clears them. Clearing hides the rows at once and brings back, with a note, any row its computer couldn't clear.
- **Coming Up**: a day at a time (Today, Tomorrow, Thu Nov 12…) in time order: the meetings left today and tomorrow (one meeting on two calendars shows once), with "In 25 min", the brief and the invite's files on the next one, and the tasks that name a day under that day as **Due** (or **Overdue**).
- **Chief of Staff's Tasks**: the tasks it's working on, and "**7 to do, with no day set**", folded.
- Empty, loading and error states say what's going on: a loading label, "Nothing needs you right now", "Nothing new to look at" with what would show there, "Nothing on your calendar for the rest of today or tomorrow, and no task with a day", "Nothing on Chief of Staff's list". A refresh that fails says "Home couldn't update: … This is what it had last" and keeps what it had. The kind filter only shows once there's something to filter. The header now shows the date.
- Phone (`.app.narrow`): one column; the computer and time sit under each row's text; titles wrap instead of being cut off; no hover actions (opening a row shows them); every control is a 40 px target and the reply box is 16 px.
- Section names are in Title Case (Waiting on You, Ready to Look At, Coming Up, Chief of Staff's Tasks). The Files kind filter is gone: an invite's files are now on its meeting row.

**Shared pieces I had to fix (please review)**
- `server/needsyou.js`: an agent's last message is cut at a whole word ("…the intro to…" instead of "…your list, fr…"). The Needs-you inbox gets this fix too.
- `src/components/NeedsYou.jsx` (`NeedsItem`): the project isn't repeated when the agent is named after it ("GIT", not "GIT GIT"). Same in the inbox, and in Everything's lane rows.

Still a trial feature: same `home` id, off by default. No other part of the app changed.

**Translations**: 38 new strings in all 7 packs, written by `scripts/i18n.js add`. `prune` removed only Home's 13 old strings from each pack. `check`: 3284 of 3284 in every pack, with no placeholder errors.

## What the tests check (`test/suites/home.mjs`, now 105 checks; the README row is updated)

- **Unit (no server)**: the same task twice on one list (with a stray space or full stop) is one row, the one Chief of Staff is working on. The same task on two computers is one row (the one waiting on you, here). Same-named agents on two computers stay two rows; a cloud agent seen from both is one. `dueOf` on 11 titles, including ones that name no day. A long last message is cut at a whole word.
- **A morning, as the owner's Home had it**: two linked Bridge AIs; Desk's real task list has a meeting's action items twice (handed on twice), plus tasks that name a day; 24 finished items of every age, a question and a failed run added to the real `/api/home` answer with `changeAnswer`; the calendar has one meeting on two calendars. Checks:
  - Desk's list has the duplicate tasks twice, and Home shows each once.
  - Sections appear in order with honest headings. Coming Up shows Today, Tomorrow, then each later day in order. The doubled meeting shows once. Dated tasks sit under their day. No undated task appears under Coming Up.
  - 7 undated to-dos are folded, each once when unfolded.
  - Ready shows six rows with Show all (newest first, all within a day) and 14 older ones folded.
  - No project is said twice, in a row or in the inbox card. Every summary ends at a word.
  - Hover actions are hidden until hovered. An opened row shows the whole message with no half word at the end.
  - Clear read clears the 2 opened rows. Clear all asks once, then clears the 14 older ones.
  - At 375 and 430 px with everything unfolded and a reply box open, the phone fit check passes (no overflow, 40 px targets, 16 px field).
  - Loading says so. An empty Home says so in every section. A failed refresh says so and keeps what it had.
- The existing desktop, phone, Everything and trial-off checks were updated for the new layout. Separately, Everything's lane check now waits for the Agent Map's list, which can arrive a moment after Home's; it failed once in a loaded run.

## Screenshots (made locally, not in the repo)

- Before (main's Home, same scene): `test/.out/shots/before-home-morning-1440.png`, `-1440-tall`, `-phone-375`, `-phone-375-tall`, `-phone-430`, `-phone-430-tall`.
- After (`node test/run.mjs home`, plus `webkit-` copies): `home-morning-1440.png`, `home-morning-1440-hover.png`, `home-morning-1440-open.png`, `home-morning-1440-tall-dark.png`, `home-morning-phone-375.png`, `home-morning-phone-375-coming.png`, `home-morning-phone-375-tall.png`, `home-morning-phone-430*.png`, `home-empty.png`, `home-desktop.png`.

## Runs

- `npm run build`
- `node test/run.mjs home needs-you app-ui rail-ui phone-parity i18n-ui --browser both --no-retry`: all 12 passed. home 105/105 in Chromium and WebKit, needs-you 58/58, app-ui 210/209, rail-ui 32, phone-parity 50, i18n-ui 61.

author: athvin
body:
`er-dev-namespace/values.yaml` justifies `limits.cpu: "40"` with an arithmetic comment that PR9's colour dimension invalidated without touching the file.

```diff
-  limits.cpu   3 × 12 (L) + 2 for the app  = 38  → 40
+  limits.cpu   3 × 12 (L) + 5 at a cutover = 41  → 40 (!)
```

Measured by rendering the chart with both colours up:

| | limits.cpu |
|---|---|
| er-dispatcher | 1.0 |
| web-api-blue | 1.5 (api 1 + web 0.5) |
| web-api-green | 1.5 — the second colour a cutover runs |
| one hook | 0.5 (weight-ordered, so one at a time) |
| er-tenant-drift | 0.5 if the CronJob fires in the window |
| **peak** | **5.0** |

**Nothing is broken today and no value changes.** The conclusion still holds — at most two concurrent L pods — but because *ephemeral storage* refuses the third (1200 > 900), not because cpu does. At two L pods it is 24 + 5 = 29 of 40.

The reason to fix it rather than leave it: raising `requestsEphemeralStorage` to 1200Gi to admit a third L pod, which the comment frames as a cost decision someone may take, would make `limits.cpu` binding at 41 of 40 — intermittently, only while a deploy overlaps a full queue. The stale `38` actively says there is room. The note now says to raise `limitsCpu` in the same change.

Found while checking the two constraints the blue/green plan flagged before a first two-colour deploy.

author: tsnl
body:
Both browser engines now delegate restoration, durable saving, and checkpoint publication to `(snail shell page)`. The existing `define-application` and `define-ui` declarations remain usable, keeping this lifecycle change separate from their replacement in the next two PRs.

The page owns one optional checkpoint and a separate completion flag. Engines explicitly acknowledge a completed initial presentation. A wall-clock save event works without animation frames, and recovery serializes the last checkpoint without entering either engine. Root ownership checks protect checkpointing and readiness, as they already protect event consumption and storage.

Browser project targets can now select a concrete `Application` type; their generated entry uses the shared root protocol. Adapt the IDE's memory fixtures to the explicit presentation callback while preserving their checkpoint assertions.

Validation: static and separately linked application-runtime fixtures; full `make test` and `make check`; Chromium scene/DOM reload, rollback, periodic persistence, stale listener handling, and both IDE suites.

author: lacymorrow
body:
Bumps this repo's CI Node version off an end-of-life release line.

## What and why

`actions/setup-node` was installing a Node major that no longer receives
security patches:

| Line | End of life |
|---|---|
| 18 | 2025-04-30 |
| 20 | 2026-04-30 |

Source: `nodejs/Release` `schedule.json`, read 2026-11-05.

This is a CI runner, not a deployed runtime, so reachability is low. It is
still a pin we control and it cannot fix itself.

## Why 22 and not something newer

Because **this repo's own `.nvmrc` already says 22**, so the bump aligns CI
with the Node version the repo already declares for development rather than
introducing a new mismatch. The value is written as a bare major so it floats
to the newest patch on the line (22.23.4 as of 2026-11-05) instead of pinning
a minor that goes stale the same way.

Worth knowing, and deliberately **not** absorbed into this PR: Node 22 itself
leaves maintenance on **2027-04-30**. Moving the fleet to 24 (supported to
2028-04-30) or 26 (Active LTS since 2026-10-28, supported to 2029-04-30) is a
real decision about toolchain support across many repos, not a side effect of
a security bump, so it is filed separately.

## Not touched, on purpose

- **`engines.node`** — left exactly as it is. On Vercel an open `engines` range
  overrides the project's own Node setting and floats to the newest major,
  which is what took townofharmony.org's build down for three days. Any change
  there is handled per-repo with that in mind, not swept.
- **`.nvmrc`** — already on 22, nothing to do.

## Verification

CI on this PR is the check: it is the thing being changed, so a green run on
the new version is the evidence. If it goes red, the pin was load-bearing and
this PR should be closed rather than forced.

Part of the Node pin sweep in LAC-5353 (audit: LAC-5349).

author: lawrencecchen
body: ## Summary Follow-up to #36590 (merged as 19abcd5a264), asked by the lead. CLAUDE.md says that changes to hidden or background content update the model only, with no layout until the content shows, then one layout to its final state. After #36590, a WebKit page parked in its pane's page area (another tab shows) still followed the page area in every frame of a key resize. Its web view took a new frame in each motion frame. - While the page is parked, `WebKitPageContainer` still follows the page area (cheap, in process), but it does not resize the web view or an attached Web Inspector. It records the size it had when the first resize reached it. - It applies that one resize when the page shows again. The catch-up runs once, from the first of these: the `isHidden` setter, `viewDidUnhide`, or the next layout pass. A page alone in the container takes the container's bounds directly. With an attached inspector or an emulation, the container resizes its subviews from the first parked size. - Emulated pages are not placed while hidden. An earlier try in #36590 (a781cbc) waited only for `viewDidUnhide` and did not catch up. This version does not depend on that one callback. ## Testing Command (fleet): `cmux-ci run --class light --script scripts/ci/package-test-lane.sh --ref SHA --arg=suite --arg=Packages/macOS/CmuxNext --arg=WebKitPagePaneMotionTests,BrowserChromePaneMotionParkTests --env CMUX_CI_XCODE_APP=/Applications/Xcode_26.6.app` - RED on the test commit (b95c94796f5, on the #36590 head): step 6bb532a0 FAILED as expected. `aParkedWebKitPageResizesOnceWhenItShows`: the parked page took a frame in 12 of 12 key-resize frames. - GREEN at 447265b2b39 (same code as this head, before the cherry-pick onto feat): step 166cfe9b PASSED. All 5 WebKitPagePaneMotionTests and BrowserChromePaneMotionParkTests pass. - An intermediate fix (9fe64ba) failed the same test (the page kept its parked width when shown). 447265b fixes that. ### Observed / Not run - Observed: the fleet red and green steps above. - Not run: a build, launch smoke and focused tests at this exact head (fb4405587ad, the same 3 commits cherry-picked onto feat 68335982c56). They run next. ## Changelog none --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic A hidden WebKit page no longer takes a web view frame in every key-resize frame. While parked in its pane's page area, the container still follows the page area but records its size instead of resizing the web view or attached inspector; that one resize applies when the page shows again, from the first of the `isHidden` setter, `viewDidUnhide`, or the next layout pass. Emulated pages are no longer placed while hidden. - A page alone in the container takes the container's bounds directly on show; with an inspector or emulation, subviews resize from the first parked size. - The parked-page motion test now asserts the web view takes no frame during 12 resize frames and has its page area's size when shown. Written for commit fb4405587ad8d5f8e2292aa5b1c09461d7645341. Summary will update on new commits.

author: tmac1973
body:
The sidebar and autoconfig label GPUs with the monitor's `gpu.Index`, while Model settings and the device lists sent to llama-server use the GPU's position in the monitor's list. Those agree only when the indices run 0..n-1 with no gap.

On AMD, the rocm-smi collector sets `gpu.Index` from the card's KFD position. If rocm-smi ever left out a card that KFD knows about, the list would have a gap (say, only index 1). Model settings would then call that card "GPU 0" and send `ROCm0` to llama-server, which is a different card, while the sidebar showed "GPU1".

This adds `checkKFDCoverage`: when rocm-smi lists fewer GPUs than KFD, the collector returns an error and the sysfs fallback, which numbers every KFD GPU in order, takes over.

I haven't seen this happen on any machine; it's a hardening change. On the local RX 9070 XT + iGPU box the rocm-smi path still passes the check (indices 0 and 1). `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass, and a unit test covers both cases. No docs change, since nothing visible changes for users.

author: uliseis
body:
Closes #498

## What changes for users

The `--baseline` jq query in the `results.json` reference and the plugin's copy named a variable `$then`. `then` is a jq keyword, and jq 1.6, the version common distributions ship, rejects it. The variable is renamed, so the query runs as written.

No other jq snippet in `docs/` or `plugin/` binds a jq keyword as a variable.

## How it was verified

```bash
! grep -rn '$then' docs plugin
npx vitest run test/plugin.test.ts
npm run check   # typecheck, build, the full test suite, version and changelog checks, smoke
```

Both queries were run on jq 1.6 against a small `results.json`-shaped file: the old one fails to compile, and the new one prints `book-a: 1/2 -> 2/2` and `book-b: - -> 1/1`.

body:
## 무엇이 바뀌나요

Keeper 효율을 달 단위로 주는 서버 경로(`GET /api/v1/keeper-efficiency`)와 디코더는 10-31 에 들어왔어요. 그런데 디코더를 부르는 곳은 시험 두 개뿐이었고, 이 경로를 읽는 화면이 없었어요. 실제로 11-06 01:46Z 에 제가 처음 부르기 전까지 이번 달 캐시 파일이 없었어요.

이 PR 은 Keepers 화면의 Info 탭에 그 달의 효율을 붙여요.

- Info 탭을 열면 TUI 시계 기준 이번 UTC 달을 한 번 읽어요.
- Keeper 한 명의 값을 전체 Keeper 의 턴당 값 옆에 보여 줘요.
  - 턴 수, 턴당 도구 호출, 턴당 도구 시간(초), 턴당 출력 토큰
  - 실패한 도구 호출 수
- 한 번 읽은 답에 그 달의 모든 Keeper 가 들어 있어요. 그래서 읽기는 달을 열쇠로 써요. 읽는 동안 다른 Keeper 로 옮겨도 다시 묻지 않아요.
- 읽는 중, 실패, 지난 값에 새로고침만 실패한 경우를 각각 다른 줄로 보여 줘요. 실패를 빈 달로 그리지 않아요.

## 제한 시간을 따로 두는 이유

라이브 서버에서 그 달 첫 호출은 41.7초 걸렸어요(11월 1~6일 엿새치, Keeper 33명). 그 뒤 호출은 0.11초였어요. 기본 제한 시간 10초로는 매달 첫 읽기가 늘 실패해요. 그래서 이 GET 하나에만 120초를 줘요.

- 장점: 첫 읽기도 끝까지 기다려요. 다른 읽기의 제한 시간은 그대로예요.
- 단점: 서버가 멈추면 Info 탭이 최대 120초 동안 "읽는 중"으로 남아요. 화면은 그동안 다른 동작을 막지 않아요.

## 같이 바뀌는 것

- 달을 계산하는 함수를 `Keeper_efficiency.month_of_unix_time` 로 옮겼어요. 서버 경로가 달을 받지 못했을 때 쓰는 기본 달과 TUI 가 보내는 달이 같은 함수에서 나와요.

## 확인

- `test_tui_keeper_efficiency` 에 시험 셋을 더했어요.
  - 읽기가 묻는 달이 UTC 기준인지 봐요. 10월 마지막 초, 11월 첫 초, 해 넘김을 확인하고, 서버 기본 달과 같은 함수인지도 확인해요.
  - 요청 경로에 늘 달이 들어가요.
  - 읽을 수 없는 답(빈 객체, 다른 schema, 객체가 아닌 값)은 실패로 남아요.
- 화면 문구와 배치는 시험하지 않았어요(constitution 353~355줄).
- 사본 디렉터리에서 type-check 했어요. 기존 의존 파일은 그대로 두고, 새 모듈·mli·시험은 lib 경고 설정으로 검사했어요. 셋 다 통과했어요.
- 같은 사본에서 시험 3개를 돌렸고 3/3 통과했어요. 로컬 dune 은 돌리지 않았어요(constitution execution_protocol).
- 아직 확인하지 않은 것: 실제 TUI 에서 Info 탭을 연 화면. 병합한 뒤 main 에서 tmux 로 찍어 확인해요.

body:
## Why

CI must not run third-party build tooling with a known advisory, and every action stays pinned to a verified commit. This bumps three CI-only pins. None of them reaches the binary or the image contents.

## What

| Pin | File | Old | New |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BuildKit driver image | `image.yml` (`publish` job) | `moby/buildkit:v0.34.1@sha256:99368f3e…` | `moby/buildkit:v0.34.2@sha256:c5f8862f52499773af85bc07695b2379ef08e8002352b0df2c4864c91d78dabe` |
| `jdx/mise-action` | `ci.yml` (`lint`, `terraform`) | `6be3c7ed… # v5.2.4` | `f5be966e4a917d54244728e6a5fdcd1d93a35e6c # v5.2.6` |
| `docker/login-action` | `image.yml` (`publish`, `verify-published`) | `81c6f93d… # v4.7.0` | `8aa5831fb8d48d8f76594c7ddde61ae58019f550 # v4.8.0` |

- BuildKit v0.34.2 fixes GHSA-2fqp-xg6f-v7gj (medium, a daemon panic in the Git source resolver, affects v0.26.0 to v0.34.1). Our Dockerfile has no Git sources.
- BuildKit v0.34.2 also ships the first fix for GHSA-w26x-xg27-7qjc (medium, xattr writes outside the BuildKit state directory). Its advisory names v0.34.1 as patched, but tags v0.34.0 and v0.34.1 point at the same commit. The fix (fsutil `Setxattr` to `LSetxattr`, commit `d4bfe06a4d`) first ships in v0.34.2, so the v0.34.1 pin was exposed to both advisories.
- mise-action v5.2.5 updates packslip to 1.11.0 (stricter check of the signed mise release). v5.2.6 exits after a failed cache restore instead of hanging up to 10 minutes. `action.yml` is unchanged between v5.2.4 and v5.2.6.
- login-action v4.8.0 sets a 1 hour default for the Docker Hub OIDC token and bumps dependencies. `action.yml` is unchanged. The bundled `undici` (6.29.1) and `handlebars` (4.7.10) are the same as in v4.7.0, and the GitHub advisory database lists no advisory for either version.

## Pin checks

- Each action SHA is the commit of its tag: `git ls-remote` and the GitHub refs API agree, both tags are lightweight, and each tag has a published, non-draft release.
- The BuildKit index digest is what `moby/buildkit:v0.34.2` resolves to. Its provenance names `refs/tags/v0.34.2` and the tag's commit `8c579433824224dc64a158cf8734495b6e2b186a`.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 and 1.7.7 pass on both workflows. `zizmor --offline` reports the same 8 `artipacked` findings as on main, and no new ones.

## Testing

- The `lint` and `terraform` jobs of this PR run mise-action v5.2.6.
- `image.yml` runs only by dispatch, and the new BuildKit and login-action pins sit in its `publish` jobs. I did not dispatch it. A local check of the BuildKit pin and of login-action v4.8.0 follows in a PR comment.

Fixes #707

body:
**Problem (seen live, 2026-11-06).** Antigravity set up Synthe on `rishabram/synthe-e2e-antigravity` from a folder where `prompts/system.md` had uncommitted edits. Setup read the **local** file (a CAD site-planning prompt) and generated CAD test cases and checks, but GitHub still had an old one-line placeholder. Rounds 1–3 tried to improve the placeholder against CAD test cases, every candidate broke something, and the run stalled after $0.39. Setup only checked that the file is tracked (`git ls-files`), never that it matches GitHub.

**Change**
- `init` (interactive and `--agent` draft) reads the prompt file from GitHub's default branch (`gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" repos/<slug>/contents/<path>?ref=<branch>`) right after the prompt is chosen, **before any test cases or checks are generated or anything is written**, and stops if:
  - the file isn't on GitHub (404): "prompt.md isn't on GitHub (main) yet…"
  - it differs from the local file: "prompt.md on this machine isn't the same as on GitHub (main)…"
  - GitHub can't be read: "couldn't read … check your connection"
  Each message gives the commands to push (`git add`, `git commit`, `git push`) and ends "Nothing changed."
- `init --agent --confirm` checks again (someone may push between draft and confirm). The draft is kept, so the team can push and confirm again.
- Line-ending (CRLF) and trailing-whitespace differences are ignored. Inline prompts check the code file that holds them.
- Agent guide step 1 (`docs/AGENT-SETUP.md` and its copy `src/cli/guide.ts`) says the prompt file must be pushed too.

**Verified**
- `npm test`: 396 pass, 0 fail (3 new tests: refuse on differs / missing / unreadable in both interactive and agent mode with no test-case generation, secrets, commits or files; accept when only line endings differ and read from the default branch; confirm refuses after a post-draft push and succeeds once it matches). `npm run typecheck` clean.
- 6 deliberate mutations, all killed: skipping either check, removing normalization, treating 404 like other errors, ignoring the branch, never refusing.
- Setup test fakes now answer the raw-content read with the repo's own file.
- `dist/` rebuilt from source; `dist/action.mjs` also picks up main's stale package description (same drift noted in #42).

Not released: needs a founder release (npm publish + moving `v1`). Overlaps #42 only in `docs/AGENT-SETUP.md` / `src/cli/guide.ts` (different steps) and the dist files; whichever merges second needs a rebuild.

author: danfuzz
body:
From: Agent @cfc-envelope working on behalf of @danfuzz (Opus 5.5)

**This lands ahead of its specs ruling, [specs#89](https://github.com/commonfabric/specs/pull/89), as that pull request's interim rule, under a `SPEC-PENDING` marker and with no flag.**

## TLDR

### The Problem

The memory engine checks that a commit's `cfc` envelope is well-formed and backed, but not whether it lowers what the store holds. A client that skips its runtime's label machinery could hand it `{ ...stored, cfc: undefined }` and erase another person's declared labels. #9648 closes that door in the runtime. This closes it at the store, for the declared component.

### The Solution

The engine refuses a commit that leaves a path whose stored declared entries hold a confidentiality clause with no declared entry, unless the space's owner signs it and every dropped clause is theirs alone to release (the owner release, §8.12.7 route 2c). The release decision moves to `memory` so that store and runtime share it.

## FabriChat Tie-In

@seefeldb, this is a CFC rule at the store, ahead of your ruling on specs#89, so your eyes especially.

A stamp of other people's `PersonalSpace` atoms on the FabriChat manager's result in a person's Home hid that person's whole Chats tab, and nobody could lower it ([`top/2566`](https://estuary.saga-castor.ts.net/topics-dev-476ea34f/fid1:Wh5pQ_tM2vxmmzJ9CYIpZJOJeOeVILpgj8F-viXsEaw)). Reproducing it, two agents both lowered and raised a stored label map by writing the document directly. #9648 closes that in the runtime. A client bypassing its runtime still reached the store untouched, and this is the store-side bound. Specs [#88](https://github.com/commonfabric/specs/pull/88) (#9639) deals with how such a stamp is minted in the first place.

## The rule, and what it leaves out

- A commit is refused when, for a document it stores and doesn't leave deleted, a path has stored entries with `origin: "declared"` holding a confidentiality clause, and the commit leaves no declared entry there. Erasing the whole `cfc` member is that case at every declared path. The check covers a `set`, a patch that reaches the metadata, and a delete followed by a re-creation in the same commit.
- The exception is an owner release. The space is the DID of the commit's acting principal (`delegated.actingPrincipal`, else the signer), and `clauseReleasableBy()` admits every dropped clause for that principal, digest commitments included. A commit naming no actor releases nothing.
- A label held by reference (`{ $ref: "cid:…" }`) is read from the label document the space stores. One that doesn't resolve can't be released.
- Integrity-only and empty declared entries (writer-claimed markers) aren't counted, since dropping a claim is monotone. Neither are legacy (origin-less), derived, structure or link entries.
- It doesn't judge a document's meta fields (`patternIdentity`, `argument` and the rest) at all. #9653 guards those in the runtime, and no store check covers them.
- It doesn't refuse a lowering that keeps a declared entry at the path, or a change to an existence entry. specs#89's proposed rule does both. They wait for the runtime's own declared-monotonicity gate (`cfcDeclaredMonotonicity`), which today runs at `observe` because some schema mints are non-monotone by construction.

## Ahead of the ruling

- **Class:** semantic gap. The specification at the pin (and at specs `main`) says nothing about what a store verifies of a handed envelope. specs#89 asks the question, applies the full rule as its proposal, and proves (`interimAdmitted_of_declaredAdmitted`) that this interim rule refuses nothing the full rule admits.
- **Fail-closed:** against the current text, it only refuses more and persists nothing new. Against the proposed rule it refuses a subset, so a ruling for that rule only widens the refusals. A ruling for no store obligation would remove it.
- **Marker:** `// SPEC-PENDING https://github.com/commonfabric/specs/pull/89` sits in `runtime/memory/v2/envelope-admission.ts`. This PR adds the memory package's CFC sources to the files `check-cfc-correspondence` governs, so the marker counts against the budget. It lands with no flag under @danfuzz's standing authorization of labs pull requests ahead of unresolved specs dependencies. That authorization doesn't supply a ruling.

## What changed

- `runtime/memory/v2/envelope-admission.ts`, new: `droppedDeclaredPaths()` and `admitsDroppedDeclaredPaths()`.
- `runtime/memory/v2/engine.ts`: `applyCommitTransaction` records the `cfc` member each envelope-replacing operation leaves its document with. After the commit's reads are validated, it refuses a commit `admitsDroppedDeclaredPaths()` doesn't admit. Running after read validation matters: a commit made against a stale view (two first custody seals racing to create one anchor, an append from a session that hadn't loaded the list) is refused as the conflict it is, which its writer retries, rather than as a drop of labels it never saw. An operation the validation elided isn't judged.
- `runtime/memory/v2/cfc-release-authority.ts` and `cfc-label-fields.ts`, new, with their definitions moved verbatim from the runner: `clauseReleasableBy()`, `isActorOwnedAlternative()`, `hasExactKeys()`, `isOrClause()`, `clauseAlternatives()`, `isCfcFieldCommitment()`, `commitmentAwareEquals()`, the `CfcConfClause` and `CfcFieldCommitment` types, and the field-classification table. The store and the runtime's release must decide the same thing, and `memory` can't import `runner`. This follows `memory/v2/read-ceiling.ts`, the one validator both sides already share.
- Every call site imports from the new home, and `cfc/label-field-classification.ts` is gone. That's 70 files, in a commit of their own (a7b6b4d9c5) that changes no behavior. The only names still exported from a runner module are the `@commonfabric/runner/cfc` barrel's, which other packages import through it. The kernel manifest's `canReleaseStoredClause` row names the new file, and the live docs that cite the table's path follow it.
- `tasks/check-cfc-correspondence.ts`: the memory package's CFC sources (`v2/cfc-*.ts`, `v2/envelope-admission.ts`) and `v2-envelope-admission.test.ts` join `GOVERNED_SOURCE`, and the sources join a new `CITATION_SOURCE`, so the release authority stays under the procedure after the move. The check also fails now when a `missing` manifest row's `decidedToday` names a symbol its file doesn't declare, or a file that doesn't exist. Deliberate breaks of the `canReleaseStoredClause` row's two symbols, and a marker naming no specs PR in `envelope-admission.ts`, each fail it. `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/cfc.md`, `cfc-spec-correspondence.md` and `automated-gates.md` list the new files.
- `docs/specs/cfc-stored-envelope.md` gets a new section, "What the store refuses of a handed envelope". `docs/plans/runner_cfc_implementation.md` notes that the store now closes the unsynced-writer erasure for declared entries.
- `cfc-declared-monotonicity.test.ts`: the fixture that rewrites a stored declared entry into a legacy or derived one now deletes the document first. That rewrite is exactly the drop the store refuses. The `speculation-overlay.test.ts` fixtures that restate a stored envelope now keep its stored entries, for the same reason.

## The runtime's own writes aren't refused

Run with the engine instrumented to log every commit that drops a declared path, in a separate worktree (RUN):

- **Route 2c releases:** `cfc-confidentiality-release.test.ts` and `cfc-release-gate-integrity.test.ts` pass. They log two drops, both `admitted`, one of them a `PersonalSpace` owner held as a `{ digestOf }` commitment.
- **`cf cell set-label`:** `piece-label.test.ts` and `test-cfc-label-store.test.ts` (CLI) pass. Three releases, at `[]`, `["body"]` and `["items", "*"]`, all `admitted`.
- **`exactCopyOf` and the per-writer integrity claim:** `cfc-exact-copy*.test.ts`, `cfc-declared-monotonicity.test.ts` (including the observe-mode non-mo

author: jisung-02
body:
Fixes #456

## Why

An agent follows tool descriptions, `next_action` text, and prompts literally, and eight of them contradicted what the tools return or what the API allows. Each one led to a wasted or wrong call. Six are wording fixes; two change a result.

## What changed

- A 4xx from `AlpaconHTTPClient` no longer carries httpx's raw line as `message`, so each tool's `default_message` reaches the agent. `state_command_purpose` now says not to resubmit.
- `raw_data_available` follows `statistics.available` on the CPU, memory, disk, and network usage tools, so an empty window reports `false`.
- Descriptions, prompts, and docs now state that an expired session cannot be extended, that a sudo inside a command is denied at once and rerun after a person acts, which CSRs can be denied, and which field carries a refusal code.

## Scope

- Covers the eight items in the issue, plus the same wrong text in sibling docs.
- Also fixes what depended on the raw line: recovery hints matched on the URL inside it, and three sites composed text around it.
- Leaves out the API's `detail` body, which a 4xx did not surface before and does not surface now. Also leaves out `work_session_extend` with a past `expires_at`, which the server answers with `work_session_expired`, so that one case still reads as an expired session.

## Tradeoffs

The fix removes `message` from the client envelope instead of preferring `default_message` in `unwrap_http_result`. Every 5xx, timeout, and `outcome_unknown` message is real information and must keep winning, and the client is where the useless value was made.

## Blast radius

A client that matched the old `Client error ...` text in `message` has to read `status_code` and `error_code` instead; both are unchanged. A client reading `raw_data_available` can now see `false`. author: stefan-migo
body:
The audio investigation is stuck one field short, and the field is being thrown away here.

## What Meta sends for 131053

```json
{"code": 131053, "title": "Media upload error", "message": "Media upload error",
 "error_data": {"details": "Audio file uploaded with mimetype as audio/ogg, however on processing it is of type application/octet-stream."}}
```

`title` and `message` are the same useless string. `error_data.details` is the only field that names the cause, and `_delivery_error` preferred `message`. Every audio failure therefore reached the operator as `131053: Media upload error — Media upload error`: a code with no reason.

## Change

- Prefer `error_data.details`, falling back to `message`.
- Keep the raw `errors` array on the audit row (`meta_errors`, capped at 2000 chars). A formatter can be wrong; the evidence should not be lost with it.

## Measured context, so nobody re-derives it

Both failing shapes are valid files, and Meta stores both uploads correctly:

- fragmented MP4 from `MediaRecorder`, AAC 48 kHz mono: Meta keeps it as `mime_type: audio/mp4`, size and sha256 matching.
- Ogg/Opus produced by our normalizer, 8 s mono: Meta keeps it as `mime_type: audio/ogg`.

Uploads with `type: audio/ogg` and with `type: audio/ogg; codecs=opus` are both accepted and both stored as `audio/ogg`. So the failure is **not** the container, **not** the codec and **not** the upload `type` — it is what Meta's processing stage does with the media afterwards, and only `error_data.details` says what.

## Verification

- RED with the formatter stashed: `assert '131053: Media upload error — Audio file uploaded with mimetype as audio/ogg, … octet-stream.' == '131053: Media upload error — Media upload error'`.
- GREEN: `focused tests/unit/test_webhook_statuses.py` exit 0 (4 tests), `db tests/integration/test_webhook_ingest.py` exit 0, `quick` exit 0.

Small and diagnostic on purpose: the next failed audio will carry its own reason in the panel and in the audit row, and that text decides the real fix.

## Summary

Builds on #160 and targets its branch. After #160 is merged, this PR goes against `dev`.

`languages.json` is the file the launcher downloads from `main`, and its URLs send every user to a download. Rules 5 to 7 under "Adding a game language" are new:

- A new language and every changed URL need a confirmation from the translation's maintainers: a comment by them in the PR, or a link to the page where they publish the URLs.
- URLs point to hosts that the translation project controls or names as its mirror. Link shorteners, redirect services and third-party mirrors are not allowed.
- A PR that changes `languages.json` is never merged automatically. The `Auto-merge` workflow now skips such PRs and turns auto-merge off when a later push adds the file. Back-merge PRs from `main` are exempt, because their changes were already reviewed on the way to `main`. The workflow runs from the base branch (`pull_request_target`), so the rule takes effect when this PR is merged.

Also:

- "translation files" in the code style, the checklist and the PR template now means the game's `global.ini` files. The launcher's own `translations/*.ts` stay in the repository.
- AI rules: issues, bug reports and review comments describe what the author observed, AI-written text is marked, and logs and claims are checked before they are posted. `SECURITY.md` asks the same for vulnerability reports.
- Checklist and PR template: a bug fix comes with a test that fails without the fix, if the bug can be tested without the game or the internet.
- `AGENTS.md`: a language PR links the translation maintainers' confirmation.

Documentation, plus one step in `automerge.yml`. The YAML parses. The new step uses `gh pr view --json files`, which reads the PR through the API and checks out no PR code.

author: josephismikhail
body:
## Why

Ix-pro is consolidating plural list commands into subcommands of the singular:

- Ix-pro#182 (merged): `ix tasks` -> `ix task list`
- Ix-pro#184 (merge-ready, head dd7358f5): `ix decisions` -> `ix decide list`. The earlier hidden `decisions` alias has been removed.

This repo still stubbed both plurals as Pro commands, its MCP server still shelled out to `ix decisions`, and its help and guides still pointed at both. This follows the same pattern as #396 (`bugs` -> `bug list`).

## What changed

1. **Stubs.** `tasks` and `decisions` are removed from `PRO_COMMANDS` (`register/pro-stubs.ts`, re-exported by `oss.ts`) and from the `scripts/check-plugin-contract.mjs` allowlist. An OSS-only `ix tasks` now gets `unknown command 'tasks' (Did you mean task?)`, and `ix decisions` gets `unknown command 'decisions'`. The `task` and `decide` stubs swallow operands, so `ix task list ...` and `ix decide list ...` still reach the Pro sentinel. The tests check both outcomes positively.
2. **Help and docs.** `ix workflows` uses `ix task list` and adds `ix decide list`. The `ix query` hint now says `ix decide list`. The docs-site command reference, `skills/ix/references/output-formats.md` and the openapi `planning` tag drop the plurals; the skill now names the `<singular> list` forms. `COLLAPSED_HELP_TOPICS` gains `tasks: "task"` and `decisions: "decide"`.
3. **MCP `ix_decisions`.** It tries the read-only `decisions` first. On Pro releases from before #184 (including v0.2.0, the latest tag) that is the answer, including any real error. A Pro that has retired it answers with commander's `unknown command 'decisions'`, so nothing runs, and only then does the tool use `decide list --format=json`. This is decided per call, not latched: Pro loads on every run, so one run where Pro failed to load would otherwise pin a pre-#184 Pro to `decide list`. A post-#184 Pro pays one extra failed run per call until the Pro floor passes #184, when the `decisions` attempt should be dropped. The tool never reaches a `decide` that could record.
   - `IxArgv` gains optional `subcommands`, emitted before the options. Options placed earlier would bind to the parent `decide`.
   - The input `path` is now refused explicitly, and `topic`/`limit` are added. Neither command ever had `--path`, and silently stripping the key would have returned every decision to a caller asking about one symbol.
   - Both Pro shapes (v0.2.0 and #184 dd7358f5) are exercised through the real in-process runner, not hand-written stderr.
4. **Help forwarding vs. older Pro.** The forwarder now applies only when the plural is absent or is an OSS stub (`isProStub`). On releases that still register a real `tasks`/`decisions`, `ix help <plural>` shows that command's own help.

## Release sequencing

`ix workflows` and the `ix query` hint now name `ix task list` / `ix decide list`, which exist only in Pro releases that include #182 and #184. The MCP tool falls back, but the help text does not. This PR should land alongside or after that Pro release.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Plugin repos.** The six plugin repos still call `ix decisions` (e.g. ix-claude-plugin `skills/ix-investigate/SKILL.md`, ix-openclaw-plugin `tools/ix-history.ts`, ix-cursor-plugin's `ix_decisions {path}`). The advisory Plugin contract job will flag them now that `decisions` is off its allowlist. That is the intended signal, since #184 removes the command.
- #920: the stale `plans`/`goals` stubs, help topics, allowlist entries and docs.
- #919: `ix_decide` with a title of `list` lists decisions instead of recording one, once #184 lands.

## Not changed

- `pending` / `inbox` (Ix-pro#183): neither was ever stubbed or referenced here.
- CLAUDE.md on main (97 lines) has no `ix tasks` or `ix decisions` references. The table at lines 177/197 exists only in older checkouts.
- The `decisions` / `tasks` JSON keys in `impact` output are data, not commands.

## Testing

- The touched suites (pro-stub, help-topics, startup-fast-path, all `mcp-*`) pass.
- **Mutation checks.**
  - Restoring the stubs or the old forwarder fails the stub and help cases.
  - Removing the `isProStub` guard fails both pre-collapse help cases.
  - Trying `decide list` first, latching the verdict, loosening the unknown-command match, or swallowing a real `decisions` error each fail an `ix_decisions` case.
  - Removing the path refusal fails its case.
- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0. `npm run lint`: exit 0 (0 errors, the same 37 pre-existing warnings).
- Full `npm test` on Windows: exit 1, but only from 8 path/read test files unrelated to this change. Run alone, those files give the same 11 failures on `origin/main` 9d43fab8.

## 变更

- **依赖**：框架与模板的 OpenIddict 全部升到 7.8.0；同组 .NET 运行库、ASP.NET Core、EF Core 包 10.0.13 → 10.0.14，避免中央版本降级（Mapster 为独立版本号，不动）。Dependabot #221 中的其余无关升级不并入。
- **兼容处理器不删除**（对照 7.8.0 与 dev 源码）：
  - `SendCancellationGuard`：7.8.0 的 `SendHttpRequest` 仍把调用方取消记成 6182 Error 并拒绝为 `server_error`，dev/8.x 才改为照常抛出取消。保留。

  - 模板替换 `ValidateAuthorizedParty` 的处理器：7.8.0 仍要求调用方是 aud 或 presenter，保留，文档版本号改为 7.8。

## 验证

author: rasmusfaber
body:
## Overview

Lets a researcher log a remote devbox into Hawk with only a restricted scope, so they and their agents can work on one lab's sensitive evals there without cross-lab contamination, and without the full login ever being stored on the box. `hawk login --provider anthropic` on the box prints a link, the researcher approves it in the viewer, and the box then renews on its own for 12 hours (`hawk login --extend` adds 12 more). Stacked on #2737.

## Approach

The box creates a login request carrying the scope, its hostname and the hash of a secret only it knows, then polls with that secret. The viewer's approval page shows what the box will read and call, what is withheld and why, and when it ends; only human logins can preview, approve or deny, so nothing on the box can approve itself. Approval creates a delegated session of a new `devbox` kind holding a snapshot of what the scope expanded to, because the box has no login to re-expand against (grants are group-level, so new models in a granted group are covered; login changes arrive at the next extension). The box exchanges its key (session id + secret) for the same 30-minute delegated tokens laptop profiles use.

On the box, a devbox login is a profile under the hood, selected when neither `HAWK_PROFILE` nor `HAWK_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set, so `hawk`, `hawk.client`, Claude Code setup and the proxy binding work unchanged. The key lives in the OS keyring (`keyrings-alt`'s file on a headless box); the short-lived token cache stays in an atomic private file. A devbox refuses every identity-provider login, a machine holding the full login refuses to become one, and `hawk logout` now also logs a machine out of its own login.

We considered pushing a session from the laptop over SSH and a paste-back Okta login on the box; the approval code needs no SSH setup and never puts the full login on the box.

## Risks

- New unauthenticated endpoints under `/token-service/devbox`; at most 10 pending requests per address, and requests are purged a day after they expire.
- The approval URL carries a 10-minute, single-use code that the access log records.
- Migration: a defaulted `kind` column and check constraints on `token_service.delegated_session`, and a new `devbox_login_request` table.
- A devbox sees login changes only at its next extension (≤ 12 h); laptop profiles re-expand at every token.
- A cap of 20 sessions per user now applies to laptop profiles too.

## Testing & validation

Tests cover the flow, the snapshot, single-winner approval under concurrency, restricted tokens refused on the approval endpoints, both machines' refusals, extension, re-login ordering, logout and keyring failures. On a dev deployment, with an isolated home directory as the box, the end-to-end checks passed (approval and preview, scoped calls, refusals, extension, denial, Claude Code setup, deletion from the laptop, logout, no full login on the box), and over 70 minutes the box renewed five times on its own.

- [x] Verified the change works (commands / manual steps described above)
- [x] Added or updated tests where it makes sense

## Code quality

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (ruff, basedpyright/mypy, eslint/prettier/tsc, shellcheck — what CI's Lint job runs)

## Before merging

- [x] PR title is a [Conventional Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) with a lower-case subject — it becomes the squash-merge commit subject and drives the SemVer bump
- [ ] Major bump: the title has the `!`, the **last** commit has a `BREAKING CHANGE: … (#<this PR>)` footer, and `docs/infrastructure/upgrading.md` gains a `### … (#<this PR>)` section (enforced by the `Breaking Change Docs` check)
- [x] All commits are **signed** and show as **Verified** on GitHub — see [Commit signing](https://hawk.metr.org/contributing/#commit-signing)

author: arul28
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #2079, which stopped a headless Duo recording coming out black.
That PR left one thing deliberately unfixed, and it is worse than its write-up
said: an iPhone Duo that changes panel mid-recording came out sideways *and*
squashed.

`AVAssetWriter` fixes the frame size at the first frame it is given. A fold then
hands the recorder the other panel — at its own size (2006x2852 against the
cover's 1398x2034) and on its own side (the inner display reports
`landscape_left`) — and `composite` drew every frame into the full rect. So the
rest of the video was one panel stretched into the other's frame, a quarter turn
off.

## What changed

`apps/desktop/native/ADESimHelper` (macOS-only native code: the helper drives
CoreSimulator and SimulatorKit, so there is no Windows half to keep in parity —
a Windows ADE reaches a simulator through a remote Mac runtime).

- **Turn it upright.** `RecordingSession` holds the live panel's quarter turn —
  the same `appleScreenRotation` the live view uses, from the existing
  `readScreenTurns`. `DeviceSession` sets it before the recording's first frame
  and `refreshRecordingScreenTurns` re-pushes it after every `posture-changed`,
  so a fold *and* a Duo merely turned in the hand both land.
- **Size the file from the upright picture**, not the raw framebuffer, so a
  recording that starts on the inner panel is a full-bleed landscape file
  rather than a landscape picture letterboxed into a portrait one.
- **Fit, don't stretch.** The other panel is fitted inside that frame at its own
  proportions and centred. A recording that never changes panel is untouched:
  `fit` returns exactly the frame when the sizes match, and interpolation stays
  `.none`.
- **Overlays follow the picture, not the frame**, so a ring after a fold lands
  on the device rather than in a bar, and its framebuffer fraction turns with
  the picture. `RecordingSession` no longer holds device metrics at all:
  `DeviceSession` normalises a tap against the panel showing when it landed, so
  a tap after a fold is placed against that panel and not the one the recording
  started on. That was wrong before, and invisible, because the picture was
  wrong too.

## Evidence

By hand on this lane's iPhone Duo (iOS 27.1), headless, no live view, driving
the helper over its own stdio protocol so the same script runs against two
builds of the same package — `origin/main` and this branch.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![After the fold, on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9f19cde-19f1-4ac8-ae52-d73cc330ba27)<!-- ade-proof:9b62f770-4642-4c58-a49b-f3d43866f2c4 --> | ![The same moment, on this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2638c574-0662-49a5-9c92-03bc4284ad23)<!-- ade-proof:621c905f-c8b8-4ad8-b28b-a4017576394b --> |

An iPhone Duo unfolding mid-recording, with nobody watching.

Started folded, unfolded 2.5 s in — 1398x2034, the cover full bleed, the inner
panel upright and letterboxed:

[Started folded, unfolded mid-recording, nobody watching](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/667fdef4-d1c8-4e77-9acb-9fc4dc8cebe5)<!-- ade-proof:8ca27fb3-4571-49ff-aa0f-013a4518987b -->

Started unfolded, folded 2.5 s in — 2852x2006, the inner panel full bleed, the
cover pillarboxed:

[Started unfolded: the file is the inner panel's own landscape](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c2fec4e-d51e-40d1-8686-d5f1fd20ff35)<!-- ade-proof:24cc9cef-f6ff-4285-adbc-d4fadc48a236 -->

Overlay placement measured, not eyeballed, by finding the ring's centroid in the
decoded frames:

- **Before the fold**, a tap at frame point (200, 400) draws its ring at
  fraction (0.43, 0.59) — exactly `200/466, 400/678`.
- **After the fold**, a tap at the framebuffer's top left (150, 150) draws its
  ring at (1177, 746): (0.84, 0.22) inside the letterboxed picture and inside
  its rect (y 525..1509). That is the top left turned one quarter clockwise,
  which is where the finger was.

**Non-foldable devices are provably untouched.** The same scripted recording on
an iPhone 17 against both builds: same frame size (1206x2622), no bars (top rows
YAVG 108.576 on both, to three decimals), and the tap ring at the same pixel,
(384, 919) against (384, 919).

`swift build -c release` is clean and the package's 84 tests pass.

## Not checked

- No Windows or Linux check: macOS-only native code with no cross-platform half.
- The rotation's sign was settled on the device, not from first principles —
  this context treats memory row 0 as the top, so its positive direction is the
  opposite of the clockwise turns `appleScreenRotation` counts. The first build
  came out 180 degrees off; the comment now records why.
- The panel that is not the first one is letterboxed, so it is shown smaller
  than it was captured. Avoiding that needs a canvas big enough for both panels
  chosen up front, which costs every single-panel recording a bigger file with
  permanent bars. Not worth it, so this PR does not take it.

author: dandocan
body:
## Summary

Configures the repo to deploy as one Vercel project with two services:

- **`web`** (Next.js, `apps/web`) is public and serves all routes (`/(.*)`).
- **`api`** (NestJS, `apps/api`) is internal. It isn't reachable from the internet directly.
- **`web` → `api` binding:** Vercel injects the API's base URL into `web` as `API_URL` at runtime.

## Changes

- **`vercel.json`** (new): defines both services and the `web` → `api` binding, with a single catch-all rewrite to `web`.
- **`apps/web/next.config.ts`:** removed the build-time `rewrites()` for `/api`. Rewrites are resolved at build time, so they can't read the runtime `API_URL` binding.
- **`apps/web/src/app/api/[[...path]]/route.ts`** (new): a Node route handler that proxies `/api` and `/api/*` to `API_URL`, stripping the `/api` prefix. It forwards all methods, buffers request bodies, strips hop-by-hop headers, and returns 500 if `API_URL` is missing on Vercel, or 502 if the API is unreachable.
- **`apps/api/src/main.ts`:** the port is now read from `PORT`, then `API_PORT`, then defaults to `3001`. Vercel sets `PORT`.
- **`apps/web/src/app/page.tsx`:** an `eslint-disable` comment on the `/api` link, which is intentionally a plain anchor.
- **Docs:** `README.md`, `.github/project-context.md`, `apps/web/docs/README.md`, and `apps/api/docs/README.md` describe the new routing and Vercel setup.
- **Tests:**
  - Removed `apps/web/test/next.config.test.mjs`, which tested the deleted rewrite.
  - Added `apps/web/test/api-proxy.test.mjs`, which covers proxy behavior against a local HTTP server.
  - Added `apps/web/test/vercel.test.mjs`, which asserts the services, binding, and rewrite in `vercel.json`.
  - Added `apps/api/src/main.spec.ts`, which covers port precedence.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm test` (web: 11 passing, api: 4 passing)
- [x] `pnpm test:e2e`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [x] Manual production smoke test: built API and `next start` with `VERCEL=1` and `API_URL` set. `/` and `/api` both responded.
- [ ] `vercel dev` end-to-end check of the `web` → `api` binding. Not yet verified.
- [ ] Preview deployment. Not yet verified.

## Reviewer notes

- **The API is publicly reachable through `web`'s `/api` route.** The binding doesn't add authentication. Confirm that's acceptable before merging.
- The binding resolves only at function runtime, not during builds or in middleware.
- The NestJS framework slug (`nestjs`) and the binding format were checked against the Vercel docs, not against the live schema validator. A preview deploy will confirm both.

author: rob2rhyme
body:
Track 3, T2: learner memory, built to the decision note Robin approved on November 6, 2026 ([`docs/decisions/2026-11-06-learner-memory.md`](https://github.com/rob2rhyme/mrig/blob/main/docs/decisions/2026-11-06-learner-memory.md)). This PR also marks that note decided and records the answers.

## Acceptance (docs/ROADMAP.md and JUMPSTART, T2)

> Robin approves the note before any code; then read, write and delete are tested; nothing is sent over the network; the offline guarantee (L5) is respected.

## Robin's answers (the recommended ones)

1. The summary goes to **local models only**, with a global `learner.shareWithCloud` opt-in for cloud models.
2. Each result is **recorded as it happens**, with a visible tool line and no prompt.
3. **`teach` records what it taught** as `introduced`; `learn` records right and missed.
4. Reviews follow a **1, 2, 4, 8, 16-day** schedule (five Leitner boxes).

## What changed

- **`src/learner.ts`** (new):
  - **Where:** one JSON file with a version, `~/.mrig/learner.json`. Inside an offline zone, `<zone>/.mrig/learner/learner.json`, whose folder gets a `.gitignore` like the zone's sessions folder.
  - **Saving** is atomic: a temporary file is renamed over the old one.
  - **Bad files are never overwritten.** A file mrig can't read (bad JSON, no topic list, or a newer version) is reported with "fix or delete it".
  - **`recordResult`:** right moves a topic up a box, missed sends it back to box 1, and introduced starts it without a score. The status follows (introduced, practising, or known from box 4 up), and so does the next review date.
    - Topic labels are normalized (NFC, trimmed, single-spaced, case-insensitive match), so "Git rebase" and "git rebase " are one topic.
    - The same topic in two varieties stays two records.
    - Notes are capped at 200 characters; an empty note clears it.
    - Unknown varieties are refused.
  - **`forget`** removes one topic, one variety, or all.
  - **`learnerSummary`:** due topics first, then the weakest, at most 30, grouped by variety, so varieties are never pooled.
  - **`learnerReport`** builds what `/learned` shows.
- **The `learned` tool** (`src/tools/learned.ts`), offered only in learn and teach mode.
  - It writes only mrig's own file, so it counts as read-only. It passes learn mode's read-only gate and never asks, even in teach mode. Every call shows as a tool line.
  - It loads, changes and saves on each call, so two sessions don't overwrite each other.
- **The summary in the prompt** (`Runtime.learnerBlock()`): only in learn and teach mode.
  - It's read once per session, so the cached prompt stays byte-identical even after the session records results.
  - **Only for local profiles**, unless the global `learner.shareWithCloud` is set. With a cloud model, a single notice says the session starts without it, and results are still recorded locally.
  - A project config can't set `learner`.
- **The mode prompts** tell the model about the tool. Learn: record each answer and start with due topics. Teach: record a newly taught topic as introduced. Both stay well under the prompt budget (default 1,308, teach 1,902, learn 2,038 characters).
- **`/learned`** (all, `due`, `where`, `<words>`) and **`/forget`** (`<topic>`, `--variety <tag>`, `all`, confirmed with `/forget all --yes`). `/forget` says that session transcripts and your own backups of `~/.mrig` are outside its reach.
- **Docs:**
  - README: a "Learner memory" section and the command list.
  - ROADMAP and JUMPSTART: T2 marked ✅.
  - AGENTS.md: the file map.
  - The decision note: status "decided by RT", the answers recorded, and the zone path made exact.

## Tests (no network, mock models)

`tests/learner.test.ts`, 19 tests:
- **Recording:** the five boxes and their review dates; the top box; missed back to box 1; status changes; label normalization; varieties kept apart; the note cap and clearing; bad input.
- **Forgetting:** by topic, by variety, all.
- **The file:**
  - a round trip, and a missing file read as empty;
  - **a failed write leaves the old file byte-identical** (the temporary path is blocked);
  - an unreadable, versionless or newer file is reported and left untouched;
  - the zone path and its `.gitignore`.
- **Summary and report:** due first, then weakest, grouped by variety, capped at 30 with a count; `/learned` everything, due, search and no match.
- **Through the runtime:**
  - **Learn mode, local model:** the summary is in the prompt, and the prompt is byte-identical on the third request after a recorded result. The write didn't ask.
  - **A cloud model (Claude):** no summary, one notice, and results still recorded locally.
  - **`shareWithCloud`:** sends the summary. A project config can't set it (reported as ignored).
  - **Default mode:** no summary and no tool. **Teach mode:** records introduced without asking.
  - **Offline zone:** the zone file is used, the global memory stays out of the prompt, and the global file is byte-identical afterwards.
  - **Commands:** `/learned`, `/learned where`, and `/forget` for a missing topic, a topic, a variety, and all (two steps, with the transcripts and backups warning).
- **The tool:** read-only, local, and its exact output. A broken file is refused, not overwritten.

`tests/modes.test.ts` now expects `learned` among learn mode's tools.

## Verified

- `bun run check` passes: lint with zero warnings, typecheck, **312 tests** (293 → 312), and the compiled binary.
- **Two sessions with only loopback networking**, run in the same network namespace as T5's check: the internet was unreachable, and a stand-in local model sat on 127.0.0.1.
  - **Session 1** (`mrig --mode learn -p …`) started with no memory, and the model recorded `Magar numerals 1-10 (mgp) missed`, note "mixes up 7 and 8".
  - **Session 2** started with that topic in its prompt ("practising, 0/1 right, due … (mixes up 7 and 8)"), with the same summary on both of its requests, and recorded a second result.
  - **`learner.json`** afterwards: `asked 2, right 0, box 1, due 2026-11-07`.

## Not verified

- **How well a real model uses it:** whether it quizzes from the due topics and records results reliably. That's worth a hand try with a local model, and it's the groundwork for T8 (the Akkha tutor).

author: emostov

## Summary & Motivation (Problem vs. Solution)

author: moyaver
body:
## What broke

Nested Maestro steps (`runFlow`, `retry`, `repeat`) were paired with the wrong start. On the flow page, block parents stayed `running` after the flow finished, and each block's end showed up as an extra unnamed "Step N" row. Reported in #62.

## Root cause

`Session::on_step` kept one `open_step` per flow. A child's RUNNING line overwrote its parent's, so the parent's end found nothing open and allocated a new index with no start.

A second cause sits in the same function: `open_flow` excludes a flow that already has a console result. In the captured `features` run, the last `Press Home key COMPLETED` line is processed after the flow's `[Passed] features` line, so that end was dropped and the step stayed running. The same happens to the last step of most fixtures.

## Fix

- Open steps are a stack of `(index, description)`. An end closes the innermost open step with the same description and drops any steps still open above it. An end with no matching start keeps the old behaviour (its own index).
- An end goes to the latest flow when that flow still holds the step open, even after its console result. Starts are routed as before.
- No protocol change (#38 is out of scope). `fleet-maestro` is untouched.

## Test evidence

- New `nested_steps_pair_their_ends_with_their_starts` (`crates/fleet-agent/tests/it/inspect.rs`), driven from the captured `features` run (runFlow, retry, repeat) and `retry-fail` (a failed child inside a retry). It checks that every step has one start and one end, and the statuses: the parents are `completed`, the optional run-flow is `skipped`, `Retry 1 times` is `failed` with both children `failed` (I3).
- Fail before, pass after. With `git stash push -- crates/fleet-agent/src/session.rs` the test fails on the pairing check (starts `[0..9, 11, 12, …]` vs ends `[0..4, 6..10, …]`). With the fix restored it passes.
- Insta snapshots (`it__inspect__*`) were regenerated, and each change is intended:
  - `features`: `steps` 28 to 25 and `step.ended` 24 to 25. The three unnamed rows are gone.
  - The other 14 snapshots each gain the one `step.ended` that the late-end fix recovers, and the event count rises by the same amount (`shard-all-2` +8, `shard-split-2` +3, `suite` and `suite-with-adb-load` +4 each, the rest +1). Insta also dropped the stale `assertion_line` header from `absolute-path`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p fleet-agent --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast`: 816/816 pass.
- `cargo test --doc --workspace`, `cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` (`-D warnings`), and `cargo xtask lint`: pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` ran against a local Postgres 18 (`DATABASE_URL`). Two full runs each stopped at a different timing-sensitive test while the host load average was about 85: `fleet-e2e` concurrent jobs, `fleet-agent` signal forwarding, and the `metrics` busy-loop CPU check. Each passes alone and in the no-fail-fast run above. `cargo xtask ci` stops at the first failure, so it was not green in a single run on this loaded host.

author: kiran-jones
body: ## Summary Empty layout boxes (title, subtitle, body, image) can now be deleted, from the editor and from MCP `delete_elements`. - `deleteElements` removes a layout box once it's empty. A text box with text stays. An image box with a picture loses the picture first, and a second delete removes the box. - A removed box is tombstoned with `slotRemoved: true`. `ensureLayoutSlots`, `slideMissingSlot` and `deckMissingSlots` leave it alone, so the open-time repair, duplicating and slot-completing writes don't bring it back. Slots that went missing any other way are still repaired. - It comes back on `setLayout` (choosing a layout in the editor), snap back, `setSlotImage`, and server writes that put text or an image in that slot (`set_slides`, `update_slide`, MCP `update_element` on the slot name). - In the editor menu, Delete and Cut are enabled for an empty layout text box. - The MCP tool description and the Slides help article say how removal works. ## Collab / CRDT This adds a `slotRemoved` field on layout box element maps in the Yjs deck. Clients that are already open ignore it: they see the box as deleted, but their own `ensureLayoutSlots` (on add/duplicate/set layout) could still revive it until they reload. Nothing is hard-deleted, so the worst case is a box coming back. ## External API consumers MCP clients: `manage_slide_deck` keeps its input schema. `delete_elements` can now include layout box ids in `removed`, `snap_back` and `update_element` accept a removed layout box's slot name, and the description has one added sentence. ## Tests Added tests in `freeform-ops.test.ts`, `deck.test.ts`, `manage-slide-deck.elements.test.ts` and `direct-pure.test.ts` for removal, keeping a box with text, the image box's two steps, staying removed through repair, duplicate and writes, coming back on layout, snap back, image and text, and the menu's Delete state. I didn't run typecheck locally. ## Release note Empty title, body and image boxes on a slide can now be deleted. Choose the layout again to bring them back. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

body: ## Después de hacer pull El error `Failed to resolve import "three"` aparece si `platform/node_modules` se instaló antes de esta dependencia. Hay que instalar **dentro de `platform/`**: ```sh git pull cd platform npm install npm run dev ``` `three@0.187.0` está en `platform/package.json` y en `platform/package-lock.json`. OrbitControls y GLTFLoader se importan desde `three/addons/...`. Luego abrir http://localhost:4321/laboratories/mruv ## Qué se agregó Simulador 3D de MRUV en la página del laboratorio (`/laboratories/mruv`), con el modelo del riel y el carrito. 1. **Modelo en el canvas.** `Riel_y_carrito_v2.stl` (mm) pasó a `platform/public/models/riel-y-carrito.glb` (metros) y se carga con Three.js. 2. **JSON paramétrico.** `platform/public/data/mruv.json` trae `x0`, `v0`, `a` y `railLength`. Al abrir la página se hace `console.log` del objeto. 3. **Bucle físico.** `requestAnimationFrame` y `THREE.Clock`. En cada cuadro: `x = x0 + v0*t + 0.5*a*t*t` a lo largo del riel. 4. **Jerarquía.** `THREE.Group` `hardware-estatico` (riel) y `movil-dinamico` (malla del carrito y una esfera de referencia). Controles en español: Reproducir, Pausar, Reiniciar, y sliders de velocidad inicial y aceleración (se aplican al reiniciar). Una línea marca la estela. [Simulador MRUV en marcha](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-0fbd0e6d-54af-55e7-9c7b-5f6037da89c3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmruv_simulator_desktop.png) [mruv_simulator_play_reset_trail.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-0fbd0e6d-54af-55e7-9c7b-5f6037da89c3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmruv_simulator_play_reset_trail.mp4) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: linqibin0826
body:
## Summary

v0.20 后端：登录、注册、找回密码接入人机验证。支持 Cloudflare Turnstile 和 TRUSTTURN，改 Nacos 配置就能切换，线上也能切。

- **登录**：同一 IP 15 分钟失败 5 次，或同一邮箱失败 3 次，就要先过验证；已锁定的账号直接返回 429。
- **注册和找回密码**：每次都要过验证。
- **验证不了一律拒绝**：第三方失败或超时都不放行，错误码和账号锁定不同。
- **公开接口**：`GET /auth/human-verification` 返回当前厂商和 `sitekey`，门户不用另配。
- **PAP-190**：第一个提交先重构登录用例，人机验证接在重构后的用例上。

设计见 `docs/patra/release-specs/v0.20-human-verification.md` 和 `docs/patra/specs/2026-11-05-identity-human-verification-design.md`。

## 必须和门户 PR 一起合并

门户 PR 基于这条分支。这版没有关闭开关，只上后端会出两个问题：

- 门户还不传令牌，注册和找回密码全部被拒绝。
- 门户还没取真实 IP，所有外网用户共用一个 IP 计数，累计失败 5 次后，所有外网用户登录都要先过验证，而门户此时还显示不了组件。

合并顺序：先合这个 PR，门户 PR 变基到新的 `main` 后立刻合并。两次部署之间有几分钟不一致，现在只有少数体验用户，可以接受。

## 合并前后要做的

- [x] mini 的 `~/.patra/secrets/identity.env` 已写入 Turnstile 凭据（只在 mini 上，不进仓库）
- [ ] 部署后确认 Nacos 里的 `patra-identity.yaml` 已是新版本
- [ ] 确认 identity 容器的 JVM 能出站到 Turnstile（目前只用 curl 验证过）
- [ ] 确认 `CF-Connecting-IP` 能经隧道到达门户
- [ ] 在 mini 上推一次 Nacos 配置，确认厂商切换能在线生效（嵌套配置的重新绑定还没有实测）
- [ ] TRUSTTURN 切换实测（等用户提供 `site_key` 和 `app_secret`）

出站超时这里是连接 4 秒、单次 5 秒，重试一次。#404 实测第三方登录的平台单次最慢 3.8 秒，这版实测 Cloudflare 单次 2.5～3 秒，余量比 #404 小。没有放宽到 #404 的 10 秒、15 秒：门户只等 15 秒，再长就比门户晚放弃。如果线上出现校验超时，把这里和门户的 `VERIFIED_SUBMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` 一起调。

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew check integrationTest` 通过（前后端合在一起的代码；之后的修复只跑了 identity 受影响模块的 `check` 和 `HumanVerification` 相关集成测试）
- [x] 适配器单测和集成测试用 WireMock 模拟两家：通过、失败、令牌重复、`hostname` 或 `action` 不符、超时、TRUSTTURN 的签名和时间戳
- [x] `HumanVerificationFlowIT`：不带令牌直接调三个接口被拒绝；校验失败不占失败限制名额，也不做密码哈希；第三方不可用时一律拒绝
- [x] 本机连真实后端跑门户 e2e 13 条，用 Turnstile 官方测试密钥。13 条都通过过，但没有一次全部通过：一轮过 11 条，另外 2 条单独各过两遍，那 2 条的失败判断是本机到 mini 走中继时延迟太大
- [x] 用户本地验收通过
- [ ] 线上用真实密钥验收（release spec 第 5 节）

## Linear

Closes PAP-190
Closes PAP-192
Closes PAP-193

## 摘要

- 变更覆盖 identity 的 domain、app、adapter 和 infra 层，并调整 gateway 的公开路径；新增文档描述 portal 接入方案，但本次没有 portal 实现变更。
- 新增 Cloudflare Turnstile 和 TRUSTTURN 人机验证，支持通过 Nacos 切换提供方。登录在邮箱失败达到 3 次或同一 IP 15 分钟内失败达到 5 次时要求验证；注册和找回密码每次都要求验证。新增 `GET /auth/human-verification`，用于查询当前提供方和 `siteKey`。
- 新增登录邮箱/IP 失败计数、验证守卫及两家提供方的适配器。验证失败不会占用登录失败次数；验证服务不可用时拒绝请求。
- 未发现 Flyway 迁移或数据库 schema 变更。
- 测试结果：作者报告后端 `./gradlew check integrationTest` 通过；线上真实密钥验收尚未完成。

author: yijunw0212
body:
第 13 批⑦「取模型列表」（用户 11-05 补充：模型要有基础的获取模型列表）。按 [§13.2](specs/assistant-service-connections/spec.md) 的决定：取列表经 `horizontal/agent-host`，不经 Prologue（Prologue 没有这个接口），取到的列表只用来选、不另存。验收新增 **ASC-56**。

## 做了什么

- **agent-host**（`horizontal/agent-host/src/model-list.ts`）：`listProviderModels`。Anthropic 格式请求 `GET {base}/v1/models?limit=1000`（`x-api-key` + `anthropic-version`），OpenAI 格式请求 `GET {base}/models`（`Bearer`）。
  - 地址规则和 Run 一样：HTTPS，或本机 HTTP；不能带账号、查询参数或片段。
  - 不跟重定向（密钥会被一起带走）；15 秒超时；最多读 4 MiB；最多 500 个模型，去重并排序。
  - 401/403、404/405、429、其他非 2xx、读不懂的回答，各有自己的错误码（`agent.model_list.*`），提示里不带密钥。
- **宿主**（`apps/local-host/src/model-provider-list.ts`，路由 `POST /api/settings/models/<id>/models`）只负责决定用哪个密钥：
  - 依次是：页面上填的、选的连接、这个供应商已保存的。
  - 已存的密钥只发往它的连接绑定的地址；绑的是别的地址，在读出密钥之前就拒绝（和保存前检查同一条规则）。
  - 取列表不写连接、不绑地址、不存列表。
  - 页面上的令牌照旧要求；服务的拒绝按错误码换成页面语言的说明。
- **设置页**：模型列表头加「从服务取模型」按钮。
  - 取到的模型用组件板的 `renderCombobox` 列出：输入即筛选，点选或回车就加进模型行（有空行就填进空行），↓ 进入列表。
  - 已在列表里的模型打勾；手填照旧。
  - 取失败时在状态行说明原因，已经填的不动。
- 顺带两项：
  - #1845 评审小修：汇总时筛选使用方，改为看 `consumer.provider.kind === "system"`。
  - 13.md 补上 #1845 的合入记录和本片说明。

## 开工前检查

- 事实主人：模型提供方的请求归 agent-host（唯一跟模型服务说话的包）；哪个密钥能去哪个地址，归宿主的连接库（`connector-connection-store`）。两处都没有另开路。
- 合同：没改 contracts、Manifest、动作 schema 和 MCP 工具名。新路由是设置页内部的 HTTP，走现有的令牌/Origin/幂等键门。
- 界面：只用组件板已有的控件（`mw-btn`、`renderCombobox`、`model-field`），没有新增组件；Design A 的「界面三块」仍等 D 轨标本（④），本片没碰。
- 红线：页面资源增长经用户 11-05 弹窗批准，在 `APPROVED_CEILINGS` 登记（见第二个提交）；没碰真实 Home、vendored 和 CI。

## 防腐与代码质量

- 安全：已存密钥只去绑定的地址，测试断言「绑了 A、问 B」时 B 一个请求都没收到，回答里也没有密钥；不带页面令牌的请求返回 403，服务收不到任何请求。
- 不跟重定向，响应读取有上限；错误提示从错误码映射，不转述服务的原文。
- 错误码用 `defineErrorCodes("agent.model_list", …)`，主人前缀和所在目录一致；宿主沿用设置页现有的 `Error(L(...))` 写法。
- 没有新的空 catch、`as unknown as`、兼容标记；`pnpm health:check --base origin/main` 通过，`pnpm boundary:check` 通过。
- 页面资源（对照 merge-base 645aa717）：settings.css +271 B、workbench.css +271 B、workbench.js +2,357 B。第一版是 +754/+754/+3,441，后来做了几处收紧：
  - 选择框复用 `.model-field` 和组件板的 combobox 样式；
  - 保存和取列表共用一个取密钥的小函数；
  - 列表头去掉包裹层。
- 测试里的密钥每次运行随机生成（`pnpm secrets:check` 干净）。

## 验证

- `tests/model-provider-list.test.ts`（ASC-56，新增）覆盖：两种格式的地址和头、解析（去重/排序/上限）、各种状态码，以及经正式 HTTP 路由走的这些情况——填的密钥、已存密钥、绑定地址拒绝、没令牌、密钥加连接同时给、密钥太短、没有密钥、401/404/429/503、回答不是 JSON、连不上，最后确认什么都没写。
- 相关用例 `--jobs 1` 跑过：`model-provider-list`、`model-settings-http`、`model-providers`、`security-invariants-connection-switch`、`security-invariants-plugin-pages`、`model-first-setup.e2e`、`model-vision.e2e`、`model-ready-cross-tab.e2e`，全部通过。没有跑全量。
- 浏览器预览：用本机的替身模型服务，看过中文 1024 深色（含 404 的说明）、英文 375 浅色（没有横向滚动）、中文 800 深色（筛选、回车加行、重复点选提示、打勾）。

author: jejezz
body:
## 변경 내용

**탭: 무엇이 어디서 도는지 한눈에**
- 탭을 두 줄로: 첫 줄은 `셸  폴더`(폴더 이름이 겹치면 부모를 붙임), 둘째 줄은 실행 중인 명령 또는 전체 경로. 툴팁에 경로·셸·명령·종료 코드.
- 명령이 0.5초 넘게 돌면 탭 앞에 진행 스피너, 마지막 명령이 실패하면 다음 명령까지 빨간 점.
- 셸 통합으로 알아냄(`shell_integration.dart`): PowerShell(`-EncodedCommand`)과 bash·Git Bash·WSL(`PROMPT_COMMAND` 환경 변수)이 프롬프트마다 폴더(OSC 7), 명령 시작·종료 코드(OSC 133/633)를 알린다. 사용자 프로필을 다 읽은 뒤 걸리고 `$?`를 되돌려 starship 등과 충돌하지 않는다.
- 탭 아이콘 색을 탭마다 다르게(같은 폴더의 셸 여러 개도, 옆 탭끼리도 구분). 한 번 받은 색은 `cd`나 다른 탭을 닫아도 그대로.
- 탭이 많을 때 마우스 휠·스크롤바로 가로 스크롤하고, 고른 탭·새 탭은 자동으로 보이는 곳으로 온다.

**설정: 화면 글자 크기**
- 설정 "외형"에 슬라이더(80~150%, 기본 100%). 메뉴·탭·폴더 이름·상태 줄 등 터미널 밖의 모든 글자가 커진다. 터미널은 영향을 받지 않고 기존 터미널 글꼴 크기로만 정한다.
- 글자가 들어가는 고정 높이(탭 줄, 파일 목록 줄, 상태 줄)도 배율에 맞춰 키운다.

## 확인한 것
- `flutter test` 287개, `flutter analyze` 통과.
- 실제 ConPTY에서 Windows PowerShell, Git Bash, WSL(Ubuntu)의 폴더·실행 중인 명령·종료 코드·`cd` 추적을 확인(`TEST_PTY=1`).
- 앱을 띄워 두 줄 탭과 스크롤을 눈으로 확인했다.

## 알려진 한계
- zsh·cmd는 셸 통합이 없어 폴더 이름 대신 셸 이름이 보인다. zsh는 이 PC에 없어 돌려 보지 못했다. PowerShell 7(pwsh)도 이 PC에 없어 실제로는 확인하지 못했다.
- 비밀번호가 든 명령이 탭(스크린샷)에 보일 수 있다. 숨기는 설정은 아직 없다.
- 큰 배율에서 LineSender 하단 줄(고정 높이)이 빠듯할 수 있다.
- `local_pty_e2e_test`의 WSL 기존 테스트 하나가 이 PC에서 계속 실패한다(이번 변경과 무관해 보임).

author: eyalamirmusic
body:
Two warnings show up when Crashout is built as a CPM dependency of tamber-web on macOS.

**Warnings**

1. `Lib/eacp/CrashReporting/Faults/Matrix.cpp:90: warning: unused function 'pending' [-Wunused-function]`
2. During configure:
   ```
   CMake Warning (author) at _deps/crashout-src/CMakeLists.txt:18 (include):
     The module name FindEacp.cmake does not match the case of the module file
     name on disk .../CPM_modules/Findeacp.cmake
   ```

**Fix**

1. `pending()` sits in the anonymous namespace with no platform guard and has no callers on any platform (none since the move out of eacp), so it is deleted. `OutcomeStatus::pendingPR` and `ExpectedOutcome::pullRequest` stay; the tests, the demo app and `expectStall` still use them.
2. `CMake/FindEacp.cmake` is renamed to `CMake/Findeacp.cmake` and included as `include(Findeacp)`, matching the CPM package name `eacp`. A consumer that already added eacp has CPM's generated `CPM_modules/Findeacp.cmake` earlier on the module path; on a case-insensitive file system `include(FindEacp)` resolved to that file and warned about the case mismatch. `CLAUDE.md` is updated to the new path.

**Verified**

- Standalone: `cmake -G Ninja -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DEACP_UNITY_BUILD=OFF`, `cmake --build build`, `ctest`: all 9 suites pass on macOS arm64.
- tamber-web full build with `-DCPM_Crashout_SOURCE` pointing at this branch: no CMake warning from Crashout's configure and no compiler warning from any Crashout target.

author: efrec
body:
### Work done

Continue cycling key presses after Context Build swaps one building for another based on terrain type. Previously, the current key would be reset because the engine does not handle the case when a keyset is empty.

Could be an engine fix, instead. Works very well here and resolves the issue with Legacy keys being unable to reach past the first contextual-build command.

Legacy can put two swappable units on the same cycle, so armllt and armtl can take "extra" presses to cycle through. I didn't check for this in the code, it's a minor defect.

This widget only works when the map has water, so it's not really the correct place to change this cycling behavior. We should consider refactoring a large amount of our controls, including this, now. Other widgets and etc that handle cycles of key presses would need similar or identical handling.

There are probably edge cases I did not think about.
