author: many-question
body:
## What

A **local viewer** for older enterprise Linux (CentOS 7 / RHEL 8 / RHEL 9), where the desktop viewer's libraries (WebKitGTK 4.1) are not to be had: `apps/local`, one program that serves the web viewer on `127.0.0.1` and is drawn by a browser. It is built static in the next PR, so it has no library to find on the machine, needs no root and no network, and with `ssh -L` the browser may be on another computer. This PR is the program and the page's side of it; the static build, the container tests on CentOS 7 / Rocky 8 / Rocky 9 and the separate release come in the PR after (own tag prefix, never the latest release, the existing AppImage and .deb untouched).

The research and a CI probe (closed, rich-netlist/rnl#354) showed what it stands on, in containers of `centos:7`, `rockylinux:8` and `rockylinux:9`: the static musl `rnl` runs; the **official Firefox ESR, unmodified and unpacked in a directory of its own, starts headless on CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17), opens the web viewer, draws a netlist and solves it through the solver service**; CentOS 7's own repository has Firefox 115 ESR, exactly the page's minimum; Rocky 8 and 9 have 153 ESR.

### The program (`apps/local`)

- **No new dependency**: the core's crates and `serde`. The HTTP is a small strict piece over `std::net` (one request and one response a connection; `Content-Length` bodies only; no chunked bodies, folded headers, two `Host`s), because an HTTP crate was one more thing to fetch and to audit.
- **Security** (README § Security): listens on `127.0.0.1` only; serves only a `Host` of `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`[::1]` (any port: `ssh -L` changes it); the first address has a 256-bit token that **works once** (spent by the right token only) and is **never on a command line** (the browser is told to open a file of the user's own, in a new 0700 folder with a name nobody could have made first, made with `create_new`; both are removed once it has). The session is a **key the page sends in a header** (`X-RNL-Key`) with every request that reads or writes files or solves, `/f/` reads included; it is given in the fragment of the address the program goes on to and kept in the page's `sessionStorage`, **not in a cookie** (a browser sends a cookie to every port of an address, so a page from another local port would have had it). A request that changes something also needs `X-RNL: 1`, the program's own origin and a request that is not cross-site. A request is judged **from its head**, before any body is read (1 MiB for most, 512 MiB for save and solve, 1 GiB in all at one moment; a body is judged by its pace, 64 KiB/s over 30 s, not by a time for all of it, so a big save over a slow `ssh -L` is taken); the head has 10 seconds in all, waiting connections are limited with the oldest closed to make room, and places are kept for the session's page, so a slow client cannot stop the page or the program. The page may read and write only below the **folders allowed**; what the *page* chooses to open or include must have no hidden part, and the root, the home folder or one that holds it is not given (a file in one alone); only regular files, at most 256 MiB; saving is whole-or-nothing where that keeps the file's owner, group, mode and names (temp file with those, flush, rename), and in place where it would not (hard links, another group's file, a folder the user cannot write in), without emptying the file first: the new bytes go over the old, the file is cut to length, and on any failure the old bytes are put back; **Save As asks before it replaces a file and never writes through a link**; the page cannot be framed and its address takes no `?url=`/`?manifest=`/`?embed=`/`?api=`; each run has a browser profile of its own (no lock of an earlier run).
- **What it does**: serves the page (embedded at build time, or `--site DIR`); reads the files by path for the core in the browser (`/f/<path>`); **Save / Save As** with the desktop's own semantics (decision 0011, written again here with its tests: each file in the encoding it had, line ends restored, asked first about a file that changed on disk, every encoding settled before the first write); **Solve** in the program with the core's `rnl_cli::preview`, through the same service the web viewer's development server offers; settings in `~/.config/rnl-viewer-local/settings.json`; the files read are watched once a second (polling, which also works on network file systems) and the page says when one changed (F5 reloads; the desktop does not reload by itself either); the browser launcher, which refuses a browser below the page's minimum with the two ways out named, opens Chromium-family browsers as an application window and Firefox in a profile of its own (`--no-remote`; the user's own profile is never touched), and stops the program when the window is closed.
- 54 unit tests (HTTP parsing and its deadlines and pace, the Host/token/key/Origin rules, bodies not read before the head is let in, the allowed folders and links and hidden names, saving incl. Latin-1, atomic writes and Save As over a file or a link, the solver, the watcher, the gate, the launcher's private folders), and `tests/local.spec.mjs`: the page against the program in Chromium and WebKit.

### The page (`apps/viewer-ui`)

- **`shells/local.js`**, the web shell with the machine's files behind it, and **`server-files.js`**, the file chooser (the machine's folders one at a time in the page's list dialog: up, in, "Choose this folder", and for a file to open the last entry is the browser's own chooser). A source's path is its path on the machine, so Document paths, diagnostics and Save say what they say on the desktop.
- **`overwrites`**, a capability of a shell of the web platform that writes where it read from: Save is *Save* and not *Download File*, with Save As and the UTF-8 forms (`commands.json`: `with: "overwrites"` / `unless: "overwrites"`; the desktop's menu plan is unchanged), and the question before leaving files with changes offers to save them. The web shell without it is as it was (tests).
- **A browser too old for the page is told so** (an ES5 script in `index.html`): the scripts use what the browsers had by 2021–2023 (top-level `await`, `Object.hasOwn`, `Array.prototype.at`, module Workers), so an older browser stopped at the first and showed nothing. It covers the page with a notice that names what is missing and what to use (tests take each feature away).
- The web shell's Solve request carries `X-RNL: 1`, which the program asks of every request that does anything (the development server ignores it).
- 8 new texts, translated in the seven languages.

### Known, and left for later

- A thread per connection under a flood of connections (the places are limited, the threads that wait for them are not): a pool is a change of its own.
- A local client that reads the page's own large files slowly can still hold the 40 places for requests that are not of the session, so that loading the page is blocked for a while (every answer has a time for the whole of it, so not for good): a local denial of service only. A follow-up could put a per-run prefix in the path of the page's own files.
- What a rename does not keep and nothing in the standard library can: ACLs and extended attributes of a file saved by replacing it (the new file has its folder's defaults; the owner, group, mode and hard links are kept, see README).
- The `#k=` address of the redirect stays in the browser's history; the key dies with the run, and the page takes it from the address at once.
- The desktop viewer's save (`apps/desktop/src/files.rs`) is not atomic either: a separate PR, with the same owner/group lessons.

### Not in this PR

- The Library's **PATH folders** (the desktop's `pathPackages`) are left out: they need the Library's index and preloading to read from the machine, a piece of its own; **Include Folder** from the machine's chooser takes their place for now.
- The static musl build, the tests

## Summary
Initial infrastructure for two low-cost, WAF-protected WordPress sites.

- **Azure**: an Ubuntu 24.04 B2s VM (Trusted Launch) whose NSG has **no inbound** rules. Also a Key Vault holding the tunnel token, read by the VM's managed identity, and Recovery Services daily backups (Enhanced policy, 14 days).

- **Bootstrap** (`bootstrap/Initialize-TerraformBootstrap.ps1`): sets up locked-down state storage (Entra auth only), the resource groups, and a GitHub OIDC identity with least-privilege RBAC.

author: lvyufeng
body:
## AI Agent Information

- **Agent**: DeepSeek agent session (Claude Code harness)
- **Model**: deepseek-v4.1-flash
- **Session date**: 2026-11-06
- **Human reviewer requested**: @lvyufeng

## Summary

Moves the Cambricon training-step operators into the CNNL code generator and fixes four correctness bugs it surfaced. 16 operators are now generated from templates instead of hand-written per file. A single Qwen3 4-layer training step (`fp32` on MLU590) drops from **856.8 ms to 459.7 ms**, and the forward pass from **392.0 ms to 132.6 ms**, against torch_mlu's 35.5 ms and 19.3 ms on the same box.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Performance improvement
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/CD

## Platforms Affected

- [ ] CUDA
- [ ] Ascend
- [ ] MetaX
- [ ] MThreads
- [ ] Iluvatar
- [ ] Kunlunxin
- [ ] Enflame GCU
- [ ] Tsingmicro
- [x] Cambricon
- [ ] Other

Cambricon only. The other platforms' generators and confs are untouched; `gen_vendor_confs.py` was rerun and every other vendor conf is byte-identical.

## Problem Analysis

### What was broken/missing?

Measured against torch_mlu 1.32.2 on the same MLU590, fp32, 4 layers / hidden 1024 / seq 512 / batch 2, one step cost **856.8 ms** against **35.5 ms** — 24x. Writing perf aside, scalar arithmetic did not work at all.

### Why did it happen?

Three performance causes and one correctness cause, found by profiling rather than by reading the code:

1. **The matmul contiguous-copied the weight on every call.** `F.linear` is `x @ w.t()`, so every linear layer handed `mm` a transposed view, and `mm` called `.contiguous()` on it. A 1024x1024 multiply cost **8996 us** that way.
2. **The binary kernels materialised every broadcast.** `add` of `[2,512,1]` against `[2,512,1024]` expanded the small operand to full size first, so the copy dominated: **5809 us**.
3. **Nothing was under the generator.** Operators lived in hand-written `.cc` files, so any fix had to be made 16 times or not at all. `AGENTS.md` requires non-CUDA platforms to integrate through their code generator.
4. **Correctness:** `x * 2.0` spells the number as a **rank-0 tensor**, and a CNNL descriptor cannot express rank zero, so `cnnlSetTensorDescriptor` returned status 3 for **every scalar arithmetic op**. It was masked because `mul.Scalar` had no native kernel and fell through to FlagGems.

### Investigation process:

I wrote C probes against CNNL before changing any kernel, rather than inferring the API:

- **Broadcast:** `cnnlOpTensor` given `[2,4,1]` against `[2,4,8]` returns status 0 and produces the `[2,4,8]` product; given a reduced-rank `[2,4]` or a flattened `[16]` descriptor it rejects with status 7. So operands must be described **at their own rank**, with no expansion.
- **Transpose:** `cnnlSetMatMulDescAttr` is unsupported on this SDK (status 3). `cnnlMatMulEx_v2` also needs an explicit algorithm — passing an empty one gives "Algorithm initialization failed" — so it takes `cnnlGetMatMulExAlgoHeuristic` then `cnnlGetMatMulExHeuristicResult`, with transposes set through `cnnlSetMatMulExDescAttrBase(desc, a_op, b_op, /*use_beta=*/false, CNNL_MATMUL_EPI_NONE)`.
- **Strided reads:** `contiguous()` on a transposed view costs 15762 us, `copy_` 18936 us, `cnnlCopy_v2` on strides 16451 us, against 59 us for the same numel contiguous. The cost belongs to the strided reads themselves, not to any one kernel, so `clone` declines strided views instead of claiming them.
- **Registration:** after adding ops, every route reported "backend not registered" while the kernels were present in the library. Two causes: self-registering statics in an anonymous namespace are discarded by the linker, and a stale duplicate `T_REDUCE_ALL` definition silently dropped the `REGISTER_IMPL_TO_DISPATCHER` line for `sum` and `mean`.

Two measurement mistakes I made and retracted, since they shaped earlier conclusions: timing a function containing N ops and dividing by N (made `mm` look like 1011 us; it is 37 us), and concluding "the device is waiting" from `run_backward` tottime when submit-only and submit-plus-sync both measured 942.2 ms — the time is CPU submission, not device work.

## Solution Design

### Implementation approach:

`scripts/codegen/codegen_cambricon.py` grows from a stub into a template-per-category generator (binary, scalar, unary, reduction, matmul, bmm, embedding backward), driven by an `OPS` table and rendering the whole kernel body from a per-category template — the same shape as the Kunlunxin and Ascend generators.

The generator covers 16 operators: `abs`, `add.Scalar`, `add.Tensor`, `bmm`, `embedding_dense_backward`, `mean`, `mean.dim`, `mm`, `mul.Scalar`, `mul.Tensor`, `mul.out`, `neg`, `ones_like`, `rsqrt`, `sum`, `sum.dim_IntList`. `mul.cc` and `embedding.cc` are deleted; their kernels are emitted from templates and match what was there before.

### Key design decisions:

- **Broadcast is native, not materialised.** The operands are described at their own rank and `cnnlOpTensor` does the expansion, which is what the probe showed it does.
- **Transposes are described, not copied.** The Ex descriptor carries the transpose flag, so `x @ w.t()` never materialises the weight. This is the single largest win.
- **A rank-0 operand is described as one element.** That preserves the broadcast meaning of a scalar and is the only representation CNNL accepts.
- **Kernels have external linkage, helpers do not.** A self-registering static in an anonymous namespace is dropped by the linker.
- **The FlagGems register file subtracts the native set.** `cambricon_flaggems_register.inc` drops the 12 operators FlagGems also served (640 -> 628 lines); a duplicate `m.impl` in one `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL` body is a compile error and both files are included side by side.
- **`clone` declines strided views.** Every gather route on this stack costs about the same, so the cost is the strided read, not the kernel; claiming it would only hide that.

### Code changes by file:

- `scripts/codegen/codegen_cambricon.py` — the generator (+1383). The OPS table, per-category templates, helper emission, `--check` mode.
- `csrc/aten/backends/cambricon/generated/cambricon_kernels.cc` — new, generated (16 kernels).
- `csrc/aten/backends/cambricon/generated/cambricon_register.inc` — regenerated (16 `m.impl` lines).
- `csrc/aten/backends/cambricon/generated/cambricon_flaggems_register.inc` — regenerated with the native set subtracted.
- `csrc/aten/backends/cambricon/mul.cc`, `embedding.cc` — deleted, now generated.
- `csrc/aten/backends/cambricon/cambricon_common.h` — `TensorDesc::SetStrided` (via `cnnlSetTensorDescriptorEx`) and a rank-0 guard.
- `csrc/aten/backends/cambricon/attention.h` — drops the declarations of the now-generated kernels.
- `torch_fl/configs/backends_cambricon.conf` — 16 routes to `cambricon`.
- `torch_fl/accelerator/cambricon/_cambricon_compat.py` — caches the `ctypes.CDLL` handle instead of re-resolving it per call.
- `tests/integration/ops/test_cambricon_native_ops.py` — 62 -> 110 cases.

### Changes by commit:

- `f22a5ae6` feat: move the Cambricon training-step operators into the CNNL code generator

## Verification

### Pre-submission Checklist

- [x] **Linting passed** (ruff check, ruff format --check)
- [x] **Type checking passed** (N/A — C++ and the Python generator have no annotations to check)
- [x] **All tests pass** (2131 unit + 110 integration; 5 pre-existing environment failures documented below)
- [x] **Manual testing completed** (reproduction of the scalar bug below)
- [x] **No debug/temporary code**
- [x] **Documentation updated** (generator docstrings and inline rationale; `docs/reference/operator-support.md` is generated from the conf per AGENTS.md, and its counts are refreshed separately)
- [x] **Commit messages follow conventions**
- [x] **All text in English**

### Linting Results

```bash
$ ruff check scripts/codegen/codegen_cambricon.py tests/integration/ops/test_cambricon_native_ops.py \
      torch_fl/

body:
## Why this change is needed

Production still runs `98d7fbb42ae9e53113cb45ada4b4301334de9c27`. #988 is merged and officially published, but deployment needs a verified application return path that preserves live PostgreSQL/MinIO data and checks the exact source, image, configuration and CI identities. This PR provides that tooling, a reproducible native proof driver, the reviewed lazy-context change and bounded HTTP warning source.

## What changes

- External clean tooling prepares an authenticated eligibility capsule and durable phase journal. The canonical manager switches API before Web and can resume an interrupted forward/return operation. Returning the application does not restore or delete the live database.

author: lihongjie0209
body:
### Background

`SHOW QUERY STATS` merges local query hit counts with counts from other live Frontends. `QueryStatsUtil.getStats()` calls each peer through a pooled FE Thrift client.

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #70317
Related PR: None
PR Type: Bugfix

Problem Summary: Every remote query stats call borrows a client without returning it, so repeated requests accumulate FE-to-FE connections and can exhaust peer Thrift workers. Return clients after completed RPCs, including skipped responses, and invalidate clients when the RPC fails. Existing query stats results are unchanged.

### Details

- **Frequency:** Every query stats request that contacts a peer FE.
- **Root cause:** `QueryStatsUtil.getStats()` borrows from `ClientPool.frontendPool` but has no matching `returnObject` or `invalidateObject` call.
- **Why existing tests missed it:** Query stats tests did not verify the pooled FE client's lifecycle.
- **Fix:** Use a `finally` block to return a client after a completed RPC or invalidate it after an RPC exception.
- **Other paths and branches:** The fix covers all query stats types handled by `getStats()`, including status checks and empty results. The same leak is present in the 2.1.8 family; a backport may be appropriate.

### Testing

- Added FE unit tests for successful response, empty response, non-OK status, and RPC failure. The success and skipped-result cases verify `returnObject`; the failure case verifies `invalidateObject`. These tests would fail before the fix.
- `git diff --check` passed locally.
- FE unit tests were not run locally because this sparse checkout lacks the required `thirdparty/installed/bin/protoc`; CI should run them.

### Release note

Repeated `SHOW QUERY STATS` requests no longer accumulate FE-to-FE Thrift connections.

### Check List (For Author)

- Behavior changed: Yes (see Details)
- Does this need documentation: No
- Pre-submission status: Partially verified: FE unit tests await CI because `protoc` is missing locally.

### AI Disclosure

- Tool: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6).
- Generated: The fix, FE unit tests, and PR description.
- Human review: Pending maintainer review.

author: lalalune
body:
## What

**Stripe delivery outbox (M3).** The Stripe webhook now writes each verified event's work into its own `webhook_events` dedupe row, in the same insert as the marker. A 200 to Stripe therefore always means the work is durable.

- The cron leases due rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and settles each one by its lease token: ack, retry with backoff, or dead-letter.
- Every claim counts as an attempt. Rows a drain claimed but did not reach inside its budget are released and their attempt is refunded.
- A Stripe resend of a dead-lettered event makes it due again.
- Retention never deletes undelivered or leased work.
- The old KV array queue is gone. `redis-queue` refuses a backend without atomic list operations, and the KV adapter refuses list push and pop.
- The cron moves anything still on the old `stripe-events`, `:processing` and `:dlq` lists into the outbox. Each entry is adopted on its own, and an entry that fails stays listed. A failure in the cutover never stops the outbox drain.

**Cancellation outcomes (M4).** A cancel or undo that crossed the dispatch fence used to stay `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` for good, and every new intent was refused with `contradictory_command_pending`. Once `CANCELLATION_DISPATCH_SETTLE_MS` (5 minutes) has passed, a command that shows no effect now becomes `FAILED`, which means "not in effect now". This covers three cases:
- a request Stripe refused or that was lost;
- a worker that died between the fence and the request;
- a command whose subscription renewed or changed while it was uncertain. These are resolved against the subscription row as it stands, under the actor lock, with generation and lease checks.

An effect the provider does show is still applied. If the subscription row already shows the target but no command owns that effect, the command stays uncertain rather than taking credit for it.

## Why

On the checked-in Worker config (`CACHE_BACKEND=auto` with `CACHE_KV`), the Stripe queue was one KV JSON value that was read and then written back whole. Concurrent webhooks, a drain racing a webhook, or a failed push-back lost events that Stripe had already been told were received. The remaining marker then made Stripe's resend a duplicate.

## Tests

- `api/__tests__/stripe-webhook-outbox.pglite.test.ts` replays concurrent deliveries through the real route on a stand-in KV. Every 200'd delivery reaches the consumer, a resend stays a duplicate, and a resend of a dead-lettered event is delivered again.
- `stripe-delivery-outbox.pglite.test.ts` covers:
  - leases and expired-lease takeover;
  - crash recovery;
  - the retry budget and dead-letter revival;
  - retention through both `cleanupOldEvents` (the cron's path) and `cleanupOldEventsForProvider`;
  - the attempt refund for unreached rows;
  - legacy adoption, including the dlq list and a poison entry that does not block the drain.
- `subscription-cancellation-settle.pglite.test.ts` runs the real service and repository on PGlite with only Stripe faked: refused, lost after the fence, never fenced, a legacy command with no dispatch state (settles as `DISPATCH_UNKNOWN_EFFECT_ABSENT_AFTER_SETTLE`, not as never dispatched), effect present, renewal while uncertain, and effect already present after a renewal. No check in the PR's CI runs this suite; run it with `bun test` in `packages/cloud/shared`.

Each new test fails when its fix is reverted. These are PGlite tests with Stripe and KV stand-ins. They are not evidence from real Postgres, real Stripe or a deployed Worker. The `*.postgres.integration.test.ts` suites and hosted CI were not run.

## Rollout notes

- Migrations: `0554` (dispatch settle column; it backfills the settle window to "now" for commands already uncertain), `0555` (outbox columns and the lease check, added `NOT VALID`), `0556` (due index, `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` under the nontransactional directive), `0557` (validates the lease check in its own transaction, under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE). Renumber if develop gains these numbers first.
- While old and new Worker versions both serve (a gradual rollout, or the overlap in any deploy), old-version webhooks still push to the KV `stripe-events` list with the old read-then-write emulation and answer 200. The new cron's legacy adoption removes entries with a KV read-filter-write, so an old-version push that lands between that read and write can be lost. Keep the mixed-version window short (no gradual rollout for this deploy); the risk ends once every isolate runs the new version.
- Rolling back to the old version strands outbox rows not yet drained: the old cron never reads `webhook_events.delivery_payload`. Drain the outbox before any rollback.
- A row recreated from the legacy queue stores a hash of the JSON event, not of the raw body. Only an app-billing resend checks that hash, and the old code only released markers for non-app-billing events, so this is not expected to happen.
- Remove the legacy adoption lane once the old lists are seen empty.
- Assumption: Stripe consumers stay idempotent on redelivery. Delivery is at least once.

## Known limits

- An uncertain command whose renewed subscription already shows the target stays uncertain, because `SUPERSEDED` is constrained to unclaimed commands.
- Commands on a configured schedule (`pending_plan_key`) whose source moved also stay uncertain.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: liam-jons
body: ## Why The goal is a codebase where types and boundaries prove what casts and trust used to assert. #1016 left two gaps. The `lent` wrapper in `transaction.ts` still hid an unsafe return behind a suppression (BA-254). And `sources.connect` took `x-upload-byte-size` on trust, so a body of 5 bytes under a declared 43 answered 200 (BA-333). ## What changed - `Tx` names the one `query` overload that callers use. `lent` builds a typed closure in place of a `Proxy`, and its `no-unsafe-return` suppression is gone. - `connectUpload` measures the body against the declared size. A body that is shorter or longer is refused as `malformed`. No object is completed and no row is written. - The stream no longer has a cap of its own. The declared size is held to `UPLOAD_BYTE_CAP` before any byte is read, and the body has to equal it. ## Scope - Before this change the row recorded the bytes received, never the declared size. No stored row needs correcting. - The refusal comes before the store completes the object. If the body ends or overruns inside the first 5 MiB part, nothing reaches the store. Past that, the upload has sent parts and aborts them. - A `Content-Length` check at the boundary would also stop those parts. It is left out because a chunked body has no length, so the stream check has to stay. - A repeat of a committed connect still returns its first outcome without reading the body. ## Tradeoffs A new refusal word such as `size-mismatch` would tell a client more. It needs a catalogue entry and web copy, and `malformed` already gives the right status and class. ## Blast Radius The web app sends `file.size` as the declared size, so only a client that misstates the size, or a file that changes during the upload, sees the new refusal. Three copies of the narrowed `Tx` remain, in the postgres door, the map door and the schema test support, because those packages do not import one another. ## Verification - At the test commit, 3 core tests and 3 api tests fail against the old code: a shorter body, a longer body, and a body past a cap-sized declaration. At the fix commit all pass. The matching and empty bodies pass both before and after, as the control. - `pnpm check:gates` exits 0. The core check passes 3024 tests and the api check passes 1936. The core, schema, api and web typechecks pass. - A scratch run, not committed, logged the object-store commands per case. A short or long small body sent none. A 64 MiB mismatch sent 12 parts and then an abort. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jordan-simonovski
body:
Add opt-in chDB durable storage through `CHGRAPH_DURABLE_URI`, allowing a project graph to recover from checkpoints and WAL after its local working data is lost. The daemon retains single-writer ownership and waits for store cleanup before exiting, so a normal restart releases the durable lease.

Closes #13.

- Keep local storage as the default; enabling durable storage creates a separate graph and requires an initial index. Project IDs retain the existing path-dependent slug, so recovery elsewhere requires the same repository path and namespace.
- Use replayable inline batches for graph and git data, flush mutations before returning, and checkpoint before full indexing reports success. Preserve the schema-version gate and propagate storage failures.
- Upgrade chDB to 4.4.0; provide optional S3 dependencies with `uv sync --extra durable`. Existing local data written by chDB 4.2.0/core 26.5.0 was verified to reopen after upgrade.

Validation: 100 tests passed with durable and eval dependencies, package build passed, and independent review passed after correcting shutdown lease release. The combined result with all eight Dependabot updates also passed all 100 tests with every dependency group enabled, including optional embeddings; optional dependency imports and file-lock exclusion checks passed. Recovery and immediate restart tests use the real local durable backend. Live S3 was not tested.

body:
## Resumo

Leva o tema de 1.0.0 para **1.2.0**.

### Manutenção e segurança (1.0.1)
- **Arquivos expostos removidos:** scripts de debug e teste que podiam ser abertos pela URL do tema e faziam ações via GET sem nonce.
- **XSS e validação de entrada corrigidos:** loterias (shortcode, widget e bloco), slider de imagens, títulos, campo ACF "fonte", nome do autor, info-bar e listas.
- **Pedido externo removido:** o hook de debug público (`?debug=ms`) fazia uma requisição HTTP externa a cada visita.
- **Cadastro duplicado removido:** o tipo de conteúdo `edital` era registrado duas vezes.
- **AJAX de clima:** valida as coordenadas e não exige nonce de visitantes, porque o nonce expirava no cache de página.
- **API da Caixa:** timeout de 5 s, disjuntor por 5 minutos após falha, último resultado guardado com atualização em segundo plano pelo WP-Cron e limite de tempo por página. Com a Caixa lenta, a página caiu de 46 s para 0,9 s.
- **Erro fatal corrigido:** sem o plugin ACF, a capa quebrava com `get_field()` indefinido.
- **Cache busting:** os assets ganharam versão pelo `filemtime`.
- **Padrões de código:** PHPCS com WordPress Coding Standards (`composer lint`), formatação aplicada e `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.

### Layout (1.0.1 a 1.1.1)
- **Destaque Misto:** as miniaturas ficavam espremidas (21×36 px) por um link dentro de outro link. Agora usam proporção 4:3.
- **Capa no celular:** a página "pulava" (CLS 0,26 → 0,002) porque o carrossel de destaques aparecia empilhado até iniciar.
- **Listas no texto das matérias:** estavam quase invisíveis, com contraste de 1,11:1. Agora o contraste é de 15,43:1.

### Google AdSense (1.1.0 a 1.2.0)
- **Configuração:** basta colar a tag ou o ID em Personalizar → 📢 AdSense.
- **O que o tema faz:** insere o script, a meta de verificação, gera o `/ads.txt` e libera o robô no `robots.txt`.
- **Exclusões:** sem anúncios para usuários logados, nas Publicações Legais, em páginas 404 e na busca vazia.
- **Posições fixas opcionais:**
  - topo (fora do cabeçalho fixo);
  - dentro da matéria, com um 2º anúncio nas matérias longas;
  - fim da matéria;
  - barra lateral;
  - entre notícias (na lista padrão e no bloco Grade de Notícias);
  - capa.

  Também há o bloco "Anúncio (AdSense)" no editor.
- **Sem deformar o conteúdo:** espaço reservado para o anúncio, espaço vazio recolhido quando não há anúncio, e Anúncios automáticos acomodados na linha inteira dentro dos grids.
- **Documentação:** especificação em `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-adsense-design.md` e plano para o Portal do Rosas em `docs/adsense-portal-do-rosas.md`.

## Testes
Tudo no WordPress Playground (WP 6.9, PHP 8.3), com os testes em `dev/tests/`, fora do .zip:
- **54 testes de lógica** rodando dentro do WordPress;
- **38 verificações de ponta a ponta** por HTTP;
- **378 verificações de layout** com AdSense simulado: 3 páginas × 3 larguras × 5 tamanhos, com Anúncios automáticos inseridos dentro dos grids. Nenhum caso de rolagem horizontal, mudança de largura, sobreposição ou anúncio no cabeçalho fixo.

Ainda não validado com o AdSense real nem no site em produção.

body:
## Summary

PR を開く・更新したときと `main` へ push したときに、**変更が届いたレーンの lint とテストが Actions で動く**ようにしました。検証は手元の devcontainer と同じイメージのコンテナの中で動き、結果は `ci-result` のチェックと Step Summary に出ます。これまではテストが手元の pre-push でしか動かず、dependabot の PR は手で取り込んで確かめていました。

## Changes

### 1. PR に `ci-result` のチェックが付く

**PR を開くか push すると、`ci` の workflow が動き、`ci-result` のチェックが付くようになりました**。範囲とレーンの選び方は手元の pre-commit の設定と同じで、pre-commit・pre-push・manual の 3 つの stage を、PR の範囲を指定して順に動かします。必須チェックにはまだしていません（ruleset は Phase 6 で入れます）。

同じ PR に続けて push すると、古い run は打ち切られます。`main` への push の run は打ち切りません。

### 2. Step Summary で、動いたレーンと失敗したレーンが分かる

**run の Summary に、範囲・stage ごとの成否・レーン・失敗・skip の件数・環境が出るようになりました**。レーンが 1 つも選ばれない PR（README だけの変更など）では、レーンの欄が「対象なし（成功）」になります。

- skip の件数はレーンごとに出るので、手元の devcontainer の件数と比べられる
- 失敗の欄には、失敗したレーンの名前と、ログを入れた artifact `ci-logs` の案内が出る
- Summary のファイルも artifact `ci-logs` に入るので、`gh run download` で読める
- 環境の欄には、イメージ名とコンテナの中の `node`・`aws`・`actionlint` の版が出る

### 3. コンテナの失敗とテストの失敗を step 名で見分けられる

**基盤の失敗は `Start dev container` の step、テストの失敗は `Run checks` の step が落ちます**。検証が最後まで動かなかったとき（buildx が無いなど）も、`Write job summary` の step が落ちるので、`ci-result` が成功のまま残りません。

### 4. `main` への push では、前回成功した run からの差分を検証する

**`main` への push の run は、前回成功した `main` の run の commit から先端までを範囲にします**。成功した run がまだ無いときと、base の commit を読めないときは、全レーンを動かします。仕様の FR-029 と contract の文言も、この動きに合わせて直しました。

### 5. 手元の pre-push は変わらない

**手元で push したときの動きは変わりません**。テストの 2 つの hook（`nx-affected-tests`・`githooks-tests`）は、pre-push に加えて manual の stage でも動くようにしました。pre-push から外すのは #66 です。CI の pre-push の stage では、manual と 2 回動かさないように、この 2 つを飛ばします。

## Verified

### 変更箇所のテストと lint が通る

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 --with pytest-xdist --with packaging pytest \
  .githooks/tests/test_run_pr_checks.py .githooks/tests/test_run_affected_tests.py \
  .githooks/tests/test_pre_commit_config_wiring.py -q --import-mode=importlib -n auto -p no:cacheprovider
# 197 passed in 2.15s
```

- shellcheck・actionlint・yamllint・文章規則の lint と、commit 時の pre-commit は通った
- nx 24 の static 出力の見出しの形（`> nx run <project>:<target>`）は、`text-rules` の `test-unit` を実際に動かして確かめた

### Actions 上の CUJ

CUJ 0〜4・6 は合格した。CUJ 1〜4・6 は、確認用の下書き PR #124 に commit を積んで観測した。#124 は閉じて、ブランチも消した。CUJ 5 は、この PR のマージの後に観測する。

| CUJ | 起点 | run | 結果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | この PR を開く | 42176703829 | `ci-result` が `pass`。必須チェックは無い |
| 2 | README だけを変える | 42180709835 | 成功。レーンの欄は「対象なし（成功）」 |
| 1 | pecot-tools のコメントを変える | 42182513667 | 成功。レーンは `pecot-tools:test-cli` だけで、skip は 0 件 |
| 3 | CI の中でだけ落ちるテストを足す | 42183438434 | `checks` と `ci-result` が `fail`。`Start dev container` は成功、`Run checks` は失敗 |
| 4 | c3 を戻し、run の途中で pecot-visual を変える | 42184251736 / 42184565113 | 前の run は `cancelled`、後の run は成功。レーンは 3 件 |
| 6 | `devcontainer.json` の actionlint を 1.7.11 にする | 42186133811 | 成功。環境の欄の actionlint が 1.7.11 |

- CUJ 3 では、失敗の欄に `pecot-tools:test-cli` が出た。`Run checks` の step のログには、`=== 失敗レーン: pecot-tools:test-cli ===` の下に、落ちたテストの名前と AssertionError が出た
- 計画との違いは 3 点ある
  - 落とすテストは、CI の作業ディレクトリ（`/workspaces/base/`）の中でだけ落ちる形にした。手元の pre-push を通すためで、`--no-verify` は使っていない
  - #124 の base は `main` にした。`pecot pr create` が `main` 以外を受け付けないため。範囲にこの PR の差分も入るが、この PR で選ばれるレーンは 0 件なので、レーンの結果は変わらない
  - #124 には version plan を足した。plugin の配下を変えると、手元の pre-push が version plan を求めるため。#124 はマージしていない
- Summary は API でも画面の HTML でも取れなかった。そのため、artifact `ci-logs` へ Summary のファイルも入れた

### 手元と CI の skip の件数が一致する（T029）

| レーン | 手元 | CI（CUJ 4） |
|---|---|---|
| `pecot-visual:test-cli` | 3022 件中 3 件 | 3022 件中 3 件 |
| `pecot-visual:test-compare` | — | 0 件 |
| `pecot-tools:test-cli` | — | 0 件（1080 件と 18 件がすべて passed） |

手元の値は、c5 の最初の pre-push のログから取った。pecot-visual と pecot-tools の残りのレーンの手元の件数は、後の push でログが上書きされたため取れていない。

### 所要（T030）

レーンを選んだ run は約 12 分かかり、PR のチェックの目安の 10 分を超えた。

| 区間 | CI（CUJ 4） | 手元 |
|---|---|---|
| run 全体（待ちを含む） | 11 分 56 秒 | — |
| `Start dev container` | 1 分 34 秒 | — |
| `pecot-visual:test-cli` | 270 秒 | 54.5 秒 |
| `pecot-tools:test-cli` | 66 秒 | 約 15 秒 |
| `githooks-tests` | 155 秒 | 約 18 秒 |
| `nx-affected-lint` | 66 秒 | — |

CI の runner は 4 CPU で、手元は 24 CPU ある。テストは CPU の数だけ並列に動くので、CI では 4〜9 倍かかる。レーンが 0 件の run は約 5 分だった。

## Risks

- pecot-visual の `test-cli` が選ばれると、PR のチェックが 10 分を超える。縮めるかは、この PR の後で決める
- `devcontainers/ci` は `@devcontainers/cli` を版の固定なしで入れる。CLI の更新で動きが変わったら、前の step で版を固定して入れる

Closes #65

author: ruy-bot[bot]
body:
Fixes #2092

Since the hidden lockfile became the default load path for the actual graph (#1068), edges a graph modifier swapped are never marked `overridden` there: only the `node_modules` walk sets the flag. So after every install, `vlt query ':overridden'`, the `(overridden)` label and `"overridden": true` came back empty. This re-runs the walk's modifier matching after a hidden lockfile load and flags those edges.

## Changes
- `actual/load.ts`: new `markOverriddenEdges`, called after a successful hidden lockfile load when `modifiers` is passed. It goes breadth first from the importers with the same `GraphModifier` calls as `parseDir` (`tryImporter`, `tryDependencies`, `updateActiveEntry`, `rollbackActiveEntries`) and flags an edge when a complete modifier targets it.
- A node's declared deps are matched when it is first reached, right after its parent edge registers the pending entry, as the ideal build does when placing it. Matching at dequeue time lets a modifier's first complete match deregister its other pending entries, so `#minimatch > #brace-expansion` with two minimatch versions would flag only one of the two swapped edges.
- Each importer is matched right after its own `tryImporter`, as the ideal build does. Registering every importer first let an importer-anchored modifier (`:project > #x`, `:workspace > #x`) flag only the first importer's edge.
- Matching runs against the specs each manifest declares, not the stored edge specs (already modified), so qualifiers such as `:root > #b:semver(^1.0.0)` still match. Edge specs stay as stored, since they hold what was installed.
- No lockfile format change: the flag is derived on load, not persisted. Edge specs are not shared when modifiers are passed (the existing guard in `lockfile/load.ts`), so flagging one edge can't leak into another.
- `.cursor/rules/graph/load-actual.mdc`: one line on the new pass.

## Tests
- New `modifiers with the hidden lockfile` tests in `test/actual/load.ts`:
  - A handwritten hidden lockfile with no store, so only the lockfile can place the nodes. Covers a nested target, the same name under another parent, a qualifier matched against the declared spec, a missing dependency, and the first selector step not being flagged.
  - A round trip: walk `node_modules`, which writes the hidden lockfile through `saveHidden`, then remove the store and load again.
  - Every target of a modifier whose first step matches two nodes (`#m > #b` with `m@1.0.0` from the root and `m@3.0.0` from a dependency).
  - Every importer: `:workspace > #x` with a root and a workspace edge to `x`.
  - 8 asserts fail on main and pass with the fix. The `m@3.0.0` one also fails when deps are matched at dequeue time, and the workspace edge one when all importers are registered before matching.
- `src/graph`: format, lint and `tsc --noEmit` pass. Full suite: 68 suites, 4105 asserts, 100% coverage on Node 26 and Node 22.
- Root: `format:check`, `lint:check`, `fix:pkg` (no diff), `knip` and `deps:check` pass.
- Source CLI QA with the issue's repro (react/react-dom 18.3.1, `"#react-dom > #scheduler": "0.23.0"`):
  - After `vlt install`, `vlt query ':overridden'` lists `scheduler@0.23.0 (overridden)`: count 1, json `"overridden": true`.
  - `:root > :overridden` counts 0, and `vlt ls` shows the label.
  - After removing the hidden lockfile it is still 1, and still 1 on the next query.
  - `rm vlt-lock.json && vlt install` writes the same nodes and edges. That path has the ideal build load the actual graph from the hidden lockfile with modifiers.
- Source CLI QA, one modifier with several targets:
  - `glob@7.2.3` + `minimatch@9.0.5` with `"#minimatch > #brace-expansion": "2.0.1"`: both minimatch versions get `brace-expansion@2.0.1`, and `:overridden` lists both (count 2).
  - Root `react-dom@18.3.1` + workspace `react-dom@18.2.0` with `"#react-dom > #scheduler": "0.23.0"`: both scheduler edges are listed (count 2).
- Source CLI QA, importer selectors:
  - Root and workspace `w` on `ms@2.1.3` with `":project > #ms": "2.1.2"`: both edges are installed as `2.1.2`, and `:overridden` lists both (count 2, `vlt ls` labels both).
  - No root deps, workspaces `a` and `b` on `ms@2.1.3` with `":workspace > #ms": "2.1.2"` (the workspaces example in the graph modifiers docs): count 2.

## Notes for maintainers
- Open question, default taken: flags follow the current `vlt.json` modifiers (what `vlt query` passes in and what the walk uses), not the `modifiers` stored in the hidden lockfile. If modifiers changed since the last install, edges still show the installed spec but are no longer flagged. QA: removing the modifier from `vlt.json` gives `:overridden` 0 while `scheduler@0.23.0` stays installed. The other way round, adding a modifier without reinstalling flags the edges it targets although their stored specs are untouched. This matches the walk and npm.
- Cost: one extra `getDependencies` per node on hidden lockfile loads, and only when `vlt.json` defines `modifiers` (`GraphModifier.maybeLoad`), for `query`, `ls`, ... Install's and uninstall's own actual loads pass none. On this repo's own hidden lockfile (1143 nodes, 3702 edges) with 3 modifiers, `actual.load` goes from a 62.6 ms to a 93.4 ms median (N=15, Node 26). There is no special case for an empty `modifiers` config.
- npm comparison (12.2.1 arborist): `:overridden` reads `node.overridden`. When loading from `node_modules/.package-lock.json`, arborist loads the root's overrides from `package.json` and propagates them through the edges, so the flag is recomputed on every load and never persisted. Same approach here.
- #2091 / #2097: `markOverriddenEdges` uses the same `GraphModifier` calls as `parseDir` (`tryDependencies` + `updateActiveEntry`), and #2097 only changes how those advance partial matches, so both pick it up unchanged. Checked with both PRs merged: two modifiers sharing `#react-dom >` swap both edges, and `:overridden` lists both, on repeated queries and after the `node_modules` walk.
- #2090 / #2093: like the walk, this pass matches peer dependencies, but on main the ideal build never applies modifiers to peer edges. Until #2093 lands, a modifier that ends on a peer edge flags that edge even though install didn't swap it. The walk already does this today. With #2093 merged, the swapped peer edge (`peer 18.2.0`) is flagged as expected.
- Unchanged, pre-existing:
  - The `node_modules` walk (`parseDir`) matches a node's deps when it is dequeued. So after `rm node_modules/.vlt-lock.json` it can miss targets of a modifier whose first step matches several nodes (the `react-dom` workspace repro above: 1 of 2). It also runs every `tryImporter` before any `parseDir`, so it flags an importer selector on one importer only (the `:project > #ms` repro above: 1 of 2). Left unchanged here.
  - The walk also flags rules that install ignores: with react and react-dom at the root and `#react-dom > #react > #loose-envify: 1.3.1` (a rule through a peer that links to the root's react, left unapplied, see #2093), `:overridden` after `rm node_modules/.vlt-lock.json` lists react's `loose-envify` edge, still on 1.4.0. The hidden-lockfile pass here returns 0.
  - Graphs loaded from `vlt-lock.json` and the in-memory ideal graph never set the flag.
  - `:host()` contexts call `actual.load` without modifiers.
  - The `:overridden` docs (selectors, pseudo-states) refer to the `overrides` field in `package.json`, but vlt reads modifiers from `vlt.json`.
- Possible follow-up: an end-to-end smoke test (install, then query `:overridden`).

body:
## What was wrong

The retest (batches 305-306) found consent alerts in the house manager's bell but not in the administrator's or the nurse's. The two roles fail for different reasons.

### Administrator: hidden by a restrictive RLS policy (database layer)

The rows are minted: 18 unread `consent.missing` rows for `role_key = 'administrator'`. The permissive `notifications_select` policy matches Sam's membership. But `public.notifications` has a second, **RESTRICTIVE** select policy from the original register build (20261027140000):

```sql
consent_notification_roles: type not like 'consent.%'
  or private.role_key_in(agency_id,'{house_manager,program_manager,nurse}')
```

Postgres ANDs restrictive policies with the permissive ones, so administrators could never see any `consent.*` row. 20261030180000 ("administrators view and manage consents") widened six consent read policies but missed this one. Then 20261104120000 started addressing alerts to a role that couldn't read them.

Production proof (read-only, Northstar agency; I replayed each user's session with `set local role authenticated` and their JWT `sub` inside a read-only transaction):

| user | consent rows the permissive policy allows | visible with the current policy | visible with the 20261105110000 policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sam (administrator) | 18 | **0** | **18** (18 unread) |
| Jordan (house manager) | 27 | 27 | 27 |
| Morgan (nurse) | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| Pat (program manager) | 54 | 54 | 54 |

Under RLS, Sam's whole session returned 46 notifications and 0 consent rows. So his consent rows were never "ranked #1" in what PostgREST returned: the earlier 64-row count was taken without the restrictive policy applied.

The other suspects were checked and cleared for Sam:
1. **`filterStaleConsentNotifications` / `consentAlertPairs`**: I replayed it over Sam's live register (6 individuals, 55 consent records, as RLS gives them to him) and his 18 rows. All 18 are kept, and the pair keys match the SQL sweep's entity and flavor.
2. **`retire_stale_consent_notices`**: this only sets `read_at`. It never hides a row, and it only fires when a current consent covers the type.
3. **The bell UI** (`groupNotifications`, `NotificationsPanel`) has no role or broadcast filtering.

### Nurse: buried past the fetch window (client layer)

The nurse can see 547 rows: 377 `med.prn_repeat`, 158 `med.unrecorded`, and only **12 truly unread**. Her 2 live (unread) consent alerts rank 367-368 by `created_at desc`, but `HostedApi.listNotifications` fetched `.limit(100)`. Her other 4 consent rows are retired (read). `LocalApi.listNotifications` had the same `.slice(0, 100)`.

### Latent: device-day vs Central-day in `consentAlertPairs`

`consentAlertPairs` defaulted to `todayStamp()` (the device's local day), while `consentGaps` and the SQL sweep judge the America/Chicago day. If a viewer is outside Central and their device date is ahead of Chicago's, a consent reviewed "today" reads as Expired. The live `consent.expiring` row then gets dropped as stale. This did not cause Sam's failure (his browser is Central), but it is the systematic mismatch suspect 1 asked about.

## What changed

- **`supabase/migrations/20261105110000_consent_notices_administrator_read.sql`**: recreates `consent_notification_roles` (still RESTRICTIVE) with `{house_manager,program_manager,nurse,administrator}`. That equals `private.can_manage_consent`'s roles and the sweep's recipient set. Auditors and HR stay excluded. **Not applied to production**: it needs Joshua's go-ahead.
- **`HostedApi.listNotifications`** now loads through `fetchNotificationWindow`, which makes two passes:
  1. The newest 100 rows of any state (the old query, unchanged).
  2. Only when pass 1 comes back full: rows with `read_at is null`, newest first, paged 200 at a time (up to 5 pages). After the `notification_reads` mapping, it keeps only rows that are still unread. This drops role broadcasts this user already read.

  `windowNotifications` merges the two passes by id, newest first. The Wave 7M `med.unrecorded` retirement filter and the consent stale filter run on the merged set exactly as before. `markNotificationsRead` reuses `listNotifications`, so buried rows can now be marked read too.
- **`LocalApi.listNotifications`**: newest 100 plus every unread row (parity).
- **`notify.ts`**: `NOTIFICATION_RECENT_WINDOW` and the pure `windowNotifications` helper.
- **`consentAlertPairs`** now defaults to `centralTodayIso()`.

Unchanged: dedupe keys, the sweep's recipient rules (house manager direct; program manager and administrator by role; nurse for medication types only), `private.sweep_consents`, `retire_stale_consent_notices`, and the #256 pgTAP suite.

## Tests

New `src/data/consentBellAudience.test.ts` (8 tests). On pristine main, 6 of them fail; with this branch, all 8 pass:

| test | pristine main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| admin: the latest `consent_notification_roles` admits every role the sweep addresses, still excludes auditor, still restrictive | ✖ (`20261027140000 … must admit 'administrator'`) | ✔ |
| nurse (hosted): unread consent alert under 540 newer read rows loads; newest-100 history unchanged and in order; broadcast reads still mapped | ✖ | ✔ |
| nurse (hosted): stale retirement still drops a buried alert whose consent is now **Active**, keeps the still-missing one | ✖ (the live row never loaded) | ✔ |
| nurse (hosted): Wave 7M retirement drops a cleared site's `med.unrecorded` row from the unread pass; the open site's rows still group (×2, 2 unread) | ✖ | ✔ |
| hosted: under 100 visible rows makes no second pass | ✔ | ✔ |
| `windowNotifications`: dedupe, newest N plus all unread | ✔ (helper is new) | ✔ |
| nurse (local): unread notice under 150 newer read rows still lists | ✖ | ✔ |
| `consentAlertPairs` under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` keeps the Central-day expiring pair | ✖ | ✔ |

The existing `consentAlertRetirement.test.ts` (an Active consent retires its alerts) still passes.

New pgTAP file `supabase/tests/consent_notice_admin_read.sql` (7 assertions). After a sweep:
- the administrator reads 9 alerts, all administrator-addressed;
- the house manager still reads 9;
- an auditor reads 0, even for a row addressed to the auditor role;
- the policy stays RESTRICTIVE.

It was **not run**: there is no Postgres in this sandbox.

Verification (run 2026-11-05, 21:11 CST):
- `node scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs`: **2262/2262, 0 failed.** Pristine main is 2254/2254, so this adds 8. The three evening clock-window tests did not fail on this run.
- `npx tsc -b`: clean.
- `npm run build`: clean (only the usual chunk-size warning).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches notification RLS (who can see consent rows) and changes bell query volume/pagination for users with large inboxes; behavior is well tested but production migration needs explicit approval per the migration comment.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **Wave 4A** retest gaps where consent alerts showed for house managers but not administrators or nurses.
> 
> **Administrator (RLS):** Migration `20261105110000` recreates the restrictive `consent_notification_roles` policy so **`administrator`** is allowed to read `consent.*` rows, matching roles the consent sweep targets. Auditors stay excluded. pgTAP and a static migration test lock this in.
> 
> **Nurse / heavy inboxes (client fetch):** The bell no longer loads only the newest **100** rows. **`HostedApi`** uses a two-pass **`fetchNotificationWindow`** (recent window plus paged unread rows with null row `read_at`, then merge via **`windowNotifications`**); **`LocalApi`** applies the same rule. Unread consent (and other) alerts buried under bulk read med history can appear without changing recent read history ordering.
> 
> **Stale consent filtering:** **`consentAlertPairs`** now defaults to **`centralTodayIso()`** instead of the device-local day so client-side retireme

body:
## Scope
Adapt the missing alias/cover delta from [#393](https://github.com/lake-of-fire/LakeOfFire/pull/393), exact donor `477aefe877fbd71faa6cb001d0a18028ab6387e0`, onto [#375](https://github.com/lake-of-fire/LakeOfFire/pull/375), exact sole parent `3fbe022aa3407db3e360f74fabf745a9cca9365f`. This is an isolated continuation of the historical hotfix-to-main proposal, explicitly requested for this review. It does not modify or replace the separately owned V3/V4 compositions.

#375's JSON model retains short acquisition/download relations that its exact typed mapper does not select; its image mapping also requires legacy relations. Valid OPDS 2 publications can therefore lack download or cover URLs.

## Changes
- Normalize exactly JSON acquisition and download aliases to existing typed URI relations. Keep restricted/custom/lookalike relations, Atom relation parsing and direct construction unchanged.
- Adapt the donor cover → image → thumbnail URL preference, then first resolvable images entry, to the existing detached BookCatalogPublicationMapper. The image fallback applies to that mapper's images collection, not only JSON.
- Keep the existing parser/loader, document.documentURL base, 16-document traversal budget, callback graph transfer, metadata and generic-before-open-access download priority. No older BookLibraryViewModel mapper or donor cancellation/traversal owner is transplanted.

author: fugaro-dev[bot]
body:
The owner's rule (2026-11-06) is that a run whose in-job review succeeded gets no
second review by a person, so for this repository the in-job reviewer is the only
reviewer a security-sensitive change gets. It is now recorded where the rulings
it builds on are, `docs/design/mixed-credentials.md` §11 ("The ruling of
2026-11-06: the in-job review is the review"), beside the B0 ruling of 2026-11-04
and the 2026-11-05 amendment. `agent.review` was unset, so the brief was
`defaultReview` — one sentence — plus the scope line, the scoring contract and
the verdict ask: nothing told the reviewer to read the whole change rather than
the hunks, to check the PR's claims against the code, to run the tests the change
touches, to break the guard a change adds, or to probe a new trust boundary as an
attacker.

This adds `.fugaro/review.md` (59 lines) and sets `agent.review:
.fugaro/review.md`. It changes no runner code: the file replaces `defaultReview`
in `reviewBrief` (`internal/runner/prompts.go:305-325`, the `promptFile` branch),
and the scope, the scoring contract and the verdict ask are still appended after
it unchanged.

## The brief is read by four readers, so it is written for all four

`agent.review`'s text is prepended verbatim to the prompt of every review stage,
and that is not one prompt: the first-line pass (level 1, the coder's model), the
senior round (level 2), the adversarial round (level 3, `AdversarialPrompt` keeps
a custom file's text) and the independent review **job** — a separate execution
that denies Bash, Edit, Write and NotebookEdit. A brief that opened "you are this
repository's senior reviewer and a run whose review you passed gets no second
review by a person" was false for the first line and the adversarial round, and
asked the shell-less job for a mutation check it cannot run. The file now says
which of the run's reviews it is, states the fact that is true for all of them
(the reviews are the review, so what any one of them misses reaches the pull
request), and scopes the test and mutation sections to a review that has a shell,
with the job's own denial named as the one exception. The runner's verdict format
is untouched: the scoring contract and the verdict ask are still appended after
the file's text, and a repository that names no brief keeps the old one.

## What the prompt asks for

1. Read the whole diff and every file it touches, and check every claim in the PR
   body and the commit messages against the code, citing `file:line`.
2. Run the targeted tests by name (`GOFLAGS=-p=2 go test ./… -run 'A|B'
   -count=1`, never a whole package) and says `fugaro verify test` is the
   runner's command, not the reviewer's.
3. For a security-sensitive path (credentials, secrets, the managed settings or
   the gateway, Terraform/IAM, the agent's environment, git tokens, the console's
   spawn/IPC allow-list, a prompt, a recipe, CLAUDE.md, a plugin skill,
   `.github/`, `ee/`): at least one mutation check in a scratch worktree — break
   the guard the change adds, confirm a named test fails, remove the scratch tree,
   report the mutation and the test's name.
4. Probe each new trust boundary as an attacker: who mints, what binds, how
   revoked, what a hostile agent or repository can do with it, fail-open on every
   error path, input reaching an argv, a path or a URL.
5. Check the pins the change touches (`go test ./internal/cli -run Docs` for doc
   changes) and CLAUDE.md's rules.
6. Report only blocking findings, each with `file:line` and the fix; never style;
   say "ship" only when the checks that reader can run ran, and name what ran.

## Verification against the code (the four facts the task asked to confirm)

**(a) The path is resolved from a repository key and read at the BASE ref, not from the
PR's own branch — not an open item.** `agent.review` is a repo-scope string key
(`schemas/fugaro.schema.json:106`, docs/project-layer.md:166). For an ordinary coding
run — the case here — bootstrap reads it once, before any stage runs, through
`readRepoFile` (`internal/runner/runner.go:2168-2170`), which is
`os.ReadFile(workdir/rel)` (`runner.go:2515`), and the workdir at that point has just
been force-reset by `CheckoutNewBranch(ctx, spec.Ref, "fugaro/<id>")`
(`runner.go:1841-1843`; `git fetch origin <ref>` then `checkout -f -B <branch>
FETCH_HEAD`, `internal/gitops/gitops.go:418-427`). So the text comes from the task's
ref — the base — and the run's own commits do not exist yet, including on a
re-execution of a run. A follow-up and a review run read the same key from the resolved
base revision explicitly: `read := func(rel string) (string, error) { return
r.readBaseFile(ctx, rev, rel) }` (`internal/runner/followup.go:108-126`), with a
leading-slash `agent.review` resolved into the same field as plain text from the base
(`followup.go:127-137`). `git.base_branch` in that base file must equal the task's ref
(`followup.go:106-110`). docs/design/v1.md:209 and
docs/cloud-senior-review/reconciliation.md:620 say the same. **A pull request cannot
change the prompt that reviews it.**

**(b) The in-run reviewer stage can run Bash, and the mutation check is possible in a
scratch tree.** Only the independent review JOB denies Bash: `writeManagedSettings`
appends `agent.ReviewJobDenyRules()` — Bash, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit,
`Read(/proc/**)` — only when `r.reviewJob()`, which is the `FUGARO_REVIEW_JOB` marker
(`internal/runner/agentenv.go:313-349`, `reviewartifact.go:931-936`), and the launcher
sets that marker only for `spec.Mode == recipe.ModeReview`
(`internal/cli/run.go:3411-3413`, `3554-3560`). A coding run's in-loop review rounds are
not that job, so their managed settings carry only `agent.DenyRules(true,
config.IsReviewStage("review"))` — `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` plus the binary-read rules
(`internal/agent/settings.go:42-58`, `95-105`) — the stage request restricts no tool
(`runner.go:2996`), and every stage runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
(`internal/agent/agent.go:103`). `Do not modify any files` is a sentence in the scope
line (`prompts.go:306`), not a permission; the prompt tells the reviewer where a
mutation may go: a scratch worktree (`git worktree add --detach "$(mktemp -d)/mut"
HEAD`, or `cp -a` if a worktree is refused), never the run's own worktree, removed
afterwards. That needs no network — the run's checkout already holds HEAD's blobs — and
`git worktree remove --force` is the cleanup.

**(c) The limits the prompt has to fit, and what it therefore asks for.**
`req.MaxBudgetUSD = cfg.Agent.MaxBudgetUSD` (`runner.go:3429`) = **500** in this file
(`fugaro.yaml`), which Claude Code applies against its own Sonnet-like estimate — the
file's own note beside the key and docs/dogfooding.md:61 say that number is not the
real stop — while the gateway's per-run cap is; the review stage's share of the per-run
cap is `stage_budget.review`, default **0.5**, counting the first-line and senior
reviews together (`internal/policy/policy.go:121`; the project layer may only tighten
it). Rounds: `agent.review_rounds` is unset, so the resolved mode's row applies and the
default mode is `pro` (`internal/rigor/mode.go:46`) — 3 senior rounds
(`internal/rigor/rounds.go:40-45`), with an adversarial step and a first line at the
same number (`first_line_review: auto` fires here: a provider serves the coder and the
review stage is account-served). Turns: nothing in the runner passes `--max-turns`
(there is no such field), so the stage is bounded by wall clock and dollars — this
file's `timeouts: {total: 3h, stage: 150m, verify: 25m, finalize_reserve: 5m}`, with
the review stage's own deadline from `budget.StageContext` and any tighter
`governance.stage_timeout` (`runner.go:3431`). The prompt therefore asks for named
`-run` tests, one mutation check and reads — never a whole package, never
`fugaro verify test` — and nothing that needs a long loop. The review stage on this

author: brimalval
body:
Adds `docs/cli-version-management.md`, a research doc on managing CLI tool versions from this repo.

It was prompted by `herdr-browser` requiring agent-browser exactly 0.41.1 while Homebrew ships 0.41.2.

## What's in it

- **Recommendation:** Nix, starting with a small flake in `nix/`.
  - The flake pins agent-browser 0.41.1 from its prebuilt GitHub release binary: one `fetchurl`, one hash, no compiling.
  - It grows into standalone home-manager, then nix-darwin.
  - mise (`agent-browser = "0.41.1"`, which uses aqua's GitHub-binary backend and needs no Node) is the fallback.
- **Comparison and sources:** a table plus a section per tool (mise, Nix, asdf, aqua, proto), with primary sources linked. It covers:
  - the Determinate vs upstream installer, and uninstall cost
  - coexisting with Homebrew
  - the home-manager vs stow symlink conflict
  - devbox and flox, and how Chrome behaves under Nix
- **Pointing `herdr-browser` at the pin:**
  - Why PATH alone loses: `path_helper` puts `/opt/homebrew/bin` ahead of everything `.zshenv` adds.
  - The fix: uninstall the brew formula and set `HERDR_BROWSER_BIN`.
  - A gotcha: a mise shim defeats herdr-browser's version cache.
- **Bumping the pin**, for both the Nix and mise routes.
- **Starter configs:** a flake, a package and a mise `config.toml`, all marked untested.
- **A Nix learning path** with five resources.

## Verification

Nothing was installed. The doc separates verified facts from inferences. Checked:
- The release binary's sha256 matches the npm-bundled copy byte for byte.
- nixpkgs-unstable has 0.41.1, and its aarch64-darwin build is on `cache.nixos.org` (Hydra build 352232255).
- nixhub only lists up to 0.38.2.
- In a clean login shell, Homebrew's 0.41.2 is found first.

## Follow-up

Add `^/docs` (and later `^/nix`) to `.stow-local-ignore` so stow doesn't link them into `~`.

author: mykolad
body:
Phase 3 of the spec: the API and the website.

- **Lists in memory:** `ListCatalog` and `ListLoader`. The lists load from SQL in the background at startup, then every 15 minutes, rebuilding only the lists whose active import changed, one at a time. There is one snapshot swap per refresh, with every source in it. A list is searched only while it has an index and its last successful check is within `MaxAgeHours`; otherwise it shows `Not checked`, with no percentage. If SQL is down, the API keeps serving and lists age out.
- **Endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/v1/screenings` returns 400 if nothing is entered or a field is over 300 characters, and 503 `warmingUp` before the first load. Rows with hits sort first. The summary is worded "No match found in: EU, as of …", never "not sanctioned". The disclaimer is included, and each cell's best candidate comes with how it aligned.
  - `GET /api/v1/status`, and `GET /api/v1/examples` (entities from the live lists: one Latin, one in Cyrillic, one with an address, one with a typo).
  - `GET /healthz`, `GET /readyz`, and `/openapi/v1.json`.
- **Rate limit:** per client IP (`RateLimiting:PerMinute`, 120 by default, 0 = off), keyed on the `X-Forwarded-For` entry the ingress added.
- **Website** (`wwwroot`, plain JS): the form, "Try an example" buttons, the summary, the table of lists by entries (each outcome has a word and a symbol, never colour alone), a detail panel per cell, the disclaimer, and the attribution footer (OGL, trade.gov's required notice, EU). Every value is inserted as text.
- **Matching fix:** a contained name (the patronymic rule) now needs the shorter name's words to be the same words, not near ones. On real data, `ООО «Авиационные Системы и Комплексы»` scored 70% against Ilyushin and Beriev because two words were close; it now sits at about 30%.

**Done-when, checked:**
- HTTP tests cover every outcome, including `Incomplete` and `Not checked` (a stale list and a list without an index), 400, 503, the rate limit and the page.
- A manual source appears as a row with no code change.
- A test proves a screening makes no database call: a connection interceptor counts zero.
- Real names from a local import match on their own lists: Rosneft and Sberbank 99% on 6 lists each, `Сечин И.И.` 70% Review on 5.
- **Memory**, measured locally with workstation, non-concurrent GC: about 320–340 MB private and 400–415 MB working set with all 10 lists, under load too. Production has fewer active lists, and Phase 4 measures it in the 0.5 GiB container.

Requests took p50 about 20 ms and p95 about 125 ms on a desktop, for two names plus an address against 10 lists. Phase 5 measures 0.25 vCPU.

body:
Game track loose ends, merged onto main with no conflicts. The tree is identical to the game track top c05745a.

## What changes
- **Pack schema v2** (`kPackSchemaVersion` 1 -> 2, `kPackMinSchemaVersion` 1). Schema 1 packs still load, and writers still emit v1 unless a v2 feature is used, so v1 pack bytes are unchanged. A v2 pack can carry:
  - `mission.json` with the pack's own title and briefing in PT-BR and en
  - mission objectives and limits
  - mark-price bars (`mark.bin`) and settlement sub-bars (`subbars.bin`)
  - margin tiers in the manifest
  
  Every new field has limits and bomb tests. Packer `build`/`inspect` handle the v2 files and `events.json` stories.
- **Market C sample** (`sample-c-shock`): a packer-built schema-2 pack in the static catalog that tells a liquidity-shock story, so the briefing and ticket shock warnings show in play.
- **Engine C ABI version** (`tl_abi_version`, `kAbiVersion` 1). The web worker refuses a pinned build with another ABI. The desktop records each run's ABI (desktop SQLite schema v5) and refuses to replay a run from another ABI. A refused run is now stored as left, so it is not offered again on every launch.
- **Last-price orders** (bug fix). With a mark series, the web and desktop tickets priced orders from the account mark: the market estimate, limit placeholder, stop/target side checks, chart drags, calibration price and option underlying. The engine prices orders at the last close, so a valid stop between the mark and the last close was blocked. Both clients now use the last close. Regression tests: `lastPrice.test.ts`, `e2e/pack-v2.spec.ts`, desktop `test_pack_runs.cpp`.
- Python binding: `abi_version()`. README, engine README, packer README, product spec and OpenSpec updated.

## Versions
- `kPackSchemaVersion` 1 -> 2 and the new `kAbiVersion` 1.
- `kExecutionPolicyVersion` 17, `kScoringVersion` 12, `kGeneratorVersion` 5 and `kCheckpointFormat` 5 are unchanged.
- Golden digests are unchanged.

## Tested
- Engine native release and debug: 346 cases, all pass.
- clang-tidy (LLVM 22) on `engine/src`: clean. Banned-API and IDL checks pass.
- WASM build and the `wasm-release` ctest pass.
- Python binding: 55 tests pass. API on this tree: 14 tests pass.
- The engine, bindings and web sources are identical on all three stack branches, so the web, desktop and Playwright runs on stack-desktop also cover this code.

## Playtested
- Web e2e: the schema-2 fixture `mark-v2.tlpack` and the liquidity-shock pack in the catalog.
- Desktop: a scripted run of the v2 pack and the Market C pack from briefing to debrief. The ticket warns on bars 15-20 and 171-180.

## Still open
- Market4Me historical packs (1b.*), which need Cyberdyne Auth registration and a legal review.
- Packer task 5.1, as noted in tasks.md.

author: lalalune
body:
## What

Four small changes to the native account path:

1. **A sign-in cancel keeps the account the host holds.** `/cloud/native/cancel` ran the enrollment cancel with `disconnect: true`. The app sends it when a person presses Stop, parks or closes the set-up sign-in, and it then revoked a key the tablet already had. It also revoked a key that a finished sign-in had just reported as connected. The route now drops only the pending sign-in. `/cloud/logout` is still the disconnect. A sign-in cancel still advances the generation and clears billing, as before this PR: the held account stays connected, but its billing session is dropped (an open checkout sees `accountSessionChanged`) and live speech streams are cut.
2. **Stable codes for sign-in conflicts.** The enrollment's 409s now carry a `code` (`SIGN_IN_CONFLICT`): `sign_in_busy`, `sign_in_cancelling`, `sign_in_cancelled`, `sign_in_account_connected`, `sign_in_saved_pending`, `sign_in_disconnect_pending`. The cloud routes pass the code on. An app can tell "busy, try again" from "disconnect first" without matching message text.
3. **One sign-in receipt at a time, and a late ack goes to Cloud.** A second accepted code made a second credential and overwrote the first one's saved receipt. Cloud then kept key 1 live with nothing on the host to finish or revoke it. The exchange now refuses while a receipt is saved. Also, after `acknowledgeBy`, finish refused locally before it sent the ack. If the first ack had landed and only its reply was lost, the person was stuck until Cancel revoked a live key. Finish now always sends the ack. This works against the real Cloud: when an ack lands, the repository's `acknowledge` moves the grant's `expires_at` to the activated key's expiry, so a replay of the same proof after `acknowledgeBy` passes `requireBoundGrantState` and returns the acknowledged state. An ack that never landed is refused with 410 `authorization_code_expired`, and the host reports that as "Sign-in expired. Start again." (410), as the old local check did. That 410 also deletes the expired grant at Cloud, so a later resume gets 400; past `acknowledgeBy` the host reports that as the same 410 "Sign-in expired". The receipt then stays so Cancel can revoke the key. Offline, a resume past expiry reports 502 "Account service is unavailable", since the host now asks Cloud instead of refusing locally.
4. **Durable task file writes.** `writePrivateFileSync` ignored every error from the directory fsync after its rename, so an EIO still counted as "written". Only the codes that mean "this platform cannot sync a directory" are ignored now, as in `writeFileAtomically`. `sealedFilePorts.removeFile` now syncs the directory too.
5. **Stranded task-key slot ops on the broker.** `TaskKeyCustody` gets `readStranded()` and `completeStranded(expectedKeyId)`, served as `task-key-stranded-read` and `task-key-stranded-complete` under the same owner guard. The native client gets the same calls. A host that refuses to adopt a launch's key, because the account already has its own key, can expose that slot. The gateway can then merge its rows and erase the slot only after the merge commits. The defaults report no stranded slot, so current hosts do not change. For now this is unused surface: no host implements the two ops and no gateway code calls them. The host implementation and the gateway caller land separately, and the merge-then-erase order is checked end to end there.

## Why

A formal model (SetupSignInCancel) and scratch runs on the real modules found items 1–2: a Stop during sign-in revoked the existing key (trace depth 5), and also revoked a key the app was told was signed in (depth 17). The NativeEnrollment model and executed probes found item 3. The CrashFile model and a recorded syscall trace found item 4. The AccountKeyCustody model and a scratch JVM run found that a refused adoption strands a launch's task data, and item 5 is the broker part of that fix.

## Tests

- `packages/cloud/sdk/native-host/cloud-services.test.mjs`: the real routes over the real enrollment and a fake Cloud. A cancel after a finished sign-in revokes nothing and stays connected; logout still disconnects. A busy host answers 409 with `sign_in_busy`. The billing-epoch test now expects a plain `cancel()` for `/cloud/native/cancel` and still expects `{disconnect: true}` for `/cloud/logout`.
- `packages/auth/native-host/cloud-enrollment.test.mjs`: a second accepted code is refused, the saved receipt is unchanged and only one key is made. The fake `/ack` models Cloud's late-ack behaviour: a landed ack whose reply was lost is replayed after `acknowledgeBy` and activates the key; an ack that never landed reaches Cloud and gets 410, a second resume gets 400 from Cloud and still reports "Sign-in expired. Start again." (410), and Cancel still revokes it. The active-key refusal carries its code.
- `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/auth-credential-policy.postgres.integration.test.ts`: the real `acknowledgeMobileAppAuthCredential` on Postgres. A landed ack replays the same result after the code's original expiry; an ack that never landed is refused with `authorization_code_expired` and its key stays inactive. The test fails if `acknowledge` stops moving the grant's expiry.
- `packages/cloud/api/__tests__/mobile-app-auth-late-ack.pglite.test.ts` (cloud-api unit lane, runs in CI): the real native-host enrollment resumes a saved receipt against the real `/api/v1/app-auth/mobile/ack` route, service, repository and SQL on PGlite; only the app registration lookup and the rate limiter are stubbed, and the clock is moved past `acknowledgeBy`. A landed ack whose reply was lost activates the key on resume (Cloud answers 200 again). An ack that never landed reports 410 on two resumes while Cloud answers 410, then 400. It fails with the old local `acknowledgeBy` refusal, and fails if `acknowledge` stops moving the grant's expiry.
- `packages/host/native-host/task-storage-sealing.test.mjs`: an injected directory-fsync EIO reaches the caller for write, sealed write and remove. EINVAL is still ignored. Remove syncs the directory.
- `plugins/plugin-native-agent`: client wire test for the stranded ops, and new cases in `LocalCredentialBrokerContract` (guarded, checks the generation, defaults to nothing stranded).

Every new test failed with its fix reverted and passes with it. (The never-landed-ack test pins a 410 the old local check also gave; it fails on old code only through its check that the ack reached Cloud.) Commands run: `node --test` on the touched suites (128 pass) and `node plugins/plugin-native-agent/scripts/test-native-host.mjs` (all pass). The broker contract ran on a desktop JVM, not on an emulator. `bun run verify` was not run.

The Postgres suite ran on a local loopback PostgreSQL 16 (`INFERENCE_POLICY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, `bun test --conditions eliza-source`, 9 pass).

Not shown here: emulator, device or power-loss behaviour, or a deployed Cloud.

author: simonhull
body:
The Program monitor keeps the frames an edit left unchanged, instead of rendering every frame again after any edit.

## Cause
Program-monitor frames and GPU plans are cached under `FrameKey { …, revision }`, and for sequences the revision is `session.revision` (`panels/monitor.rs`). Every edit bumps it, so after any change at all, every cached frame of the sequence was left behind and rendered again on the next request. That includes a label, a marker, a mute on another track, another clip's parameter, and each step of a value drag.

`revision` also orders frames for playback, so it can't simply be replaced by a content hash:
- `recent` falls back up to `PLAYING_REVISION_LAG` revisions while a value is dragged during playback (#1673).
- Job retention drops queued frames of older revisions.

## Change
When the Program monitor sees a new revision of its sequence (`monitor::carry_program_frames`), it moves the cached frames the edit didn't touch over to the new revision. Keys, scheduling and playback stay as they are.

- **`frames::unchanged_frames(was, now, seq, old, new)`** decides which frames show the same picture in both projects:
  - a frame in a render-bar segment with the same content hash, start and length in both;
  - a frame in a gap in both, under the same sequence settings.

  The segment hash (`filmcraft_render::preview`) already covers everything that shapes those pixels, nested sequences included.
- **Two things the segments leave out disable the carry entirely:**
  - the sequence's own caption tracks, which the monitor draws into its frames;
  - the project's LUTs, which the renderer reads by id.
- **The segments are the render bars' own,** memoized per project snapshot (`PreviewStore::segments`). In the usual case both the old and new snapshot's are already computed.
- **`FrameServer::carry(seq, from, to, kept)`** files the matching CPU frames and GPU plans of `Sequence`, `SequencePlan` and `SequenceLive` under `to`:
  - they keep their last use and byte count, and nothing is copied;
  - a frame already rendered at `to` stays, and the carried one is dropped;
  - other sequences and other revisions are untouched.

## Measured
Demo project with a Gaussian Blur (40) on Desert_Dunes.
- **Method:** step through 25 of its frames once to cache them, make an edit, then step through the same 25 again. Each step is `playhead.set`, then waiting until `perf.stats` reports the monitor showing that frame at the current revision. "Frames rendered again" is the `perf.stats` frame-job count.
- **Setup:** release builds of main 177661d5 and this branch, M3 Pro, load 13–36 (other work on the machine), one run each.

| Edit | Frames rendered again: main → this PR | Step to the frame shown (median) |
|---|---|---|
| Label of another clip | 24 → 0 | 25.0 → 16.7 ms |
| Opacity of another clip | 24 → 0 | 25.0 → 16.6 ms |
| Blur of Desert_Dunes itself | 24 → 24 | 25.0 → 25.0 ms |

The last row is the correctness check: an edit to the clip itself still re-renders its frames. A screenshot afterwards shows the new blur.

## Tests (`crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`, `carry_tests`)
- **`an_edit_changes_only_the_frames_of_the_segments_it_touched`**
  - A parameter of clip A's blur changes A's frames only.
  - A label keeps every frame.
  - Sequence settings change every frame, including a gap.
- **`captions_and_luts_change_every_frame`**
  - A caption track or a LUT added keeps nothing.
  - Mutation check: without that guard, the test fails.
- **`carry_files_unchanged_frames_under_the_new_revision`**
  - Kept frames move, including `SequenceLive` frames.
  - Changed frames, other sequences and other revisions stay where they were.
  - A frame already rendered at the new revision is kept over the carried one.
  - The byte count stays equal to the frames it holds.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
- **Scopes** (`scopes.rs`) and other revision-keyed caches still re-render after any edit.
- **Item and Source-monitor targets** keep their per-item revision.
- **Ripple edits:** a segment moved by a ripple edit isn't carried, since its frames' positions changed. It could be, by offset, later.
