  * Cached results aren’t reused when caption tracks or project LUTs change.
* **Documentation**

author: danipopes
body:
The `push constructor; jump` that `emit_constructor_stackified` emits over the constructor's helpers carried no origin, so every deployment with internal helpers had a stackify gap (`<Contract>_deployment bb0 terminator jump`, for example `tests/ui/codegen/size-limits/call-stack-depth-constructor.sol` at `-O none`). The push and jump now take the constructor's declaration span.

solc emits everything that enters the constructor under `CompilerContext::LocationSetter locationSetter(m_context, _constructor)` in `ContractCompiler::appendConstructor` ([libsolidity/codegen/ContractCompiler.cpp L286-L288 at v0.8.38](https://github.com/ethereum/solidity/blob/v0.8.38/libsolidity/codegen/ContractCompiler.cpp#L286-L288)). `deployment.rs` already maps the constructor argument copy to `ctor.declaration_span` for the same reason. On a constructor that calls an internal function, solc 0.8.38 maps the constructor's code to `134:53`, the declaration, and the compiler now gives the jump the same span (`134..187`).

The legacy source map does not change: a code unit without an origin repeats the previous entry, which here is already the argument copy's span. Bytecode and source maps are identical to `origin/main` over every `tests/ui/codegen` source at `-O none` and `-O gas` (1413 files each, 0 bytecode diffs, 0 source map entries changed).

Debugify gaps, UI test mode:

| | origin/main | this PR |
| :-- | --: | --: |
| stackify `jump` | 900 | 655 |
| stackify total | 1,363 | 1,118 |
| all passes | 8,485 | 8,240 |

Closes #85

A model on the operator's machine reads each thread with no tools and returns rows, with quotes checked word for word. A read-only copy of the store goes to files. The two job email agents compare the two using only Read, Grep and Glob, so they hold no mail access and no way to write. Threads that could change a status, or that the operator replied on, reach the agents whole. Writes still happen only in the session the operator talks to, after they choose.

The daily run stays model-free: src/ is untouched.

Not ready to merge: the side-by-side run on a real window has not happened, and merging is the switch. Real Keychain, Gmail and Ollama paths have only run against fakes so far.

## Outcome

Accepting just two new reference screenshots makes PR #4171 fail the existing archive headroom invariant: the reference set is 268,745,290 bytes, so its required 2× allowance exceeds the 512 MiB candidate limit. [Failing final-head CI](https://github.com/copse-dev/agent-pane/actions/runs/42153474979/job/127685081070).

Raise the finite candidate archive allowance to 1 GiB and update its existing invariant. This accommodates twice the supported 512 MiB persisted-manifest ceiling and both new screenshot sets together (269,417,044 bytes across 1,476 references). The persisted-manifest ceiling, 16 MiB image limit, 4,096-file limit, safe paths, real-PNG checks, symlink rejection, trusted policy checkout and integrity verification stay unchanged. This is the shared follow-up needed by #4171 and #4178.

## Risk and review

Medium: a bounded increase to the CI screenshot publisher's resource allowance. No application, permission-policy, dependency or reference-hash changes. Copse reviewed the staged two-file patch in the real Electron UI, found no actionable defect, and committed it using native `git_commit`, retaining SSH signing and Copse/model attribution.

## Validation

Source: `112c2189d5cf3037872922fd09e37a082e7b6335` (SSH signature verified; only the workflow and its existing invariant changed).

- `pnpm run check:local`: passed.
- `pnpm run build`: passed.
- `pnpm run oracle -- --explain`: HIGH, direct invariant coverage.
- `pnpm test -- ci-workflow-invariants screenshot-publication screenshot-storage`: the capacity assertion passes; the ordinary Mac run has 204 passing tests and four host-fixture failures. With commit signing disabled only for disposable test repositories, 207 pass and the remaining Mac Bash 3 empty-array failure reproduces on untouched main. Actual product commits keep signing enabled.
- Combined-reference calculation covers both screenshot PRs without changing their accepted hashes.

There are no new failures and no tracked-source or index movement. This is a noise-only result under `docs/host-environment-test-noise.md`.

Linux validation of this source is recorded in [CI run 42157538472](https://github.com/copse-dev/agent-pane/actions/runs/42157538472), with required `precheck` and `check` gates. No renderer change, so no additional visual fixture is required. Both existing feature PRs preserve their completed original full-unit/native/visual evidence and contain this exact shared commit in Copse-signed integration merges.

## Remaining work

This is the shared base for #4171 and #4178; merge it before those feature PRs. Required cloud gates and owner review apply before merging. All three remain draft, and no public PRs have been merged.

author: yasuyuki-baba
body:
Add a global 1x/2x/4x/8x/16x quality selector, retained across patch loads and saved with instance state. Old states restore 1x; existing 129 parameter IDs and patch data remain intact, with a non-automatable native quality parameter appended.

Preserve oscillator/FM/Sync/noise updates at the host rate and reconstruct intermediate waveforms along signed phase advances, including stack/sub histories. This avoids FM+Sync cycle-frequency drift: an isolated example stays near 3607 Hz instead of rising to 3730 Hz at 16x. Quality changes preserve FM history, and oscillator noise holds its base-frame sample. Aliasing already embedded in the retained feedback model is not removed by this construction.

Run complete voice filters/limiter/saturation and output drive at the selected rate. Decimate summed voice audio so tails outlive voice retirement. MIDI, ARP, LFO, envelopes, shared RNG and intentional decimation retain host cadence. Report 0/48/72/84/90 frames of latency and fade live switches without callback allocations. Higher factors still change level/harmonic balance and cost more CPU; preserved oscillator timing does not guarantee an unchanged strongest spectral peak in a distorted sound.

Validation at f07a5dd:
- All 9 portable CTest entries pass, including heap/bounds and header/naming audits; all 30 focused oscillator, oversampling and FM tests pass.
- Generated tests cover waveform/Ring/Sync/sub/stack changes, signed phase advances beyond half a cycle, analytic folded-carrier suppression, and bridge phase identity during quality changes and MIDI history with nonlinear filter/drive enabled.
- 1x retains all 203 preceding C4 WAV hashes and 20,097 loaded controls, plus 215 multi-pitch WAV hashes. Existing native numerical failures and review thresholds are unchanged.
- All 40 product oscillator renders match the separately alias-evaluated phase-preserving prototype byte for byte. Its eight synthetic conditions reduce output sampling error while preserving phase timing; this is not a whole-instrument alias-free claim.
- Windows APP MinGW cross-build passes. Native MSVC/macOS and DAW validation remain separate boundaries.

Remote CI for this commit: run 42178393824 fails all three portable OS jobs and skips Native. The inspected Ubuntu job reports no steps and its log fetch returns 404 BlobNotFound. The underlying remote failure is unconfirmed; the local passing checks above do not establish remote CI success.

Additional practical validation (2026-11-06, same commit): 8 privately supplied patches across MIDI 36/60/84, 44.1/48 kHz and all five factors, with fixed and changing controls, completed 480 conditions. All inspected physical phase/modulation and envelope states matched a corresponding 1x instance at every callback; candidate audio stayed finite and event-drop counters stayed zero. Dynamic cases include FM sweeps, bend, overlapping notes, retriggers, wheel and live quality switches. Each case covers 48,000 frames, not long tails or hardware playback.

Serial offline CPU measurements at 48 kHz / 64 frames show a material cost: for four notes with eight-voice Unison, median thread CPU time consumes approximately 14%, 37%, 87%, 145%, and 249% of the callback deadline at 1x/2x/4x/8x/16x respectively on the test VM. These short three-round measurements do not certify hardware xruns or universal performance. 8x/16x are unsuitable for that workload on this machine.

Output level remains patch dependent: whole-capture RMS changes from 1x to 16x ranged from -3.47 to +1.93 dB. One percussive patch already exceeds full scale at 1x and peaks can increase at higher quality; no automatic level normalization was added. Audible switching clicks and native DAW/device behavior remain unverified. CI failure remains unresolved: portable jobs contain no executed steps; check annotations exist but their endpoint is unavailable through the current connector.

author: jay23606
body:
## Bug

In the research-store pipeline template list, the 移除 (remove) button was bound to `delete (props.row)`. Vue compiled this to the JavaScript `delete` operator, so the component's delete method was never called and the slot's `row` property was removed. Clicking 上架 on the same row then threw, because its handler reads `props.row.templateCode`.

## Change

- `template.vue`: the click binding is now `deleteHandle(props.row)`. `deleteHandle` opens a confirmation dialog and, on confirm, calls `deleteTemplate(row.templateCode)` and refreshes the list.
- Locale files (en-US, ja-JP, zh-CN): add the `removeTemplateTips` confirmation text.
- New regression test `src/frontend/devops-atomstore/test/template-remove-handler.test.js`: compiles the template and asserts that the remove click does not produce `delete props.row` and does call `_vm.deleteHandle(props.row)`.

## Testing

- `node src/frontend/devops-atomstore/test/template-remove-handler.test.js`: passes on the fix (`fail 0`).
- The same command against the base `template.vue` fails with `remove handler compiled to the JS delete operator: "delete props.row"`.
- `node -e "for (const f of ['en-US','ja-JP','zh-CN']) JSON.parse(...)"`: the three locale files parse as JSON.

**Regression test:** fails on base twice (/remove handler compiled to the JS delete operator/), passes on fix twice (`node src/frontend/devops-atomstore/test/template-remove-handler.test.js`)

Fixes #13826

body:
CCEX 2.1.0, the changes since 2.0.1. The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md → 2.1.0](https://github.com/CQML-SKKU/CCEX/blob/try-2.1.0/CHANGELOG.md). No input key of 2.0.1 was renamed or removed. After the merge, tag the merge commit `v2.1.0`.

### Added
- **method `noise`.** The Gaussian phase-noise coherence exp(−χ), from the modes of the bath's clusters or from a model spectrum (OU, power), the semi-classical CCE. `hamiltonian.noise.compute` gives the coherence, the spectrum S(f) or the correlation C(t). With `backend` `cuda` the mode sums run on the GPU.
- **method `pseudospin`.** The pair clusters of cCCE in the pseudospin model of nuclear flip-flops (Seo et al. 2016, Lee, Park, Seo 2022), with `hamiltonian.pseudospin.channels` `grouped` or `pairwise` and a table of every channel. It is meant for finding the pairs that drive a decay.
- **`execution.gpu_options.ranks_per_gpu`.** Only k ranks per GPU open it, and each cluster goes to a GPU rank or a CPU rank, whichever would finish it first. With `backend` `auto` or `cuda` the `gpu_options` an input leaves out are chosen at the start.
- **A GPU batch of cCCE clusters is diagonalized in one call** (`cusolverDnXsyevBatched`).

### Fixed
- Two runs of one path wrote different last digits with MKL. The MKL builds now set the reproducible mode.
- `quadrupole.structure` `"strained"` took the wrong tensor for a far spin, and `"strained"`/`"bubble"` with a vertex-format file never ended.
- `cluster.mode` itb and dsjitb took the power of each inter-bath pair from the wrong spin.
- A bath spin on a face of a tensor file's cell stopped the run. A face without a row now counts as outside, as in a periodic cell.
- The `cluster.adaptive` block with `cluster.mode` pcce is refused at input (the refinement works with bundle only). cCCE with `quantity` dm is refused at input.
- Smaller fixes to messages, `summary.txt` of the automatic convergence and the exit status of BathGenerator.

### Builds
- CUDA 13.2 is required only for compute capability 12.0 and above. An older nvcc (CUDA 12.8) is accepted below it, for example on a GH200 with the system MPS.

### Tutorials and documentation
- `example/tutorial/` is split into `basic/` (six topics in order) and `advanced/` (thirteen topics), with new tutorials for noise, pseudospin, the automatic GPU options, DFT tensors from a VASP run, the analyzer and a Slurm run.
- One documentation page per input block, a page of old names, and method pages for noise, pseudospin and the automatic convergence.
- A final proofreading of the documentation against the code (dates, counts, defaults, paths).

### Checks
- `test/code_verification/run.sh`, all 12 checks pass.
- `make numeric-test cpu-test` and the AutoConvergence pytest (190 tests) pass.
- `make gpu-test` (219 pass, 0 fail), `check_options.py` (110 pass) and a P1 run on the GPU against the CPU (max|dL| 4.1e-10) on a GH200 node, with CUDA 12.8 and with CUDA 13.2.

author: openipc-ai
body:
Two S3L fixes that came out of the review of #2763.

**CPU target.** `s3l_lite_defconfig` targeted a Cortex-A7 with VFPv4, but the S3L is a Cortex-A9 with NEON and VFPv3 (`cpuinfo` in OpenIPC/ipctool#266). With the old flags gcc emits `sdiv` and `vfma`, which an A9 doesn't have, so ordinary code can take SIGILL.

**`load_ambarella`.** The script was 0 bytes, so `S70vendor` ran it and nothing loaded. It now does the following, in the vendor's order:
1. Loads `iav`; `modprobe` pulls in `dsp`, `hw_timer`, `imgproc` and `vout`.
2. Creates `/dev/iav` and `/dev/ucode`, root-only, because `iav` registers no device class and mdev never sees them.
3. Loads the sensor driver, using `sensor` from the environment or `ipcinfo -s`. A stored `unknown` falls through to detection. A bare name means MIPI, because `ipcinfo` can't tell the interface; `imx290_lvds` and `imx326_lvds` reach the LVDS drivers.
4. Runs `load_ucode /lib/firmware` if the tool and microcode are present.

**This does not produce video on its own.** The microcode isn't in this package, and it needs a licensing decision. The stock `load_ucode` is a glibc armhf binary that won't run on this musl image. `s3l_lite_defconfig` selects no streamer, and #2763 lists more that video needs: the board's device tree, a 3A process, an exact 30 fps VIN and an ISP configuration. The author plans PRs for those. Without them the drivers load, the DSP stays down, and the script logs that video will not start.

**Hardware evidence**
- This PR's image has not run on a camera. No S3L board is available to us, and nothing in CI builds `s3l_lite`.
- The author reports, from their Amcrest IP4M-1026E, that a hand-run bring-up works in the same order, with `/proc/devices` showing `248 iav` and `248 ucode`, and `modules.dep` resolving `iav` to `hw_timer imgproc vout dsp`. `ov4689_mipi` needs no arguments.
- The same board runs a `BR2_cortex_a9` NEON build with H.264 after a warm reboot, but that is a glibc armhf toolchain, not this musl softfp one. A cold boot doesn't stream yet.

**Tested here**
- Buildroot 2024.02.10 resolves the defconfig to `-mcpu=cortex-a9 -mfpu=neon`. Before, it was `cortex-a7` and `neon-vfpv4`.
- The same C file compiled with each set of flags: the A7 flags emit `sdiv` and `vfma.f64`, and the A9 flags call `__aeabi_idiv`.
- The final script under `dash` with stubbed commands, 15 cases: load order, node creation and mode, each sensor spelling, stored `unknown`, unsupported and missing sensors, and no microcode. `iav` failing ran on the previous commit, and that code didn't change.

**Not tested:** a full `s3l_lite` image build, its size before and after, and a run of a binary built with the new flags. No toolchain is published yet (#2765).

author: ryanng1403
body: This PR builds every fighter's atlas with the 3D-to-pixel pipeline in `tools/sprites3d` (the approach Dead Cells used). Each fighter is a parametric MakeHuman body rigged in headless Blender, posed in code and toon-rendered. The renders are reduced to pixel art, and a photo-referenced 2D likeness head is composited in four views. It includes PR #12 (the likeness heads, merged into this branch) and `origin/main` at #11. Against main, the diff touches only `tools/sprites3d/**` and `assets/fighters/**`. ## In the game (main, quick-start, all 6 fighters on main) [In-game, all six fighters](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-85119983-e60c-5faf-ace2-0d3c55abced3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fingame-3d-roster.png) I ran three quick-start 1v1s (`sam` vs `dario`, `andrej` vs `yann`, `liang` vs `mustafa`) and one 2v2 in headless Chrome, with P1 driven by the keyboard and CPU-vs-CPU passes. - **Loading:** every fighter loads its atlas: 21 animations, 3072×2816. The animations the engine played included idle, walk_fwd, walk_back, dash_fwd, dash_back, run, jump_start, jump_air, jump_land, crouch, block, hit_high, hit_low, knockdown and getup. - **Console:** no errors, warnings, failed requests or HTTP errors in any run. - **Speed:** body speed equals the atlas `strideSpeed`. For Sam, walk measured 200.6 px/s against 200.3 in the atlas, and run 450.5 against 449.9; the others match the same way. - **Planted feet:** in every sample the displayed frame equals distance travelled ÷ (`strideSpeed`/fps), with a single phase constant per walk or run (27/27 to 75/75 samples per fighter and state). So the cycle advances exactly with distance, and a planted foot returns to the same world x at every frame change. The only movement left is within a frame, as with any sprite cycle: at most one frame's travel, about 11 px for the walk and 22 px for the run. ## What's in it **Atlases.** One `assets/fighters//atlas.png` and `atlas.json` per fighter, following the contract: 256 px cells, anchor 128/244, frames packed into a 12-column grid. - `strideSpeed` is on `walk_fwd`, `walk_back` and `run`. - Every landing frame carries a footstep event (`{"frame", "type": "footstep", "foot"}`). **Shared states.** `idle` (orthodox guard), `walk_fwd`, `walk_back`, `run`, `dash_fwd`, `dash_back`, `jump_start`, `jump_air`, `jump_land`, `crouch`, `block`, `crouch_block`, `hit_high`, `hit_low`, `knockdown`, `getup`, `ko`, `dazed`, `thrown`, `tag_in` and `tag_out`. **Likeness heads (from PR #12).** These are `heads/_{tq,profile,hurt,shout}.png`, with rows taken from `heads/heads.json`. - Each fighter config points at `_tq.png` and lists every view. - `process.py` picks a view per animation: - profile: walk_back and the dashes - hurt: hits, knockdown, ko, dazed and thrown - shout: special*, super*, victory*, intro* and finisher* - three-quarter: everything else - Each head rotates with the head bone, so it stays attached when a fighter falls, lies down or flips. - The 3D skin tone is sampled from the head, so the neck shows no seam. - Fei-Fei's neck cut sits at the bottom of her hair, so her hair falls over her shoulders. [Head views in place](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-85119983-e60c-5faf-ace2-0d3c55abced3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fheads-insitu.png) **Props hook.** `blender/props.py` provides `props.add` and `props.register`, and `posing.apply_pose` applies them. A pose or keyframe sets `props: {name: True | {offset, rot, scale, space, visible}}`, and every registered prop's visibility and transform is keyed on every frame. This replaces the forks' `moves/_props.py` monkey-patch. **Move modules.** Files under `blender/moves/**` (written by the move forks) are discovered and merged into the atlas. The interface is documented in the README. **Polish.** - The neck seam is gone. - Feet are smaller, with smoothed shoe shells. - Fists are real fists. - The run leans 19°. - Hems that hang below the hip now wrap the thighs instead of cutting up between them. ## Sam and Fei-Fei, all shared states [Sam](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-85119983-e60c-5faf-ace2-0d3c55abced3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fshared-sam-v3.png) [Fei-Fei](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-85119983-e60c-5faf-ace2-0d3c55abced3/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fshared-feifei-v3.png) ## Reproduce ```bash tools/sprites3d/setup.sh JOBS=4 tools/sprites3d/build_all.sh # all 16 fighters, about 6 min on 8 CPU cores ``` ## Known limits - Clothing is the body surface pushed outward, so there are no jacket flaps or hoods. - No hitboxes or hurtboxes are written; the engine falls back to the character data. - The shout view appears only once the forks' special, super, victory and intro animations are merged in. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

Adds the indication from FDA's 2026-09-04 Etcamah (camizestrant, NDA220359) label, with nine derived statements. This is the first FDA curation of Etcamah, so it also adds the Etcamah documents and their label URLs.

## Database content updates

### Added entries

- (FDA) [ESR1 activating variants, HER2-negative, and Hormone receptor positive and therapeutic response sensitivity to camizestrant in combination with abemaciclib, palbociclib, or ribociclib for patients with locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer upon detection of ESR1 mutation during aromatase inhibitor and CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy](https://moalmanac.org/indications/ind:fda:etcamah:0). The indication received accelerated approval. Statements were derived for camizestrant with each of the three CDK4/6 inhibitors named in the label, each for ER-positive, PR-positive, and ER- and PR-positive disease.

## Feature updates

No repository or schema changes were made. This pull request only updated database content.

## Implementation details

- [`doc:fda:etcamah`](https://moalmanac.org/documents/doc:fda:etcamah) and [`doc:fda:etcamah:2026-09-04`](https://moalmanac.org/documents/doc:fda:etcamah:2026-09-04) were added, along with `url:fda:etcamah:label`, `url:fda:etcamah:overview`, and `url:fda:etcamah:label:2026-09-04`.

All statements reuse its camizestrant therapy groups ([`txgrp:199`](https://moalmanac.org/therapy-groups/txgrp:199) through [`txgrp:201`](https://moalmanac.org/therapy-groups/txgrp:201)), so no new therapies, therapy groups, or biomarkers were needed.

Its indication status is Approved rather than Accelerated, it cites `ctrb:vanallenlab:2026-10-30:0`, its propositions are `prop:vtxr:1015` through `prop:vtxr:1020`, and its document citations give a different access date. author: bbockelm
body:
A delegated subtree in a ClassAd Script now reads the script's locals, instead of being refused.

## The escape hatch

`classad.SetResolver` replaces scope resolution outright, so a resolver has no way to say "not mine". `Evaluator.SetPartialResolver` installs one that returns `(Value, bool)`: a declined reference resolves exactly as it would with nothing installed — the full resolver if one is set, otherwise the ClassAd scope, with the scope chain, the MY/TARGET/PARENT rules, the evaluation of the referenced attribute's expression and the CurrentTime substitution all intact.

A declining resolver rather than a "resolve as if nothing were installed" call, because the two cases that make this hard both want the evaluator to carry on down its own path rather than re-enter it: an ad that defines `CurrentTime = undefined` cannot be reported through a value, and a re-entrant call would resolve the attribute's own expression with the overlay still in force. `SetResolver` is untouched and composes with it.

The overlay is suppressed while an attribute's own expression is evaluated, so `A = B + 1` means the ad's B wherever A is read.

## Wiring

The compiler records, per delegated node, the bare names bound as locals where that node sits, with the register each lives in. Both interpreters — `OpEvalNode` and `REvalNode` — call one shared `evalDelegated`, which installs the resolver over the register file, evaluates, and removes it however the evaluation returns.

Which names the overlay answers is decided at compile time, from the compiler's local map, so the binding rules inside a delegated subtree are the rules outside it: a bare bound name is the local; `MY.x` is the attribute; `x = x + 1` reads the attribute and binds the local; a function body sees its own locals and never the caller's. Each is a test case.

## What is still refused

`LocalCaptureError` stays reachable, for three positions that evaluate in an evaluator of their own which no overlay installed on the caller's reaches:

- a list literal's elements, which are lazy — materialized from a captured scope, possibly after the script has finished and its registers are gone;
- an ad literal's attribute values, which resolve against that literal;
- the first argument of `countMatches`/`evalInEachContext`, evaluated once per nested ad in a child evaluator.

`TestDelegatedLazyListEscapes` demonstrates the lazy-list hazard directly: build `{x}` under an overlay, drop the overlay, materialize, and the element reads the attribute. That is the refusal's reason, held down by a test rather than left as a comment.

## Interactions

**Read set.** `scriptReads` subtracts, per node, the names that node resolves from a register. `TestDelegatedLocalReadSet` covers a delegated subtree mentioning both a local and a genuine attribute.

**Purity gate.** Unchanged and confirmed: `checkPure` rule 4 still refuses any registered function containing a delegated node. `TestScriptFuncPurityGate/ternary_over_param` now reaches that rule (it used to stop at the compiler) and `list_over_param` still stops at the compiler.

**Optimizer.** `REvalNode` reads the registers of the locals its node mentions although it names none of them, so `regUses` lists them and `substitute` rewrites them; `Optimize` detaches `nodeLocals` before copy propagation. Without either, dead-code elimination deletes the store that fills a local.

**Concurrency.** Nothing shared is installed: each run allocates its own evaluator, register file and resolver closure. `TestDelegatedLocalConcurrent` runs one compiled program from 16 goroutines, each with its own ad. Suites run with `-race`.

## Parity

`TestDelegatedParity` evaluates 33 delegated shapes — ternaries, list literals, ad literals, selects, lazy built-ins, unknown names, bad arities, nested combinations, cyclic references — through an expression program, through a script, and through a script carrying an unused local, asserting all three agree with the plain evaluator.

`TestDelegatedLocalBothInterpreters` runs one straight-line script through both interpreters; the stack form gained the two local opcodes so it can.

body:
> 🤖 Opened by arslanarm's AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5), not by arslanarm personally.

## What and why

Shader packs now read a colortex's mipmaps blended between the two nearest levels, as Iris 1.11.7 does. Before, Horizon took the nearest level: the buffers' sampler (`SamplerKind::Linear`) kept wgpu's default mipmap filter, nearest. The colortex buffers get a sampler of their own (`SamplerKind::Buffer`: linear, with a linear mipmap filter). Shadowcolor, custom textures, the lightmap and the stand-ins keep theirs, because they weren't measured. #9765 did the same for the block atlas.

Fixes #10451
Part of #9307

This doesn't move PotatoShaders' Nether (measurements below). Our Nether probes found this difference on the way.

### How the cause was found

All probes are packs of our own, run in Iris 1.11.7 (`iris-ref`) and in Horizon main cd547654d, in the caves and Nether scenes of our `scenes.json`.

1. #9765 found Iris blending the atlas's two nearest levels, and #9896 measured colortex levels only at whole levels. So we read colortex between levels.
2. `composite` writes per-pixel noise into colortex1 (RGBA16F). `final` declares `colortex1MipmapEnabled` and averages, over 64 points, `|textureLod(L) - mix(level floor(L), level floor(L)+1, fract(L))|` for L = 0.5, 1.25, 2.5, 3.75, 4.5 and 6.5:
   - Iris: 0.0001 to 0.0005.
   - Horizon: 0.003 to 0.021, with the read equal to one of the two levels (to the bit).
3. The same for all 16 colortex (0-7 read in `composite2`, 8-15 in `final`, at levels 2.5 and 1.25). Iris: 0.0002 to 0.0004 for every buffer. Horizon: 0.016 to 0.019.

With a build of this branch's working tree before the test was added (its non-test code is 4c0ef1d7d's), probe 3 reads 0.00025 to 0.00038 for colortex0–3 in `nether_basalt`, the values we checked, where Iris reads 0.00026 to 0.00040.

### Tests

`pack_post/colortex_mip_blend_tests.rs`: `composite` writes 1.0 into the left half of a 4×4 colortex1 and 0 into the right half. `final` reads it at (0.25, 0.5) at levels 1.5 and 1.25, and must get 0.75 and 0.875 (191 and 223, ±2). On main cd547654d it fails with red 127 and green 255 (levels 2 and 1); it passes on this branch.

### Measurements

- `real_packs` (`SHOW_ERRORS=1`, all 40 packs), main cd547654d against this branch: no difference (`horizon-shaders` is untouched). Both outputs have 812 lines; besides the diff, we read only those line counts.
- PotatoShaders, pictures only, 64×36 mean absolute difference to Iris 1.11.7 (the same Iris run). Main cd547654d, then two runs of this branch:

| scene | main | branch, run 1 | branch, run 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ow_cave_dark` | 0.31 | 0.30 | 0.37 |
| `ow_cave_lit` | 1.14 | 1.16 | 1.47 |
| `ow_lush_cave` | 0.46 | 0.44 | 0.45 |
| `nether_wastes` | 2.38 | 2.12 | 2.19 |
| `nether_crimson` | 2.46 | 2.41 | 2.45 |
| `nether_warped` | 5.21 | 5.21 | 5.29 |
| `nether_soul_sand` | 0.90 | 0.90 | 0.91 |
| `nether_basalt` | 7.16 | 7.09 | 7.10 |

Horizon run-to-run noise in these scenes is 0.25 to 3.9 (basalt).

- Other packs, pictures only, our 16-scene suite against Iris 1.11.7's references (`suite3`, 2026-11-01), 64×36:
  - BSL v10.1.8: mean over the 16 scenes 1.97 and 2.00 on main cd547654d, 1.99 on the branch.
  - Photon v1.4: its overworld flips between two pictures, on main and on this branch alike (main 1 of 5 runs close to Iris, this branch 2 of 4). The other scenes stay within main's range.

## Kind

author: timeless-hayoka
body:
## Changes
- Adds a manual-only GitHub Actions workflow to authenticate pinned Optimism historical registry snapshots using repository secrets `OP_ARCHIVE_RPC_A` and `OP_ARCHIVE_RPC_B`. It checks for missing or identical secrets, runs offline regression tests first, and uploads evidence only after successful live authentication.
- Hardens the verifier: EIP-1898 `blockHash` + `requireCanonical: true` for `eth_getCode` and `eth_call`, with no silent downgrade to block-number reads.
- Adds a regression test for block-hash binding and wires the new workflow into PR offline CI.

## Security boundary
- Secret-bearing workflow runs **only via manual `workflow_dispatch` on reviewed main**, not on PRs. The workflow checks out `main` and uses read-only token permissions. No RPC secrets appear in CLI arguments.
- Two distinct URLs do not guarantee independent operators: owner must configure different providers and confirm archive/EIP-1898 support.
- Does not execute `debug_traceTransaction`, prove source equivalence or authorize liquidation replay. Live authentication cannot run until both secrets are set and PR merged.

## Review gates
Check PR CI, inspect manual workflow security, merge only after review; then configure secrets and run Actions → Extra Finance independent archive registry authentication → Run workflow. **Do not auto-merge.**

author: watzon
body:
Closes #4.

This PR adds the SVG features that were still open after #8 and #9 (see the checklist in #4).

## Changes

- **`use` and `defs`:** `x`/`y` offsets, `symbol` and `svg` targets with `viewBox`, and the referenced element takes its style from the `use` element. A `use` that points back at its own ancestor stops instead of looping.
- **Text:** `tspan` with `x`, `y`, `dx` and `dy`, including one value per character. `tspan` inherits style from its parent, and white space collapses as in browsers. `text-anchor` works per text chunk. `em` lengths use the font size.
- **Fonts:** `font-family`, `font-weight` and `font-style` map to the 14 standard PDF fonts (serif to Times, monospace to Courier, everything else to Helvetica).
- **CSS:** `<style>` sheets with type, class, id and attribute selectors and the `>` and descendant combinators. The cascade is: presentation attributes, then rules by specificity and source order, then `style=""`, then `!important`.
- **Gradients:** `linearGradient` and `radialGradient` become PDF shadings. They support `href` inheritance, `gradientTransform`, both `gradientUnits` and the focal point. `stop-opacity` (and `rgba()` stops) uses a luminosity soft mask.
- **`clipPath`:** user space or `objectBoundingBox` units, `clip-rule`, and the union of overlapping children.
- **Opacity:** `opacity`, `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity` and `rgba()`/`#RGBA` colors.
- **Rounded rects:** `rect` `rx` and `ry`, with the SVG rules for a missing value and clamping.
- **Strokes:** `stroke-dasharray`, `stroke-dashoffset`, `stroke-linecap`, `stroke-linejoin` and `stroke-miterlimit`, inherited from groups. A `stroke-width` of 0 draws nothing.
- **Viewports:** nested `<svg>` viewports with clipping, and `preserveAspectRatio` with all alignments, `meet`, `slice` and `none`. The root drawing is clipped to its output box.
- **Parsing:** root sizes given in `%` fall back to the viewBox size, then to 300 x 150. Before, they caused a NaN error. Non-finite numbers are ignored.

Main's arc conversion, root transform, `viewBox` handling, default of no stroke and group inheritance are unchanged, and all the earlier specs pass without edits.

Library changes outside SVG:

- `Page` gets shading and pattern resources: `register_shading`, `shade`, `register_pattern`, `fill_pattern` and `stroke_pattern`.
- `ExtGState#hash_key` now includes the soft mask, so two states that differ only in their mask are no longer merged.

## Limits

These are also listed in the README:

- `opacity` on a group applies to each child separately, so overlapping children blend with each other.
- Gradient strokes and gradient text assume that the page has no transform of its own when `page.svg` is called.
- `spreadMethod` reflect and repeat draw as pad.
- `image`, `mask`, `pattern`, `marker` and `filter` are skipped, and the renderer records a warning.

## Verification

- `crystal spec`: 799 examples, 0 failures. That is the 699 existing specs plus 100 new ones: 23 CSS specs in `spec/pdf/svg/css_spec.cr` and 77 feature and regression specs in `spec/pdf/svg/features_spec.cr`.
- `crystal tool format --check`: clean.
- `bin/ameba`: 123 files inspected, 0 failures, and no rules disabled.
- `examples/svg_demo.cr` draws one sample per feature. I rendered it with macOS Quartz and poppler and compared the samples with `rsvg-convert`.

author: pmstander
body:
## Thinking Path

- Studio 0.1.4 is live with `partnersinbiz.studio` tools (estimate, generate, status, get-asset, import, link, review).
- The live `higgsfield` company skill still told agents to call the Higgsfield REST API with `HF_KEY` through `hf.py`. `pib-creative-studio` still sent files through Social's `import-media-from-attachment`.
- PAR-7946 (under PAR-7749) asks for both skills to cut over to the Studio tools.
- `higgsfield` is a `local_path` company skill with no source in git, so this PR adds its source next to the plugin it describes. `pib-creative-studio` is generated from `plugin-social/src/skills.ts`.

## What Changed

- New `packages/plugins/plugin-studio/skills/higgsfield/SKILL.md`: Studio tools only (`studio-estimate` before `studio-generate`, a wake comment plus a fallback monitor, `studio-get-asset`, `studio-review-asset`, `studio-link-asset`). Removes all `HF_KEY`, `hf.py`, REST and MCP guidance. Keeps the Drive rules and the quality bar.
- `plugin-social/src/skills.ts`, `pib-creative-studio`:
  - Render: generate with Studio; local HTML/ffmpeg renders go in through `studio-import-from-attachment`.
  - "Store in Studio": approve keepers with `studio-review-asset` into Social's library, then `list-media-assets` for the post.
  - No more `import-media-from-attachment` / `import-media-from-url` in this skill.
- Tests:
  - New `plugin-studio/tests/higgsfield-skill.spec.ts`: every Studio tool is named, nothing unregistered, no key, script or REST strings.
  - `plugin-social/tests/skills.spec.ts`: updated for Studio tools, plus a new "Studio only" test.
- Studio README: how the skill cut-over works.

## Verification

- `cd packages/plugins/plugin-studio && npx vitest run tests/higgsfield-skill.spec.ts`
- `cd packages/plugins/plugin-social && npx vitest run tests/skills.spec.ts tests/skills-budget.spec.ts tests/role-skills.spec.ts tests/manifest.spec.ts`

## Risks

- **Cut-over is a separate deploy step.** The live company `higgsfield` skill only changes after someone copies this SKILL.md over `instances/default/skills/<company>/higgsfield/SKILL.md` and removes `hf.py`. That needs Peet's approval. `HF_KEY` stays in agent env; removing it is a separate Peet-gated ticket.
- **Alt text workaround.** Generated assets have no alt text, because `studio-generate` and `studio-review-asset` take no `altText`. The skill uses a workaround: re-import the file with `altText`. A follow-up could add `altText` to the Studio tools.
- **Studio tool grant.** Creative agents need the Studio tools granted. If they are missing, the skill tells the agent to block, not to fall back to the API.
- **Rollout.** The Social plugin needs a release, so the new `pib-creative-studio` text syncs to companies.

## Model Used

Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), via Hermes Agent, with tool use. Haiku helper for read-only exploration.

## Checklist

- [x] Thinking path, changes, verification, risks filled in
- [x] Tests added/updated and run locally
- [x] No secrets in the diff
- [x] No merge or deploy by the author

author: nilscost
body:
Fixes the two intermittent WebKit failures in the `web-smoke` job. Only test code and the evidence note change; the app is unchanged.

**1. `request failed: pushup-standard.mp4`** (runs 42007885134, 42039131194)
- When the user taps Done, the app releases the clip (`DemoClips.wasmJs.kt`: `removeAttribute('src')` + `load()`). Linux WebKit reports that release as "Load request cancelled".
- The test now treats a cancelled demo-clip request as benign only if the app released that clip URL, or the test reloaded the page after the request started. These show up in the results as `benignAborts`.
- Every other failed request still fails the run.

**2. `onboarding Next button did not appear`** (run 42047696791), and the older "end screen / dialog mid fade-out" flake
- Playwright's Linux WebKit shows a WebGL canvas one frame late: frame N reaches the screen only when frame N+1 is drawn.
- Compose draws only when something changes, so its last frame before going idle never appeared. That frame held the "Next" label that had just loaded, the end-screen cards, or the end of a dialog fade.
- Proof: at a failure, the test cleared the app's own context to red and the screen did not change. It turned red only after a green frame was drawn next.
- The test now creates WebGL contexts with `preserveDrawingBuffer`, in WebKit only.

**Not changed:** no retries were added, the console allow-list is the same, and there are no new fixed sleeps.

**Ruled out:**
- The service worker deleting Compose's cache: the failure also happens without a service worker.
- Lost coroutine dispatches: every `postMessage` dispatch was delivered.
- WebGL context loss.
- A failed string load: the string loaded, and both the state write and the draw happened.

**Verification:**
- Linux container `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1-noble`, unchanged app: 6/6 passes. The original test failed 3/4 there.
- macOS: WebKit and Chromium passed 5 runs in a row, and `web-pwa-test` passed.
- CI `verify`: three runs on this branch, linked in the comments.

Details are in `docs/evidence/kmp-port.md`, under "Web smoke flake fix".

Completa os filtros da listagem pública de sementes do site (RF-04 e CDU-01 do Apêndice B). Antes dava para filtrar só por nome popular, disponibilidade, tipo e comunidade. Agora também dá para filtrar por município, estado, região, nome do produtor, data de inclusão e data da última alteração. Perfil do produtor/propriedade e impressão em PDF ficaram de fora, como o time combinou.

## Como ficou

**Backend (`GET /catalogo/produtos`)**: o `CatalogoProdutoResponseDTO` ganhou três campos:
- `nomeProdutor`: nome de exibição do produtor. Só vem preenchido quando ele marcou `exibirNoSitePublico` (a mesma regra do `ProdutorPublicoService`, RNF-06). Sem autorização, vem `null`; a oferta continua no catálogo, só sem o nome. Nenhum outro dado do produtor sai (id, e-mail, telefone, documento, endereço), e o DTO agora diz isso em comentário.
- `dataInclusao`: `Produto.dataInclusao`.
- `dataUltimaAlteracao`: a mais recente entre a alteração do produto e as datas da oferta (`dataUltimaAtualizacao` e `dataMovimentacao`). Preço, saldo e disponibilidade mudam na oferta sem mexer no produto. Sem nenhuma alteração, fica igual à inclusão.

Os filtros da consulta não mudaram: o site continua filtrando no navegador, sobre o catálogo inteiro.

**Site (`/`)**:
- Novo painel de filtros (`components/filtros-catalogo.tsx`, com a lógica em `lib/filtros-catalogo.ts`):
  - **Nome popular** e **Produtor** são campos de texto. A busca ignora acento ("feijao" acha "Feijão"). O campo de produtor sugere os nomes que existem no catálogo (`datalist`) e avisa que só aparecem os produtores que autorizaram mostrar o nome.
  - **Comunidade**, **Região**, **Estado** e **Município** são selects montados só com o que existe no catálogo, como o de comunidade já fazia. As opções seguem umas às outras: a região limita os estados, o estado limita os municípios, e escolher um município marca o estado dele (o mesmo nome existe em mais de um estado, por isso aparece como "Rio Pomba - MG"). A região é tirada da UF pela divisão do IBGE.
  - **Data de inclusão** e **Última alteração**: qualquer data, últimos 7, 30 ou 90 dias, ou último ano.
  - As pílulas de disponibilidade e de tipo continuam iguais.
  - **Limpar filtros** aparece quando tem algum filtro ativo. Ao clicar, o foco volta para a busca, para não se perder quando o botão some.
- **URL**: os filtros vão para a query (`?q=&produtor=&uf=&municipio=&regiao=&comunidade=&disponibilidade=&tipo=&incluido=&alterado=`) com `replaceState`, então o link filtrado pode ser compartilhado e continua funcionando depois de recarregar. Há um atraso de 300 ms para não chamar uma vez por tecla. O `?comunidade=<id>#produtos` do "Ver produtos" do `/mapa` continua igual: a URL não muda, o hash fica e o filtro abre marcado. Valores da URL que não existem no catálogo são ignorados, como já acontecia com a comunidade.
- O card mostra o nome do produtor (só quando autorizado) e "Atualizado em dd/mm/aaaa".
- "Mostrar mais" volta para 24 cards a cada mudança de filtro, como antes.
- Com filtro e sem resultado, a mensagem passa a ser "Nenhum produto encontrado com esses filtros.", no lugar de "Nenhum produto no catálogo ainda.".
- Acessibilidade: cada campo tem rótulo visível, e o nome acessível contém o texto do rótulo ("Estado" / "Filtrar por estado"). O painel é um `form role="search"`. A contagem de resultados é anunciada (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic`). Os nomes acessíveis que os testes já usavam ("Filtrar por comunidade", placeholder da busca, pílulas) continuam os mesmos.
- Responsivo: os selects ficam em 1 coluna no celular, 2 a partir de 480px, 3 no tablet e 6 no desktop, com `min-w-0` para a página não rolar para o lado.

## Testes

Backend:
- Novo `CatalogoPublicoServiceTest` (Mockito): o nome sai só com `exibirNoSitePublico = true`; produtor sem autorização e nome em branco dão `null`; o DTO não tem outros campos pessoais; `dataInclusao` vem do produto; `dataUltimaAlteracao` é a mais recente entre produto e oferta e, sem alteração, é a inclusão.
- Novo `CatalogoProdutorEDatasIntegrationTest` (MockMvc + Postgres do Testcontainers): pelo JSON de `/catalogo/produtos`, produtor público aparece com o nome e com as datas em ISO, sem e-mail/telefone/documento; produtor privado vem com `nomeProdutor: null`.
- Rodado localmente: `mvnw test -Dtest=CatalogoPublicoServiceTest,ProdutorPublicoServiceTest,ProdutorPublicoControllerTest`, 22/22 passando. `mvnw test-compile` ok.
- **Não rodado localmente**: o `CatalogoProdutorEDatasIntegrationTest`, que precisa de Docker (Testcontainers). Ele roda no `ci.yml`.

Site:
- `npm ci`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` e `npm run build` ok.
- A lógica de `lib/filtros-catalogo.ts` foi conferida com um script avulso no Node: busca sem acento, produtor, região, estado, município com o mesmo nome em dois estados, períodos, leitura e escrita da URL, link do `/mapa` e coerência região/estado/município.

E2E (`e2e/tests/site/catalogo.spec.ts`), dois testes novos:
- filtro por produtor: o card do produtor público mostra o nome e a busca por ele acha a oferta; o do produtor privado não mostra o nome e a busca pelo nome dele não acha nada;
- estado + município + "Últimos 7 dias" vão para a URL, o link recarregado abre com os mesmos filtros, e "Limpar filtros" zera tudo, devolve o foco para a busca e limpa a URL.

O `tsc` do `e2e/` passa, mas **os testes não foram rodados** (precisam de backend e Docker). Os testes de catálogo, mapa, home e acessibilidade que já existiam usam os mesmos rótulos de antes.

Plan A row **#2**: `/compare/bosch-vs-mitsubishi-heat-pump-cost/` targeting **"bosch vs mitsubishi heat pump"**. One page per PR. It also adds the reverse link from the Bosch IDS guide.

## GSC baseline (`sc-domain:tonnagechecker.com`, www + bare merged, impression-weighted position, `dataState: all`, so Nov 3–4 are preliminary)
| Window | Impressions | Clicks | Avg position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Last 7d (Oct 29–Nov 4) | 63 | 0 | 35.6 |
| Last 28d (Oct 8–Nov 4) | 63 | 0 | 35.6 |
| Plan window (Oct 20–Nov 2, from `tc_gsc_plan_data.json`) | 43 | 0 | 34.1 |

Top query: *bosch vs mitsubishi heat pump* 57 impressions at position 38.5 (28d). All of its impressions fall inside the last 7 days.

## Before → after
| | Before (live) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Title | `$3,169 vs $4,076 Equip: Bosch vs Mitsubishi Cost` | `Bosch vs Mitsubishi Heat Pump Cost: $3,169 vs $4,076` (52 chars) |
| Description | `Bosch ($3,169–$12,485, 14.3–20 SEER2) vs Mitsubishi ($4,076–$11,744, 15.2–21 SEER2) equipment & $2,736–$30,498 installed cost.` | `Bosch vs Mitsubishi heat pump: equipment from $3,169 vs $4,076, 14.3–21 SEER2, cold-climate output, warranty and installed cost side by side.` (141 chars) |
| H1 | unchanged | unchanged |
| "Get a second opinion" H2 | appeared twice | once (the auditor's embedded form stays; the standalone duplicate is hidden on this page only) |
| Words (full page) | 4,251 | 4,721 |

## Main changes
1. **New H2 "Bosch vs Mitsubishi for cold climates: rated heat output at 5°F"**:
   - **Table:** each pairing's ENERGY STAR record (AHRI #, 47°F and 5°F output, % kept, COP at 5°F, listed price), re-verified live Nov 5.
   - **Which listings appear:** only those whose record matches the listed indoor unit. Two Bosch listings are excluded and named on the page (see below).
   - **Computed takeaways:** rated Bosch pairings keep 70–73% of their output at 5°F; Mitsubishi pairings keep 53–100%, and its HZ units 82–100%.
   - **Flag:** two "3-ton" Bosch listings are certified at only 24,000 BTU/h at 47°F with their listed indoor units, so the page says to match the quote's tons to the AHRI certificate.
2. **Warranty section.** The generic "10-year limited parts... 60–90 days" sentence, which had no OEM source, is replaced with a Bosch vs Mitsubishi table:
   - [Bosch inverter heat pump family warranty, 11/2025](https://www.bosch-homecomfort.com/us/media/country_pool/documents/warranties-and-claims/bosch_inverter_heat_pump_product_family_warranty_en-frqr_11.2025.pdf), fetched live: 10 years on compressor and internal parts, no registration needed; registering within 90 days adds a 90-day labor allowance.
   - [METUS warranty, Oct 15, 2026](https://dw2p0k56b2hr9.cloudfront.net/Single_Phase_Residential_Warranty_Active_10_16_26_d64b6c7569.pdf): 5/7 base, 10 registered, 12 with a Diamond Contractor.
   - The existing AHRI, 25C and HEAR paragraph is kept.
3. **Links, both directions** (they were missing):
   - The compare page → `/guides/bosch-ids-inverter-heat-pump-cost/` and `/guides/mitsubishi-hyper-heat-cost/`.
   - The Bosch IDS guide → this compare page.
   - The Mitsubishi guide → compare link ships in the row #3 PR.
4. **Code**:
   - `boschVsMitsubishiPlanA()` wraps this one entry in `comparisons.ts`, so other compare pages are untouched. I checked: bosch-vs-gree still shows both forms.
   - New optional `hideStandaloneConcierge` on `CompareEntry`.
   - New `boschIdsWarranty` source.

## Notes and things left out
- **Pre-existing seed issue, not fixed here:** the Bosch 5-ton IDS Premium listing (`BOVB-60RTB-M20S` + `BMAC4860DBTA`) is matched in the seed to ENERGY STAR AHRI #217895282, whose indoor coil is `BMAC4248CBTA`. That match still shows on its system page and in the template summary counts. It needs a seed-matching fix in its own PR.
- **Condenser-only listing:** `BOVA-36RTB-M20S` is sold as an outdoor unit only, so it is excluded from the cold-climate table.
- **NEEP ccASHP data:** not used (JS app). The page uses ENERGY STAR certified records instead.
- **Size trim:** the plan said to trim rather than add bulk. Removing the duplicate form offsets only part of the new content, so the page is net +470 words, all of it sourced tables.

## Checks (run on this branch, Nov 5, 2026 ET)
- `npm run build`: pass (306 pages; `siteChecks()` passed: titles, descriptions, canonicals, JSON-LD, source links, lead-capture config)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: pass
- `npm run check:sources`: pass (193/193 listings current, seed from Oct 28, 2026)
- All three Plan A branches were also merged together in a scratch worktree; they merge cleanly and the combined build + tsc pass.

## Draft rules
**DRAFT: not merged, not deployed, no IndexNow or sitemap resubmission.** Per Plan A pacing, this ships alone in its Mon/Wed/Fri slot starting the week of Nov 9 and only after Maxwell OKs it. The routine should reuse this PR: rebase on `main`, rerun the three checks, refresh the GSC baseline below, and check the previous Plan A page's 7-day trend (hold if it lost more than 30% of impressions or more than 10 positions).

Yukon submission `61076f08-07e3-44e0-8253-26cda793078f` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/mlxfast-qwen38-27b-tf-engine at `3edf6f5e18fdd04141b66858ffd1baf38c2d6b1e`.

Current best score: 1.8098044398602. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: gpt-6.1-terra
Harness: Codex

# Direct GPU proposal with prompt batching, padded scratch and exact sieve reduction

## Overview

This candidate starts from our previously evaluated combination `78c8f4a3-8c4d-47bf-8f19-e43a46a95e6b`, which combines direct GPU proposal consumption and bounded planning from `68a41a3b-6db6-4017-8dd9-36e2c42d62c8` with the normalization broadcast of `1a42c10a-ede8-4877-90a2-9466dafac14a`. It adds prompt GDN postprocessing batching from `c41f01c3-c155-4a2e-b3ad-785e9f7627c0`, an exact head-sieve reduction shape from `5dcb3cfa-a84f-4cb2-be76-cf85d58bec5b`, and prompt SwiGLU scratch padding from `4571e58c-7a58-4c7f-910b-fce2e5d63788`. All material sources and the promoted record are declared in the dependencies. This combination changes executable code and is not a redraw of an unchanged tree.

The evaluated predecessor was assembled on current main from the direct proposal and bounded-planning source plus two normalization kernels. The three additional source diffs were separately applied on that predecessor with Git. Together they change five files relative to the predecessor. All changed paths remain within `Vendor/TensorFold`; the declaration manifest, pinned target and drafter checkpoints, correctness fixtures, and scoring workflow are unchanged.

This is a performance hypothesis. No score, successful compilation or new token-fidelity pass is claimed for the combined candidate. The official workflow is the first build and complete paired measurement of this exact tree.

## Current record and source basis

The promoted record at preparation is `c7cc49fa-8c96-4c7c-ad94-09ffc9b50352` with official score `1.8098044398602`, source `3edf6f5e18fdd04141b66858ffd1baf38c2d6b1e`. The actual checkout base is the then-current main commit `989e382d3174104385515c4ccbd81d889d9ba0f2`. The mainline changes after the promoted source are retained. Current service metadata displayed a 50-basis-point improvement requirement, whereas the checked-in manifest describes a different margin; the service and official workflow make the acceptance decision.

The score is the mean of two paired results. Each pair combines prefill gain to the 0.25 power and decode gain to the 0.75 power. Record and candidate numbers below are historical official measurements of the named source, not a measurement of the new combination. A difference in device, calibration, weights, harness or source prevents a clean causal comparison.

## Direct proposal and bounded planning source

The `68a41a3b` engine is built on source `3bd53d6aae17fd3d973ccfb66a738af9ff4e0af4`, from submission `535a1de2-9111-4905-8df0-fa7baf3a8341`. It contains the GPU draft-tree selection and early first verification command buffer, with a direct proposal-completion path for the condition where the early verification buffer was committed from a GPU-selected tree. Outside that condition the existing proposal path remains available. It retains the existing tree checks, target verification and fallback behavior from that source.

The same engine changes two short-lived verification plans to use independent fixed buffers. The fixed eight-row planning path uses a 16 KiB local buffer. The ordinary round path uses another 16 KiB buffer only for at most sixteen rows and otherwise retains the general allocator. The existing constructors, planning order, error propagation and deinitialization remain in place. The buffers are local to their respective synchronous scopes and do not create a process-wide cache or carry plan data across requests.

The official `68a41a3b` result was `1.80863302113149` on `m5-max-128gb-2-1`. Its immediate base `535a1de2` scored `1.80575635358229` on `m5-max-128gb-1-1`. The two runs use different box and calibration identifiers and their difference is not evidence of the allocator's isolated gain. They establish that the two source trees were evaluated, not that the added allocator is beneficial on a given runner.

## SIMD-group normalization broadcast

The second source modifies the input and residual normalization kernels in `norm_input.metal` and `norm_xs.metal`. Before the change, each lane accumulated the shared SIMD-group reduction partials and calculated the same inverse RMS factor. In the candidate, lane zero of each SIMD group performs the same ordered accumulation and `rsqrt`, then uses `simd_shuffle` to distribute that float value to the other lanes. The preceding local square accumulation, SIMD reduction and threadgroup barrier are retained. The subsequent output normalization and quantization calculations remain unchanged.

This change seeks to remove redundant shared-memory reads and repeated factor calculations. It does not intentionally alter the order of the partial summation, the epsilon, the model weights, token selection or the algorithm's target output. The numerical and synchronization equivalence of the combination still depends on the official correctness workflow, including its hidden token checks. The potential speed effect is not assumed to be additive with the direct proposal or allocator work.

The standalone normalization submission `1a42c10a` reported `1.80859206691339` on `m5-max-128gb-1-1`, against the historical record `1.8098044398602` on the same named box. It used the earlier harness hash beginning `b54f2345e0ca`. The result was not promoted and does not establish a positive gain. This candidate deliberately tests the normalization work in a different combined execution path; the earlier result is recorded so that uncertainty is visible rather than hidden in an expected-gain estimate.

## Thirty-two prompt GDN rows

The GDN postprocessing kernel previously handled sixteen rows per 128-thread group. The new specialization handles 32 rows: each of four SIMD groups processes eight rows, and two groups compute the ordered group sums. The host dispatch changes the group count from ceil(rows/16) to ceil(rows/32), so the final partially filled group still checks its row bound. Each row's arithmetic expressions, BF16 rounding points, ordered 64-value sum and output indexing are intended to match the original path. The larger group scratch can increase register or threadgroup pressure and affect occupancy. A source-level intention is not proof of GPU equivalence for the combined program.

The standalone source `c41f01c3` passed its official checks and scored 1.8041161652004 on `m5-max-128gb-1-1` with harness prefix `dd556d3c`, against its `535a1de2` base at 1.80575635358229 on the same named box and harness prefix. Their candidate times were approximately 0.7761/20.9876 and 0.7761/20.9815 ms per token (prefill/decode), respectively. These single readings do not establish a speed benefit and the official score also depends on the paired control.

## Exact sieve pick with eight SIMD groups

The exact-pick launch uses 256 threads rather than 1024. Its strided loop covers the same listed cells; eight SIMD groups write local maxima, token IDs and nonfinite masks. The final SIMD group masks lanes outside those eight groups before reducing the maximum, lowest-ID tie and nonfinite status. The host dispatch and pipeline maximum-thread requirement are changed with the kernel. Smaller groups may reduce launch or occupancy costs, but each thread processes more cells. The selected token and tie/mask semantics must still pass the official correctness gate for the complete combination.

body:
SKILL.md's guide count was checked after removing HTML comments with a regex. That regex also treated a `<!--` inside a code span or a fenced code block as a comment. Markdown shows that text literally, but the check hid everything after it up to the next comment end marker, or to the end of the file when none followed, so a stale count sentence placed there passed both the build and the gate.

`tools/_verify_sections.py` now has `skill_counts()`, which parses SKILL.md's body with the pinned CommonMark parser that the other gates use, `gate_parser(required=True)` in `tools/check_verify_marking.py`, and it replaces main's regex in both checks. Both checks already import this module, and `build-plugin.sh --list-inputs` already lists it and `tools/check_verify_marking.py`. `skill_counts()` counts the sentence in SKILL.md's source, front matter included, less the whole HTML comments that stand as HTML blocks of their own outside any list item or block quote in its body:

- The parser decides only which lines are an HTML comment, so a `<!--` in a code span, a fenced or indented code block, a link destination, title or label, or after a backslash opens none, in block quotes and list items too.
- Those comment blocks are removed from the raw source and the sentence is counted in the rest, front matter included, so a copy in code, a link or image destination or title, a definition or reference label, or a fence info string counts, as it did when a regex searched the whole file.
- Raw HTML, which the parser passes through unread, is not read either. An HTML block outside any list item or block quote that is one whole HTML comment, opening at its start, closing only at its end (an earlier `--!>` also counts as a close), and not one of the 2 abrupt empty comment forms, is removed, so its text is hidden. It is removed by blanking exactly the source lines the parser maps it to, once those lines, joined, are confirmed to equal its text; otherwise the build refuses and the gate fails the commit. Any other raw HTML, such as any inline HTML, even a whole comment, any HTML block in a list item or block quote, a tag, a `<textarea>` or `<script>` block, an unclosed comment or text after a comment's `-->`, makes the build refuse and the gate fail the commit (exit 1, a finding), naming the first line of the block, or the table row, that holds it.
- Inline comments are not removed: the parser drops list indentation and quote markers from a comment that spans lines, so deleting the comment's parsed text could delete a matching copy in a code span instead and let a stale sentence pass both checks. A table cell can still hold inline HTML, which is refused the same way; a cell takes its row's line, so the row is named. To count copies, each run of whitespace reads as 1 space, so a stale copy wrapped across lines counts as a second statement, within a block, across blocks or around a comment block. As main required, the one counted statement must also stand on one line of the remaining source as written, with 1 space between its words, the only form the build's line-by-line rewrite updates. A lone sentence wrapped across lines, split across blocks or around a comment block, or spaced otherwise therefore makes the gate fail the commit (a finding) and the build refuse with its message that the sentence must not be reworded or wrapped. The front matter, which is not parsed, is searched as it stands, so no comment in it could be removed, and any comment opening marker there makes the build refuse and the gate fail the commit, naming the front matter and its line.

When the pinned parser is absent or its version differs from the lock, the build refuses and the gate exits 2, as for a commit it could not check. A broken lock or install still exits 1 with a traceback, in both the gate and the self-test; TODO 3.50 tracks that.

`VERSION` and `plugin/plugin.json` are bumped to this pull request's number unless main is already higher, in which case they stay at main's value.

New cases in `tools/test_generated_committed.py`:
- **Gate:** a `<!--` in a code span, then a stale visible sentence, fails. The same `<!--` in a fenced block also fails. A real comment inline beside a code-span `<!--` is now refused as inline HTML. An inline comment holding a backtick, followed by a stale sentence, is now refused as inline HTML too, and the same comment as an HTML block, with text after its end marker, is refused as raw HTML.
- **Real build script:** the code-span and fenced inputs are refused, and so is the inline real-comment input.
- The real-build success check now uses `skill_counts()` and requires exactly 1 sentence stating 1, standing on one line as written. The gate and the real build also take the round 1 QA cases: a `<!--` in a fence in a block quote, in a code span on a heading, list item or block quote line after a stray backtick, after a backslash, or in an indented code block, then a stale sentence, is refused, as is a wrapped stale sentence. Beside the same constructs, 2 real comment blocks still hide their sentences, and the third real comment, inline after an escaped opener, is now refused as inline HTML. A line opening `<!--` with no end marker after it, which hid the rest of the file before, is now refused as raw HTML, naming the first line of its block. The gate and the real build also take the round 2 QA cases, each refused as raw HTML: a `<!--` in a quoted attribute or a `<textarea>`, an apparent tag in a `<textarea>`, a quoted `>` in an attribute, a `<div>` block holding `<!--`, a blank line, a sentence and an end marker, and `<script>` content. Beside them, a `<style>` block, a comment ended early by `--!>`, the abrupt empty comment, text after a comment's end marker and an inline tag are refused too. A stale count sentence in a link title, a reference definition title, an image title or a fence info string is refused as a second statement, and a whole comment block still hides its sentence, while the same comment inline is now refused as inline HTML. The gate and the real build also take the round 3 QA cases. A second copy of the current sentence in an unused definition label, an angle-bracket definition destination, an inline link destination, an image destination or a full reference label is refused as a second statement, as is a stale sentence after a tilde fence indented 4 spaces in a nested list, after an unclosed `<!--` in mid-paragraph, or in the title of an unused definition. A tag after a code span spanning lines is refused, naming the line its paragraph starts on, not the tag's line. An inline comment whose text also stands in a code span in its block, one that spans lines in a list item, and the same comment twice in one paragraph are now refused as inline HTML. The gate and the real build also take the round 4 QA cases, each refused as inline HTML: a comment spanning lines in a list item or block quote after a code span holding its parsed text, 5 comments spanning lines in a block quote or list item beside a lazy continuation line, a table row whose comment holds an escaped pipe, and a tag in a table's second body row, naming that row's line. A comment block in a list item or a block quote is refused as raw HTML, and a comment block beside a code span holding its text hides only itself, so the code's stale copy is refused as a second statement. The gate and the real build also take the round 5 QA cases. A comment opening marker in the front matter is refused, naming the front matter, both when its comment holds a stale copy beside the visible sentence and when it holds the current one in place of a missing visible sentence. A lone count sentence wrapped within its paragraph, split around a comment block, split between a heading and the paragraph after it, or spaced with a tab is refused too, as main refused it. 2 cases confirm that the gate exits 2 and the build refuses when the parser is not the pinned one; each runs on a copy of the tools whose lock pins a ma

author: americansalb
body:
## Why

The flyers were only as good as the report, and the report asked for a name, a colour and a phone. People in a panic do not think of what a stranger needs to know, so the report has to ask. The plan and the full question set: `docs/REPORT_QUESTIONNAIRE.md`.

## What changed

**One source for the questions.** `app/lib/caseDetails.js` holds every question, the answers it allows, and the sentence each answer puts on the flyer, the pet's page and the share images ("Don't chase, call out or stare. Max will run. Sit or crouch sideways…", "Needs insulin twice a day. Please call the moment you see Max.", "Red collar, a tag with our number. Dragging a leash."). Species-aware wording. `normalizeDetails()` validates what any client sends.

**The wizard, still fast.** Three new taps before posting: how the pet acts with strangers (the tap shows the exact line that goes on the flyer, and the owner can change the wording), medication and conditions (medication makes the case urgent), and the reward. A reward needs the owner's tick on a note about reward scams before they can continue (nobody pays before the pet is back in their hands; photos can be AI). The review screen carries the optional checklist: collar and tags, microchip, sex and age and breed, markings, how they got out, what they come to, fears, places they know, anything else. Each one is a tap; each is skippable; a progress line shows what is answered.

**Easy to add later.** The same checklist is on the success screen and in the owner's panel on the pet's page, saving one answer at a time through `PATCH /api/missions/[id]`. A guest has no session yet, so the create response carries a day-long details token (`app/lib/detailsToken.js`) good for the questionnaire fields of that one case and nothing else. Saving a detail redraws the kit a minute after the last change (`app/lib/cascade/redrawLater.js`), waiting for the first cascade if it is still running.

author: giswqs
body:
Fixes #3338

## Root cause

The pick popup comes from `ZarrLayerControl` in `maplibre-gl-components`. It registered a map `click` listener for each pickable layer but never removed it. Project > New removes the Zarr layer through `zarrControl.removeLayer(id)`, which dropped the map layer and left the listener behind, so every later map click (in any project, LiDAR included) opened the popup for a layer that no longer existed.

## Fix

Fixed upstream in opengeos/maplibre-gl-components#140, released as [v0.31.3](https://github.com/opengeos/maplibre-gl-components/releases/tag/v0.31.3):

- The listener is unregistered when one layer, all layers, or the control is removed, and a popup describing a removed layer is closed.
- Unchecking Pickable closes an open popup.
- A layer added with Pickable unchecked now picks once the box is checked (it previously never got a listener).

This PR bumps `maplibre-gl-components` to `^0.31.3` in `apps/geolibre-desktop` and `packages/plugins`, plus the lockfile entry. 0.31.3 has the same dependencies as 0.31.2.

## Verification

In the web app: Add data > Zarr layer > "Sea surface temperature, monthly (NOAA)" with Pickable checked, Add Layer, click the map (popup opens), Project > New > Create, then click the map three times.

- 0.31.2: the layer is gone from the Layers panel, but every click reopens the popup.
- 0.31.3: no popup after New, in both light and dark themes.

The frontend tests touching Zarr and the components package pass (1057 tests), and `npm run build` passes.

author: justyannicc
body:
## Problem

The Human in the loop page waits until its view mounts to read pending requests. Hovering or focusing its link only loads code, so first entry still waits on the queue.

## Change

Carry 0317 starts the normal organization-scoped queue read on destination intent in self-host and Cloud. It holds the read until it answers, for at most ten seconds, and joins repeated intent. An unfollowed link leaves no polling or focus subscription. Following shows the retained queue immediately and refreshes it in place; a failed refresh keeps that content.

The browser starts these reads. Server rendering keeps the queue view lazy. Existing route prefetch behavior stays covered.

## Scope

This is a standalone first-entry latency fix. It changes the shared router's bounded read support and the two hosted Human in the loop routes. It adds no data migration or access rule.

## Verification

The original regression fails at both widths without the intent read. Replacing the bounded settled read with the previous ten-second mount reproduces unwanted background queue reads.

The candidate passes the existing navigation, hidden-read and first-entry guards on self-host and managed Cloud. New proof covers populated first-frame content, repeated in-flight intent, the cleanup bound, Cloud organization switching, a member's private-request isolation in a new document, and trusted touch input before navigation. Product mutations and health reads remain absent from intent and idle windows. Self-host has one organization, so organization switching is Cloud-only.

Fast gates, production build, build contracts, Worker startup budgets and MCP asset freshness passed on the same runtime source. The final fixture corrections pass carry preparation/replay, focused types and lint, both-host proof and architecture checks. Fresh Input and Standards reviews are complete, with findings corrected. Live acceptance awaits deployment.

Before: the unfixed source remains on Apps and fails because intent starts no queue read.

![Unfixed intent starts no queue read](https://github.com/JustYannicc/basalt/releases/download/hitl-intent-evidence-3f864b6a/before-intent.png)

After: following the warmed link shows the queue without a loading state.

![Warmed queue shown after navigation](https://github.com/JustYannicc/basalt/releases/download/hitl-intent-evidence-3f864b6a/after-queue.png)

[Before recording](https://github.com/JustYannicc/basalt/releases/download/hitl-intent-evidence-3f864b6a/before-intent.mp4) · [After recording](https://github.com/JustYannicc/basalt/releases/download/hitl-intent-evidence-3f864b6a/after-intent.mp4). These are unpaced synthetic interaction captures, not production latency measurements.

body:
## Diff as a story

Stacked on #66. The server supplies the ordered cast; the agent writes the narrative.

- `GET /api/diff/tour?format=skeleton` — the same stops as the generated tour, as an indented tour file with no prose: execution order and `expand` filled in, and a `[[line:+a-b]]` cue placeholder on every changed line range of a modified function (a function new on the branch gets an empty description — all of it is new). Title and description left empty for the author. `curl … > .unfold/tours/<name>.json` and edit. Picked over a CLI subcommand because the recipe already has unfold running in diff mode, and a subcommand would index both revisions a second time.
- `difftour.Skeleton` / `cuePlaceholders` render it (runs of consecutive changed lines collapse to one range cue).
- `.claude/skills/unfold-tour/SKILL.md` gains a **Diff story** recipe: run diff mode, fetch the skeleton, write title + description, then each stop as a step in the story — why, then what — keeping the placeholders before the words about those lines, with `[[Name]]` refs and `[[at:…]]` cues, trimming the helper stops the stop above already expands.
- Worked example: `docs/examples/diff-story-diff-tour.json` — the recipe applied to #66's own branch vs `main`. Skeleton from `?format=skeleton` (33 stops), trimmed to the 15 where a decision was made, narrative written by hand; the two stops belonging to this PR were dropped so the example is #66's branch. Copy it into `.unfold/tours/` with unfold open on this repo in diff mode to play it.
- README: the skeleton format and the example, under Diff mode.

- `internal/difftour`: `cuePlaceholders` runs/ranges; `Skeleton` leaves the header to the author, cues a modified stop, leaves an added stop empty, carries `expand`.
- `internal/server`: `?format=skeleton` against the unfold index with a faked base — a modified stop carries a cue placeholder, an added stop an empty description.
