author: couchpotato7572
body:
Fixes #21. Correct Rembrandts' hood articulation and intake collision profiles so clear trench-edge starts work and the shooter retracts safely during transit.

## Robot and resulting behavior

The two original `TR26-SH-4006` hood cheeks now move with the `4011` skin and `4021` brace about the measured flywheel axle. Preparation normalizes the exported extended hood into its retracted pose; extension restores the exported shape. The rendered turret reaches about 547 mm retracted and 593 mm extended, against the 565 mm arm clearance.

The inclined `TR26-IN-4019` side panels and sloped `4020` front panel previously used three broad rectangular proxies. Those proxies incorrectly assigned the raised section's height to the low front. Twenty-four conservative CAD-profile envelopes now preserve the actual changing panel height. Starts at alliance-relative X=4.57 m, Z=±3.5 m are admitted on both alliances, with the intake still retracted; the existing passive deployment then runs normally. The high section remains about 628 mm tall, and deeper obstructed starts at X=4.30 m remain rejected.

Rembrandts also opts into automatic trench protection: predict the offset bearing's swept envelope using point velocity, acceleration, hood radius and travel time; retract before the arm, keep the inclined intake extended and inhibit both new and queued fuel releases. The check runs before and after physics. Held Shoot resumes normal behavior outside the zone. Other robots retain their existing behavior.

## Sources and estimates

- All 14 uploaded CAD volumes were reassembled and SHA-256 verified as `6502ca903919ef90fab559e73bab930cd6335a362fc9585fb2a552beca893fc4`.
- [Team hood-retraction explanation](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-4481-team-rembrandts-2026-build-thread-open-alliance/507296/402) and [zone-priority explanation](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-4481-team-rembrandts-2026-build-thread-open-alliance/507296/423).
- Official code pinned to `e00d344b705b5e272229ba6ca5b6de26d93337af`: stops −75°/−49°, final travel time 0.15 s and hood diameter 300 mm. Final timing supersedes February's 0.08 s. File URLs/hashes are recorded in `sources.json`.
- Guarded `measure-intake-contacts.mjs` measures exactly three original panel solids, generating eight intervals per panel with 0.75 mm padding. Repeated generation is identical. The planar convex envelopes fill small cut-outs and conservatively approximate the profile; existing slide travel/rise remain fitted estimates.
- A [Worlds finals match video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tSeGDeeX4JE) was located via TBA, but playback was blocked. No match-video observation is claimed.

## Integration points and merge conflicts

Shared files: `src/robot/types.ts` and `validateDefinition.ts` add/validate optional `shooterGeometry.trenchSafety`; new `src/sim/TrenchSafety.ts` computes the envelope; `Shooter.ts` retracts/inhibits releases; `RobotSimulation.ts` prevents shooting compression from raising the intake near an arm. All other edits are Rembrandts-owned contacts, definition, preparation/measurement, source/runtime records, model, README and tests.

No registry, controls, camera, UI, common asset manifest, dependency, hosting, mass/capacity, drive tuning, starting-rule or shot-scatter changes. Field and robot dimensions are preserved.

Main `79dc5e9`, this head `be790bc` and open #40/#41/#42/#43/#44/#45/#46 heads pass all 36 pairwise merge checks. Forward/reverse integration yields the same tree. Future edits or rewritten histories require rechecking.

## Validation

- 104 focused cases across 13 files pass: Rembrandts mechanisms/assets/clearance, shared shooter and definitions, starting configuration, session starts and all-robot wall contacts.
- All four newly admitted starting placements fail against the original proxies. Corrected cases retain every original preload body, deploy without ejection and settle on supported wheels. Deeper invalid starts remain blocked.
- Every actual prepared polycarbonate vertex is enclosed by the new profiles, and the full raised height is retained.
- Trench tests cover all four arms, velocity prediction, retained intake extension, pause, stable bodies, shooting after leaving and a queued-release veto after aiming.
- Actual prepared-CAD tests check retracted clearance, restored extended height, measured pivots and rigid modules. Isolated Chromium renders the actual hood at 0.546745 m / 0.593405 m with no browser errors.
- Release integrity, TypeScript/Vite and production-payload checks pass. The collision-profile follow-up leaves the prepared model unchanged from the visually reviewed hood correction.
- Runtime: 3,653,292 bytes / 573,898 triangles / 71 primitives, within unchanged budgets; same 894 retained CAD bodies and five removed decorative fuel bodies. Raw CAD/volumes remain ignored; attribution and pending redistribution status are retained.
- The combined main + #40/#41/#42/#43/#44/#45/#46/#47 tree passes all 542 tests across 81 files and the complete release integrity/build/payload checks. This head's GitHub Release checks are green.

## Remaining limits

Only starts where the actual low front clears the arm are allowed. Placing the raised section directly below the arm remains a real clearance conflict. This preserves the supplied CAD, field clearance and retracted starting state. Muzzle/exit-angle calibration, slide travel/rise and conservative contact envelopes remain documented simulator estimates.

author: johnamcruz
body:
## Summary

The training loop's proposer is given "trend-blocker" findings built from the trend set's missed legs. Measured on two real replay runs, 47% of the decisions PPC labels "expected take, did none" (16 of 35 and 8 of 17) were the runner's late-entry or unfilled check, not the model passing: the model decided to enter and the order did not go. Those legs were filed as findings with no examples and an unowned "any skill may be edited", so the proposer would try to fix timing with skill text.

A leg lost **only** to the runner's own timing is now counted (`missedTally.timing`, said in the round's status and log lines) and is never a finding. "Only" is what the two review rounds on the earlier attempt taught:
- **Code and source:** the gate's `late-entry` or the executor's `unfilled` (one fixed meaning each, `trend-capture.js classifyCycle`); the same word from another source is not timing.
- **A late entry counts only as the runner computed it:** its cycle carries `movedR`. A gate refusal that merely lists `late-entry` first (`violations[0]`) may hide another check behind it, so it stays a finding.
- **The model's own earlier passes on the same leg are not timing:** the blocker is only the furthest stage a leg reached; if an earlier entry bar had a valid plan that ended in anything but a late or unfilled entry (a head pass, a veto), the leg stays a finding.
- No gate-check NAME is used anywhere (the dropped attempt excluded legs by name, e.g. `[skills-loaded]`, which cannot tell a harness fault from a model omission).

## Evidence

Tests first, red before the change (`tests/lib/train-trend-facts.test.js`): each timing source is counted and not a finding; a mixed leg set keeps only the real miss; a model pass hidden behind a late entry stays a finding; an earlier correct pass or an earlier late entry is still timing; a gate refusal without `movedR` stays a finding; every other blocker (executor block or abort, other gate refusals, phase-2 veto, unreadable verdict, floor refusal, head pass) is filed as before; the code alone is not enough, who set it counts. `tests/lib/train-trend.test.js` had a fixture shape production never produces (`unfilled` set by the gate); it is now the executor's, and that leg correctly drops out. 92 related tests pass locally.

Known and left alone: the base rate of valid plans on bars with no leg (`controlsOf`) still includes the timing legs' bars; the late-entry kinds `no-price` and `failed` (price-read faults) are also excluded as timing, which is right (no skill edit fixes them) though the docs say "late or unfilled".

## Regression (required)

- [ ] `npm run verify`: CI. Locally: 92 pass, 0 fail (train-trend-facts, train-trend, ecc-architecture, no-platform-specifics, no-tunable-literals, content); eslint and markdownlint clean. `tests/lib/train-loop.test.js` and `train-ppc.test.js` refuse to run while a replay loop is live on the author's machine; CI runs them.
- [ ] Goal regression: CI. Touches no entry, exit, sizing, gate or runner code: only what the proposer is shown.

## Adversarial review (required)

- [x] Opus round 1 (not ready): one major (a late or unfilled blocker hid the model's earlier passes on the same leg); minors: a gate refusal naming only its first check, the "timing" wording, a stale docs sentence, the status line not logging `timing`, a run name in a test comment, an unrealistic fixture. All fixed test-first, the two rules exactly as the reviewer proposed them.
- [x] Golden files, baseline, move goldens, PINS: none changed.

body:
## Why

The Supervisor's routine digest took about 700 seconds and roughly 950 charged REST core calls a run, so it was skipped whenever App core quota fell under 5,000 (3 of 7 checks on the evening of November 5). It must stay complete.

One measured run on the live queue showed where the cost went. The conditional cache did not help: the host cache is capped at 16 MB and held only 55 entries, and the radar's repository comment scan moved its `since` on every run. Every one of its 653 REST reads came back 200, with no 304s. That scan re-paged each repository's whole 30-day comment history, about 166 pages for launchplane and 146 for codex-skills. The readers also ran one after another, and the question reader fetched about 200 source discussions one at a time.

## What changed

- The radar's repository comment scan (issue and inline review comments) keeps a per-repository watermark beside the Supervisor ledger (`<ledger>-radar-scan.json`), with the external and wait-marker comments it found. Later runs read only comments updated since the watermark minus 10 minutes, and keep the rows still inside the window.
- The scan rereads the whole window whenever the watermark is missing, unreadable, written for other self, bot or automation identities, or no longer covers the window start.
- The watermark is the newest `updated_at` GitHub returned, not the local clock. Paging uses an updated-time cursor, so an edit during the scan cannot shift a comment past a page. When a full page shares one timestamp, paging falls back to page numbers, and the watermark stays before that tie so the next run rereads it. A failed lane keeps its previous watermark.
- Digest readers run concurrently. The radar still runs after the question reader, so it reuses the discussions that reader collected. Question sources are fetched in parallel, in order, with per-source errors kept.

Removed: offset paging of repository comment lanes, and the full 30-day comment re-read on every check.
Net lines: +271 (code +108, tests +159, docs +4). The growth is the watermark and its fallbacks; each fallback has a test.

## Measured (live queue, same inputs)

| | Before | After (warm watermark) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wall time | 700 s | 290 s |
| Charged REST core calls | 956 | 626 |
| Radar REST calls | 685 | 237 |
| Radar time | 280 s | 162 s |
| Questions time | 287 s | 129 s |

Global next is time-budgeted, so its count varies (about 260 to 380 a run). It is now the largest consumer and is tracked separately in the follow-up linked on #3567.

## Verification

- Full touched modules pass locally: `test_github_unanswered_comments.py` (191), `test_routine_check.py` (22), `test_question_record.py` (16), `test_message_routing.py` (32).
- New tests fail when coverage drops. Mutations that drop retained rows, revert to offset paging, save the local run time as the watermark, or advance past a tie each fail a test.
- Native PyCharm inspection on changed files: GREEN, 0 findings.
- New-comment gate: clean.
- Review by another provider (OpenAI via Codex), two rounds; disposition is in the review comment.

Closes #3567

author: plainprogrammer
body:
Implements [spec 037](docs/specs/037-filter-collection-by-location/spec.md) (0.2.2) per its [plan](docs/specs/037-filter-collection-by-location/plan.md). The collection's filter bar gets a **Location** select: All locations, No location, or one of the collector's locations. The grid, the table, paging, sorting and bulk mode all honour it, combined with the name search (AND).

![Walkthrough: filter the grid by Blue binder, then No location, switch to the table, Edit many, Select all, Remove, Undo](https://github.com/plainprogrammer/Collector/blob/96c3fbede5f9a216472e8c7658e29cd322875a3b/docs/specs/037-filter-collection-by-location/screenshots/walkthrough.gif?raw=true)

## What each phase did

- **Phase 1, models** (`ff995c1`)
  - `CollectionFilter::Place` turns `location` into its canonical form: `""`, `"none"`, or an id of at most 18 digits. Anything else counts as all. It is then applied as a plain `lots.location_id` predicate.
  - `CollectionFilter` reads the account's locations once (`places?`, the options, the chosen name) and checks the URL's value against them for display. Under a location filter the grid skips its place line.
  - `bulk_selections.location_filter` is a new string column, default `""`, `null: false`, reversible. `BulkSelection#context?`, `#restart!`, `#lots` and `#record!` use it, never re-resolved, so a removed or another account's location selects nothing (decision 7).
- **Phase 2, controllers and helpers** (`1c57170`)
  - The page, `collection_listing_path` (which leaves out all), the sort headers, Edit many and the bulk form all carry `location`.
  - Bulk submissions use the rendered `rendered_location` for their context, pagers, sorts, actions and Done. Only Filter applies the select's value, and it keeps the page only when neither filter changed.
  - `BulkSelected`'s return path carries the stored location; Undo needed no change.
- **Phase 3, views** (`2f4c2bd`)
  - The FilterSelect sits in the filter bar with a Filter button, shown only while the account has a location.
  - In bulk mode it joins the bulk form, and the existing default `go=filter` button becomes visible beside it; it is still the first submit, so Enter still applies the filters.
  - The view-switch and Edit-many forms and both pagers carry `location`.
  - The empty sentences name the place: "No cards in your collection are in “Blue binder”.", "…are without a location.", and the forms with a query.
- **Phase 4, measurement and documents** (`0690b63`)
  - A `:timing` request spec: 5,000 lots over 300 locations, plus two other accounts' 5,000 lots each. Every page is under 500 ms (largest: the unfiltered table at 163 ms; with a filter, 21–106 ms), so the reserve `[account_id, location_id]` index is not added.
  - Updated: `verification.md`, the collection-and-lots area doc, the roadmap, the specs index and CLAUDE.md.
- **Review follow-ups** (`afe0ce8`): tests for findings 1–3 (below).
- **Wrap-up**
  - Screenshots and review record (`96c3fbe`).
  - Session learnings (`46f7ae5`): screenshot memory, one lesson.
  - Distillation (`1acece1`, `5b47f03`, `8628b13`): the index row is Frozen by collection and lots, plan retirement owed.

## Rulings and deviations (each also in its commit body)

- **No per-phase subagents.** I implemented each phase myself, test first, because the Orca brief forbids helper agents other than the review.
- **Empty sentence as a partial.** `collections/_no_match` replaces the plan's `no_match_message` helper. A helper's String is escaped whole, which turned spec 004's literal quotes into `"` and broke three existing body assertions. The partial keeps them raw without `html_safe`.
- **Migration rollback.** The `down` uses SQLite's native `ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN`, so the table isn't copied and its marks aren't cascaded.
- **No CSS.** FilterSelect's existing rules suffice; the 390px system spec checks both modes.
- **AC-5.8 refusal shows All locations.** The removed location no longer resolves (decision 7).
- **System spec written after the views.** The request markup specs were the red step for Phase 3.
- **Measurement as a timing spec.** It runs with `SCANNER_TIMING=1` and never gates.
- **Commit trailers.** `ff995c1` and `1c57170` say `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5` by mistake. The work ran on Opus 5.5; later commits say so, and the pushed commits were not rewritten.

## Implementation review: SPEC-ALIGNED

An independent read-only `sdd-review` Mode B on Opus found nothing blocking or major. It reported five minor findings:

1. A selection's ticks shown under a location had no direct test. **Fixed** (`selection_state_spec`).
2. The confirm page's Cancel/Back links, and the confirm page for a removed location, weren't asserted. **Fixed**.
3. The filtered table's pager count was covered only indirectly. **Fixed**.
4. `verification.md` sections were missing. **Fixed**.
5. A local `Gemfile.lock` platform change. **Kept out** of every commit.

The review also traced tenancy, the fail-closed paths and every caller; details are in [`verification.md`](docs/specs/037-filter-collection-by-location/verification.md).

## Tests

- **New:** `place_spec` (4), `collection_location_filter_spec` requests (21), `collection_location_select_spec` markup (14), system spec (6).
- **Extended:** grid (+8), table (+3), bulk selection (+5), bulk removal (+1), selection state (+1).
- **Not in the suite:** one timing example, excluded unless `SCANNER_TIMING=1`.
- **Suite:** 2,483 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending. Local `bin/ci` is green, also in the pre-push hook on `8628b13`.
- **Flake:** one earlier pre-push run failed on the known cross-worktree tmpdir race in `Upgrade::Harness` (#178), unrelated to this change. It passed on re-run.

## Screenshots

Taken with headless Firefox against a dev database seeded with placeholder printings (no card art): one collector, three locations, 14 lots.

| ![Grid under Blue binder, light](https://github.com/plainprogrammer/Collector/blob/96c3fbede5f9a216472e8c7658e29cd322875a3b/docs/specs/037-filter-collection-by-location/screenshots/desktop-grid-blue-binder-light.jpg?raw=true) | ![Grid under Blue binder, dark](https://github.com/plainprogrammer/Collector/blob/96c3fbede5f9a216472e8c7658e29cd322875a3b/docs/specs/037-filter-collection-by-location/screenshots/desktop-grid-blue-binder-dark.jpg?raw=true) |

body:
## Why
Across many repos and parallel sessions, work gets left uncommitted, unpushed, unmerged or waiting on a yes. A daily nudge names the one move that frees the most work, and the loose ends worth closing, before they are lost.

## What
- `skills/capture-lesson/scripts/loose-ends.py`: stdlib scanner. Git repos under `~` (uncommitted files, unpushed commits, no remote, merged clean worktrees), open PRs via `gh`, open markers in project memory, `PROGRESS.md`, the lessons inbox, the watch's proposals, an optional session-tidy log. First-seen dates in `~/.claude/nudges/state.json`; `--no-state` is read only. Finds the config folder through `lessonlib.CONFIG`, like its siblings.
- `skills/capture-lesson/daily-nudge.md`: the routine prompt, shaped like `weekly-watch.md`. Read only; five groups (one-touch, at risk, momentum, stale, can go); one pick with a three-step why; an 8-row table; one push line.
- One line each in README (install notes, plus `nudges/` under what it writes), AGENTS.md (install, file map) and `coding-skills.md`.
- `tests/checks.sh`: the `watch` check also runs `loose-ends.py --test` and a read-only scan, so the count stays at six and `checks.yml` is unchanged.

## Checked
- `python3 loose-ends.py --test`: ok. `--no-state` scans write nothing (an empty temp HOME stays empty).
- `sh tests/checks.sh`: all six ok locally (python, audit, install, watch, check-repair, mermaid).
- Diff grepped for personal names, project names and home paths: no hits.

Lane: open (a new script, a prompt, wording, a test). No hooks, `install.sh`, workflows or `index.html` touched.

body:
Implements F06; closes #103. The existing native reactive architecture now has opt-in bounded profiling, reproducible warm workload evidence, and two measured reconciliation improvements: O(n log n) LIS discovery and native/script metadata reuse within one preflight tree. User syntax, compiler/editor, native lifetime/ownership and minimum-move commitment stay intact.

The baseline was published before optimization. Same official binaries and source-authored workloads (8/64/128 rows, two warmups/seven samples) passed 248 invariant assertions before and after on Linux 4.0.4 and 4.7. For 128-row no-op, order comparisons fell 8,794→694 and metadata collection 144 visits→6 types, with 144 validations retained. Instrumented median mutation/drain time changed 101→15 ms on 4.0.4 and 84→11 ms on 4.7. Large 4.0.4 reverse remains slow from native child-order/layout work; full tables report small regressions/noise too. No speed threshold or release-throughput guarantee.

[Report, exact boundaries, environment, commands and remaining roadmap](docs/F06_PROFILING.md); [full 4.0.4 comparison](docs/evidence/F06_4_0_4.md), [4.7](docs/evidence/F06_4_7.md). Raw samples/provenance/logs and failures/repairs are linked in #103. Profiling is disabled by default; no per-frame loop, helper Node, model metadata, hooks or new render pipeline.

Validation:
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check` (typecheck + all six policy/evidence/UID/map checks), `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Focused baselines: [4.0.4](https://github.com/papercraftgames/Estragon/actions/runs/42165060806), [4.7](https://github.com/papercraftgames/Estragon/actions/runs/42165232952). Focused after: [4.0.4](https://github.com/papercraftgames/Estragon/actions/runs/42165474231), [4.7](https://github.com/papercraftgames/Estragon/actions/runs/42165380928). All build/import/runtime and logical checks PASS.
- [Final strict CI 42166097420](https://github.com/papercraftgames/Estragon/actions/runs/42166097420): tooling and both approved Linux engine jobs PASS, **66/66 observed addon stages each**, retaining all 63 prior stages plus profiling build/import/runtime. Profiling **249 assertions, zero failures** per engine, including the exact twelve-WeakRef object delta. Existing compiler/editor/metadata/UID/cold/source-only/pack/native UI/input/2D/3D regressions PASS; unexpected errors empty.
- Combined downloaded-artifact `tools/assert-release.ts` audit PASS: exact clean source, approved engines, hashes/logs/provenance verified. Tested merge `f72649fb` is content-identical to head `6d892d4`. Inspected final Counter/2D/3D/conditional/inventory/toggle captures on both engines, no visible regression.
- [Completed acceptance, exact commands/source/engine/artifact hashes and durable handoff](https://github.com/papercraftgames/Estragon/issues/103#issuecomment-6677551835). Initial strict run exposed a missing profiler Resource in the narrow native-runtime test sandbox; dependency/provenance repaired, superseded run canceled, final run passes without removing any stage.

Scope is the final reactive-architecture profiling milestone, not general UI-framework completion. Layout/padding/margins/position (#55/#88), richer inputs/IME/focus/themes/accessibility, editor UX (#6) and broader release readiness (#51) remain separately scoped. Only official Linux 4.0.4/pinned 4.7.0 tested; manual interactive Godot 4.7 smoke NOT RUN, physical F5/F6 not required. Owner review/merge only; do not auto-merge.

body:
## 변경
- 새 다운로드 작업은 먼저 저장 폴더(baseDir) 하위 폴더의 `post.json`을 읽어 링크의 게시물 코드와 같은 첫 게시물을 찾는다 (`findSavedArchive`).
- 미디어 파일이 모두 남아 있으면 Threads 페이지를 열지도, 미디어를 받지도 않고 그 폴더로 바로 완료(`skipped: true`).
- 파일이 하나라도 빠졌거나, 미디어 없이 저장했거나, 단축 공유 링크(`/share/`)처럼 코드를 바로 알 수 없으면 예전처럼 받는다.
- **다시 받기**(retry)는 항상 새로 받는다 → 건너뛴 게시물도 덮어쓸 수 있다.
- UI: 알림 창·다운로드 결과 카드에 "이미 저장된 게시물이에요" + 다시 받기 버튼, 내역에 "이미 저장됨" 표시, 여러 건 요약에 건너뛴 건수.

## 검증
- `npm test` 51개 통과 (새 테스트 4개: 찾기, 파일 누락, 미디어 없이 저장, 폴더 없음·단축 링크)
- core·desktop 타입 검사 통과
- 빌드한 엔진으로 실제 확인: 저장된 게시물 작업이 173ms에 `done/skipped`로 끝나고 브라우저 프로필이 생기지 않음. 같은 작업을 다시 받기하면 `Threads 페이지를 여는 중…`으로 실제 추출 경로를 탐.
- 데스크톱 앱 화면(Tauri)에서는 직접 눌러 보지 않음.

author: 0xb1ob
body:
## Scope of this PR

Before this PR, every native Claude review recorded `usage: "unavailable"`, 0 tokens and $0. This PR measures such runs, or estimates them when no result arrives. Changed: `src/drivers/claude-usage.ts`, `src/drivers/claude-worker.ts`, `src/drivers/claude.ts` (`nativeSpawnOptions`), docs/native-drivers.md, a changelog.d fragment, a new unit file `tests/claude-usage.test.ts` (with its migration-ledger row and test-timings entry), and the N4k cases in `tests/e2e/native-worker.test.ts`. Unchanged: `src/worker-process.ts` (pinned), `src/worker-manager.ts` (still 793 lines), data/native.json, data/routing.json, the lockdown, the reviewer read guard, report_verdict parity, the review deadline and verdict handling. No file passes 800 lines and no pin is raised.

## What stops the reviewer after its verdict

`awaitVerdict` (src/gate.ts) returns as soon as `verdict.json` exists. diff-review's `finish` then calls `WorkerManager.shutdown(managedKey)` (src/diff-review.ts:805; gate.ts:1013 and quality.ts:485 do the same). That runs `WorkerProcess.shutdown()`: stdin end, then the 5 s `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS`, then SIGTERM. In the worker, stdin close starts `stop()`, which waited 4 s (`NATIVE_RESULT_GRACE_MS`) for the in-flight `result` and then aborted. The parent's SIGTERM is a second stop and aborts at once. The query does not end on its own. An opus closing turn takes longer than 4 s, so the result never arrived and usage was never read.

## Change

- **Longer grace for reported runs.** The worker sets `accepted` when it relays a non-error `tool_result` for `report_result` or `report_verdict`. A stop then waits `NATIVE_REPORTED_GRACE_MS` (45 s) for the result. Unreported runs keep the 4 s wait, and a second stop still aborts at once. The verdict still counts as soon as it is filed, because nothing on the parent's verdict path changed.
- **Parent grace aligned.** `nativeSpawnOptions` now returns `shutdownGraceMs: NATIVE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS` (57 s: the 45 s wait plus claude's exit after the abort). The parent therefore never SIGTERMs into the wait. This needed no change to worker-manager.ts, because the existing spread of `nativeSpawnOptions` passes the option through. An unreported native worker still exits by itself after its 4 s wait.
- **Estimate fallback.** When a run ends without a `result`, the worker sums the usage on the streamed SDK assistant messages, counting each message id once and keeping each counter's largest value, because the CLI repeats a message once per content block. It records the sum as `usage_status: "estimated"` (`native_run` `usage: "estimated"`) in the same `message_end` shape, so status.json, the fleet record and the grant's spend all see it.
- **Cost of an estimate.** picp has no per-model cost table: the only cost source in picp is the SDK result's `costUSD`/`total_cost_usd`. An estimate is therefore recorded with cost 0 and a `cost_unknown: true` flag on both `native_run` and `message_end`.
- **No double counting on resume.** The session baseline advances by the estimated tokens per model and keeps its cost unchanged. A later resume's restored cumulative totals therefore do not count those tokens again. If the restored totals turn out to lack them, the growth goes negative and reads `unbaselined`, which undercounts and never counts twice.

## Scenarios

```gherkin
Feature: native usage when a run is stopped before its result

  Scenario: a reviewer-style stop after an accepted report, result within the longer grace
    Given a native job that has filed an accepted report
    And its closing model answer is held for 15 s, past the 4 s unreported grace
    When the parent tears it down
    Then native_run records result_subtype "success", usage "measured", usage_status "complete"
    And run status carries a cost above 0

  Scenario: a reported run whose result never comes
    Given a native job that has filed an accepted report
    And its closing model answer never arrives
    When the parent tears it down
    Then teardown finishes within NATIVE_REPORTED_GRACE_MS + 3 s
    And native_run records usage "estimated", usage_status "estimated", cost_unknown true
    And run status has tokens above 0 at cost 0, not marked unavailable

  Scenario: an unreported stop mid-turn
    Given a native job that has written its artifact but not reported
    And its next model answer never arrives
    When the parent force-tears it down with an operator quote
    Then teardown finishes within NATIVE_RESULT_GRACE_MS + 3 s, the old bound
    And native_run records report false and usage_status "estimated"

  Scenario: an estimate is never counted again after a resume (unit)
    Given streamed assistant messages, one id repeated with growing output
    When the run is estimated and the session later resumes with cumulative totals
    Then the estimate counts each id once and is marked estimated with cost_unknown
    And the resumed run counts only its own growth, 240 tokens rather than 455
```

## Tests

- Unit: `tests/claude-usage.test.ts` covers `nativeRunUsage`, the estimate's per-id dedupe and estimated marking, and resume without recount (with a stale-baseline control). It is a unit file because CI has no `claude` binary and skips the native e2e cases, so this accounting would otherwise go unchecked in CI. It has an `incoming` row in docs/testing-migration.md and an entry in scripts/test-timings.json.

body:
## What this adds

**Alarms** (main spec 5.5):
- **Definitions** on points: high or low limit (with deadband), state (Bool or Str), or stale data, each with a level (Info, Warning, Critical), a delay and an optional message. They are part of the setup and config file, and are checked like everything else.
- **Device offline alarms** only where an admin adds one (your decision).
- **Equipment templates** carry alarm defaults per role. A changed alarm on a point is an override, and roll-outs keep it. The built-in templates now raise a Warning (after 30 s) on equipment alarm inputs and an Info on filter signs.
- **Engine:** checks once a second. Limit and state alarms only react to Good values, so a dead device raises its offline alarm instead of a flood. An alarm stays listed until it is both **acknowledged** and back to normal. Comments can be added at any time, and the history is kept for a year.
- **Live:** alarm changes are pushed over the existing live connection.

**Delivery** (main spec 5.5.1):
- **Channels:** SMTP email, ClickSend SMS and ntfy push (the server is a site setting, default ntfy.sh). Defaults per level: Info screen only; Warning email and ntfy; Critical everything.
- **Recipients** tick the levels they receive. **Quiet hours** hold Warnings only and send one summary afterwards; Critical is never held.
- **Reliability:** failed sends are retried for up to a day, there are test buttons per person and channel, and a delivery log.
- **Secrets** are only ever environment variables named in the settings.

**Screens:**
- An Alarms button in the header showing the count and the worst level's shape.
- The Alarms page: active alarms (acknowledge with comment), history, and notifications sent.
- Setup → Alarm definitions and Setup → Alarm delivery.
- Alarm defaults in the template editor, an alarm count in the commissioning checklist, and active alarms on the HMI overview (view only).

## Tests

- Backend: 208 passed, 1 skipped. Delivery is tested end to end against fake SMTP, ClickSend and ntfy servers.
- Browser: new `npm run test:alarms` (12 checks, with a stand-in ntfy server). The setup, auth, smoke and HMI tests still pass.
- **Not tested with real accounts:** a real email, SMS and ntfy push need your SMTP login, ClickSend key and a phone with the ntfy app (bench step). TimescaleDB is still untested here.

## Assumptions to confirm

- If an alarm comes back before it is acknowledged, nobody is notified a second time.
- Return-to-normal is not notified, only shown.
- Recipient details are stored with the site in the database, not in the setup file.

Closes #160
Part of #157 (one criterion is not verified, see below)

## What changes

- **No toon material in `?look=pbr`.** Procedural cars, crowd NPCs, street sign blades, landmark sign boards and the landmark far LOD now use the look material (metal/rough under pbr). `window.__atl.materials` lists the material types and any toon material left. - **New pure module `src/render/pbr-palette.js`** (Vitest, 44 tests): albedo ceiling 0.6 linear, roughness/metalness per material class, palette + accent + grade tint + fog tint per district, grade by time of day, height fog, env light by sky luma, bloom threshold by daylight, bold far-window colors, material audit.
- **New `src/render/pbr-look.js`** sets the light each frame: grade (time of day × district at the camera, blended over 120 m), fog tint, skater rim, pbr sun (weather sun × 1.4), bloom threshold, and an env map baked again when the sky colors move. `?pbrgrade=0` and `?heightfog=0` turn parts off.
- **Lighting fixes from the art direction findings:**
  - The env map was baked once from the noon sky, so dusk and night were lit by a noon sky. That caused the blue-gray dusk and night. Now the map follows the sky.
  - The weather sun was too weak for pbr, so no day frame had a highlight.
  - The bloom threshold is high in the day, so no sunlit surface glows.
- **Grade pass:** contrast on the luma around 0.18, saturation, split tone, black lift, district tint.
- **Height fog** (pbr only): thinner high up, light ground haze, full at the far plane at every height.
- **Far windows:**
  - Under 34 px per window cell, a window becomes one bold color (blues, teal, one warm pane in five).
  - Under 16 px, the interior room is not computed at all.
  - Fine facade detail fades from 48 to 20 px per cell.
- **Ground:** mid-green grass (was mint-gray) with roughness 0.92. Asphalt is about 0.09 linear, with no lilac cast.
- **Skater:** rim light from the horizon color (no ink pass), and a roughness floor so skin does not look like plastic.
- **Docs:** `docs/style-sheet-pbr.md` (palette hex, roughness/metalness per class, three screenshots, light table). Decision entry in `docs/decisions.md` (put mid-file to avoid end-of-file conflicts).

- **Tests:** `npm run build` passes. `npm test` has 1 failure: `styles.test.js` "district mix". It fails the same way on `epic/city-look` adf3577. Some heavy tests time out at 5 s while a headless browser runs, and they pass with a longer timeout.

author: lanjak
body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

The ACP bridge reads only Grok's `_meta` context figure from a `session/prompt` result. It drops the result's `usage` object, so an ACP thread never records `thread/tokenUsage/updated`, even when the agent sends token counts (#6968). The `usage` delta and its assembler path already exist for other providers. Only the ACP bridge did not use them.

Report: https://get-bb.github.io/reports/issues/6968.html

## What changed

- `packages/provider-bridge-acp/src/prompt-usage.ts` (new): parses `usage` from a prompt result and maps it to `ThreadEventTokenUsageBreakdown` as the issue proposes. `bridge.ts` keeps a running `total` per session and sends the existing `usage` delta after `session/prompt` resolves, for a turn and for `/compact`. `modelContextWindow` comes from the last `usage_update.size`, else `null`. A result without `usage` sends nothing, as before.

The report left two questions open. Real agents answer both:

| Agent | Per turn | Covers all calls in a turn | `inputTokens` and cache |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 2.2.4 | yes | yes for its own session: equals the sum of its per-call database rows. Subagent sessions are not included | beside |
| claude-agent-acp 0.99.1 | yes | not separately checked | beside, with cache writes |
| rai-agent, local build that sends `usage` | yes | yes: equals its cost ledger | inside |
| codex-acp 2.5.0 (one turn, no cache) | not checked | not checked | no cache reported |

- Counters: the SDK 1.7.0 text conflicts ("for this turn" and "across all turns"). The bridge treats `usage` as per turn. I did not add a mode for session totals because no agent I could run sends them.
- Cache convention: differs between agents, so `totalTokens` decides it. When the total shows that `inputTokens` includes cache, the bridge subtracts cache read and cache write tokens, clamped at 0. This differs from the per-dialect flag in the issue.
- Reasoning: differs between agents too. codex-acp counts `thoughtTokens` inside `outputTokens` (`10773 + 54 = 10827`, 40 thought). OpenCode counts them separately (`8806 + 256 + 57 + 43 = 9162`). bb reports reasoning as part of output, so when `totalTokens` shows they are separate, the bridge adds them to `outputTokens`: 100 for that OpenCode turn, with `reasoningOutputTokens` 43.

The running `total` is in bridge memory and starts again when the runtime restarts, as in the Claude Code and Pi bridges. `promptCacheTtlMs` stays unset, so the compaction offer does not change. The context ring reads `contextWindowUsage` only and does not change.

No wire change: the `usage` delta and `thread/tokenUsage/updated` are unchanged, and `HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays the same. No new dependency, schema, migration, stored-data change, public API, CLI or documentation change.

Changed text lines against `main` (`5538a27bccb4c6de3191dc99f36975ec1cbaa4d5`): **391 total = 391 additions + 0 deletions**, across **5 files**.

## How you verified

All runs use Node.js 22.19.0 and pnpm 9.15.0.

Regression:

- Before the production fix (`bridge.ts` from `main`, new tests kept), the two-turn regression fails with `AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 2 but got +0`. The no-usage control passes. The result is the same in two clean checkouts with separate dependency installs.
- After the fix, on `5538a27bc`: `pnpm exec turbo run test typecheck lint --filter=@bb/provider-bridge-acp` passes: **26 test files, 583 passed, 4 skipped**, 0 lint warnings. `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck lint test --continue`, on `a0f291b80` and on this change rebased on it: 10 tests fail on both, and this change touches none of those packages. One other test failed on each side: a timeout in `install-machine-script.test.ts` with this change, and `CommandPalette.test.tsx` on `main`. Each passes in 3 of 3 isolated runs on both checkouts.

End to end, with the packaged app (`packages/bb-app`) built from this branch before the reasoning commit, an isolated data directory, and real agents:

- OpenCode 2.2.4 and rai-agent: `thread/tokenUsage/updated` equals the agent's own records for simple turns and multi-tool turns.
- claude-agent-acp 0.99.1: Burn 0.9.3 from its repository shows the sum of the turns' token counts, over 4 turns that include a stop and a resume.
- Burn's panel on that thread, in headless Chrome: 4 calls, 84% cache hit and a per-call chart. Cost stays "Unsplit" because the agent reports one total and Burn has no prices for custom agents.
- `bb thread stop` during a turn: usage so far is recorded, inside the interrupted turn. The next turn counts in full.
- A steer during a turn: two prompt results in one turn add up, equal to OpenCode's database.
- `kill -9` on the agent during a turn: the turn fails with no usage event, and the next turn records normally.
- `bb thread compact` on OpenCode: completes with no error. OpenCode sends no `usage` for it, so the 12,604 input tokens of that compaction are not recorded.

Not verified:

- A live Copilot session. No Copilot access was available for testing. The Copilot values in the tests come from the probe in #6968.
- Non-zero `thoughtTokens` through a bb thread. The real results from OpenCode 2.2.4 and codex-acp 2.5.0 are unit test fixtures. The bridge test for a real prompt result has no thought tokens.

Known limits:

- OpenCode's `usage` covers the parent session only. In one real turn it reported 9,228 input while a subagent session used 15,755 more, so these events undercount OpenCode subagents.
- OpenCode sends no `usage` for `/compact`.
- A turn whose agent dies before it answers records no usage.

Fixes #6968

author: qichu-yun
body:
## Motivation

With `ATOM_FP8_BLOCKSCALE_USE_E8M0_SCALE=1`, the KDA output norm (`rmsnorm_gated`) fuses only a per-token quant. For an E8M0 per_1x128 `o_proj` it writes bf16 and `o_proj` runs a separate `per_1x128_e8m0_quant`, once per KDA layer (69 in Kimi-K3). In TP8 decode (12 heads, 115 rows at concurrency 32) the two kernels take 4.05 us; fused, 1.70 us.

## Technical Details

Source +198/-4 (the Gluon kernel file is 149 of it), tests +56. Stacked on #2994.

- `rmsnorm_gated_gluon.py` (gfx1250): one wave per (token, head) row, which is one 128-wide quant group. It keeps the num_warps=4 Triton kernel's variance reduction order and its single bf16 rounding of the gated product, so the FP8 output and E8M0 scale are byte-identical to `rmsnorm_gated` + `per_1x128_e8m0_quant`. Programs are remapped so each XCD writes a contiguous run of rows of the column-major scale.
- `rmsnorm_gated(..., e8m0_scale=True)`: decode on gfx1250 runs that kernel; prefill (the multirow kernel) and other archs run `rmsnorm_gated` + `per_1x128_e8m0_quant`.
- Kimi-K3: the KDA o_norm fuses for an E8M0 `o_proj` when `head_dim == 128`.

An E8M0 epilogue on the existing four-wave Triton row kernel was slower than the separate quant from T = 1024 (11.7 vs 8.3 us), hence the separate kernel.

Behavior changes only for an E8M0 per_1x128 `o_proj` on KDA layers.

## Test Plan

`tests/model_ops/test_kimi_k3_onorm_e8m0_quant.py` (GPU): FP8 and E8M0 bytes against `rmsnorm_gated` + `per_1x128_e8m0_quant`, T = 1..16384, decode and prefill, both scale layouts, an all-zero head and a 2^30-scaled head, strided gate. Plus `test_kimi_k3_activations.py`, `test_kimi_k3_norm_batch_invariance.py`, `test_fused_rmsnorm_mxfp8.py`, `test_kimi_k3_out_gate_e8m0_quant.py`, `test_kimi_k3_situ_e8m0_quant.py`, `test_e8m0_online_blockscale.py`, `test_mla_fused_qkv_quant.py`, and the Kimi-K3 mono, plugin-config and prefill-token-graph tests.

## Test Result

MI455X (gfx1250), one GPU, `rocm/fw-bringup:gfx1250-atom-k3-20261105` (ATOM `7bc9c02d`, which carries #2994, #2995, #2996 and #2814) with this PR and the attn-res PR: all passed except 8 that fail the same way without them (the image has no `tests.aiter_stub`).

Kernel time, CUDA-graph replay, median of 7 rounds (a second run within 0.2 us), us per call:

| T | rmsnorm_gated + per_1x128_e8m0_quant | fused |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | 3.44 | 1.63 |
| 115 | 4.05 | 1.70 |
| 320 | 4.87 | 2.12 |
| 1024 | 8.01 | 5.87 |
| 8065 | 35.60 | 17.67 |

End to end, Kimi-K3 TP8 + DCP8 on two MI455X trays (`rocm/fw-bringup:gfx1250-atom-k3-20261105`, the repro kit's c32 settings: agentx, MoE TP8, DSpark 4, max-num-seqs 64; plus `ATOM_DCP_PREFILL_KV_AG_OVERLAP=1`), the image's ATOM against the image's ATOM + this PR and #3054:

| | image | + #3053 + #3054 |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot strict-match, full set | 0.9704, 0.9659 (two runs) | 0.9644 |
| `bench.sh` 8192/1024 c32, output tok/s | 1626.22 | 1666.86 |
| median TPOT / TTFT (ms) | 16.18 / 369.37 | 16.30 / 367.47 |

The server runs the fused kernels: with the PRs it compiles `_rmsnorm_gated_e8m0_kernel` and the E8M0 variants of `_attn_res_tdm_kernel` on both trays, without them neither. GSM8K stays within run-to-run noise: the two image runs give the same response text on 315 of 1319 questions, the PRs and either image run on 328 and 329. The throughput numbers are single runs.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

## Summary

Define how a real native menu action reaches the correct application callback and action-time window. Preserve role-owned actions, menu generation, checkbox and radio state, custom accelerators, default menu behavior, and the actual Zettlr Cmd+S effect.

Adds one future implementation document for #556: 12 acceptance criteria and 4 ordered tasks. Status: draft. Merge intent: **do-not-merge**. The local implementer must first close the spec's entry gates.

## Spec refs

- `docs/specs/gh556-non-role-menu-click.md`, current implementation pin `0eb3ce203187f35c5276a4237189c906a5220d5a`.
- Section 2 records the governing sources and distinct owners. Follow the stricter proposed #1321/#1325 rule at `95c38ed325c96867f360dd78487f85bbafa5db91`; no exemption or baseline change.

## Review gates

- Public API: callback identity, focus, event fields, mutable state, default menu and sync getter semantics.
- Permission model: verified `app.system` `menu` at the existing owner. Menu actions confer no additional resource authority.
- Wire protocol: Host-origin receive class, bounded fields, install barriers and retirement require exact reviewer approval.
- Unsafe: none in this document. Future AppKit operations require exact-operation and lifetime review.
- Dependency addition: none proposed. Any new binding feature needs independent approval.

## Tests

- Cloud supplemental structure audit: `python3 keld-future-specs/rule/audit_specs.py wave2/docs/specs/gh556-non-role-menu-click.md`. Result: **0 errors, 0 warnings**. 409 lines, 35823 bytes, maximum 257 characters per line.

- Pinned source and citation checks are documented in the spec and tracker handoff. The exact proposed Rust checker and local `just ci` were not run; the cloud authoring workspace has no Rust toolchain. Hosted CI is verified separately at the published commit.

## Platforms

Future macOS menu integration. No native menu or app run. No runtime or device acceptance is claimed.

## Perf impact

None from this documentation-only change. Section 9 defines what later implementations must measure.

author: bogdan-alexandrescu
body:
Product Oracle reported on 6 November 2026 that its review lanes cannot run `gh pr view` ("no GH_TOKEN in this container": tasks task_24ed8d5fda344051abdc, task_dafda076f8f94b96b269, task_2974919122fb460a92f2). They fall back to the checked-out head and never see the pull request's body or comments. Agents have no GitHub token by design. Issues already have a fix for this (`issue.py` stages a scrubbed `work/issue.md`), and this PR does the same for pull requests. Part of the agent quality program epic, part of #2688.

## What changed

- **New `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/pull_request.py`.** It reads the pull request, its conversation comments, its reviews and its review comments (paged, up to 5 pages each). All requests go through `issue._get`, the issue's own path: the tenant's `-git` token is sent only to a GitHub host and no redirect is followed. It renders `work/pull_request.md` with:
  - the title, state, base, head and labels;
  - the body;
  - the conversation (comments and reviews), oldest first and newest last;
  - the review threads, each under its `path:line` with replies in order.

  The file is capped at 1 MiB and each body at 64 KiB. Anything cut is counted in a closing line. The file is never written through a symlink.
- **`lifecycle.py`.** `_requested_pull_request()` finds the pull request a step works on, in this order:
  1. `input.pull_request`, once a profile declares it (see the contract request below);
  2. the signed `publish_to_pr`;
  3. the pull request its signed `builds_on` step recorded (`result_summary.git.pull_request.number`);
  4. for a single-pr reader or amender, the pull request its `pr_author` step recorded.

  It only applies to steps with a `prompt`. When there is a pull request:
  - the brief gains one line naming the file by absolute path;
  - the name is reserved from `input_from` staging;
  - STEP 6b' stages the file after the credentials step, so every secret is registered before the scrub, and before the generation re-check and the agent start.

  The text goes through `self._scrub`, the same scrub issue.md uses. It also goes through `swarm_redaction`'s pattern redaction, so a token-shaped string nobody registered is masked too. A 401 re-reads the slot once (`call_reading_again`), as the issue fetch does.
- **A read that fails does not fail the attempt.** This is different from the issue path, on purpose. The pull request is context next to a checkout the step already has, and a forge timeout must not take a review's whole workflow down. A refusal, or a forge that stayed down through the retry policy, writes a short file that says the pull request was not read and why. Then the agent starts.

## Tests (red first)

The tests were committed before the code, in `tests/unit/worker/test_pull_request_context.py`:
- A review-shaped workflow step that `builds_on` an author step that opened #42 gets `work/pull_request.md` with the body and a review thread (`path:line`, with its reply). Its brief names the file exactly once, and every request carried the tenant's token.
- A token-shaped string in a review comment, built at runtime and never registered, is scrubbed. Removing the pattern redaction makes this fail (mutation checked).
- An oversize thread is cut, and the file says how many comments were left out. One oversize body is cut where it stands.
- A step with no pull request gets no file and no line. This is checked twice: the upstream recorded no pull request, and the step has no `builds_on`. In both cases no request is made.
- A pull request the forge refuses gets a "not read" file, and the step still succeeds.
- A single-pr reader resolves its author's pull request. A step with no brief resolves none.

## What I ran

- `uv run pytest tests/unit/worker/test_pull_request_context.py -q`: 9 passed.
- `scripts/related-tests.sh` selected 766 files, because `lifecycle.py` is widely imported. I did not run the whole selection. I ran the 26 files in this change's area: the issue tests, publish_to_pr, builds_on, review verdict, security review, the cli prompt tests, single-pr roles and the new file. Result: 467 passed, 1 failed.
  - The failure is `test_issue_input.py::test_a_task_that_asks_for_no_issue_gets_the_prompt_it_got_before`. It also fails on main in this container: the container's own `SWARM_CHILDREN` adds the child-tasks line to the prompt. With `env -u SWARM_CHILDREN` all 39 tests in that file pass.
- `scripts/publish-scan.sh`: clean.
- CI runs the rest.

## CONTRACT.md invariants

- **1–3** (demand, all-or-nothing reservation, concurrency from LEASED): untouched. This is read-only forge I/O inside an attempt that already holds its lease.
- **4** (no sleeping through a provider wait): the reads are bounded by issue.py's connect and read timeouts and by the worker's forge retry policy, and the lease is heartbeated after every request.
- **5** (fencing): staging runs before `revalidate_generation`, so a stale worker still exits before the agent runs. The token read raises `FencedError` exactly as before.
- **6–8** (Spot, resources, checkpointing): untouched. The file is in `work/` and travels in checkpoints like `issue.md`; a resumed attempt rewrites it.
- **9** (tenant isolation): the read uses the tenant's own `-git` credential through the existing path. The upstream task is read with `fetch_upstream_task`, which refuses another tenant's task. No new token, environment variable or file holds a credential.
- **10** (callers pick a profile by name): the number comes from signed dispatch fields or a declared input. The text is data, and the file and the brief line both say so.

## Frozen-contract request

`input.pull_request` cannot reach the worker yet. Both swarm-api and the worker refuse an input key a profile does not declare. The request is to add `pull_request: RunnerInput("integer", minimum=1, maximum=999_999)` to `_CLI_AGENT_INPUTS` in `apps/common/swarm_common/profiles.py`. `pull_request.from_input` already reads it once declared. This is also in questions.json. I did not edit `apps/common/swarm_common/`.

## Day One install

Nothing a fresh deployment needs has changed: no infrastructure, IAM, manifests, settings or secret slots. The read uses the existing `-git` slot.

---

Opened by SwarmCloud's control plane. This branch is written only by this task.

- task: `task_0ad7caeb39ef40b5b7f8`
- tenant: `eng`
- branch: `swarm/task_0ad7caeb39ef40b5b7f8`
- head commit: `65027fd61550401b0588358733ca8fcda5ba59bf`

No worker ran for this step: the review's verdict did not name it, so there was no agent to run, and the branch is the implementer's as it was pushed (and scanned) by the implementer's own worker.

author: conman688
body:
## What

- `run weekly` (backup, `ingest all`, `screen`, `fetch-text`, `sync-vault`) and `run daily` (Form 4). A run takes a lock (`data/.run.lock`), uses one database connection and one SEC client, and stops at the first failed step. It logs to `run_log` (migration 8) and writes a health report to stdout and the vault's `Reports/Health.md`.
- Health warnings: a failed step, a table that shrank (ledgers on any drop, snapshot tables beyond 1%), failed Form 4 or price ledger entries, a latest price more than 4 days old, SEC throttling or dropped connections, and a backup that did not happen.
- `backup`: copies the database to `EOQ_BACKUP_DIR` as `edgar-YYYY-MM-DD.duckdb`, checks that the copy opens and matches, then keeps the newest 4. It never creates the folder, refuses a folder on the database's own disk, skips when there is too little room, and deletes only its own files.
- The SEC client also retries dropped connections and timeouts. The first live weekly run stopped on one `RemoteDisconnected`.
- `schedule` writes launchd agents: weekly on Saturday at 07:00, daily on weekdays at 21:00, both under `caffeinate`, with unbuffered logs. It does not install them.
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: runs the tests on every push.

## Checks

- `uv run pytest`: 184 passed (`tests/test_m9_ops.py`: 19), including a real `SIGKILL` of a Form 4 fetch: the rerun gives no duplicates and refetches at most the one uncommitted batch.
- Live: a backup to an external USB drive (4.7 GB in 54 s; the copy matches the live database's counts). Two daily runs: 807 filings, then 0 refetched. An overlapping run is refused. The weekly run's numbers are in `reviews/M9-operations.md`.

Not done here: installing the launchd agents and the "two unattended weeks" check. Both are for the user.

author: krischen-77
body:
A Daily OCR synthesis with 67 of 68 summarized reports can legitimately produce a disclosed Market Views edition, but the workflow incorrectly treated that success as a complete 68-article source. Article generation then stopped immediately and the complete original-page fallback was skipped.

Determine article readiness from the validated synthesis receipt. Keep partial synthesis available to Market Views while selecting complete original OCR pages for articles; authenticate the explicit partial-synthesis branch before accepting its page fallback. Preserve the existing complete-source, generation-checkpoint, and publication checks. Also allow the read-only startup-failure inspector to observe an empty articles directory omitted by archive packing and report the fixed incomplete-source category. Pin its job evidence to the original failed attempt even when a later attempt succeeds.

Validation: 160 targeted tests passed across Daily page fallback (14), source readiness (20), inspection (30), workflow routing (48), article generation (16), and delivery (32); git diff --check passed. Tests cover a real partial synthesis fixture, complete-page routing, and refusal of missing or unsuccessful source gates. No provider generation, publishing, or checkpoint migration was performed for validation.

author: barcoderesource
body:
This is by an automated agent, not a human.

Implements **issue #6 / MC3**: add **Depth Anything V2 Small** (monocular depth estimation) to Browse and to AI Workflows, by writing the model in MLX Swift. One commit per MC3-k step. **Ready for review; a person merges it.**

## What changed

- **MC3-1 — the kind and the catalog entry.** `ModelType.depth` (`cube.transparent`), `RunnerKind.depth`, the
  `MLXTools` kind map, the new case in every exhaustive switch. New *Images → Depth Estimation* leaf after Frame
  Interpolation, and the `depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf` card (family `depth-anything`, `source: mlx`,
  `format: mlx-fp32`, Apache-2.0, 24.8 M params, 0.10 GB, provisional `ramGB` 0.15 = 1.5× weights). Catalog guard 55→56.
- **MC3-2 — description, facts, download.** About text (relative depth, not metres; near = bright; the 8,192 px /
  3:1 limits; the 8-bit grayscale PNG contract; the Apache-2.0 notice), the pinned HF file list as
  `Fixtures/DepthAnything/repo-files.json`, and `DepthAnythingCatalogTests` (facts, exact `hfModelId`, leaf/section
  placement, the selector taking exactly `model.safetensors` + the two configs, the provisional RAM figure).
- **MC3-3 — reference fixtures.** `make_depth_golden.py` runs `transformers`' `DepthAnythingForDepthEstimation` +
  `DPTImageProcessor` (transformers 5.12.0, torch 2.7.0, numpy 2.2.6) on the pinned revision and writes raw f32
  tensors: (a) the 196×140 synthetic scene, a 112×154 non-square probe for layer-by-layer parity, (b)
  `sample-image.png`, and the preprocessing size table for five inputs.
- **MC3-4 — the backbone.** `DepthAnythingConfig` (the published `config.json` omits every field `transformers`
  defaults; those decode with the same defaults and the config is validated by name), PyTorch-compatible
  bilinear/bicubic resize to an exact target size, the PyTorch→MLX weight-layout conversion, and `DINOv2Backbone`
  (ViT-S/14, 12 blocks, exact-erf GELU, layer scale, CLS/mask tokens, bicubic position-embedding interpolation for
  non-518 inputs, the four `out_indices` feature maps each after the backbone layer norm). Strict loader: every
  tensor used, every parameter set, the first offender named.
- **MC3-5 — the head, pre- and post-processing.** `DPTNeck` (four reassemble layers — transposed conv at ×4/×2,
  identity, stride-2 conv at ×0.5 — per-level 3×3, fusion smallest-first with bilinear `align_corners=False` for the
  residual mismatch and `align_corners=True` for the fusion resize), `DepthHead` (64→32, bilinear
  `align_corners=True` to patch grid ×14, 32→32+ReLU, 1×1, ReLU), `DepthAnythingPreprocessor` (the reference's
  keep-aspect-ratio target size exactly, including round-half-to-even; EXIF orientation applied and sRGB) and
  `DepthAnythingPostprocessor` (decision 4: bicubic upsample, per-image min–max, 8-bit grayscale; a constant
  prediction is all black).
- **MC3-6 — the module and the Run screen.** `DepthAnythingEngine`/`Stage`/`SDK` (claim by family, never by
  architecture) / `Module` (registered before `ChatModule`), `DepthRunModel` and `DepthAnythingRunView` (Open… or
  drag and drop, Estimate depth, input and map side by side, Grayscale/Colour preview toggle — colour is display-only,
  Save PNG always writes grayscale, the caption, no Stop button). Errors are one plain sentence; the input limits are
  refused before any work; the run goes through the handed `LeasingStage` (the memory lease). Tests: input-limit
  refusals, the EXIF-orientation case, determinism (two runs byte-identical), the main-actor probe, the 8-bit
  grayscale output at the input's size, and the screen renders.
- **MC3-7 — memory.** Whole-process `phys_footprint` measured through the Run path in one fresh process per phase
  (sample photo, 12 MP, the 8,192 px / 3:1 worst case); the measured `.depth` working-set row is booked from it
  (below). `ramGB` is **not** changed — the maintainers set it from their own run.
- **MC3-8 — AI Workflows.** `Estimate Depth` is a served `.depth` task (`taskKinds`, served prefix, pool
  `["Depth Anything V2 Small"]`); bridge rows **"Depth Anything V2 Small" → `.same`** and **"Depth Pro" →
  `.substitute`** (appended last, so the row shows `running Depth Pro as depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf`);
  the MLXUI-authored manifest `depth-anything-v2-small.json` (`engine: mlx-depth`, `tasks: ["Estimate Depth"]`,
  `settings: {}`); the row refuses `seed=`, `steps=`, `width=`, `height=`, `scale=` and `quantize=` **by name**;
  gallery 62 leaves `AppState.hiddenFlowNumbers` (now `[61, 67, 68]`). `Resources/Gallery/` is not touched.

## Before / After — real app views

Captured from the app's own views with `NSHostingView.cacheDisplay` (the MC2-5 method — `ImageRenderer` leaves
lazy/AppKit content blank), same 1100 × 2000 / light-theme viewport. **Before** is Browse → Images with `main`'s
bundled catalog at `6788e19` (55 entries); **After** is the same view with this branch's catalog (56). `BrowseView`,
`ModelCard` and `ModelDetailView` have **no** code changes on this branch (`git diff origin/main -- MLXUI/Views` is
empty), so the only difference is the catalog this ticket adds. The Run screen is new, so its "before" is that no such
screen exists on `main`.

| Before (`main` @ `6788e19`) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|
| ![Before: Browse → Images, 6 models, no Depth Estimation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misfits-Rebels-Outcasts/MLXUI/agent/depth-anything-v2-1acb28b7adda/docs/screenshots/depth-anything/mc3-before-browse-images.png) | ![After: Browse → Images, 7 models, Depth Estimation leaf and card after Frame Interpolation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misfits-Rebels-Outcasts/MLXUI/agent/depth-anything-v2-1acb28b7adda/docs/screenshots/depth-anything/mc3-after-browse-images.png) |

After only (new surfaces; no baseline exists):

| Model page | Run screen — grayscale | Run screen — colour preview (display-only) |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misfits-Rebels-Outcasts/MLXUI/agent/depth-anything-v2-1acb28b7adda/docs/screenshots/depth-anything/mc3-after-model-detail.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misfits-Rebels-Outcasts/MLXUI/agent/depth-anything-v2-1acb28b7adda/docs/screenshots/depth-anything/mc3-after-run-grayscale.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Misfits-Rebels-Outcasts/MLXUI/agent/depth-anything-v2-1acb28b7adda/docs/screenshots/depth-anything/mc3-after-run-colour.png) |

The run-screen captures are the **real model output** on the bundled `sample-image.png` through the real engine
(`DepthAnythingEngine.estimateDepth`), hosted on `DepthRunModel` for the capture. PNGs committed under
`docs/screenshots/depth-anything/`.

**Limitation (the issue's "look at these"):** this environment has no owner photos, so the two "real photos of your
own" (one indoor, one outdoor) could not be captured here — the committed run-screen evidence uses the bundled sample
photo instead. The harness also writes `sample-image`, `sample-img-02` and `sample-img-03` input/output pairs when run
with `DP4D_SHOTS`; they are **not committed** (the issue asks for them in the conversation, not the tree). Please look
at depth maps of your own two photos before release.

## Tests

```
# both app schemes
xcodebuild -scheme MLXUI        -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath .dsh-dd build   # BUILD SUCCEEDED
xcodebuild -scheme MLXUI-Direct -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath .dsh-dd build   # BUILD SUCCEEDED

# full unit-test suite

author: ecarrig
body:
## What changed and why

Refreshing a large graph of derived dimensions repeatedly evaluates shared ancestors and can exceed Python's recursion limit. Evaluate the graph in dependency order with a memo scoped to one `derived_values()` call, and reuse the derived-name set when ordering dependencies. Later input edits still trigger fresh JAX evaluations.

It changes parameter evaluation, adds regressions for a 1,200-node chain and an out-of-order shared diamond, and includes a patch changelog note.

## Linked issue

No linked issue.

## How was this tested?

`uv run python scripts/verify.py` passed on this branch: Ruff, formatting, mypy, schema regeneration/drift, and the full `pytest -n auto` suite. Result: **2,040 passed, 70 skipped**. The local macOS environment does not provide the EGL/GLES software shader runtime; CI installs it and requires those shader tests.

The new tests also change the base dimension between evaluations and confirm that both direct reads and `refresh_derived()` receive the new values.

## Checklist

- [x] Added regression tests for deep shared graphs and fresh values after edits.
- [x] Added a user-facing patch changelog note.
- [x] Preserved the public API and serialized format.

author: aaronjgirard
body:
## Description

`snap()` on a time coordinate stored in a unit coarser than nanoseconds builds a grid that is too short by the unit ratio. The step is computed as `float(dur.astype(np.int64)) / (len(self) - 1)` and then labelled nanoseconds, but `dur.astype(np.int64)` counts in the coordinate's own unit. For `datetime64[us]` labels 1 ms apart the step comes out as 1000 ns, so the snapped coordinate spans 4 us instead of 4 ms, with no error. `timedelta64` coordinates take the same path and have the same problem. `Patch.snap_coords`, `update_limits(step=...)` on stored labels, and the released-snap fallback in `get_coord(data=...)` all reach this code, and pandas 3 parses many datetimes to microseconds.

The fix converts the span with `dc.to_timedelta64` before taking its integer value, which is the conversion `_fit_run` (used by `fuse`) already does. Nanosecond coordinates are unchanged. The new tests snap jittered `datetime64` and `timedelta64` labels in `ns`, `us`, `ms` and `s` and check that both ends and the step are kept; the six non-nanosecond cases fail on `dev`.

Month and year labels are spanned in days between their two ends, so calendar units keep their actual span: with the first commit alone, snapping January, February and April 2024 (`datetime64[M]`) put the last label about 7.5 hours past April 1, because months converted at their average length. `TestSnapTimeUnits::test_snap_calendar_units` covers it and fails without the change. A datetime span too long for a nanosecond step (about 292 years) raises `TimeOverflowError`; `test_snap_wide_span_raises` covers it.

One assumption: the snapped coordinate is `datetime64[ns]` (or `timedelta64[ns]`) whatever the input unit, as it already was on `dev`. I left that alone to keep this change to the step.

This is s01 F2 in Aaron's pre-v1.0 review.

## Changelog

- fixed: Snapping a datetime or timedelta coordinate stored in microseconds, milliseconds, seconds, months or years now keeps its span instead of shrinking or shifting it.

author: corgan2222
body:
Two independent fixes in the clawdmeter UI modules, found while chasing a display that showed `2147483647` where a percentage belongs.

## 1. Reject NaN before casting a sensor state to int

`has_state()` turns true as soon as a Home Assistant sensor has published anything, and an unavailable or unknown entity publishes `NAN`. So this guard does not do what it looks like it does:

```cpp
int p = id(x_session_pct).has_state() ? (int) id(x_session_pct).state : 0;
```

`(int) NAN` is undefined behaviour and on ARM it comes out as `INT32_MAX`, which is where the `2147483647` on the panel comes from. The percentage bars take the same cast, and the extra-credits tile renders the same missing value as `nan cr` because it formats a float instead.

The file already knows the right pattern, a few lines further down in `stats_panel.yaml`:

```cpp
bool have_min = id(x).has_state() && !std::isnan(id(x).state) && ...
```

This adds that `isnan` check to all 39 places that cast a percentage to int, across the nine `layout_modern_*` variants, `remote.yaml` and `stats_panel.yaml`. The fallback stays `0`, which is what the no-state branch already returned.

## 2. Cap how long `time_to_100` may hold its last answer

When an input goes away, or the burn rate is flat, both lambdas in `time_to_100.yaml` return the previously published string. With no bound on that, the panel keeps showing a confident `in 2270 min` and an ETA clock next to a burn rate of `0`, hours after the input died, and nothing on screen marks the number as stale. The reading is not wrong, it is a fossil.

A new `hold_min` var bounds it, default 10 minutes. Short dropouts still keep the tile steady, which is why the hold exists in the first place; past that the sensor falls back to its unknown string. `hold_min: 0` restores the old unbounded behaviour for anyone who wants it.

The hold uses one `uint32_t` global per instance holding `millis()` of the last successful computation, compared as an unsigned difference so the 49-day `millis()` wrap takes care of itself.

**This one changes behaviour by default.** It seemed worth it since a stale number that looks live is worse than an honest "unknown", but the default is one word to change if you disagree.

## Testing

There is no CI in this repo, so nothing checks this automatically. What I did verify: all 39 call sites matched a single textual pattern with the same id on both sides of the ternary, every rewritten line is paren- and quote-balanced, and the diff is 39 one-line changes plus the `time_to_100` block, with no line-ending churn. It still wants a real `esphome config` run and a flash on one panel before you trust it.

## One open question

For a value that is genuinely unknown, both branches now render `0`. On a bar that is fine, it just sits empty. On the text tiles it reads `Session 0%`, which looks like real data rather than missing data, so it trades a loud wrong number for a quiet one. A dash would be more honest, but it means touching the format strings and the lang packs, so I left it alone. Say the word and I will do it as a follow-up.

Implements [spec 039](docs/specs/039-art-index-missing-file/spec.md) (plan: [plan.md](docs/specs/039-art-index-missing-file/plan.md); evidence: [verification.md](docs/specs/039-art-index-missing-file/verification.md)).

## Summary

The art index is two things that can disagree: the latest `mtg_art_builds` row and the file under `storage/catalog/mtg/art/index/`. After a restore, which holds the database only, or after the directory is lost, the **Art index** panel on `/admin/catalog` and the art line of `catalog:status` said "Ready." while the scanner offered text recognition only.

Now a finished latest build whose own named index file isn't on the volume reads:

- **Panel:** "Index file missing. Build the art index again.", with the facts Finished, Index file, Artworks indexed, Without an image and Failed images, and an enabled **Build art index** button. The page doesn't poll.
- **`catalog:status`:** `Art matching: index file missing (<name>); press Build art index on the admin catalog page to write it again. <counts>`

Pressing the button rebuilds the file without downloading any image, and both read "Ready." again. Only MTG code changed; the core, the controllers, the views and `AdminHelper` are untouched (FR-4).

## Phases

1. `446b507` **feat(art):** `MTG::Art::Index.file?(name)` checks the name against `NAME` and makes one `stat`; `MTG::ArtBuild#index_file_present?`; spec helper `art_index_name`.
2. `f73f537` **fix(art):** `MTG::Art::Operation` gets the `:index_missing` state. It is judged only once nothing is queued or running, so those states win. The five existing "Ready." examples now write a real index file.
3. `5712f67` **fix(art):** `MTG::Art.status_line` gets the missing wording, with "(no file name recorded)" for a row that has no name.
4. `474ee49` **test(art):** AC-3.1 (pressing the button queues one build) and AC-3.2 (a rebuild after the art directory is emptied makes no image request, writes the same file name, and the panel and line read ready again).
5. `fa3a0f4` **docs:** the catalog operations and release and deploy area docs, both restore places in the README, the specs index supersessions (015 AC-4.1, 011 AC-3.11 and 030 decision 12, each in part, recorded both ways), and the roadmap line.
- `80aad73`: the screenshots. `7633920`: fixes from the review. `af1e7ae`: verification and review. `fef8f9b`, `6aa432a` and `e75c454`: distillation.

## Rulings and deviations

- **AC-1.5's "nothing outside `index/` is looked at"** is proven where it lives: `Index.file?` refuses any name that isn't of the index's shape (example with `../../config/master.key`). The operation example checks the state and the fact rather than stubbing a `stat`.
- **The plan's "no Index file fact on ready" check** went into the AC-4.7 example, the one that reads facts.
- **The 030 index row** had its Superseded-by text in a stray seventh cell. I moved it into Superseded by and appended 039's clause there, as the plan asked.
- **The spec header** already read Approved v1.0.1 on `main`, so that plan item needed no change.
- **Branch name.** The worktree's branch was renamed from `plainprogrammer/039-art-index-missing-file-2` to `039-art-index-missing-file`. That name had carried the spec PR #165, which merged; this push recreated it.
- **No subagents.** The work was done inline, without the subagent per work unit that the skill asks for, because the brief said no helpers except the review.
- **Commit trailers.** `446b507`–`474ee49` and `fa3a0f4` say `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5`; the session runs on Opus 5.5. The coordinator said not to rewrite pushed commits, so later commits carry the Opus trailer.

## Tests

- Local `bin/ci` at `474ee49`, the last code commit: every step passed, with **2435 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending**.
- `7633920` added one example and tightened another. Their files pass (76 examples, 0 failures), and the pre-push hook's full `bin/ci` gates each push.
- Red-then-green evidence for each phase is in `verification.md`.

## Implementation review

**SPEC-ALIGNED WITH MINOR GAPS**: `sdd-review` Mode B, Opus, read-only. Nothing blocking or major. The minor findings:

- **Fixed in `7633920`:**
  - The README now quotes the status line as it prints.

- **Ruled:**
  - The upgrade seeds' `art-index-upgrade.bin.gz` now reads as missing; the spec already accepts this.

Details are in `verification.md`.

`/admin/catalog` with art matching on. The worktree's dev database was seeded by a scratch script: one admin, one applied refresh with 0 cards, and one finished build row. For "ready" an empty index file was written through `MTG::Art::Index.write!`; for "missing" it was deleted. No real art index is involved.

author: tmorius-eng
body:
Item 7 of the research round. Globe International's 2025 test sent 59 requests and only 16 were answered in full; nothing on the site helped a reader ask.

**What the page does**
- A client-only form builds the request letter the Law on Public Information Transparency (2021) describes.
- The reader copies it or opens it in their own mail app (`mailto:` with no address). Nothing typed is stored or sent.
- The page lists the complaint routes and links the law on legalinfo.mn.

**Clauses used, read from the law's Mongolian text**

| Clause | What it says |
|---|---|
| 13.4 | What a written request contains |
| 14.1.2 | No purpose or reason needed for open information |
| 15.6 | Answer at once or within 5 working days |
| 15.7 | Extension of up to 10 more working days |
| 16.3 | Electronic delivery free as a rule |
| 14.1.6 / 14.2 | Complaint to the higher body or a court, and to the National Human Rights Commission |

**Details**
- The deadline is computed in working days (`addWorkingDays`, weekends only); the page says holidays are not counted.
- `missingFields` lists what 13.4 still needs. An e-mail is required when electronic delivery is chosen.
- Organisation suggestions come from our `SOURCE_SEEDS` names via a datalist.
- The page is in the site map's "Төр, улстөрчид" group and in the sitemap.

**Checks**
- `npm run check`: 649 pass. New tests: `tests/info-request.test.ts`.
- Filled in the demo at 390 px: no horizontal overflow.

author: thecap213
body:
## Etapa 13B — decisiones H e I

Base develop con PR #13 integrada. Solo elegibilidad veterinaria e idioma de correos; no incluye Stripe (etapa14), despliegues, proveedores reales o nuevas funcionalidades.

## Cambios

- Invitaciones solo a VETERINARIO con cuenta ACTIVA y correo verificado. Cuenta desconocida, otro rol, pendiente/suspendida reciben el mismo 422 RECIPIENT_NOT_REGISTERED y mensaje genérico.
- ACCEPT revalida rol/estado/verificación actual antes de ocupar cupo, conservando comprobación del destinatario y vencimiento. JWT/sesiones siguen bloqueando cuentas no utilizables; el servicio también rechaza con 409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION sin exponer el estado privado.
- Cupos, duplicados, REJECT, vencimientos y revocaciones conservados. Log de error de invitación sanitizado sin destinatario ni excepción bruta.
- **Accept-Language opcional, aprobado expresamente por el Team Leader antes de implementar**, en registro, reenvío con credenciales, solicitud de recuperación e invitación. es/en, variantes/reglas ponderadas, español predeterminado/fallback. DTO y rutas intactos.
- En invitaciones selecciona el idioma el emisor; no se inventa una preferencia del destinatario.
- Idioma capturado como argumento inmutable antes de la cola de recuperación. Subject/HTML/text se materializan en el JSON cifrado de la emisión. Workers/reintentos/reinicios reutilizan los mismos bytes: no dependen de locale/hilo HTTP ni cambian código, cuota, vencimiento o idempotency key.
- No hay preferencia de cuenta, columna de idioma, migración ni dependencia nueva. Invitaciones conservan su transporte directo de texto, sin nueva promesa de durabilidad.
- Documentación de contratos/fallback/compatibilidad actualizada; overloads internos antiguos mantienen español.

## Validación local

Maven Wrapper/Java21: **511 pruebas = 462 de base + 49 nuevas**, 0 fallos, 0 errores, 0 omitidas. Tiempo local5 min45 s.

- Elegibilidad: 11 casos HTTP/servicio con estados/verificación, privacidad, cambios entre envío/aceptación, rol, destinatario ajeno, ausencia de efectos, cupos/duplicados/vencimiento/revocación.
- Selector: 22 casos de variantes, pesos, ausencia, malformado/no soportado y límite de longitud.
- Integración de idioma: 15 casos con PostgreSQL16 y servidor HTTP localhost simulado para registro/reenvío/recuperación/invitación; cola en otro hilo, payloads cifrados, reintentos y unicidad.
- Reinicio completo de contexto de aplicación: 1 caso conserva y envía el payload inglés confirmado en PostgreSQL temporal.
- Una aserción preexistente se adapta al overload interno para comprobar explícitamente español; ninguna prueba se eliminó ni debilitó.
- V1–V18 intactas y SHA-256 de los 18 archivos validado antes del commit. Estos resultados son locales: verificar Backend CI de esta PR por separado.

## Límites

La elegibilidad se relee en la transacción; no se añadieron locks entre contextos ni se promete serialización con cambios de cuenta posteriores/in-flight. La cabecera es por operación y no traduce JSON, notificaciones, logs o catálogos. Una nueva emisión sin cabecera vuelve a español.

Sin acceso a secretos reales, bases persistentes, anitec-pg o Render. Los modos resend/Recovery habilitados en tests son exclusivamente simulados, sin envío real ni activación operativa. **No realizar merge automático. No iniciar etapa14.**
