author: tamler
body:
Stacked on #84, targeting `claude/leftovers-r3` at `1b4a377330b894d85c0f88ee3ef34085218bee63`. Addresses r10 F1/P2.

The installer interpolated the selected archive name into `grep -E`. A checksum entry naming `another-0x1x0-<target>.tar.gz` could authorize the selected `another-0.1.0-<target>.tar.gz` when its digest matched the downloaded bytes; exact `+build1` names were rejected. Compare the full filename literally with POSIX awk, then enforce the existing static digest/marker format and single-entry check before checksum verification or unpacking.

The new regression runs each real checker alone on PATH, with a tar-call log, over stable/prerelease/build-metadata versions. All wrong-name fixtures contain the correct downloaded-byte digest. It asserts selection errors, no tar call and no installed binary, while accepting exact text/binary-marker entries, unrelated entries alongside the selected archive, and an entry without a final newline. Duplicate and malformed entries still reject. Baseline failed through both checkers; fixed installer suite passes 5/5 with no skips.

Validation on macOS arm64: full offline workspace/all-features tests (224 passed), stable Clippy all targets/features with `-D warnings`, Rust 1.88 locked all-targets workspace check, fmt, `sh -n` and `git diff --check` passed. Shellcheck is unavailable; Linux runtime, real release downloads and hosted CI have not been verified locally.

Self-review: checked fixed-width digest/marker boundaries, full literal filename equality, duplicate handling, unterminated input, quoting, tool isolation and pre-unpack failure. The added dependency is standard POSIX awk. Digest authenticity and install replacement behavior are unchanged.

NEEDS JACOB: automatic approval review rejected sending the scoped plan to the external Claude service because repository/task disclosure to that destination was not approved. Per charter, this draft carries self-review; independent cross-family plan/final review remains pending. No merge or release acceptance is claimed.

author: stephanbaum
body:
M6 track T1: the sync protocol foundation. The engine and folder transport (T2), server (T3), HTTP transport (T4) and desktop (T5) follow.

**mosaic-core**
- Nine new labels and a per-install `InstallId`.
- `sync_auth`: checkpoint MAC, folder MACs for segment, account and blob-delete, device-info seal/open, and `session_token`. The keys are derived only in core from AK.
- KATs checked against an independent Python script (`tests/vectors/sync_kat.py`; its output is checked in and reproduced byte for byte).

**mosaic-vault**
- Store schema v3, with a migration test showing v2 data is kept. It adds:
  - upload queues for vault keys and metadata (M2-R1);
  - install identity, sync config, opaque cursors and local sequence blocks (never reused);
  - a monotonic checkpoint counter enforced by a trigger;
  - attachment deletions (recorded only after upload).
- A session sync API that keeps keys inside the vault:
  - two-phase rotation (prepare/commit);
  - `reset_sync_state`;
  - a password-change prepare/commit split;
  - join keys;
  - checkpoint and folder MAC helpers.

**mosaic-sync (new)**
- `wire`: strict parsers for folder segments, checkpoints, account files, blob delete markers, device info and folder cursors. Each checks bounds before allocating, verifies the MAC in constant time before parsing, and rejects trailing bytes.
- `wire` also holds the canonical folder-name parser (cloud conflict copies are ignored), email normalization, and every hosted-API JSON type with `deny_unknown_fields`.
- The `Transport` trait; implementations come in T2 and T4.
- 8 fuzz targets, added to CI fuzz smoke, coverage, deny and audit.

**Docs**
- CRYPTO_SPEC §2, §3, §9, §10 (+ §10.1 folder backend, §10.2 hosted write rules), §11 and §12.
- ADR-0042 to 0046.
- THREAT_MODEL R54–R60.
- CORE_API.

`opaque-ke` and the HTTP code enter with T3 and T4 (ADR-0046); no new external crate in this PR.

author: bluefiref5ran
body:
Found while replaying a real two-player Absorbing Man game from its save: when Avalanche! was revealed, the player who revealed it picked the option for both players.

## The rule

- **Avalanche! (04091):** "Each player must choose to either spend a [energy] resource or take 2 indirect damage…"
- **Corrupted Timestream (11022):** "Each player must either discard 1 random card from hand, or place 2 threat here."

RRG 1.8 "Each Player" (p. 17) says "each player resolves that effect one at a time", and "Choose (Option)" (p. 12) defines the choice. Each player makes their own choice.

## The fix

Both cards wrapped the choice in `forEachPlayer`, but the choice inside was `chooseOne`. That is `chooseOneBy(you, …)`, and `forEachPlayer` doesn't rebind `you`, so the revealing player chose every time. The choice is now `chooseOneBy(thatPlayer, …)`. The options already acted on `thatPlayer`.

The reviewer swept every `forEachPlayer` in `packages/cards/src`, and every card that prints "each player (must) choose(s)", and found no other card with this pattern.

## Tests

New `packages/cards/src/wave2/each-player-chooses.test.ts`: two players, with the card as the next one dealt. Both players are asked, in player order. Without the fix the first player is asked twice.

## Checks

- `src/wave2` card suite passes; typecheck passes.
- e2e gate: 842 passed, 0 failed, 96 skipped
- Reviewed with the `code-reviewer` agent: no blockers; its test nits are in.

## What's new

**Breakdown by effort.** `/token-bar:token breakdown` now shows how many requests each model took, and, when the logs record an effort level, the share of usage by effort. Whatever values appear (medium, high, and so on) are shown as they are, so nothing is tied to particular models or levels. The effort section only appears when the logs have it.

**`cost`, optional.** `/token-bar:token cost` shows what your tokens would cost, by model and by effort.

- token-bar ships with **no prices**: they change, and they differ by account. The first time it prints how to create `~/.claude/token-bar/prices.json` with your own prices per million tokens, and lists the model ids found in your logs.
- With prices set it counts input, output, cache writes and cache reads. An id ending in `*` matches a family of models.
- A model with no price is listed as "no price" and is never guessed. A mistake in the file is explained.
- On a subscription this is not what you pay, since plans are not billed per token. It shows where the expensive usage is, and the output says so.

The scan now keeps the effort level and the four kinds of token for each request, so the scan cache moves to version 2 and is rebuilt once on the first run after updating.

## Checks

- 141 plugin tests, 22 Codex tests and the Rust tests pass; ruff is clean.
- Tested on a real week of logs: models with request counts and effort showed correctly, and `cost` printed the setup message.

author: hyukjinkwon
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

[SPARK-60963](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60963): the artifact uploads of the Rust transport now run under the retry policy, as PySpark's do.

- **Cache uploads** of large local relations: the `ArtifactStatus` check and the `AddArtifacts` upload are one attempt, as in `SparkConnectClient.cache_artifacts`. So a transient error of either is retried from the status check.
- **`addArtifacts` and `copyFromLocalToFs`** upload each path in an attempt of its own, as `SparkConnectClient.add_artifacts` does. That makes one `AddArtifacts` call per path, as PySpark makes.

An attempt sends all the frames again, since a stream cannot be resumed. The checks of the response, its CRCs and the acknowledgement of each cached artifact, stay outside the retries.

### Why are the changes needed?

Each of these requests was sent once, so a transient error, such as an `UNAVAILABLE` of a reset connection, failed `createDataFrame` of a large PyArrow table, or `addArtifacts`, at once. PySpark retries it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, these calls survive transient errors, as with PySpark 4.3.0. `addArtifacts` of several paths makes one upload per path.

### How was this patch tested?

- New tests against the mock Connect server of the Arrow handoff tests, which can now fail `ArtifactStatus` and `AddArtifacts` calls with given status codes:
  - A cache upload whose status check and upload each fail once with `UNAVAILABLE` succeeds, with three status checks and two upload attempts, and the server reads the cached data.
  - A `PERMISSION_DENIED` of the upload is not retried.
  - `addArtifacts` of two paths, with one transient failure, uploads both in three attempts.
  
  The retry tests fail without this change.
- The test of the frames of `addArtifacts` now expects one upload per path.
- The lib tests and every integration test, e2e included, against a local Spark 4.3.0 server (660 passed, and 123 of the transport crate), the build of all tests with `wasm-udf`, the offline Python suites (913 passed, 9 skipped), and the live drop-in and Arrow suites (82 passed) and live cases (10 passed). Clippy reports no diagnostics in the changed lines.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

The model is unchanged: gpt-5.4-mini Global Standard, reasoning effort low.

| insufficient-history | 0/3, 0/3 | 3/3 |

author: quellabs
body:
## Summary

Audit-driven hardening of Canvas's existing security code, done at the user's request to find and fix real gaps rather than add new features. Four rounds: round 1 covered Sanitization/Validation, Security (CSRF/JWT/rate-limiting), and the Legacy bridge/upload handling; round 2 covered security header/CORS policies, `Kernel.php`, error handling, the Inspector debug panel, and file-based cache; round 3 covered the Scheduler, DependencyInjection, and Discover subsystems, finding a HIGH-severity gap in the `canvas-scheduler-rabbitmq` subtree package; round 4 confirmed and fixed the identical bug (plus a related type-validation gap) in its `canvas-scheduler-redis` sibling.

### Round 1

- **`PathSafe`**: traversal removal now works segment-by-segment instead of stripping the substrings `../`/`..\`, closing a bypass via a bare `..` and absolute/Windows drive-letter paths.
- **`StripTags`**: strips every attribute from allowlisted tags except a safe `href` (scheme allowlist: `http`/`https`/`mailto`/`tel`/no-scheme, normalized the way a browser would before checking).
- **`SecureUploadAspect`**: extended the dangerous-extension blocklist and added rejection of reserved filenames (`.htaccess`, `.htpasswd`, `web.config`).
- **`JwtAuthenticationAspect`**: now requires an HS256 secret of at least 32 bytes.
- **`LegacyHandler`**: resets the `$__canvas_headers` global per request instead of once per process — without the fix, any legacy file calling `header()`/`exit()` threw a `TypeError` on the very first request in a fresh process. The `chdir()` race under coroutine/persistent-worker runtimes is documented as unsupported.
- **`RecursiveLegacyPreprocessor::resolveIncludePath()`**: fixed a `file_exists()`/`realpath()` path mismatch.
- **README**: rate-limit/CSRF example now shows `throwOnFailure=true` with the default explained.

### Round 2

- **`Kernel::createErrorResponse()`**: falls back to `DefaultErrorHandler` if a custom `ErrorHandlerInterface` throws, instead of skipping security-header application entirely.
- **Inspector default**: flipped `enabled` to `false` in both this repo's config and the `canvas-skeleton` project template — it was the literal out-of-the-box default, exposing POST data, cookies, and SQL with bound parameters to every visitor.
- **`FileCache`**: hashes the namespace into the context directory name the same way a cache key is hashed.

### Round 3

- **`canvas-scheduler-rabbitmq` — HIGH severity**: `JobEnvelope::fromJson()` validated a queue message's class against the broad `JobInterface` instead of `QueueableInterface`. Since every Cron `TaskInterface` also extends `JobInterface`, `RabbitMQWorker::processEnvelope()`'s `$container->make($envelope->class, $envelope->payload)` could be pointed at any `JobInterface` implementor — including any registered Cron task — with attacker-chosen constructor arguments, given publish access to the queue. Fixed in both the envelope check and the worker's redundant check; added a README security note on the trust model.
- DependencyInjection and Discover audited and found sound.

### Round 4

- **`canvas-scheduler-redis` — same HIGH severity bug, same fix**: identical `JobInterface`/`QueueableInterface` confusion in its own `JobEnvelope`/`RedisWorker`. This package had zero existing tests, so a full `tests/SchedulerRedis` suite (13 tests) was added and wired into `phpunit.xml`, plus the same README security note.
- **`JobEnvelope::fromJson()` type validation**: ported the RabbitMQ sibling's `is_string`/`is_array`/`is_int` field checks, which Redis's version lacked. Without them, a malformed queue message (e.g. a non-array `payload`) crashed with an uncaught `TypeError` instead of the `InvalidArgumentException` that `RedisQueue::pop()` catches to discard malformed messages gracefully — so one corrupted message could crash the entire worker process rather than just that job.

## Test plan

author: winter2897
body:
## Why
Owner feedback, round 4: the salary entered in onboarding was never split into the jars, and the Budget tab showed a total budget of 0 đ and −113.000 đ left while ACB held 38.000.000 đ. The assistant also said income was 0.

**Root causes**
- The monthly income was only saved to UserDefaults.
- `applyJars` copied opening wallet balances into `Jar.initialBalance` once. A wallet added or renamed later (ACB), or onboarding closed early, left that money outside every jar, and nothing showed it.
- The chat tools recomputed jar math themselves and had no notion of a budget, unallocated money or an expected salary.

## What changed
- **No money outside the jars**
  - `Ledger.unallocated` = wallets + money lent − money borrowed − jars.
  - The Budget tab shows **Unallocated** with a one-tap **Split into jars**. It is saved as a dated `jarTransfer` with no source jar and one `IncomeSplit` per jar, written by `allocate`.
  - The onboarding jar step splits everything this way, so it no longer writes `Jar.initialBalance`.
- **Salary becomes real income**
  - Onboarding asks for the payday and saves an income `Recurring` (category Salary).
  - On payday the Budget tab shows the salary with **Mark received**. It is also in Recurring & Bills, swipe → Mark received. This records income into the bank wallet and splits it into the jars.
  - A salary already logged in chat, from 7 days before payday on, counts as received: it is not asked for again and moves to the next payday.
- **Budget totals**
  - The tab's numbers are one struct, `BudgetFacts`, built from `Ledger`.
  - Total budget = start of month + added; Left = Total budget − Spent.
  - There is now an **Income** row, and it matches the Overview.
- **The assistant**
  - New `monthBudget` tool reads the same `BudgetFacts`: total, spent, left, left after bills, unallocated, income received, expected salary and payday, bills due this month.
  - It is added to spending-coach, jar-budgeting and close-management; the en/vi skill text is updated.
  - When no model answers, the chat states the same numbers.
- **Bug found while testing:** `AmountField` used `TextField(value:format:)`, which only commits when editing ends. Tapping Save while typing 2000000 saved 200000. It now parses on every keystroke. This affects every Budget amount field.
- Income recurrings are left out of the bills-due totals, the Overview's bills and the reminders.
- The decisions are written into `docs/FEATURES.md` §4.1, §4.3 and §7. CLAUDE.md is updated.

**CloudKit:** no schema change. Income recurrings are told apart by their category kind; the allocation reuses `Txn` and `IncomeSplit`.

## Tests
`xcodebuild test` passes: 230 tests. New `MoneyFlowTests` covers:
- onboarding (15tr salary on the 25th, ACB 38tr) → jars hold 38tr, nothing unallocated → Mark received → +15tr split → a 113k food expense comes out of Essentials → `BudgetFacts` numbers;
- a wallet added later → unallocated 2tr → split → budget +2tr, per-jar shares;
- a salary logged in chat → not due again, moves to the next payday;
- lending, borrowing and wallet transfers don't change the unallocated amount;
- the `monthBudget` tool answer equals `BudgetFacts` (left, total, unallocated, left after bills, expected salary, bills), and the no-model chat text states the same "left".

## Simulator: fresh install, iPhone 17 Pro
Onboarding: income 10–20M, fixed salary, payday 25, bank 38.000.000 đ, default jars.

| Payday question | Budget after onboarding | Wallet added later |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/1-payday.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/2-budget-after-onboarding.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/3-unallocated.png) |

| After "Split into jars" | Salary in Recurring | Salary received |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/4-after-split.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/5-wallets-salary.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/6-salary-received.png) |

| Overview income agrees | Assistant: "How much can I still spend this month?" |
|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/7-overview.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/winter2897/moonee/claude/s12-budget-flow-7fae3f/docs/screenshots/s12/8-assistant.png) |

The "Unallocated" screenshot shows an older, longer subtitle that wrapped the amount; it is now "Not in a jar yet.".

## Not done
- There is no payday notification; the Budget row and the bills list are the prompt.
- There is no auto-posting: the salary is recorded only when the user confirms it.
- A negative unallocated amount (jars promise more than the wallets hold) shows a warning only, with no automatic fix.
- The owner's existing device data: after updating, ACB's 38tr shows as Unallocated, and one tap splits it.

author: 0xsoftboi
body: Phase 1 of the Commons v2 design (`docs/plans/commons-v2.md`, also in #1106): an ownerless credit-clearing network that replaces v1 `SuwappuMutualCredit`. **MONEY-PATH.** Testnet only; an independent audit is required before mainnet. ## Contract: `contracts/commons/CommonsClearingHouse.sol` - **Terms-hash–bound accept.** This fixes the v1 bug where a proposer could cancel and re-propose with worse terms before the accept landed. - **Adjustable limits.** Each party can move the credit it extends at any time. Interest can exceed a limit; new principal can't. - **`payPath`.** Payments route atomically through intermediaries who opt in with a fee **and** a cap per outbound line (`routeCap`). - **`clear()`.** Anyone can submit a batch of debt cycles. The contract checks it in O(E): each edge is within what's owed, and each node's inflows equal its outflows (tracked in EIP-1153 transient storage). - **Pull-based settlement.** Repayment goes into escrow (`claimable`) and the creditor calls `withdraw`. Creditors can write off debts, and standing counters are kept per token. - **EIP-712 signed intents** for every action: ECDSA, then ERC-1271, with unordered bitmap nonces. ## Review An Opus money-path review returned SHIP WITH FIXES, and all of them are in `d6ac0d24`: - HIGH: routing could push an intermediary into debt on another party's terms. Fixed with the per-line route cap. - MEDIUM: a creditor could block repayment and then claim default. Fixed with pull-based settlement. - MEDIUM: standing could be farmed across tokens. Fixed with per-token standing. - LOW: added write-off and wider counters. ## Tests - 31 unit tests, including a regression test for each review finding and cold-storage gas benchmarks (about 24.5k gas per edge in steady state). - 7 stateful invariants over 128k calls with interest: - `clear` preserves net positions - principal stays within limits - custody equals the sum of `claimable` - route caps are respected - nets sum to zero - line status stays consistent ## Deployment (Base Sepolia) - **Address:** `0x489b93a02a5ad429b444c0e5370f6d39089677dd`, [verified on Blockscout](https://base-sepolia.blockscout.com/address/0x489b93a02a5ad429b444c0e5370f6d39089677dd). - **How:** deployed through Turnkey from a dedicated deployer wallet (`contracts/deploy/turnkey/`). Gas was bridged from Ethereum Sepolia via Base's L1StandardBridge. - **Live E2E passed** (`contracts/deploy/turnkey/e2e.ts`): signed intents relayed by the deployer, then accept, pay, multilateral clear, settle into escrow, and withdraw, ending with custody at 0. ## Client `@suwappu/primitives-client` 0.2.0 adds the ABI, the deployment, and intent helpers. Its digest is verified identical to the live contract's `intentDigest()`. ## Not in this PR - A `/commons` v2 tab in the terminal. It builds on #1104. - Typed EIP-712 structs per action (review LOW-4). Until then, UIs must decode the params before asking a user to sign. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds `CommonsClearingHouse`, the first phase of the Commons v2 design: an ownerless credit-clearing network that replaces v1 `SuwappuMutualCredit`. Testnet only and requires an independent audit before mainnet. - Terms-hash–bound accept fixes the v1 bug where a proposer could cancel and re-propose with worse terms before the accept landed. - Each party can move the credit it extends at any time; interest may exceed a limit, new principal may not. - `payPath` routes payments atomically through intermediaries who opt in with a fee and a per-outbound-line `routeCap`. - `clear()` lets anyone submit a batch of debt cycles, checked in O(E) with EIP-1153 transient storage. - Repayment goes into escrow (`claimable`) and the creditor calls `withdraw`; creditors can write off debts. - Every action uses EIP-712 signed intents (ECDSA, then ERC-1271) with unordered bitmap nonces. **Review fixes** The Opus money-path review returned SHIP WITH FIXES; all findings are fixed in this PR: - HIGH: routing could push an intermediary into debt on another party's terms — fixed with the per-line route cap. - MEDIUM: a creditor could block repayment and then claim default — fixed with pull-based settlement. - MEDIUM: standing could be farmed across tokens — fixed with per-token standing. - LOW: added write-off and wider counters. **Tests and deployment** - 31 unit tests, including a regression test per review finding and cold-storage gas benchmarks (~24.5k gas per edge). - 7 stateful invariants over 128k calls with interest. - Live on Base Sepolia at `0x489b93a02a5ad429b444c0e5370f6d39089677dd`, verified on Blockscout; live E2E passed. - `@suwappu/primitives-client` 0.2.0 adds the ABI, deployment, and intent helpers; its digest matches the live contract. Not in this PR: the `/commons` v2 terminal tab and typed EIP-712 structs per action. Written for commit 0de0512a981c1f5fe2c0bf2acba2ea8c4e8cca88. Summary will update on new commits.

author: sargekhan
body:
## Problem

On `@hyperswarm/rpc` ≤ 3.5.0 a pooled client to a peer that was down when the
client was created never recovers. With a capability (the path this facility
uses) the stream never opens, `_rpc` is never created and `close` is never
emitted, so the pool keeps a client that throws `RPC client closed` on every
request until the calling process is restarted. Any worker restart wedges its
callers.

Fixed in holepunchto/rpc#20, released as 3.5.1.

## Fix

Require `@hyperswarm/rpc` `^3.5.1` so a fresh install cannot resolve the broken
version, and refresh the lockfile to match. No code change.

## Testing

Reproduced against 3.5.0 with a standalone testnet script (server child
restarted while a client polls through the pool); the pooled client recovers on
3.5.1.

author: adamxbot
body:
A scored polish pass over fxcss's terminal interface. Eight screens were captured in a real ~100-column terminal (light: macOS Terminal Basic, dark: GitHub Dark) and scored by three judges beside `gh`, `uv` and `brew`, then re-captured after each round of fixes until every judge scored every category at 9 or above in the same round.

## Score history

Overall score per judge (1–10). Rounds 2–5 used Sonnet alone as the pace judge; the full council judged rounds 0, 1, 6 and 7.

| round | Opus 5.5 | Fable 5.1 | Sonnet 5.5 | lowest category |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5.5 | 5.5 | 5.5 | 4.5 |
| 1 | 8.0 | 8.0 | 8.0 | 7.5 |
| 2 | – | – | 8.5 | 8.0 |
| 3 | – | – | 8.5 | 8.5 |
| 4 | – | – | 8.5 | 8.5 |
| 5 | – | – | 9.0 | 8.5 |
| 6 | 9.0 | 9.0 | 9.0 | 8.5 |
| 7 | **9.0** | **9.0** | **9.0** | **9.0** |

Round 7, by category: hierarchy, typography, spacing, consistency and clarity at 9 from all three; colour/contrast 9–9.5; iconography and character 9–9.5. The judges scored the references 6.0–8.5 in the same round (`gh pr list` highest).

## What changed

**One style layer** ([`fxcss/style.py`](fxcss/style.py)), used by every screen. Before this, colour and layout were decided separately in each command.
- Colour follows the terminal: on for a TTY, off when piped, under `NO_COLOR` or with `--no-colour`, and forced with `FORCE_COLOR`. Only the 16 ANSI colours plus bold and dim are used, so the user's terminal theme picks the shades.
- One glyph set (`✓ ! ✗ · ● →`) with ASCII fallbacks, always paired with a word.
- One status rule: the mark carries the colour, the word carries the weight. Bold yellow renders bright yellow on light terminals, so colour never sits on the word.
- Aligned `label  value` rows, bold sentence-case headings with a dim note, `~` paths, real plurals (no more `file(s)`), and wrapping that never splits a word.

**Per screen**
- `fxcss --help`: argparse's `{try,install,…}` brace list and the duplicate positional block are replaced by one grouped table, an Examples block and a one-line pointer. `fxcss <command> --help` is unchanged.
- Bare `fxcss`: uses the same groups, order and summaries as `--help`, from one `COMMANDS` table.
- `try --info`: facts in one aligned block, optional sheets packed into columns, setup rows marked `✓ automatic` / `! check`, README flags last and quiet, and a closing line naming the next command.
- `install`: the profile is settled first; the 30-sheet menu is three right-aligned columns; one prompt shows its default; prefs are listed once; a one-line consequence sentence; the question names both theme and profile.
- `profiles`: a title line, the shared profile folder named once, the default profile first, empty profiles on one line, and edits flagged with `!`.
- `watch`: a context line instead of an echoed title, dim instructions, and reload rows as `✓ time  files  duration`.
- `audit`: verdict first, a `✗ / ! / ·` status column ordered by consequence (RENAMED and UNDEFINED above the housekeeping heading), one file:line column, and the context and collection log reduced to two closing rows.
- `doctor`: a checklist with `✓ / ! / ✗`, lower-case aligned labels, words instead of Python reprs (`True`, `[1280, 480]`, `Darwin`), and a verdict that names what to know.

## Behaviour changes reviewers should know about

- `audit` no longer emits ANSI codes when its output is piped (it used to unless `--no-colour` was passed). `fxcss check` already passed `--no-colour`, and that switch is now scoped to the audit call ([cli.py `_run_audit`](fxcss/cli.py)).
- `audit` prints a transient progress line on a TTY instead of the per-state ids/classes table. The totals remain in the closing `checked` row.
- `audit` lists 5 NOT IMPORTED sheets and points to `--all` for the rest (it used to list 12).
- `install` asks which profile (when that is ambiguous) before the optional-stylesheet menu, not after it.
- `profiles` lists the default profile first, then the rest by name. `--json` output is unchanged.
- The checklist shows the `applied` state as **automatic**. Before installing, "applied" read as though it had already happened. The data model is unchanged.

## Beyond polish (left for you to decide)

- **A context line on the welcome screen** (`Firefox 155.0.1 · default-release · whitesur installed`). All three judges asked for it in rounds 4–7. It needs profile and Firefox detection on bare `fxcss`, which is a feature.
- **Collapsing `try --info`'s README flag table.** Asked for repeatedly, but `FlagLineTests` guards each flag with its description, so it stays as the last, quiet block.
- **Splitting optional stylesheets into tweaks and colour schemes**: this would rely on the `theme-` prefix heuristic.
- **Echoing the stylesheet choice when none is picked**: the judges disagreed.
- **Shortening repeated path prefixes in audit's file:line column**: these are paths people copy.
- **Highlighting slow reloads in `watch`.**

## Method

- **Judges**: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, run as independent read-only subagents with the same brief and screenshots. None saw the target score or each other's reviews. Opus is the same model that made the fixes; it judged from a fresh context with no access to the fix work.
- **References**: `gh` 2.102 (`--help`, `pr list`, `run list`), `uv` (`--help`, `python list`), Homebrew (`brew info ffmpeg`).
- **Capture**: VHS 0.12 with Menlo 15 px, about 102 columns. The seeded data was a WhiteSur checkout with three stale selectors, plus four Firefox profiles in a demo HOME, one of them an fxcss-managed install with an edited file. Firefox ran headless.
- **Rounds**: 7 after the baseline.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes: 691 tests, 1 skipped.
- [x] New `tests/test_terminal_style.py` covers plurals, column gutters, wrapping between words, the welcome and help screens at 80 and 100 columns, every command listed once, shared summaries, and the scope of `--no-colour`.
- [ ] Run `fxcss audit`, `fxcss doctor` and `fxcss install` in your own terminal theme, and check the piped output of `fxcss audit | cat`.

author: werner-scholtz
body:
The calendar reads the current time from `package:clock` when no `nowCallback` is set, so a test can set it with `withClock` or `fakeAsync`. This is the change from #644 by Jonas Wanke, with his commit kept as the first commit and the changes its review asked for on top. A clock that returns a UTC time is converted to local time in `currentTime`, `KalenderTime.now` and `kDefaultRange`, since `DateTime.now()` was always local. The device timezone is read from `DateTime.now()` again, because a fixed clock would report its own zone as the device's zone. The time indicator and the drag target read the time through `currentTime` as well. New tests cover a UTC clock with no location, and a widget test covers the week a default week view opens on and the day column of the time indicator under a fixed clock. In a widget test the calendar now follows the test's fake clock, so `tester.pump` with a duration moves the time indicator, which gets a Behavior Changes entry. author: tyler-builds
body:
Stacked on #52 (scenes). This is item 4 of the rune review: running a real app with no window, so agents and scripts can drive it and take screenshots without taking the keyboard focus or showing anything on the desktop.

### What it does
- **`JAMB_HEADLESS=1`** selects a new platform adapter, `internal/platform/headless`. Its windows exist only in memory, and the CPU renderer (`render/soft`) draws them, on Windows too. The app's platform functions now go through `app/headless.go`, which picks the headless adapter or the OS one. The OS backends' functions are renamed `os…`, with no other change.
- Everything else is the real app: `JAMB_SCRIPT`, `JAMB_SCENE`, `jamb ctl` (including `shot`), multiple windows and `jamb dev` restarts.
- **Same output on every machine:** a headless run uses the default platform settings (light mode, 100% text, animations on; the `JAMB_DARK`-style overrides still apply). `JAMB_HEADLESS_SCALE` sets the scale, 1 by default.
- **Leaves the system alone:** the clipboard is the process's own, file dialogs answer as canceled, message boxes answer with no button, and links and notifications are printed instead. No tray icon, jump list, recent document or AppID is registered. A single-instance app runs on its own instead of handing off to the user's running copy.
- **Pacing:** frames are drawn when something changes, and at 60 per second while something animates, on the real clock.

### Script additions
- `#KEY` in place of `X Y` in `move`, `click`, `rclick`, `down`, `up` and `scroll` aims at the element's center at the time the step runs (`click #save`). An unknown key stops the program with an error.
- `tree PATH` writes the accessibility tree as JSON, in the same node format as `jamb ctl tree`.

### Fixed
- `jamb dev` now stops the app on SIGTERM as well as Ctrl+C. Before, `kill` on `jamb dev` left the app running, and a headless app would keep running unseen.

### Usage
```
JAMB_HEADLESS=1 JAMB_SCENE=Notes/Many \
  JAMB_SCRIPT="idle; shot many.png; click #preview-toggle; idle; tree tree.json; exit" jamb dev
JAMB_HEADLESS=1 jamb dev &   # then drive it with jamb ctl
```
Docs: a new "Headless runs" section in `docs/tools.md`, two env var rows, and the script additions. Changelog fragment included.

### Not in this PR
Rune also has a virtual clock, video and strip export, and keycap overlays. Here, frames run on the real clock. A virtual clock would make `wait` instant and recordings exact, but it needs the host's frame time plumbed through `app`. I can do that as a follow-up if you want it.

### Testing
- `internal/platform/headless`: frame pacing, focus on open, `Open` outside `Run`, buffer and clipboard.
- `app`: `TestHeadlessRun` runs a real `app.Run` headless in a child process, with no display variables set. The script clicks a button twice by key, then checks the screenshot size at scale 2 and finds "Clicks: 2" in the JSON tree. Parser tests cover `#KEY` and `tree`.
- Manual runs, all headless on Linux:
  - `examples/hello`: clicked and screenshotted.
  - `examples/notes` under `jamb dev`: opened on `Notes/Many`, toggled the preview by key, and took a screenshot.
  - A live `jamb dev` driven by `jamb ctl scenes`, `scene`, `wait`, `shot` and `find`.
  - `kill` on `jamb dev`: no app process left behind.
- `go vet` passes for Linux and Windows (`GOOS=windows`). `gofmt`, vet with and without `-tags jambdev`, and tests pass on every module.

author: fabiodalez-dev
body:
Patch release 0.9.1.

## Problem

The updater treats a migration recorded in `migrations` as proof that its tables and columns exist. That is not always true:

- The 0.3.x updater split a migration on `;` and dropped every chunk that began with a `--` comment (`!preg_match('/^--/', $s)`). Installs it upgraded to 0.4.x recorded `migrate_0.4.0.sql` while most of its statements never ran.
- A file-only upgrade can skip migrations altogether.

On one production install upgraded from 0.3.x, after a clean 0.8.4 → 0.9.0 update, 51 columns of `schema.sql` were missing: `user_sessions`, `gdpr_requests` and `consent_log`, `utenti.privacy_accettata` (written by registration, so new readers could not register), and 23 `libri` columns from `migrate_0.4.6.sql` and `migrate_0.4.7.sql`, which were never recorded there.

## Change

- `App\Support\SchemaRepair` parses `installer/database/schema.sql`, creates every missing table (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, retried once for foreign keys to tables created later) and adds every missing column with its schema definition, after the previous schema column. It never drops, renames or alters anything, and leaves the indexes of existing tables alone. When `utenti.privacy_accettata` arrives late, readers with a recorded `data_accettazione_privacy` get `1`.
- `Updater::installUpdate()` runs it after the migrations; a failure is logged and does not fail the update.
- `public/index.php` runs it once per version, on the first request after `version.json` changes (marker `storage/.schema-repaired`, `GET_LOCK` against concurrent requests). This is needed because the update that installs 0.9.1 runs the 0.9.0 updater already loaded in memory, and it also covers file-only upgrades.
- No migration. Version 0.9.1, README lead and CHANGELOG entry.

## Tests

`tests/schema-repair-091.unit.php` builds a sandbox from `schema.sql`, reproduces the damage above (3 tables and 24 columns dropped), and checks:

- the repair restores them with the same type, default, comment and position;
- the privacy backfill applies only to readers with a recorded acceptance date;
- registration can write the column again;
- a second run adds nothing;
- the once-per-version marker and the lock work.

Removing the backfill or the column positioning fails the suite.

author: nooshu
body:
## Summary

**What changed**
- `.azure/pipelines/pr.yml` ("Install Playwright browsers (background)"): added `sudo -n apt-get -y -f install` after `dpkg --configure -a`, and expanded the comment to describe both repair steps.
- `apps/manage/scripts/playwright-install.mjs`: new `repairDpkg()` runs the same two commands before the install loop — this is the synchronous fallback path used by the "Wait for Playwright install" step and `npm run playwright:install`.

**Why**
Build 222396 (PR #336) failed in "Wait for Playwright install" with apt exit 100. The agent image had a killed kernel upgrade: `linux-azure` was unpacked but its dependency versions (`linux-headers-azure`/`linux-tools-azure`/`linux-cloud-tools-azure` 6.8.0-1070) were never fetched. The existing repair chain runs `dpkg --configure -a`, which finishes half-*configured* packages but cannot resolve *missing* versions — it left the package unconfigured and every subsequent `apt-get` (including `playwright install-deps`) exited with "Unmet dependencies. Try 'apt --fix-broken install'". `apt-get -f install` is exactly that repair: it installs the missing versions or removes what can't be satisfied, after which `install-deps` works normally.

**Advantages**
- Both Playwright install paths now survive the broken-apt image state, not just lock contention — the failure the pipeline already half-guards against.
- Non-fatal (`|| true` / `sudo -n`): no-op where apt is healthy or passwordless sudo is absent (local dev).

**Disadvantages / trade-offs**
- When the image is broken, `apt-get -f install` downloads the missing packages (kernel headers can be ~100MB) — bounded work in the backgrounded chain that overlaps `npm ci`.

**Risks**
- Low: worst case the repair can't fix the image and the install fails as it does today. `apt-get -f` with the lock-timeout drop-in still respects dpkg locking.

#### Test plan
- [x] `npm run format-prettier-check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run commitlint` — clean
- [x] `node --check apps/manage/scripts/playwright-install.mjs` — parses
- [ ] Pipeline green on this PR — the e2e job exercises the changed chain; if the agent image is healthy the repair is a no-op

**Feature 4: export. Implementation.** Change folder: [openspec/changes/thought-export](https://github.com/eskres/focus-funnel/tree/claude/feat-11-thought-export/openspec/changes/thought-export). The plan is #38. **Stacked on #44** (feature 3). This is the top of the built stack. Features 5–7 are **on hold** at your request; their plans stay in #40, #41 and #42. ## Story You can download all your thoughts from Settings, as JSON or Markdown. The **Export** card sits right above "Your data" and its delete options. Each thought includes: - title, summary and raw text; - tags and category; - status, and when it last changed; - its date; - filed and changed times; - origin; - additions. The download is owner-scoped and streamed in batches; nothing is written to disk on the server. It makes no provider call and contains no vectors. ## What changed - **One thought shape (decision 18).** `thought_view()` and `addition_view()` now build both `GET /api/thoughts/{id}` and the export. The GET still runs the same 4 statements, and a test pins that. - **`GET /api/me/export?format=json|markdown`:** - It reads keyset batches of 200, each in a short REPEATABLE READ session, and closes the request's session before streaming. - Response headers: - `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="focus-funnel-thoughts-.json|.md"` - `Cache-Control: no-store` - Leases: one running export per user and format, and at most 4 connected. A fifth gets 409 `export_running` (decision 21). - JSON: one document, one thought per line, with the count last (decision 22). - Markdown: - All data is escaped, and the summary is a block quote, so nothing from your data renders. - Raw text sits in an adaptive code fence and round-trips exactly. - Each tag is a code span (decision 31). - Web addresses stay clickable (decision 30). - A delete, ending the demo, or the demo session expiring stops a running export. The file then has no count line, so it never looks complete (decisions 20 and 29). - Every export logs one end line: `complete`, `failed` or `client_gone`. `app` loggers now go to stderr at INFO. - **Settings.** An Export card with "Download JSON" and "Download Markdown", downloading through a hidden frame (decision 26). - **Proxy.** - It refuses an export started by another site with 403, based on `Sec-Fetch-Site`, whatever the method. - It keeps the upstream `no-store`. - `safeReturnTo()` no longer lets a login return to `/api` or `/auth`, nor to a resolved path starting with `//` (decisions 27 and 32). ## Tasks: 17 of 19 done - [x] 1.1, 2.1–2.10, 3.1–3.2, 4.1–4.3, 6.1. - [x] **2.3, ticked after amending its check.** The by-hand clause expected the tab-indented test line, written without its protective reference, to render as a code block. markdown-it 14.1.0 renders it as a paragraph instead, because after `> ` a tab counts as only two columns. I narrowed the clause to the four-space line, as decision 24 explains. I then ran it by hand with markdown-it 14.1.0: - With their references, both lines render as `

` holding the stored text, with no ``. That holds both as the first quote line and after a blank one. - Without its reference, the four-space line renders as `

`.
- [ ] **5.1, end to end with a real key.**
  - The substitute run passed. It used Playwright and Chromium, with demo mode and a local fake model.
  - Design decision 28, which this task's note asked you to settle, is already settled by decision 30: addresses stay unescaped.
  - **For you:**
    1. Start the app with a real key and a tool-calling default model.
    2. Run steps 1–5 of task 5.1 in a browser.
    3. Check the JSON file with `python3 -m json.tool` and `grep -c embedding`.
    4. Open the `.md` file in a real viewer such as GitHub or VS Code, and confirm nothing in it renders.
- [ ] **5.2, a large store in real browsers.**
  - The substitute run passed:
    - 20,000 seeded thoughts.
    - A `curl --limit-rate 100k` export.
    - A second local origin standing in for a cross-site page.
    - Memory readings.
  - The 10,000-thought run peaked at about 3.8 MB of traced memory for 23 MB of JSON.
  - **For you, on the 5.1 app (not demo mode):**
    1. Run the "Download JSON" check in Firefox while the slow `curl` runs.
    2. Record the Chrome and Firefox versions.
    3. Run the cross-site check from a real `https://example.com` tab in Chrome.
    4. Note how long `curl` takes to exit after "Delete content".

## Decisions to look at (18–32, added during the build)
- **18:** the GET keeps its two reads, not the "one join" the plan describes. The statement count is unchanged.
- **20:** `stop_exports()` runs in `delete_user_by_id()` and `delete_user_content()`. Every caller stops and claims turns first, so a refused delete stops no export.
- **24:** a tab-led summary line keeps its `	` reference, which preserves the tab.
- **29:** a delete ends a slow download once the bytes already sent have drained.
- **30:** characters that are plain text inside a bare web address stay unescaped. Escaping them showed backslashes and broke links in GitHub and VS Code.

author: hardbyte
body:
A handler can return while its completion write is still queued or blocked. Removing that attempt from the heartbeat registry lets rescue run the job again before its first completion commits.

Keep the attempt registered through finalization and release it with a drop guard created before the finalizer-capacity wait. Finalizing attempts stop flushing progress. Heartbeats skip held closer locks, use a fresh statement snapshot to check closure evidence, and cannot recreate state for a closed claim. Legacy lease and canonical progress updates skip locked rows; skipped progress remains eligible for retry.

Validation: The stalled-finalizer regression uses a separate trigger gate after completion owns all of its attempt locks, then holds it for four five-second staleness windows. The identical fixture fails with duplicate executions before the heartbeat-retention fix and passes afterward on PostgreSQL 17 and 18, retaining durable-completion and exact-execution assertions. A measured WAL-sync delay let the earlier one-second fixture reach 1.315s of heartbeat age under contention; the new margin keeps that capacity limit separate from the retention invariant.

Required formatting, offline all-target/all-feature Clippy (-D warnings), and workspace build pass. Full CI is temporarily deferred while the approved release merge checks run.

No schema migration.

author: sidorares
body:
No transition ran on an anchored box. `anchor()` is the length it comes to (CSS Anchor Positioning 1, 3.2), and that's what a transition is about. But the cascade computes styles before layout works anchors out, so it saw `top: anchor(top)` before and after, and nothing changed. That held whether the anchor moved, a name moved to another element, the default anchor changed, or the box took a position option. Here, layout's resolved values reach a transition.

**What changed**
- **Layout hands placed values to a hook** (`PlacedTransition`, `layout/block.ts`). Once `layoutPositioned` has chosen an option and resolved its anchors, it passes the style the box was placed by, the option, and the fields an anchor function gave a value. Where the answer differs, the box is placed again at it. `getComputedStyle` reads it (`PLACED_STYLE`). What a layout keeps of the box's sizes is forgotten first: `layoutOwn` had kept the height of the placement a moment before. A box with no anchors or options is handed to the hook too, so a box taking an option later has somewhere to start from.
- **A second timeline** (`HtmlViewNode._anchoredTimeline`, on the document's clock) runs those transitions with the cascade's own algorithm: start, retarget, reverse, events. Its state is apart from the cascade's timeline, which would otherwise cancel them as it sees `anchor()` both sides. Only the fields an anchor gave a value, now or last time, take part, or every inset and size where the option changed, so a plain change the cascade already transitions doesn't run twice. Its frames are layouts. Its events go out with the others, and its pending starts begin at paint like the main timeline's.
- **A trap worth knowing.** The timeline was first called `_placed`, and core assigns a `_placed` of its own on every node (`nodes/animation.js`). Every page crashed at paint. AGENTS.md's warning about underscore names on a node subclass is real.

**WPT `css/css-anchor-position`, master vs this branch** (all 551 tests, two processes, no connection errors): 73.5% → 74.9%, eight up:
- `anchor-transition-001` 0/2 → 2/2; `-002`, `-003`, `-default`, `-name` 0/1 → 1/1; `-eval` 0/2 → 2/2
- `position-try-transition-basic` 0/2 → 2/2; `position-try-transition-flip` 0/2 → 2/2

`anchor-scroll-position-try-002` up and `-005` down are the pair whose second subtests flip with timing on master too.

**Not done:**
- `getAnimations()` doesn't list these transitions, so a page can't seek or cancel them.
- What's left among the transition tests is about other things: `scale` read from `getComputedStyle`, `display: none` transitions, and `::backdrop`.
- The docs paragraph overlaps #1343's; whichever merges second needs its sentence reconciled.

**Tests:** `test/html/positioned.test.ts` has the default anchor changing (`top` and an `anchor-size()` height half-way), the anchor moving, and a fallback taken as the containing block narrows. It fails with the hook turned off. The positioned, animations, scroll, values, refresh, scripts, subtree-build, html-elements and forms suites pass locally.

author: valentinherrmann
body:
Resolves #228.

## What changes for teachers

- **Exam step → Layout tab**, now in sections with a heading and ⓘ each (Cover page, Answer sheet, Writing space, LaTeX packages), two columns on wide screens:
  - **Paper**: squared (5 mm, default for new exams), lined (8 mm) or empty, as tiles. It applies to every writing space: the rest of the last page, extra pages, and the extra sheets.
  - **Heading and note** (default "Platz für weitere Lösungen"), printed on one line. They head the rest-of-page area and every extra page.
  - **Fill the rest of the last page** with min/max height. When not even the minimum fits, the area takes a whole new page.
  - **Extra pages (at least)** (0–20).
- **Grade in Examance** switch at the top of the Layout tab, for teachers who only create the exam here and grade on paper:
  - When off, the exam prints no corner markers, page codes, cut lines or sticker spots, and page 1 gets a name line. Their room is kept, so nothing else moves.
  - **Box for a results QR code** keeps one sticker box on page 1, e.g. to send results with DiRueLei.
  - Scan upload and personalised copies are greyed out with the reason. The scan template is no longer prepared after compiling, so no failure message. Paper grading and Statistics stay available.
- **Printed copies always fill whole sheets** with extra pages: an even page count double-sided, a multiple of 4 as a booklet, following the print type on the Print step. The filler-page setting is gone. The Exam step's preview shows the exam without these pages; the Print step shows them.
- **Exercises tab**: the order, page-break and MC-group help sits behind ⓘ, with a summary line (items, points) and an "Add exercises" tile when the list is empty.
- **Print step**: the **Extra sheet (stock)** card is always there, and "Create print files" makes it too. It is one double-sided sheet with no exam title and a code that says only "extra sheet". One printed stack serves every exam.
- **Scanning**:
  - Extra sheets and stickered loose paper go after the student's exam pages. Extra paper scanned later is appended to the student's existing scan instead of creating a second submission. Loose pages give an info note.
  - **Uncut booklet sheets** are recognised from any scanner: a landscape scan whose two halves both carry a page code is read as two pages, also when the scanner stored it rotated, scaled or cropped. Before, such scans reported missing pages and failed MC detection. The raw scan stays attached to the student's scan.
- **Paper grading** now saves the scores of students entered on the Students page who have no scan yet. Before, their scores were lost on tab change.
- **Preview "outdated" fix**: editing an exercise from the Exam step now marks the preview as outdated.
- **Boxed tiles for every setting choice** (Layout tab, Print step, Send to students, Check MC, Archive, export dialog):
  - on/off settings become toggle tiles, or two tiles with a short line each where both cases need explaining (name line, page codes, graded PDFs double-sided);
  - text fields everywhere share the tile look.
- **Every exam form saves itself**, with "Saving… / Saved" in its header: the Layout and Exercises tabs, the Overview details, the grading key on Statistics and the Print step.
  - The Save/Discard buttons, the grading key's "not saved" prompt and the "unsaved changes" prompts on the Exam step and Overview are gone. Leaving a page saves a waiting edit.
  - Fixes the Layout tab hanging on "Saving…" when you kept typing during a save.
- **Booklets that come out centred**:
  - Sheets Examance arranges carry a thin line exactly on the fold, with ticks at top and bottom, so you cut and fold on it instead of measuring from the paper edge.
  - If a printer prints off-centre, **Shift (mm)** (±10 mm, saved with the exam) moves every A3 sheet. A two-sided **Test sheet** with a ruler shows the value: fold it edge to edge and read where the crease crosses the ruler.
  - The print instructions now say: print at 100 %, without "fit to page" or centring.
- **More scissors**: six along each booklet fold line. The corner cut line, with two scissors, is now on every page of the plain sheet, not only on personalised copies.

## Implementation notes

- Migration `0060_exam_extra_paper`:
  - adds `paper_style` and `extra_pages`;
  - sets `paper_style = squared` where `extra_notes` is set;
  - **drops `padding_pages`**. Older clients that still send it are ignored, since the schema doesn't forbid extra fields.
  - `extra_notes` gains `fill` (absent = true).
- Migration `0061_exam_booklet_offset`: `booklet_offset_mm` (float, −10…10, default 0). It is in the header fields (PATCH, duplicate) and the account export.
- Migration `0062_exam_digital_grading`: `digital_grading` (default true) and `results_qr_box` (default false). They are in the same places as `booklet_offset_mm`, plus the ZIP manifest. `printSettingsOf` forces sticker mode when digital grading is off, and `ExamPreviewPanel` skips the OMR template.
- `docs/openapi.json` is regenerated.
- `Schulaufgabe.sty`:
  - one `fuellen` option; `fuellleer` and `fuellplatz` remain accepted aliases;
  - filler pages are `\SA@extrapage` writing pages, which draw their pattern at shipout;
  - `\EN@head` puts the note on the heading line;
  - `\SA@scissors` is the one scissors shape;
  - new `ohnescan` option skips the fiducials, the corner tab, the fold zone, the page codes and the sticker spots at shipout, keeping their room. The QR box becomes an empty strut unless `ergebnisqr` is set.
- Scan ingest:
  - `isLandscape` and `isA3Landscape` read the page through its `/Rotate`;
  - `splitA3` splits along the displayed width and keeps the rotation;
  - `ScanPass.halvesCoded` decides on non-A3 landscape pages.
- Paper grading: `scoreService.submissionForStudent` creates the empty submission on the first score. `createStudentWithSubmission` reuses it, and `ScoreGrid` calls it before a save when the student has none.
- `buildExamLatex(…, { fill })`: the Exam step compiles a `draft` cache variant without the filling pages.
- `utils/autosave.ts` `createAutosave` and `ui/SaveStatus` are the one autosave helper and its status line, added to the reuse map in `frontend/CLAUDE.md`. The leave guards in the content and overview routes and their strings are removed.
- `qr/booklet.ts`: `imposeBooklet(pdf, n, offsetMm)` draws the fold mark. `bookletTestSheet` is new. `printFileKey` includes the shift.
- `help/SectionHeading` is shared by the Print step and the Exam step tabs. `OptionTile` gained `type="checkbox"`. `controlClass` restyles every text input app-wide.
- SonarCloud cleanup:
  - `classifyCodes` and `bookletTestSheet` are split into helpers;
  - the offset parsing no longer stringifies objects;
  - the extra sheet's LaTeX uses `String.raw`;
  - the two intentionally sequential awaits are marked.
- Content stamps of existing exams change once, because the print settings lost a field, so made print files show as outdated after the update.

## Verification

- Passed: `svelte-check --threshold error` (0 errors), eslint on the changed files, ruff, mypy, the OpenAPI export and `docs:build`.
- Playwright `layout.spec.ts`: desktop and phone, 18 of 18 passed (earlier commit).
- Tests run and passing:
  - backend `test_refactor_contracts`, including round-trip tests for the booklet offset and the digital-grading switch;
  - frontend:
    - `scoreService`, with a new regression test: a listed student without a scan gets a submission that keeps their scores;
    - `scanPdf`, with a new regression test for a rotated A3 scan;
    - `printLayout`, with a new test for digital grading off;
    - `autosave`, `extraNotesKey`, `booklet`, `scanIngest`, `examPreview` and `locale`.
- **Not done**:
  - no LaTeX compile, since no TeX engine was available in the session;
  - no screenshot of the Grade in Examance switch.
- Please check:
  - the Exam step preview without filling pages;
  - the Print step sheet filled

author: wqaed401
body:
L5e of the L5 series (the engine runs in its Worker): the capture, file store and lock services answer over the engine bridge. Based on `runtime-v2` after #1856 (L5b). Build plan: L5e HEAD 0 r6, approved by orchestrator 2. No behaviour change for players.

Refs #1144 (milestone Runtime 2). Witness: B-resource.

## Scope

- **Ops** (`player/engine-bridge/ops/resources.ts`): `answerCapture`, `answerFileStore`, `answerLock`.
  - Each wraps its adapter function on the host's session and publishes. A refusal publishes unchanged, so the earlier basis stays accepted.
  - Arguments are checked exactly: `actionId` a non-negative safe integer, `answer` a plain record, `held` null or a table.
  - A capture answer must be exactly `captured {reference}` or `unavailable {reason}`. The adapter turns any other kind into an unavailable camera and drops extra keys, so without this check the engine could not refuse a malformed answer. File store and lock answers reach the engine as their payload, which it validates as before.
- **`holds` answered in advance** (`player/engine-bridge/held-media.ts`):
  - The engine asks `CapturedMediaAdmission.holds(reference, kind)` only while it resolves an answer's payload, and only about the references inside it (`actions/capture.ts:59`, `file-store.ts:475`, `lock.ts:684`/`:700`).
  - So the service asks its store about each of those references, for all four kinds, and sends the kinds held (`heldMedia`). The host answers the engine from that table (`admissionOf`); anything not listed is not held.
  - `held: null` (the fallback answers) passes no admission, as before, so the recorder's query log is unchanged.
  - The table is indexed once per answer, so an answer that stores many files stays linear. Sol r1's probe on an ordinary `fromJson` of 8,000 / 16,000 files: 42 / 77 ms (418 / 1,485 ms before; its probe `held-scale-large.mjs`).
  - L5c's `askImage` answer will import this module (orchestrator 2, D1).
- **Services** (`session-camera.ts`, `stored-files.ts`, `lock-service.ts`): each observe → answer chain is one section of the session (L5b's `section`, with its in-section observation).
  - The camera, Blob and crypto work runs before the section, unchanged.
  - Nothing can recall a posted request. So whether to answer is decided right before each send, with no await in between (`#current`: not stopped, same key, same generation). The same check runs after every reply, before any bookkeeping.
  - Refusals: a `basis` refusal keeps the answer for the next service; `session` settles the key; `halted` (the stop) does nothing more. Every other error propagates, as before.
  - After `invalidPayload`, the fallback becomes the key's answer, so a retry offers the fallback, not a second photo, and the diagnostic shows once.
  - `SessionCamera`, `answerFileStore`, the lock dialogs and `LockService`'s crypto work are unchanged. Only `LockService.#service` changes; the ask/work split stays.
- **Publication:** what the services send shows through `publishOwned` (`usePlayerSession.ts`, `serviceSection`'s `send` passes it as the request's publish hook, in the same tick as the store applies the reply). The hosts lose `observe` and `publish`.
- **Inventory:** the six L5e entries leave `RATCHET` (three adapter imports, three `hatch` imports), and `COMPLETED_FAMILIES` gains `L5e`. `ADAPTER_EXPORTS` is unchanged.

## Hunks outside L5b's L5e file table

- `player/vue/src/usePlayerSession.ts`: the three service host literals lose `observe`/`publish` (6 lines), and `serviceSection`'s `send` passes the `publishOwned` hook (3 lines). Shared with L5c/L5d as an ordinary rebase (D3).
- `player/player-bridge.ts`: `refusalCode(error)`, used by all three services, and `ServiceSection.send`'s comment.
- `player/engine-bridge/ops/session.ts`: `sessionOp` and `publishing` are exported for the other families' op modules, with no other change.

## Tests

body:
Fixes `menu-key --expect-kind usage-menu` against the layout the pinned Cursor 2026.10.14 client really renders (live 80x24 capture, helper e753cb71): the typed draft FIRST, two blank rows, the inline menu BELOW it with the selected row arrow-marked, and no status footer while the menu is open. The merged gate expected the selected row ABOVE the draft and a status tail, and refused the live screen (screen-mismatch, nothing sent).

Static derivation (pinned `7000.index.js`): the prompt column renders the input box (draft) first, then the menu box (height = rows shown, page size 10), and the model/status footer only when no menu overlay is active; the menu list renders one row per item (`↑ more above`, items, `↓ more below`), descriptions cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped; the selected row is `→ `, the rest two spaces. This matches the capture.

Gate (usage-menu only; run-everything-menu is unchanged, follow-up): expected text is the bare draft then the selected row, in render order. On the visible screen each appears once; 1 to 3 blank rows separate them; the menu is a block of at most 10 consecutive nonblank rows with exactly one arrow-marked row (the expected one); nothing below the block, and the last pane row blank. The expected selected row must be IN the block exactly once (a copy of it elsewhere on the screen does not count). Every other block row must be a menu row (starts with `/`) or the scroll row `↑ more above` (first) / `↓ more below` (last); a status or model row directly under the menu refuses. The one-key rule, fresh receipt, owned pid, unspent ledger, last-moment recheck, history/duplicate/modal/identity refusals are unchanged.

Live-input binding on this path, stated plainly: the old cursor_y == last row rule is NOT carried over, and nothing replaces it for the cursor. The retained capture has no cursor_y and the source does not fix it, so I did not invent one. What binds the live input instead is layout-relative: the draft row exists once, the menu (which the client renders only for a focused slash draft) sits directly below it with exactly one marked row, nothing follows it. The last-blank-row rule is kept. A test shows the gate is independent of cursor_y (0, 17, 23).

Fixture: the retained live capture, 55 rows (31 history + 24 visible). Layout rows are verbatim; the answered trust box in history keeps its shape with an example path; transcript text is replaced by synthetic lines.

Tests: full file 162 OK (exit 0, final head); UsageKeyTests 22 + the new witnesses. Cases: positive on the real capture and on scrolled menus (more above/below); wrong row, another command, run-everything menu, argument draft, no menu, menu above the draft, 0 or 4 blank rows between (the 4-row case ends on a blank last row so only the gap check refuses), two marked rows, duplicates, 11-row block, status/model row under the menu, output below a blank row with a blank last row (only the rest-below check refuses), loading text, plain composer, copies in history and transcript, prompt before and after the approval is spent, row replaced, menu closed.

body: ## Problem The current resources hub layout wastes screen space - chat is cramped in a small box (~40% viewport height) while most of the screen is unused. ## Solution Created 4 alternative layout options that maximize screen real estate and make better use of available space. ## Layouts Available ### 1. **Sidebar Navigation** (`?layout=sidebar`) - Vertical navigation on left (60-80px) - Chat takes 90%+ of viewport height - Clean, app-like feel - **Best for:** Desktop power users ### 2. **Messenger Style** (`?layout=messenger`) - Thin header with icon tabs - Content uses 95% of viewport height - Mobile-first, feels like WhatsApp/iMessage - **Best for:** Mobile, simplicity, PWA ### 3. **Split Dashboard** (`?layout=split`) - 70/30 split screen layout - Chat on left, quick info panel on right - Shows countdown, phase, today's tip, navigation - **Best for:** Desktop, always-visible context ### 4. **Floating Tabs** (`?layout=floating`) - Full immersion, content uses entire screen - Bottom floating tab bar (iOS/Android pattern) - Maximizes chat space (90%+ viewport) - **Best for:** PWA, mobile, immersive experience ### 5. **Original** (`?layout=original`) - Current implementation (kept for reference) ## How to Test Visit `/resources` with query parameter: - `/resources?layout=sidebar` - `/resources?layout=messenger` - `/resources?layout=split` - `/resources?layout=floating` - `/resources?layout=original` **Or use the layout switcher** in the bottom-right corner to instantly toggle between all options. ## Comparison | Layout | Chat Height | Wasted Space | Mobile | Desktop | |--------|-------------|--------------|--------|---------| | Original | ~40% | ❌ High | ✅ OK | ⚠️ Cramped | | Sidebar | ~90% | ✅ Minimal | ⚠️ OK | ✅ Great | | Messenger | ~95% | ✅ Minimal | ✅ Perfect | ✅ Good | | Split | ~85% | ✅ Low | ⚠️ Collapses | ✅ Great | | Floating | ~90% | ✅ Minimal | ✅ Perfect | ✅ Good | ## Files Added - `components/resources-hub-sidebar.tsx` - Sidebar layout - `components/resources-hub-messenger.tsx` - Messenger layout - `components/resources-hub-split.tsx` - Split dashboard layout - `components/resources-hub-floating.tsx` - Floating tabs layout ## Files Modified - `app/resources/page.tsx` - Added layout switching logic and switcher UI ## Next Steps 1. Test all layouts on desktop and mobile 2. Decide which layout(s) to keep 3. Make chosen layout the default 4. Remove unused layout options (or keep switcher for user preference) ## Screenshots Needed Once deployed, please test and provide feedback on which layout feels best for: - Desktop browsing - Mobile browsing - PWA installed experience Current recommendation: **Messenger** for mobile/PWA, **Sidebar** for desktop.

author: sargekhan
body:
## Problem

On `@hyperswarm/rpc` ≤ 3.5.0 a pooled client to a peer that was down when the
client was created never recovers. With a capability (the path this facility
uses) the stream never opens, `_rpc` is never created and `close` is never
emitted, so the pool keeps a client that throws `RPC client closed` on every
request until the calling process is restarted. Any worker restart wedges its
callers.

Fixed in holepunchto/rpc#20, released as 3.5.1.

## Fix

Require `@hyperswarm/rpc` `^3.5.1` so a fresh install cannot resolve the broken
version, and refresh the lockfile to match. No code change.

## Testing

Reproduced against 3.5.0 with a standalone testnet script (server child
restarted while a client polls through the pool); the pooled client recovers on
3.5.1.

author: enesonus
body:
The Go SDK has fallen behind the TypeScript SDK, leaving Go integrations to write protocol frames for app monitoring and other newer capabilities. This ports SDK APIs and helpers from [TypeScript v0.69.1 at `319078e`](https://github.com/limrun-inc/typescript-sdk/tree/319078ef75a7f8a4e1abf36b73570ff11064453d) into Go while retaining existing Go library entry points. It covers simulator and emulator controls, persistent app monitoring with crash and hang details, log streams, REST resources, snapshots, Xcode and Gradle execution, RBE, file sync, and network tunnels with inspection and HAR output.

The [examples index](https://github.com/limrun-inc/go-sdk/blob/codex/typescript-sdk-parity/examples/README.md) maps all 18 TypeScript example directories to their Go equivalents, with setup, outputs, and instance cleanup documented. SDK provisioning and supported instance operations are in Go. React frontends remain unchanged; Appium, Playwright, Detox, and the optional MCP transport retain their JavaScript integrations. Detox still requires a TypeScript instance client through its separate package. Publishing and device installation keep the original CLI workflows, with Go backends for scoped tokens, signing-secret storage, and authenticated build webhooks. The standalone CLI and browser libraries are not ported to Go.

SDK validation passed with the full local mock-backed suite, the race detector, Go 1.22, and `go vet`. Tests include TypeScript-derived protocol, HAR, ignore-rule, and workspace fixtures, plus WebSocket and SSE lifecycle checks. The REST audit covers 431 fields across 84 interfaces; a checked-in OpenAPI fixture makes the mock tests reproducible.

Example validation includes all Go builds and vet checks, race tests, Go 1.22 tests, all three frontend production builds, adapter syntax/import checks, and an MCP tool call against a mock build endpoint. Local tests exercise detached CLI workflows, signing-profile selection, webhook authentication, and exact-asset authorization after a successful install build. No live cloud, device, or store-publishing runs were performed.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large surface-area API and protocol expansion with new token minting, remote build/exec flows, and reworked asset uploads increases integration risk though changes are accompanied by generated REST tests and targeted build helpers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **High-level:** Ports the TypeScript v0.69.1 surface into Go, expanding REST coverage, instance control models, and long‑running execution helpers while refreshing developer docs and examples.
> 
> **REST & client wiring:** Adds **AccessTokens**, **Analytics**, **ScopedTokens**, **Xcode/Gradle instance** and snapshot services, default HTTP setup via `defaultHTTPClient` (header timeout + proxy‑aware transport), optional `LIMRUN_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, and safer ID routing with `url.PathEscape`. Android/iOS resources gain richer specs (roles, tunnels, stream tokens, termination reasons), `Update` flows with `If‑Match`, and session artifact helpers.
> 
> **Assets:** New kind/platform metadata, TTL/expiry controls, list filters, `PATCH` updates, signed upload URL helper, and a rewritten `GetOrUpload` that hashes in memory, honors optional progress callbacks, and reuses shared upload metadata types.
> 
> **Build & remote sandboxes:** Introduces the `build` package with Xcode/Gradle daemon clients, streaming exec follower, TestFlight/Play/XCTest event parsing, RBE lifecycle helpers, Bazel workspace renderers, and WebSocket tunnel bootstrapping—backed by focused unit tests.
> 
> **Docs & examples:** Replaces `api.md` with a parity guide, expands README requirements/monitoring guidance, and reorganizes `examples/` to mirror the TS catalog with new walkthroughs for tunnels, recordings, Appium, etc.
> 
> **Risks:** Broad API/schema churn plus new privileged endpoints (`access_tokens`, analytics) and remote execution paths warrant careful integration review despite thorough mock-backed tests.
>

body:
Chunk 9 of the accessibility plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-05-accessibility.md`): an automatic check. It's from `main` and independent of #132 (chunk 8).

**What it adds:**
- **`e2e/axe.spec.ts`** runs axe-core over setup and every page in `PAGES`, in light and in dark. It checks against the WCAG 2.0–2.2 A and AA rules axe can judge on its own: contrast, names, labels, ARIA, lists and ids.
- A serious or critical finding fails the run. The checks are soft, so one run lists every page's findings, each with its rule and up to three elements.
- What axe can't judge stays with the specs and the phone try: where the focus goes, whether a name makes sense, and what is read out.

**The dependency (Roshan's OK, 06-11-2026):**
- `@axe-core/playwright` **4.14.0**, pinned as a dev dependency. It was released 15-10-2026 and only the specs use it.
- It brings `axe-core` 4.14.0, which was already in the lockfile through `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`.
- The lockfile was updated without a local install, as Roshan chose: the install was queued behind another session's long e2e gate on the heavy lane. The new entry is the registry's own metadata (version, tarball, integrity), and `npm ci --dry-run` accepts it.
- Because of that, the spec isn't typechecked locally: the package isn't installed in this worktree. CI's checks job typechecks it.

**Map and notes:**
- The spec is in `e2e/affected-map.json` for every route, so a change to any page runs it; the map's unit test passes.
- CLAUDE.md lists the package and what the check covers.

**Expected:** this first run is where axe reports what it finds. I'll fix the findings in this PR, or name any I'd rather leave, with the reason.

body:
The New project and New sub-project dialogs built their choices from the workspace's copy of the roster, the teams and the projects the person leads, and the app placed a new project by counting the siblings it held.

This moves both dialogs onto the server's pickers and project lists, which shipped in v0.1.129 and v0.1.134. The Lead fields read `projectSettings.leadCandidates` 25 at a time with a search, for the home organization in New project and for the chosen parent in New sub-project, starting on the creator. Project access reads `projectSettings.candidates` without a project and with the chosen lead, teams first and then people, 25 at a time with the server's search and Load more, and keeps the checked choices by name in a Selected group through searches, batches and the popover closing; the browser filters, sorts and counts nothing, and organization admins are offered as the server offers them. The New sub-project dialog checks its parent live with `projectSettings.get`, says why a parent cannot take a sub-project, offers another parent from `projectSettings.projects` with `sub_project_parents` in that parent's organization, 25 at a time with a search and equal names tagged, and reads its Lead with that parent. Create is enabled only from what the server answered: a parent the check says may take a sub-project, and a lead that is the creator's seat or a popover pick. A create sends the organization of the dialog that showed the parent and the creator's seat there, paints only where the workspace holds the parent, and the app moves into a new sub-project only once the workspace holds it. The store's roster helpers the dialogs no longer call go, and Settings › Projects offers New sub-project from the row's own right alone.

author: gracedeternalkingcabbageman
body:
blindrawtransaction, with its default ignoreblindfail=true, returned an
issuance without reissuance tokens with its amount explicit when nothing
in the transaction could balance its blinding. Confidentiality is the
holder's choice per transfer, so a blinding the caller asked for is never
dropped silently: the call now fails with the error that names the
missing confidential output, whatever ignoreblindfail says.

An issuance without tokens carries no blinding mark in the transaction
(rawissueasset's blind flag only affects token derivation), so
blindrawtransaction's blind_issuances, true by default, is the request.
A caller that wants the issuance explicit passes blind_issuances=false;
feature_issuance's explicit-issuance case now does.

Neither consensus nor block production: wallet RPC only.

Closes #293.

Proof: `wallet_raw_issuance_transparent` (both wallet types) fails on master at the new default-call case (`No exception raised`) and passes here; `feature_issuance`, `feature_confidential_transactions`, `wallet_blinded_change` pass.

author: jorgensandhaug
body:
## What

A running startup step in the chat timeline now says how long it has been running, and a running environment setup step names the environment.

- `StartupPhaseItem` gets an optional `subject`; the projection sets it from `payload.rigName` on `rig.setup.*` events and clears it when a later attempt replaces the row.
- A running setup step with a name reads "Setting up {name}" (new message key `timeline.platformActivityPresentation.settingUpNamedSandboxEnvironment`). Without a name, or once settled, the existing titles are unchanged.
- While a startup step runs, its title ends in the elapsed time, formatted by the existing `formatElapsed` and ticking once a second, the same way the turn header shows " · 41s". The right edge stays clean while running (the timeline's chip doctrine); a settled step keeps its final duration chip. No public API change.
- Web (`platform-activity-row.tsx`) and iOS (`react-native` `activity.tsx`) both change. On iOS the existing `useLiveNow` clock moved from `turn.tsx` to `primitives.tsx` so both rows share it (`turn.tsx` still exports it).

## Why

In a staging chat with a repository and a custom environment attached, environment setup took 66 s while the timeline showed only "Setting up sandbox environment" with no time, so the chat looked stuck. This makes a slow setup visibly progressing and says which environment is being set up. Speeding the setup itself is in #7221 (the first model request no longer waits on it) and #7228 (prebuilt environment templates on compute).

Known limit: when an environment's database row is gone mid-session, the worker's display-name fallback is the word "rig", so the row would read "Setting up rig". That fallback is also used in model-visible text, so it is left unchanged here.

## Tests

- `packages/react/test/timeline.test.ts`: the projection carries the environment name as `subject`, and a later attempt's row drops the old name.
- `packages/react/test/timeline-renderers.test.tsx`: a running row reads "Setting up cloudgeni · 41s", then "· 42s"; the settled row shows the settled title and the "1m 06s" chip.
- `packages/react-native/test/tool-output-preview.test.tsx`: the same on iOS, asserting the time counts up rather than an exact second.
- These fail on the old source. Two react tests ("explicit image-activity collapse… rolling=true" and "compacting before the first model request…") fail on main as well on the shared test machine and pass elsewhere; they are unrelated.

The static "Includes overlapping sandbox startup…" note on the model preparation step is unchanged.
