body:
## Summary

This draft PR adds the first implementation pass for the requested NutriAI improvements.

### Analytics
- Fix analytics to use the populated `/api/nutrition-analytics` endpoint instead of the missing `/api/analytics` route.
- Add daily, weekly, and 30-day views.
- Use the user's saved macro targets.
- Calculate average intake over days with recorded food logs.
- Improve the analytics page heading and tracking-consistency summary.
- Add an opt-in AI period analysis for daily, weekly, and monthly date ranges.
- Reuse cached AI summaries and invalidate them when the underlying logged-food totals change.
- Limit new analytics AI generations to three per Philippine day; charts and logging do not depend on AI.

### AI monitoring
- Add AI usage event storage.
- Record successful, failed, quota-limited, and cached activity for the centralized Gemini client and key AI endpoints.
- Estimate input/output tokens from text length (clearly labeled estimates).
- Add an admin AI usage page with daily activity, cached responses, failures, quota errors, token estimates, and per-user totals.
- Add an admin dashboard shortcut and explicit user/admin role fields.

### Food tracking
- Add piece-based serving units alongside grams, milliliters, and servings.
- Standardize the custom-food unit picker to those core units.
- Validate food-log nutrition values and remove fabricated macro fallbacks.
- Improve edited food-log validation and amount conversion.
- Preserve existing searchable Open Food Facts and custom-food database functionality.

## Notes / verification needed
- AI usage monitoring starts collecting data after deployment; it does not backfill historical Gemini requests.
- Estimated tokens are approximate, not Google's official token counts.
- To expose the admin page, set the intended administrator account's `role` to `admin` (or `isAdmin` to `true`) in MongoDB.
- This PR has not been run through `npm run build` or `npm run lint` in this environment. Please run both locally and test food logging, edits, daily/weekly/monthly analytics, and admin monitoring before merging.
- The app's existing authentication approach is not redesigned in this feature pass.

author: phj2000
body:
Fixes #987.

Included non-structured arguments currently always use Jackson object serialization. Add the opt-in `writeNonStructuredArgumentsAsString` property, with the name and `false` default suggested in [the issue discussion](https://github.com/logfellow/logstash-logback-encoder/issues/987#issuecomment-2254248677).

When enabled together with `includeNonStructuredArguments`, it writes each non-null non-structured argument as a JSON string using `toString()`. Null arguments remain JSON null. Leaving the option disabled retains the existing JSON object serialization. Structured arguments, inclusion flags, argument indexes, field prefixes and wrapping retain their behavior.

Expose the property on `ArgumentsJsonProvider`, `LogstashFormatter`, `LogstashEncoder` and `LogstashLayout`, and document both standard and composite configuration. For a standard encoder:

```xml
<encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder">
    <includeNonStructuredArguments>true</includeNonStructuredArguments>
    <writeNonStructuredArgumentsAsString>true</writeNonStructuredArgumentsAsString>
</encoder>
```

For a composite encoder/layout, configure the two properties on its `arguments` provider.

Validation on Linux with JDK 17 and the repository's Maven wrapper:

- The same 17 focused tests compile and run on both versions: base has 2 failures, 9 errors and 6 passing controls; the patched version passes all 17. The XML cases show the old encoder reading bean properties; the reflection cases demonstrate the missing public configuration property without a base compilation failure.
- The new cases cover string/number/boolean/list/null values, escaping, structured and excluded arguments, wrapping/prefixes, all four public entry points, actual layout output, and real standard/composite XML configuration.
- With the default Jackson 3.2.4 dependencies, `clean install` passes all 642 tests with no failures, errors or skips. The license and Checkstyle checks, Javadoc and packaging also succeed.

author: el-bri-ga
body:
Fixes #2025.

## What was wrong

After a start that rotated the storage id, `UncleanStart::led_before` reads the copy's ballot: one naming this broker, at a generation this process did not open, counts as "the copy it led before the crash". The broker's own candidacy writes exactly that ballot. A broker that only followed before the crash, stood after it and lost (or was still fencing), then refused every newer candidate's fence in `refuse_short_copy` and gave the generation up on disk. With the leader's broker down in a set of three, the two remaining copies are the only majority, so the shard stalled until the control plane came back.

A second path ends the same way: a copy that is unvouched after the crash (followed at an older generation, nothing shipped since) could stand, and if it won, `may_lead` refused it and gave the generation up, after which `gave_up()` refused everyone too.

## The fix

- `UncleanStart::stand` is called by the candidate (`stand` and `restand` in `election/candidate.rs`) right before it writes its own ballot. It records the generation together with what the copy said about the crash before the first such ballot: led before (or given up), and the generation it had followed. Later candidacies carry that forward.
- `led_before` and `unvouched` read that record when the current ballot is one this process wrote, instead of reading the candidate's own ballot.
- The candidate does not stand on a copy `unvouched` says the open would refuse to lead.

## Safety argument

`led_before` exists so that a broker whose copy may be short of what it acknowledged as leader neither leads from that copy nor counts as a vote for it. The rule is unchanged for every ballot the crash could have left. Only ballots this process provably wrote are read differently, and for those the old answer is kept.

1. The evidence is the ballot (or give-up mark) on disk when the process starts. Without a newer leader being accepted, the only thing that can replace it is a ballot naming this broker, written by this process.
2. `stand` records only while its generation is above the accepted one. Accepted generations only grow, so a recorded `(generation, this broker)` can match only a ballot written after the record, in this process. A ballot naming this broker that was never recorded, whether from before the crash or from an earlier process, is still read as led before, as on main.
3. Before the first own ballot, `stand` evaluates the unchanged rule (`led_before || gave_up`) on the ballot the crash left and stores the result. `led_before` returns that stored answer for as long as the ballot is the process's own. A copy it led stays refused after it stands, and is still given up on disk when a fence comes, as on main (`a_copy_led_before_stays_led_after_it_stands`). Only a copy whose crash-time ballot named another leader, or none, now answers.
4. `unvouched` keeps the generation the copy followed before standing, so the candidacy cannot turn a follower copy that nothing has shipped to into one the open accepts.
5. The record is kept in memory only. A later restart reads the self-naming ballot on disk as led before again, which is the conservative reading. An unclean restart starts with an empty record.
6. The candidacy gate only takes ballots away. Pre-vote answers are unchanged.

So the broker acts on evidence (the ballot the crash left) and never on its own later ballot. Voting more often makes the only difference, and only for copies the unchanged rule already treated as followed.

## Tests

- `a_copy_that_stood_after_an_unclean_start_takes_a_newer_fence` (replica/tests/fence.rs) reproduces the stall: before the fix the newer candidate's fence is refused with `Unavailable` ("this broker led the shard before a crash ...").
- `its_own_candidacy_is_not_a_copy_it_led`, `a_copy_led_before_stays_led_after_it_stands`, `a_standing_overtaken_by_a_newer_ballot_records_nothing` (unclean/tests.rs).
- `an_unvouched_copy_does_not_stand` (election/candidate/tests.rs).
- I reverted the fix (`own_ballot` returning `None`, gate off) and three of the new tests failed. They pass again with the fix restored.

## Spec

`FelixShard.tla` gains `UncleanCrashes`, `OwnBallotLedBefore`, a `doubt` variable, `UncleanRestart` and `RefuseOpen` (the `may_lead` give-up). Ship now vouches for the copy. With the knobs off, every existing config is unchanged.

| Config | Outcome | States | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| FelixShardElectLiveUnclean (fixed rule, CpDown, storage ids, unclean restart) | passes ElectionSettles | 29,352 | 3 s |
| FelixShardElectLiveUncleanOwnBallot (main's rule) | violates liveness, as expected | 15,336 | 2 s |
| FelixShardElectLiveUncleanLed (the restart can hit the leader, a candidate still fencing, or one that stood, and loses any suffix; no fail-stop; no detector misfires) | passes ElectionSettles + NoStandAgainstHeardLeader | 503,556 | 71 s |
| FelixShardElectUnclean (safety, two writes, with `VouchOnGeneration`) | passes OneLeaderPerGeneration, AckedHeldByLeader, AckedAgree | 11,060,578 | 9 min 47 s |
| FelixShardElectUncleanVouchOnShip (the code today: any batch vouches) | violates AckedHeldByLeader, pinned to #2029 | 2.28M at violation | 82 s |
| FelixShardElectUncleanForgetsLed (no refusal) | violates AckedHeldByLeader | 22k | 2 s |
| FelixShardElectLive, FelixShardElect, FelixShardLeaderCrashGivesUp, FelixShardFencedLeaderCrash | pass | | |

A crash between `stand` and the ballot write leaves nothing on disk, so the model treats it as a follower's restart. GiveUpRound and FenceStuck now leave out a doubted copy. Without that change, a split vote waits forever on a copy that will never answer, but the code's open timeout withdraws it.

**New finding, #2029, already on main and independent of this PR:** any batch from a newer leader vouches for an unclean copy and rewrites its ballot. A crashed leader that has had only part of its lost suffix shipped back can then stand and win with an empty copy's vote. The proposed fix is to vouch only once the copy holds a record of the leader's generation (`VouchOnGeneration`). This PR does not change that code.

With detector misfires on, FelixShardElectLiveUncleanLed grew past 5.6M states in 12 minutes without finishing. The proposed bound is to keep misfires off, as now, or to run it with misfires in an Actions dispatch.

The twin's trace is the bug: the restarted broker stands and wins, its open is refused and it gives the generation up, then it refuses the other broker's fence for good.

Model limits:
- A restarted copy votes again only after it has been re-admitted. The code's rotated-id check (`names_other_in_view`) already refuses until then, so the candidate gate never fires in the model.
- A one-write variant that lets a crashed, never re-admitted follower count fails AckedHeldByLeader. Its liveness fails too. That is the two-fault case #1295 accepts, so the variant was dropped.
- FelixShardShortCopySeat ran past 15M states in 7 minutes locally and has no weight in check_tla.sh, so TLA_QUICK treats it as quick. It needs a weight entry, which this PR does not add.
- The CpDown positive configs (FelixShardCpDown and its variants) are still unregistered. This PR does not bound them.

## Review notes

- The gate makes an unvouched copy ineligible to stand. Before, it could stand and then could not lead what it won. This is a behaviour change worth a look.
- The `stood` map keeps one entry per shard for the life of the process. A stale entry is ignored because it must match the current ballot.

body: ## Problem API key permissions (personal and bot keys: create, edit, duplicate) were a flat list of 19 checkboxes with no grouping, no bulk actions and no presets. The whole desktop dialog scrolled (`DialogContent` is `overflow-y-auto`), so the Name field and the Create/Save button scrolled out of view. ## Solution The permissions are now a picker of areas at three levels, with presets on top: `api-key-permission-picker.tsx`, with the model in `api-key-scopes.ts`. - **Areas.** There are 11, each with None / Read / Write in the settings `SegmentedControl`. Write includes Read. An area that can only be read offers None and Read. Opening an area's row shows its individual permissions. A row holding only some of a level's permissions shows a dot, and no segment is selected. - **Group bulk setters.** The Conversations, Workspace and Agents headers set every area in the group at once. Read-only areas stop at Read. - **Presets.** - Read only. - Connected bot: `CONNECTED_BOT_SCOPES`, now the one constant shared with `pages/connect.tsx`. - Full access. - Presets compare only key-eligible permissions. Scopes outside the picker are left as they are. - **Fixed dialog chrome.** The title and Name field (or the key name on Edit) stay at the top. The "N of 19 permissions" count and the actions stay at the bottom. Only the body scrolls, with edge shadows: `ScrollEdgeShadows` is extracted from `SettingPeopleList`. The Edit sheet gains `disableSnapPoints` so Save isn't pushed below the phone fold. - **Key rows.** Each row shows the matching preset badge, or otherwise one badge per area, such as "Messages · Write". - **Hill-climb findings applied:** - 44px touch targets; - one shared right edge for the level columns, and one x for the chevrons; - descriptions only when a row is opened; - keyboard radio groups. **Connected bot now also grants `bot-runtime:read` and `bot-invocations:read`.** `threa-bot`'s `GET /decisions/{id}` requires `bot-runtime:read`. Kris approved this. These settings dialogs keep `historyEntry={false}` from #2940, so Back closing the sheet isn't part of this PR. ## Before / after Before, scrolled (the name and header are gone): ![keyperm-perm-cap-desktop-new-scrolled](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_tsyv3dfnrt/keyperm-perm-cap-desktop-new-scrolled.webp) After, desktop light, with a preset applied and one row open: ![keyperm-perm-after-desktop-2-preset-expanded](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_z4gbzeppm9/keyperm-perm-after-desktop-2-preset-expanded.webp) After, desktop dark, scrolled: ![keyperm-perm-after-desktop-dark-3-scrolled](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_7t8wma8v34/keyperm-perm-after-desktop-dark-3-scrolled.webp) Phone, before and after: ![keyperm-perm-cap-phone-new-scrolled](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_z3afvkfnfj/keyperm-perm-cap-phone-new-scrolled.webp) ![keyperm-perm-after-phone-2-preset-expanded](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_r33xz3apeh/keyperm-perm-after-phone-2-preset-expanded.webp) ![keyperm-perm-after-phone-3-scrolled](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_265g22066v/keyperm-perm-after-phone-3-scrolled.webp) Key rows: ![keyperm-perm-after-desktop-4-key-rows](https://seer.build/ws_vbyzjvdg6g/i/img_bbn8de3zkg/keyperm-perm-after-desktop-4-key-rows.webp) ## Test plan - [x] `api-key-scopes.test.ts`: level math, preset coverage, group clamp, and every eligible permission sitting in exactly one area. - [x] `user-api-keys-section.test.tsx`: create through a preset, then a group level, then a single permission; ## Tóm tắt
Thay avatar Vaulty dạng SVG trong widget trợ lý nổi bằng phiên bản 3D dựng bằng three.js.
Mô hình được dựng hoàn toàn từ các hình khối cơ bản (không dùng file .glb), nên không cần
thêm asset nào để tải hay lưu trữ.

## Thay đổi
- **Thêm mới `Assistant/ChibiAvatar3D.jsx`**: thay thế trực tiếp cho `ChibiAvatar`,
  giữ nguyên props (`action: 'idle' | 'wave' | 'jump' | 'talk'`, `mini`).
  - Toon shading 3 bậc cùng viền đen (inverted hull) để giữ phong cách nét vẽ 2D gốc.
  - Chú cú đeo kính một mắt có dây xích vàng, ôm cuốn sổ có ổ khoá, có tai lông, má hồng và bóng dưới chân.
  - Animation:
    - `idle`: nhún nhẹ, chớp mắt ngẫu nhiên, đầu nhìn theo con trỏ chuột.
    - `wave`: vẫy cánh phải.
    - `jump`: nhảy với squash & stretch, bóng co lại khi nhảy.
    - `talk`: mỏ nhép và đầu gật nhẹ.
- **`Assistant/AssistantWidget.jsx`**: import `ChibiAvatar3D` thay cho `ChibiAvatar` 2D.
  Logic widget (lời chào, mẹo, khung thoại, chat panel) không thay đổi.

## Độ ổn định / hiệu năng
- **Fallback về 2D**: nếu máy không có WebGL hoặc mất context thì tự dùng lại `ChibiAvatar` SVG.
- **Avatar `mini` giữ nguyên 2D**: avatar 32px trong khung chat vẫn dùng SVG để tránh tạo nhiều WebGL context.
- **Vòng lặp render**: tạm dừng khi tab bị ẩn, dùng `powerPreference: 'low-power'`, giới hạn pixel ratio tối đa 2.
- **Giảm chuyển động**: khi bật `prefers-reduced-motion` chỉ vẽ 1 khung tĩnh.
- **Dọn dẹp**: geometry, material, texture, renderer và event listener đều được dispose khi unmount.

## Phụ thuộc
- Cần thêm `three` (`npm i three`).

## Cách kiểm tra
1. Chạy `npm i && npm run dev`, đăng nhập (widget bị ẩn ở các trang công khai).
2. Chú cú xuất hiện ở góc dưới bên phải: kiểm tra trạng thái idle (nhún nhẹ, chớp mắt) và đầu nhìn theo con trỏ.
3. Tải lại trang hoặc đăng nhập lại: cú vẫy cánh kèm khung thoại chào.
4. Bấm vào cú: cú nhảy và chat panel đóng/mở. Gửi tin nhắn: mỏ nhép khi trả lời.
5. Tắt WebGL hoặc bật "reduce motion": lần lượt chuyển về avatar 2D hoặc hiện 1 khung tĩnh.

## Ghi chú
- `ChibiAvatar` 2D và `assistant.css` được giữ lại làm fallback và cho avatar `mini`.

author: kryonix
body:
Follow-up to #28408. The total list length statistic is accumulated with an unchecked `+=` in `ListStats::Merge` and `ListStats::MergeInLengths`. When the sum exceeds `uint64_t`, the total wraps silently and consumers of `ListStats::TotalListLength` read a small but "known" value. The statistic is meant for cardinality and memory estimates (for example the average list length for UNNEST estimates in the in-flight #28299), where a wrapped total produces arbitrarily wrong results without any indication that the statistic is invalid.

The total already has an unknown sentinel, the `has_total_list_length` flag, which `Merge` uses for `EXPAND_BOUNDS` and `ResetAdditiveStatistics` uses after deletes. The fix follows that idiom: both accumulation sites now use `TryAddOperator` and mark the total as unknown when the sum overflows. The min/max bounds are unaffected, they cannot overflow. Clamping to `NumericLimits<uint64_t>::Maximum()` was rejected because a clamped value would still be read as a real total by average-length estimates.

The per-vector sums that feed `MergeInLengths` (`ListColumnData::Append`) count elements of an in-memory vector and cannot overflow, so they stay unchecked.

Tests:
- `test/common/test_list_stats.cpp` exercises `Merge` and `MergeInLengths` at the `uint64_t` boundary: sums below and exactly at the maximum stay known, one element past the maximum turns the total unknown while the bounds survive. The magnitudes are unreachable through SQL, a real table with a summed list length past 2^64 cannot be constructed, so this cannot be a sqllogictest.
- `test/sql/storage/list_length_stats.test` gains a multi-row-group section pinning that normal totals still merge exactly across row groups, a checkpoint, and a restart.

`StringStats::Merge` has the same unchecked `+=` for `total_string_length`, which the list statistics were modelled on. That is left for a separate change to keep this one focused.

## 무엇을

UX 점검 15번("위험 표시가 실제 위험과 맞지 않음"). 네 모듈의 `[[commands.fields]] risk`와 마인크래프트 플러그인 카탈로그의 `risk`를 사용자 기준(2026-11-06)으로 다시 매긴다. 위험도는 기본 권한(기본 프리셋 안전 Lv0·주의 Lv1·위험 Lv2)과 확인 여부를 함께 정한다.

- 안전: 조회, 단순 변경, 영향이 작은 게임 안 변화
- 주의: 위험할 수도 있는 게임 안 명령, PC 자원을 많이 쓰는 명령
- 위험: 특정 유저에게 큰 영향을 주는 게임 안 명령, 설정·로그 파일을 직접 바꾸는 명령

### 모듈 명령 (17개)

| 모듈 | 바뀐 것 |
|---|---|
| minecraft | weather·time 위험→안전, difficulty·give·tp 위험→주의 |
| zomboid | startrain·stoprain 주의→안전, additem·addxp·godmod·invisible 위험→주의 |
| terraria | dawn·noon·dusk·midnight·password 주의→안전 |
| palworld | players 주의→안전 (`remote = false` 그대로) |

게임에 직접 끄라고 보내는 명령(minecraft `stop`, palworld `shutdown`, zomboid `quit`, terraria `exit-nosave`)은 위험 그대로 두고 `remote = false`로 디스코드·챗봇 명령 목록에서 뺀다. 채팅 `stop`은 이미 데몬 내장 [정지]로 가므로(`src/chat/mod.rs:553`) 디스코드에서 끄는 길은 [정지] 하나가 된다.

### 플러그인 카탈로그 (282개)

- 선택 영역, NPC 꾸미기, 개인 시간·날씨, 회복, 공지, 서버 시간·날씨 → 안전
- WorldEdit 영역 편집, Chunky 생성, 이동, 주기만 하는 명령(give·god·fly), 게임 규칙·월드 경계 → 주의
- 남의 권한·차단·허용 목록·보호 구역 멤버·소유를 바꾸는 명령, 설정·데이터 파일을 바꾸는 명령(setworth, essentials homes fix, mv modify) → 위험
- IP·위치 조회(whois·seen·getpos·near)는 개인정보라 주의 그대로
- 전체 목록: 제안 페이지(스레드 링크)의 "플러그인 명령 바뀐 목록"

테스트: 주기만 하는 명령까지 danger로 묶던 `GRANTING_COMMANDS`를 권한을 바꾸는 `ACCESS_COMMANDS`로 좁혔다. 카탈로그 diff는 `"risk"` 줄만 바뀐다.

author: noel-lang
body:
Owner decisions of 06.11.2026, written into ADR 0039 as an amendment.

Shared trunks: an edge may ask for one trunk at its shared box however its
other ends stand (`GraphEdge.trunk: 'whole'`); class diagrams ask it for
generalizations and realizations, so every one of them meets its target in
one trunk with one triangle (`Signierbar` in `schnittstellen`, `Fahrzeug` in
`hierarchie-quer`). The order counts a piece of the same box that stands
between members of a trunk as the crossings it makes, tracks count crossings
of a whole trunk per pair of lines, and a whole trunk moves onto a member that
slipped beside it. Concept links keep their trunks: a bus for `raute` is no
convention of the kind.

Detour against crossing: a refinement after the order of fewest crossings
prices the estimated length of every piece at 10/600 per pixel against 10 a
crossing, incrementally by layer, place and swap. Where it moves anything,
both orders are drawn roughly and the shorter one stays only where crossings
and length together cost less (a crossing 600 px) and no line check rule gets
worse. Placeholders between boxes drawn beside each other share the room of
their line. `beobachter` trades the 768 px round the top for one crossing
(budget raised by name); `vererbung-acht`, `ueberspringen`, `rollen-gross`,
`schichten`, `fan-aus`, `begriffe-netz` get shorter at equal crossings;
`dg-n-big` 230 to 233 crossings for 2,026 px less line.

Owner decisions 06.11.2026: one trunk per interface (yes), a crossing is worth ~600 px of detour (ok). beobachter: crossing instead of a 1000 px detour (3376 → 2608 px of line), named trade. Probe dg-n-big 0.63 → 0.75 s, 230 → 233 crossings for 2026 px less line.

Verified: pnpm verify green (1,554 tests). Contact sheet /diagrist-kern/fix/trunks-and-detours.html.

author: dastari
body:
## Summary

Static top-level and relation offset connections now use their selected fields to omit unused SQL. Count-only pages skip entity reads; row-only pages skip counts; `hasNextPage` without a total probes one extra row. Aliases, named fragments, inline fragments, boundary cursors, empty pages and offsets preserve their selected values. Fixes #313.

## Decisions

- Preserve the complete result contract of existing direct `fetch_connection` / `fetch_connection_with_auth` callers; add `EntityQuery::fetch_connection_selected_with_auth` and `graphql::pagination::ConnectionSelection` for generated resolvers and explicit partial-result callers.
- Retain the original paired fetch whenever rows and count are both required, preserving its pinned auth transaction even when `hasNextPage` is omitted.
- Keep residual row-authorization scans unchanged, including for count-only selections. A regression asserts 50 readable rows rather than the 120 stored rows.
- Preserve relation batching without adding fields to existing public keys: the additive `graphql::loaders::SelectedRelationQueryKey` partitions batches/caches by selection requirements.
- Reuse the inherited Item 19 relation renderer. Skip a new top-level primary-key-first strategy to keep this change independent of backend-specific projection/join planning. Row-query sorting remains measurable below.
- Keep `operations.rs` to two call-site changes. ORM and macros move together from 0.91.2 to 0.91.3.

## Verification

All Cargo commands and scripts that spawn Cargo used this prefix:

```bash
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/toby/dev/cargo-target/wo-item-20 \
  systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryHigh=11G -p MemoryMax=14G -p MemorySwapMax=4G --
```

The final owned-database and full-suite runs additionally set `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` to reduce build artifact size.

The regression was executed on the base implementation with only query-count instrumentation routed through the existing counted wrapper: count-only failed with 2 statements versus 1 expected. The same fixture is retained.

SQLite selection coverage compares every nonempty combination of edges, totalCount, hasNextPage, hasPreviousPage, startCursor and endCursor against the complete answer at five offset/limit boundaries, for both top-level and relation connections (630 comparisons). Named and inline fragments and aliases are used throughout. Additional tests cover residual authorization, batching across parents and differing selections on aliases of the same relation.

| Command (with prefix above for Cargo and Cargo-spawning scripts) | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | Passed |
| `cargo test -p graphql-orm` | Passed: 801 passed, 15 ignored, 0 failed, including downstream fixture results |
| `cargo test -p graphql-orm --test conditional_relations --test composite_relations --test authorized_pagination` | Passed: 19 passed, 2 ignored; includes all 630 selection comparisons |
| `cargo test -p graphql-orm-macros` | Passed: 20 passed, 6 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p graphql-orm --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed on final code |
| `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p graphql-orm --no-deps` | Passed |
| `cargo check -p graphql-orm --no-default-features --features postgres --all-targets` | Passed |
| `cargo check -p graphql-orm --no-default-features --features mssql --lib` | Passed; library-only lane requested for #265 |
| `scripts/run-owned-database-lanes.sh postgres` | Passed: 234 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored |
| `scripts/run-owned-database-lanes.sh postgres-legacy` | Passed: 84 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, including the router fixture wrapper |
| `cargo test -p graphql-orm --no-default-features --features postgres --test postgres_rls --test row_policy_and_input_transform -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1` | Passed on final code: 7 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored; disposable owned PostgreSQL |
| `python3 scripts/check-documentation.py` | Passed: 218 governed Markdown files |
| `python3 scripts/generate-workspace-inventory.py --check` | Passed |
| `python3 scripts/check-release-state.py` | Passed: 9 packages |
| `scripts/check-workspace-dependencies.sh` | Passed, including dependency-tree checks |
| `scripts/check-package-release-policy.sh origin/agent/wo-item-19-relation-window` | Passed |
| `cargo metadata --locked --offline --format-version 1 --manifest-path <fixture>/Cargo.toml` | Passed for all 10 tracked fixture/skills lockfiles; each invocation used the build-limit prefix |

The first full ORM run exposed process-wide counter races in the conditional-relation tests. They now share a mutex without relaxing their existing query limits; the complete suite passed afterward. The final paired-dispatch adjustment was followed by the 19 targeted tests, full suite, Clippy, Rustdoc, backend compile checks and focused PostgreSQL auth tests. The two broad PostgreSQL scripts passed before that final dispatch-only adjustment.

PostgreSQL tests used test-owned disposable Docker databases only (including the focused tests' `support/owned_postgres.rs` harness). SQLite tests used temporary/in-memory databases. MSSQL native tests were not run: `scripts/run-owned-database-lanes.sh mssql` and the all-targets compile lane `cargo check -p graphql-orm --no-default-features --features mssql --all-targets` remain blocked by existing fixture errors (#265); the requested library lane passed.


Measurements use `wide_relation_measurement`, a retained ignored test: 16,434 matching rows, indexed filter column, indexed text sort column, 6,656-byte payload, limit 1. Setup is excluded. These are medians of four debug-profile runs on this host; relation measurements include the enclosing parent connection. Baseline uses the same modified fixture against the PR base, plus behavior-neutral counted-wrapper instrumentation for top-level connections.

| Connection | Selection | Before ms | After ms | Statements before → after |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Top-level | Count | 13.571 | 2.572 | 2 → 1 |
| Top-level | Rows | 12.882 | 11.158 | 2 → 1 |
| Top-level | Both | 13.490 | 11.961 | 2 → 2 |
| Relation | Count | 29.931 | 5.903 | 4 → 2 |
| Relation | Rows | 30.281 | 25.899 | 4 → 2 |
| Relation | Both | 30.934 | 29.728 | 4 → 3 |

Exact measurement command, run before and after:

```bash
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/toby/dev/cargo-target/wo-item-20 \
  systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryHigh=11G -p MemoryMax=14G -p MemorySwapMax=4G -- \
  cargo test -p graphql-orm --test composite_relations wide_relation_measurement -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The top-level row-only GraphQL path still costs 11.158 ms median and issues the full entity projection with `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1`; SQL statements were not timed separately. This fixture did not reproduce the reported 960 ms latency. Selection-aware execution removes that cost only when rows are unselected; it does not solve wide-row sorting itself. The existing relation narrow-key renderer remains in place.

## Migration

No consumer action or data migration is needed. Upgrade ORM and macros together. Generated static connections change their SQL statement counts without changing selected values or authorization. Detect the optimization through counted statements or emitted SQL. Existing direct full-result methods retain their result contract. New explicit callers may request a partial connection:

```rust
let selection = graphql_orm::graphql::pagination::ConnectionSelection {
    rows: false, count: true, has_next_page: false,
};
let connection = query.fetch_connection_selected_with_auth(&db, None, selection).await?;
// Only requested components are meaningful.
```

## Documentation impact

- [x] Documentation updated
- [ ] No documentation impact

Explanation: changelog, migration guide, both package version notes, canonical pagination reference, generated workspace inventory, all tracked moved-package lock entries, and router notice lock hash updated.

author: geezoria
body:
## Problem

The notebook (`.ipynb`) preview shows a cell's error output as run-together lines full of terminal color codes.

Jupyter saves an error's traceback as a list of lines, each colored with ANSI escapes. `openNotebook` passed the list to `notebookText`, which joins array parts with no separator, and kept the escapes. For a cell that runs `ratio(1, 0)`, the preview showed:

```
[31m---------------------------------------------------------------------------[39m[31mZeroDivisionError[39m                         Traceback (most recent call last)[36mCell[39m[36m [39m[32mIn[1][39m[32m, line 4[39m
[32m      1[39m [38;5;28;01mdef[39;00m ratio(a, b):
...
```

`text` and `text/plain` arrays are fragments that already carry their own newlines, so joining those with `""` is right. Traceback entries are separate lines without them. Jupyter joins them with `\n` and renders the colors.

## Change

A small `notebookTraceback` helper joins traceback entries with `\n` and strips the SGR color codes with the existing `terminalOutputPlainText` from `@t3tools/shared/terminalOutput`. It runs only when an output has no `text` or `text/plain`, the same fallback position `output.traceback` already had. Stream and `text/plain` outputs are unchanged.

The server's agent-facing extractor (`apps/server/src/provider/documentTextWorker.ts`, `notebook()`) already writes each traceback entry on its own line and strips the escapes. This makes the preview match it.

## Scope and approval

This is a very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so it uses CONTRIBUTING's exception for those. Error outputs are a standard nbformat 4 output type, and every saved notebook with a failed cell hits this. The change is limited to the traceback fallback in `openNotebook`.

I found no existing issue or PR. I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `notebook traceback`, `notebook error output`, `ipynb traceback`, `notebook preview ANSI`, `jupyter`, `notebook preview`, `ipynb`, and `openNotebook`. The only open PRs that touch `extendedDocumentPreview.ts` are my RTF fix #30812 and #31886 (cell-count pluralization). Neither touches the notebook output code.

## Verification

Windows 11, Node 26.12.1, base `202d5b5616`.

- **Regression test.** Added `shows notebook error tracebacks as plain lines` to `FilePreviewPanel.test.ts`. Its input is an IPython traceback for `1 / 0`. With main's `openNotebook` it fails, receiving the run-together text with `[0;31m` codes. With this change all 32 tests in the file pass (`vp test run src/components/files/FilePreviewPanel.test.ts` in `apps/web`).
- **Real notebook.** I executed a notebook with a real IPython 9.18.1 kernel (`nbclient` with `allow_errors=True`). Its cell is `def ratio(a, b): return a / b` followed by `ratio(1, 0)`. Then I ran `openNotebook` on the saved file. Main gives the output quoted above. With this change it gives:

  ```
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ZeroDivisionError                         Traceback (most recent call last)
  Cell In[1], line 4
        1 def ratio(a, b):
        2     return a / b
        3 
  ----> 4 ratio(1, 0)

  Cell In[1], line 2, in ratio(a, b)
        1 def ratio(a, b):
  ----> 2     return a / b

  ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
  ```

  This matches what Jupyter shows, without the colors.
- **Running client.** I ran `vp run dev` with a fresh `--home-dir` and added a folder that contains only the saved notebook. Then I opened `error.ipynb` in the Files panel, maximized. *Before* uses main's `extendedDocumentPreview.ts` in the same session:

  **Before (main)**

  ![Notebook preview on main: the traceback runs together and shows raw escape codes](https://github.com/geezoria/t3code/raw/pr-assets/notebook-preview-traceback/31929/before.png)

  **After (this branch)**

  ![Notebook preview on this branch: one traceback line per row, no escape codes](https://github.com/geezoria/t3code/raw/pr-assets/notebook-preview-traceback/31929/after.png)
- **Fast checks.** `vp run check:changed origin/main` passed format, lint, both Knip checks, typechecks for 2 packages, the tests beside the change, and the React Compiler check.

**Not checked:** I checked only the web client, on Windows in Chromium. I didn't run the Electron desktop build, which renders the same preview code.

Implemented and verified with Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in the Claude Code harness.

author: denn-gubsky
body:
## Why

The voice-input language switch showed bare codes (`uk`, `en`). An earlier commit on this branch made it always visible and hard-coded Russian and English in the app. The owner decided instead (2026-11-06) that **the server decides** which languages are offered and whether the switch shows. So that commit is reverted here, and only the readable names remain.

## What

- **Reverted** (`42b6691`): the always-visible switch, the app's `["ru", "en"]`, `ChatProps.voice.languages`, and the client-side mirror of loomcycle's 43 accepted codes. The switch is back to the P2 rule: it offers the server's speech-to-text default plus the languages its read-aloud voices speak, and shows when that makes two or more.
- **Kept** (`a602342`): each option is named in its own language, `uk · Українська`, `ru · Русский`, `en · English`, via `Intl.DisplayNames`, falling back to the code.

loomcycle 1.142 has no setting for a list of speech-to-text languages: `transcription.stt.language` takes one code, and `speechInfo()` publishes only that default. **G33** asks for `transcription.stt.languages` and `speechInfo().transcription.languages`; loomboard will read that list in place of the read-aloud languages once it ships. Until then, a deployment can show more languages by configuring read-aloud voices for them.

## Tested

- `npm run typecheck`, `build:lib`, `build:standalone`, and for the workflow package `typecheck` / `test`: exit 0. `npx vitest run`: 773 / 773.
- New tests: `languageName` (uk, ru, en, and the fallback); each option named in itself; the switch hidden when the server offers one language, with the mic still shown.

author: robmitchellengineering-hub
body:
What the pacland method gives MorpheOS, written up (doc 27) and its first slice implemented in Rust.

## The design note

`docs/27-verification-discipline.md` ports the pacland discipline: every Conductor claim carries an oracle class + falsifier + remedy + status; constraint-first Manifest design; the five graders; a tension register on Strata.

## The first slice, implemented

- `Claim` type + `OracleClass`/`ClaimStatus` in `morph-manifest`.
- `Manifest.claims` (serde-default).
- The **judge** in `validate`: demonstrated-with-no-falsifier is an error (`CLAIM-NO-FALSIFIER`); stated is a warning; duplicate id and empty remedy are warnings.
- The **tension register**: two claims with one id that disagree are `CLAIM-TENSION` (naming the field), identical are `CLAIM-DUP`.
- `/claims` classified security-critical in the risk table.
- Enforcement proven: a falsifier-less demonstrated claim is refused at `apply`, writes nothing.

The judge's key rule and the tension detection are both mutation-tested.

author: someson
body:
Closes TODO item 11.

## Problem

`navigate(page, url, response: true)` returned only `%{status, url}`. ReqBot needs the main document's headers and body, so it re-implemented the capture (`Network.responseReceived` with `type: "Document"`, then `loadingFinished`, then `getResponseBody`).

## Change

- The `response: true` map gains `headers` (the final response's headers as Chrome reports them; a repeated header such as `Set-Cookie` joined with `"\n"`; `%{}` when none) and `request_id`, so the body is one `Page.response_body/3` away.
- Docs: after a `:load` or `:network_almost_idle` wait the document has finished loading; with `wait_until: :none` the body may not have arrived yet. New recipe for reading the raw HTML; page-operations row updated.

Additive: code matching `%{status: s, url: u}` keeps working; only an exact `==` on the old two-key map would change.

## Tests

- Unit (`FakeCDP`): headers and request id returned, repeated header kept as Chrome sends it; a response without headers gives `%{}`.
- Integration: through a 302, the final document's `Content-Type` and its HTML read with `response_body/3`.

`mix ci` green; `mix test --only integration` 155/155 on macOS (Google Chrome 156), no orphaned Chrome. Independent of #28 (both touch `CHANGELOG.md`; whichever merges second needs a rebase).

author: bolichen97
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** Let someone close every folder in the sessions sidebar with one click, so a grown folder tree can be reset and only the branch they need reopened.

The sessions sidebar has no single action that collapses every folder. Each folder has to be closed through its own disclosure, so the cost of resetting the tree grows with every folder added, which hits hardest the people who use nested folders the most.

Builds on #16035 by @tim-finnigan.

## Why it matters

People who route their work through nested folders end up with a tall sidebar of mostly irrelevant context. Today the reset is manual and gets longer as the tree grows, so the folder tree becomes less useful the more it is used.

## Not a goal

- **Collapse all but the active branch.** This closes everything, the branch holding the open session included; opening a session or a folder reveal still reopens its branch.
- **Expand all, or restoring the tree's earlier shape.**
- **The board view's per-column collapse state.** Board columns keep their own collapse choices in the browser, so the action is offered in the folder tree view only.
- **Any change to folder order, visibility, ownership or membership.**

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Folder collapse state is stored on the server, one folder per `PATCH /api/chat/folders/{id}`. Done that way, a collapse-all would be one request per open folder, which can fail halfway and leave the tree half closed, and writes one audit line per folder.

So the reset is one write. A new route, `POST /api/chat/folders/collapse-all`, sets `collapsed` on every folder in a single pass under the folder-store lock, the same all-or-none shape as `POST /api/chat/folders/reorder`. It changes nothing else, and `collapsed` stays a layout field, so it never claims a folder an agent created. An app caller is refused (`folder_collapse_all_forbidden`), because through `PATCH` an app may collapse only the folders it owns; a crew member is already refused at the chat gate.

In the sidebar, the header ⋮ menu gains **Collapse all folders**, next to **Clean up empty folders**. It shows in the folder tree view while at least one folder is open. The click closes the tree at once in the cached list and sends that one request; if the request fails, the error notice says so and the refetch redraws what the server holds. Offline it closes the cached tree and sends nothing, the same as a single folder's toggle. The dashboard spec and feature map name the route and the menu item.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| the route, registered beside reorder and cleanup | `dashboard/chat_folders_routes.py`, `dashboard/routes/sessions.py` |
| the client method | `api/client/chatOrganization.ts` |
| the menu item | `chat-sidebar/SidebarHeader.tsx` |
| the one-request write and its offline path | `chat-sidebar/folders.ts` |
| the label, in every catalog | `i18n/locales/en.json` and each other locale (`pages.chatSidebar.collapse_all_folders`) |

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: one new route and one new menu item. No existing route, stored field or behaviour changes.

Removes nothing: the diff adds a route, a client method, a menu row and a string, and takes nothing away.

## Tests

- `test/test_chat_folder_collapse_all.py`: one request closes every folder in exactly one store write, leaving every other field (order, parent, owner, the agent-created mark) unchanged; an app caller gets 403 and nothing is written.
- `website/src/test/ChatSidebar.collapseAllFolders.test.tsx`: the header menu item closes the tree and sends exactly one collapse-all request, never a per-folder `PATCH`.
- `website/src/test/ApiClient.refactor.surface.test.ts`: the new client method takes its place in the method order.

Determinism: the backend file passed 20 runs at `-n0`, then 10 runs at `-n 4 --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=2` beside `test_chat_folder_reorder_atomic.py` and `test_chat_folder_cleanup.py`, and a shuffled order with seed 27021. The vitest file passed 5 runs with `--sequence.shuffle`, seeds 27022 to 27026, beside `ChatSidebar.flatFolderFilter.test.tsx`.

## Manual verification

Ran the built dashboard against fixture data in a headless browser: opened the header menu, picked **Collapse all folders**, and checked that every folder closed and exactly one `POST /api/chat/folders/collapse-all` was sent. Dark and light themes below.

## Screenshots / video

The sidebar header ⋮ menu opened, with **Collapse all folders** between **Clean up empty folders…** and **Switch all to model…** (dark, light). Rendered from this branch's frontend with sample folders:

![Header ⋮ menu with Collapse all folders, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3eafcf32-aa68-4e5e-8fb9-f25ce0097d5b)
![Header ⋮ menu with Collapse all folders, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d54c7fd7-27e7-42f6-b63a-9cd57d0e49c9)

Before and after the click (dark):

![Folder tree before Collapse all folders, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22b72e22-a909-4c24-bd86-6f21f366c1c2)
![Folder tree after Collapse all folders, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/083e1dfd-67d6-4bc4-9498-84df0afe7210)

<details><summary>Before and after the click (light)</summary>

![Folder tree before Collapse all folders, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0403aa9c-aad8-41ee-a7a0-c51ff40c0d28)
![Folder tree after Collapse all folders, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89e23765-8da9-48b2-9f3f-b902cdc38a94)

</details>

Package metadata (README, LICENSE, description, repository.directory, keywords, peer deps `effect ^4`) was already complete.

## Verification

- `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test run`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check-dist-types`, `pnpm check-packages`: pass.

author: nikolagorannaumovski
body:
## CLA

- [x] I have signed the [Stream CLA](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFKsKkAJI7mhCr7K9rEIOpqIDThrWxuvxnwUq2XkHyG154vQ/viewform) (required).
- [x] Code changes are tested

## Description of the changes, What, Why and How?

Ticket: https://linear.app/stream/issue/REACT-1375
Spec: [CHA-2667 Quiet hours – client SDK](https://app.notion.com/p/stream-wiki/cha-2667-quiet-hours-client-sdk-e1a6a5d7f9f682c48cec816312c107af)
v9 counterpart: #2000

The backend already supports quiet hours for push notifications. A user-level push preference can carry a `schedule` (a timezone and 1–7 quiet windows), and `remove_schedule` clears it. v10's generated client already has these types and sends them through `updatePushNotificationPreferences`. This PR adds the helpers a UI needs, and keeps the connected user's preferences up to date after a save.

### Helpers (`src/pushPreferences/`, exported from the root)

- `isInQuietHours({ schedule, date? })` tells whether a schedule is quiet at `date` (default: now).
  - It reads the wall clock in the schedule's timezone with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, so it follows daylight saving time.
  - A window whose end is earlier than its start runs past midnight. It belongs to the day it opens on, so `days` is checked against the previous day after midnight.
  - A rule without `days` applies every day. `00:00`–`24:00` covers the whole day.
- `getDeviceTimeZone()` returns the device's IANA timezone, to pre-fill a schedule.
- `QuietHoursDay` names the day values (`mon` … `sun`).

### Connected user

`StreamChat` overrides `updatePushNotificationPreferences`. After a successful request it merges the user-level preferences of the connected user into `client.user.push_preferences`:
- It uses the server's `user_preferences[userId]` when the response has it.
- `remove_schedule` drops the stored schedule unless the response returns a new one. `remove_disable` does the same for `disabled_until`. So "switch from a schedule to a snooze" (`remove_schedule` + `disabled_until`) ends with only `disabled_until`.
- Channel-level items and items for other users leave `client.user` unchanged.
- `client.user` is replaced, not mutated, and only when the preferences changed.

### Tests

- `test/unit/pushPreferences/utils.test.ts` covers `isInQuietHours`: windows, past midnight, the whole day, several rules, timezones and DST. It also covers `getDeviceTimeZone` and the merge cases.
- `test/unit/pushPreferences/updatePushNotificationPreferences.test.ts` covers the request payload and the connected user's state.

## Changelog

- Add `isInQuietHours`, `getDeviceTimeZone` and `QuietHoursDay` for push notification quiet hours.
- Keep `client.user.push_preferences` in sync after `updatePushNotificationPreferences`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes board task #244: in an interactive workflow with several sub-step sessions, the run page showed the **Session starting…** spinner again while a session was ending.

**Cause.** A step stays `running` until the workflow advances past it, so its console outlives the session. Once the session leaves `ready`, `websocketUrl` goes `nil` and `StepConsole` fell back to its only placeholder, **Session starting…**.

**Fix.** `StepConsole` now reads `terminalSessionState`. When the session is `finishing` or already ended (`finished` / `failed` / `cancelled`), the placeholder says **Session finishing…**. Otherwise it still says **Session starting…**. The spinner goes away as before, when the step leaves `running` / `waiting_input` and its console is removed. Frontend only: the state was already serialized on `StepRun`.

Also:
- added a Vitest case for the `finishing` and `finished` session states;
- updated the user docs (`sessions-and-runs.md` and both copies of `user-guide-outline.md`);

body:
## What and why

PR #47 got a failing `Vercel` status: "Deployment rate limited — retry in 24 hours". Every push to any branch started a Vercel deployment that `ignoreCommand` then cancelled, and those count toward the Hobby plan's daily deployment limit; today's sprint pushes used it up, so main cannot deploy either until it resets.

`git.deploymentEnabled: { "**": false, "main": true }` turns automatic deployments off for every branch except main (Vercel: a branch matching several rules deploys if one of them is `true`; `**` also matches branch names with slashes, e.g. `sprint1/ellipsis`). `ignoreCommand` stays as a second guard. The `issue-assets` branch got `deploymentEnabled: false` separately.

Docs: https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/git-configuration#git.deploymentenabled

## How it was tested

JSON parses. Effective once on main: the next sprint branch push should create no Vercel deployment (no Vercel status on its PR), and the next merge to main should deploy once the daily limit has reset.

author: rasheshpal27
body:
Sixth pass over the listening room. The headline is a security fix; the rest is
making the sync survive bad networks, and clearing the remaining quality debt.

## The security problem

`src/lib/constants.ts` contained:

```ts
export const PARTY_PASSWORD = process.env.PARTY_PASSWORD ?? "hirashesh";
export const ADMIN_PASSWORD = process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? "adminrasheshadmin";
```

That module is imported by client components, so both literals were compiled
into the browser JavaScript. Anyone with the public repo — or with devtools
open on the deployed site — had the guest password *and* the host password.

Now:

- `src/lib/env.ts` is server-only and has **no fallbacks**. Missing secrets log
  a config error at boot, and every auth path answers `503 not-configured` with
  a message naming the missing variables. Failing closed beats a default.
- `secretEquals()` hashes both sides with SHA-256 and compares with
  `timingSafeEqual`, so neither the password nor its length leaks through
  response timing.
- `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` adds per-IP token buckets: auth 8 then 1/7.5s, chat
  12 then 1/s, reactions 15 then 1.5/s, queue 20 then 1/2s. Denials return
  `429` with `Retry-After`.
- `env.ts` deliberately never throws at import time — a build on a machine
  without secrets must still succeed.

## Sync under bad conditions

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A hidden tab stopped polling, but YouTube kept playing — a phone in a pocket drifted for minutes, then snapped | hidden tabs poll every 6s on a Web Worker ticker (browsers clamp `setInterval` to 1/min in background pages) |
| One dropped poll looked like a dead connection | two consecutive failures before the banner; `navigator.onLine` shows "offline" instantly |
| A flaky link retried tightly against a struggling server | 1s → 20s exponential backoff with ±25% jitter |
| After a gap the deck drifted back in from a stale anchor | ≥2 failures or ≥4s blind triggers a clock burst and a hard re-anchor |
| Every poll carried `serverNow` and threw it away | each poll is now a free RTT sample into one shared clock store (lowest-RTT anchor, 12 samples, >4s discarded) |
| Drift was corrected by seeking — audible | steer at 0.97x/1.03x and settle back to 1.0x; seek only when steering can't win, or when the player ignores `setPlaybackRate` (detected by re-reading the rate ~900ms later) |
| Any failed `/api/player` call could be retried | only `ended`, `duration` and `unplayable` retry. Retrying `skip` would skip two songs; `429` is never retried |

## Features

- **Paste a link.** `watch`, `youtu.be`, `shorts`, `embed`, `music.`, bare
  11-character ids and playlists, with `t=90` / `t=1m30s` / `t=1h2m3s` start
  offsets preserved. Pasted ids resolve via oEmbed, so no API key is needed.
- **Floating reactions** — six emoji, persisted as `kind = "reaction"` chat
  rows, 9-second window capped at 24, golden-ratio lane hashing so a burst
  doesn't stack in one column.
- **Media Session** — lock-screen controls. Host buttons drive the room; guest
  play/pause maps to local mute, so a headphone click can't pause the party for
  everyone.
- **Per-track theming** — dominant artwork colour sampled in a 36×36 canvas,
  normalised for a near-black background, pushed onto `<html>` as `--vibe-*`
  channels that `Aurora` reads. Grey artwork keeps the house palette.
- **Shortcuts** — `space`/`k`, `n`, `←`/`→` (host), `m`, `/`, `r` — dispatched
  through a small `CustomEvent` bus rather than threaded props.

## Lint: 12 errors → 0

No rules were disabled. The two interesting ones were `QueuePanel` and
`LyricsOverlay`, where `setLoading(true)` sat at the top of a
fetch-on-prop-change effect. Rather than defer the `setState` to a microtask —
which games the linter without fixing the cascade — the response is now stored
together with the request it answers (`{key, data}`) and `loading` is derived as
`result.key !== currentQuery`. That removes the extra render *and* makes a stale
response unable to overwrite a newer one.

## Repo basics

`README.md` (with an explanation of how the sync actually works), `.env.example`,
MIT `LICENSE`, committed Drizzle migrations in `drizzle/`, `npm test` /
`npm run typecheck` scripts, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running typecheck →
lint → tests → build on every push and PR.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint .` — **0 errors** (was 12), 2 pre-existing `exhaustive-deps` warnings
- `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` — **53/53** (23 new: clock anchoring, backoff,
  retry eligibility, URL parsing, reactions, token buckets, fail-closed auth,
  HSL round-trip, dominant colour, every branch of the drift planner)
- `next build` — 13 routes, clean

**Not verified in a browser.** The build environment has no Postgres and no
display, so none of the UI or playback changes could be exercised at runtime —
they're covered by unit tests over pure functions and by source assertions.

## Not done

`NowPlaying.tsx` is still one very large component; no Playwright or k6 suites;
no Sentry wiring; beat-reactive visuals, Auto-DJ, PWA install and chat threading
remain in the backlog.

body:
## CLA

- [x] I have signed the [Stream CLA](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFKsKkAJI7mhCr7K9rEIOpqIDThrWxuvxnwUq2XkHyG154vQ/viewform) (required).
- [x] Code changes are tested

## Description of the changes, What, Why and How?

Ticket: https://linear.app/stream/issue/REACT-1375
Spec: [CHA-2667 Quiet hours – client SDK](https://app.notion.com/p/stream-wiki/cha-2667-quiet-hours-client-sdk-e1a6a5d7f9f682c48cec816312c107af)
v10 counterpart: #1999

The backend already supports quiet hours for push notifications. A user-level push preference can carry a `schedule` (a timezone and 1–7 quiet windows), and `remove_schedule` clears it. v9 has no types for them, so this PR adds the types, the helpers a UI needs, and keeps the connected user's preferences up to date after a save. The helpers and the merge are the same as in the v10 PR.

### Types (`src/types.ts`)

- `PushPreference`: `schedule?: PushScheduleInput`, `remove_schedule?: boolean`.
- `PushPreferencesResponse`: `schedule?: PushScheduleResponse`.
- New types: `PushScheduleInput`, `PushScheduleResponse`, `QuietHoursRuleInput` and `QuietHoursRuleResponse`. They follow the OpenAPI models (`start`/`end` as `HH:MM`, optional `days`).

### Helpers (`src/pushPreferences/`, exported from the root)

- `isInQuietHours({ schedule, date? })` tells whether a schedule is quiet at `date` (default: now).
  - It reads the wall clock in the schedule's timezone with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, so it follows daylight saving time.
  - A window whose end is earlier than its start runs past midnight. It belongs to the day it opens on, so `days` is checked against the previous day after midnight.
  - A rule without `days` applies every day. `00:00`–`24:00` covers the whole day.
- `getDeviceTimeZone()` returns the device's IANA timezone, to pre-fill a schedule.
- `QuietHoursDay` names the day values (`mon` … `sun`).

### Connected user

After a successful request, `setPushPreferences` merges the user-level preferences of the connected user into `client.user.push_preferences`:
- It uses the server's `user_preferences[userId]` when the response has it.
- `remove_schedule` drops the stored schedule unless the response returns a new one. `remove_disable` does the same for `disabled_until`.
- Channel-level items and items for other users leave `client.user` unchanged.
- `client.user` is replaced, not mutated, and only when the preferences changed.

The second commit removes a `node_modules` link that the first commit included by mistake.

### Tests

- `test/unit/pushPreferences/utils.test.ts` covers `isInQuietHours`: windows, past midnight, the whole day, several rules, timezones and DST. It also covers `getDeviceTimeZone` and the merge cases.
- `test/unit/pushPreferences/setPushPreferences.test.ts` covers the request payload and the connected user's state.

## Changelog

- Add the quiet hours `schedule` / `remove_schedule` push preference types.
- Add `isInQuietHours`, `getDeviceTimeZone` and `QuietHoursDay`.
- Keep `client.user.push_preferences` in sync after `setPushPreferences`.

body:
## What changed

### Settings tabs (Google Sheets, Profil Toko, Akun Kasir, Database & Backup, Kepatuhan BI)
- One subtab style (aria-selected) and one button set (`.set-btn` primary/secondary/ghost/danger) instead of a different colour per subtab.
- Panels are split into sections with dividers instead of cards nested in cards. Labels are 12–14px instead of 10–11px. Light-theme variants are checked against WCAG AA.
- The Google Sheets badge shows the saved config ("Belum diatur" / "Auto-sync aktif" / "Auto-sync mati") instead of an "AKTIF" badge that was always shown.
- Top nav: "Pengaturan" opens Profil Toko, "Google Sheets" opens the Sheets subtab, and the highlight follows the active subtab.
- Cashier tables: the role badges, Reset/Hapus buttons and hovered rows could not be read in light theme. They now use the themed components.

### Bugs fixed along the way
- **Database & Backup panel never showed.** Its markup was inside `#tab-pos`, so it stayed hidden while Settings was open. It now lives in `#tab-settings`.
- **DB stats were always "-".** `loadDatabaseInfo` called `apiFetch`, which does not exist, and now uses `authFetch`.
- **The DTTOT table and screening result put unescaped data into `innerHTML`.** All fields are escaped now.

### Official DTTOT list (530 entries)
- `tools/dttot-xlsx-to-json.py` (stdlib only) converts the official Excel export into `data/dttot-list.json`.
- `pos-db.js` re-syncs that file into `dttot_list` on server start whenever its hash changes. The sync runs in one transaction.
  - Official rows are identified by the new `ref_code` column (Kode Densus).
  - The sync replaces the 17 hard-coded sample seeds and keeps entries added by hand.
- Official rows cannot be deleted from the POS (the API returns 400). Search also matches the Densus code, and the list badge shows the real total (it used to stop at the API limit of 100).

### DTTOT matching: substring → whole word
With 530 entries, the old `LIKE %x%` and token matching flagged most ordinary names: 12 of 16 common names, including "Budi Santoso", "Muhammad Rizki" and "John Smith".

New rule in `dttot-match.js`, shared by transaction save, offline sync and `/api/dttot/check`:
- Every word of a listed name or alias must appear as a whole word in the customer name (any order, case- and accent-blind).
- One-word aliases are nicknames (JOHN, ADAM, UMAR; there are 214 in the list), so they only match a customer name that is exactly that word.

Result: 2 of 20 common names are still flagged, and both are exact official aliases (`ABDUL RAHMAN` in ILQ-288, `ABU HASAN` in ILQ-281). Every listed name tested is still caught.

## Reviewer notes
- **Compliance trade-off:** spelling variants that are not listed as an alias (e.g. Hasan vs Hassan) are no longer caught.
- **Personal data in the repo:** `data/dttot-list.json` holds personal data from the official list. The raw `.xlsx` is not committed.
- **Production DB:** on the first deploy the server replaces its DTTOT sample seeds with the official list. Entries added by hand stay.
- **Docs:** `docs/pos/PRODUCT.md` is new (product context for design work).
- **Dev config:** `.claude/launch.json` adds a local preview config.

## Testing
- `node --test tools/dttot-match.test.js`: 3/3 pass.
- Local server:
  - The sync log shows 530 entries.
  - A second start skips the sync because the hash is unchanged.
  - Screening was checked through the API with the names above.
- Browser, dark and light theme, desktop and 375px wide:
  - All five subtabs render, with no horizontal scroll.
  - Light-theme contrast on the cashier table measured ≥ 4.5:1.
- **Not tested:** submitting a real transaction from the cashier screen against the new matching.

body:
## Why
pivota-backend#2715 adds `scope=protocol` to `GET /agent/v1/merchants`. It lists the merchants a purchase reaches through a checkout protocol, one row per `merchant_domain` and `market`, with `checkout_routes`. The default list stays the portal list #28 documents, so the quickstart is unchanged; this PR adds the new scope.

## Change
- **`/developers/first-call`:** a new "Protocol merchants" section.
  - The request, and the row shape: no `merchant_id`, the `market` filter, daily freshness.
  - **For `storefront_checkout`:** `search_catalog`, then `create_checkout`. It returns a UCP checkout in `requires_escalation` whose `continue_url` is the merchant's storefront. Pivota collects no payment, and the totals are the last observed price.
  - **For `agentic_checkout`:** a payment partner places the order; it is listed only where the key is enabled for it.
  - It also defines `merchant_checkout_accepts_cards` as a fact about the merchant's checkout, not a Pivota payment capability.
  - The existing portal section links to it.
- **`/developers/request-types`:** mentions `?scope=protocol`.

`tsc --noEmit` passes locally; CI's Docker build checks the production build.

## Merge order
**Merge only after pivota-backend#2715 is live.** This site deploys on merge.

## Update 2026-11-07 (a495aa8): accuracy fixes from a partner-guide audit
- **agent-integration:**
  - The checkout-intents example carries `quote_id`. Without it the API returns `400 QUOTE_REQUIRED_BEFORE_PURCHASE`.
  - The response note now describes the real 200: `intent_id`, `checkout_url`, `expires_at`.
  - The OpenAPI proof point uses `/agent/docs/openapi.json`, because bare `/openapi.json` answers 307.
- **REST buyer identity:** the API key is enough to quote and order on REST, and `X-Agent-User-JWT` is optional. A verified buyer is required on the MCP/UCP doors only.
- **first-call:**
  - The default list is portal merchants.
  - Search results from other merchants carry `merchant_id: "external_seed"` and `external_domain`, and the order call refuses them.
- **Protocol section:**
  - `storefront_checkout` is on the UCP door and needs a verified buyer; otherwise it returns `USER_AUTH_REQUIRED`.
  - Totals are the merchant's own cart price when its checkout can price the cart, because `AGENT_CHECKOUT_UCP_MERCHANT_PRICING_ENABLED=1` in prod. Otherwise they are the last observed catalog price.
  - The list is built from "recent" checkout checks, not "daily" ones.

author: chemitaro
body:
## 概要

SpecDock のダッシュボード（別のオリジン）に置いた「Orca で開く」のボタンから、この Mac の Orca の**既存のタブ**を前面に出せるようにしました。偽の要求（別のオリジン、許していない Host、トークンのない要求）は、Orca に何も送る前に止めます。epic-00003 の slice（R-04、R-05、F-03、F-04）です。

Refs #7
Refs #3

## 変わること

### 書き込みの守り（`src/server/config.ts`、`src/server/guard.ts`、`src/server/app.ts`）
- 設定は iss-00006 と共通の `PORT`、`ORCA_BIN`、`ORCA_WEB_READ_ORIGINS`、`ORCA_WEB_SETTINGS_FILE` に、`ORCA_WEB_TAILSCALE_IP` を足しました。待ち受けは 127.0.0.1 と Tailscale の IP だけです。SpecDock のオリジン（`ORCA_WEB_READ_ORIGINS`）は、読み取りの CORS と `frame-ancestors` の両方に使います（空なら `'none'`）。
- **すべての要求**（静的な画面を含む）で Host を `127.0.0.1:<port>`、`localhost:<port>`、`<Tailscale の IP>:<port>` との完全一致で確かめます（違えば 421 `misdirected_host`。DNS rebinding）。
- 書き込み（`POST /api/open` と、iss-00006 の項目の選択の保存 `PUT /api/settings/fields`）は、決めた method、`application/json`、`Origin` が `http://<Host>` と完全一致、`Sec-Fetch-Site` があれば `same-origin`、`X-Orca-Web-Token` の有効なトークン、4 KiB 以下、`{ worktree, agent? }` だけの物を要します。CORS の許可は付けません。
- トークンは `POST /api/token`（同じオリジンの JSON の POST だけ）が出します（256 ビット、10 分、メモリーだけ）。

### 開く口（`src/orca/open*.ts`、`src/orca/wiring.ts`）
- worktree（ID かパス）を最新の `worktree list` で解決し、`session.tabs.list` から、指定の paneKey → 最後に動いたエージェント → 最後に見ていたタブ → worktree だけ、の順に1つを選びます。
- 動いている端末は `orca terminal switch`、ほかのタブは `session.tabs.activate`、worktree だけは `worktree.activate`。どれも `navigation: "host"` で、送るのは1回だけです。
- 門（`OpenOrcaCli`、`OpenRpc`）が、読む操作とこの3つ（activate は host だけ）のほかを送らずに拒みます。タブやファイルを作る操作を送る経路はありません。
- 時間切れや結果不明は `unconfirmed`（504）で、別のタブへ切り替えません。機能の欠け、形の違い、runtime の ID の変化は何も送らずに理由を返します。重なった要求は `busy`（409）。
- 統括の判断：タブのない worktree を選ぶと、Orca 自身が最初の端末を作ります（サイドバーで選ぶのと同じ通常の動き）。これは許し、応答の `mayCreateInitialTerminal: true` で示します。

### ボタンの部品（`web/embed/`）
- 1行のスクリプト `<script src="http://127.0.0.1:8791/embed/open-button.js" data-worktree="…"></script>` が、自分の位置に iframe を差し込みます。親の幅が 390px 以下の間は隠し、読み込みません。
- iframe（`/embed/open-button`）は CSP（`frame-ancestors` に SpecDock のオリジンだけ、inline なし）で返り、同じオリジンから得たトークンで開く口を呼びます。

### そのほか
- 実機の確かめの道具 `npm run open:live`（作業の場所と同じ repo の worktree だけを対象に、押す前と後のタブの集合を数だけで比べる）。
- iss-00005 の最終品質ゲートの FQG-001（`_meta.runtimeId` の食い違い）と FQG-002（keepalive が時間切れを延ばす）のテスト。

## iss-00006（PR #11）との統合
- PR #11（0a0e76c）が先にマージされたので、`origin/main` をマージのコミット（10fca65）で取り込み、`src/server/app.ts`・`config.ts`・`main.ts` の衝突を解きました（履歴の書き換えと強制 push はしていません）。
- `createAppServer(options)` は iss-00006 の形（poller、settings、readOrigins、extraHosts、webDir）に `open` と `tokens` を足しました。待ち受けのアドレスごとのサーバーで1つの処理を共有するため `createAppHandler` も出します。
- iss-00006 の小さな守り `src/server/same-origin-write.ts` を消し、**項目の選択の保存も、この PR の書き込みの守り（同じオリジンの JSON と短期のトークン）の下に置きました**。画面の保存は、新しい `web/write.js`（iframe と共有）でトークンを得て送ります。状態の画面にも `frame-ancestors` を足しました。

author: shortarrow
body:
Two faults at the start of a page turn, both handled in the [script in the head](https://github.com/ShortArrow/hugo-theme-bestiary/blob/cdbbde4ed5cde497a169e0ee6963fe5b338e4929/layouts/baseof.html#L19) that runs as a new page is revealed.

## A blank sheet over the leaf before every turn

The flap of a page turn is drawn by an empty `.bestiary-fold` element in the leaf, as the leaf's blank back. Its [rule](https://github.com/ShortArrow/hugo-theme-bestiary/blob/cdbbde4ed5cde497a169e0ee6963fe5b338e4929/assets/css/bestiary.css#L509) drew it whenever a transition of type `page-turn` was active. That includes the page being left, while the browser captures it. For that moment the old page showed a blank sheet of paper over its leaf, hiding the text, and then the turn began. The script now puts the class `bestiary-revealing` on the root of the page being revealed, and removes it when the transition finishes. The flap is drawn only under that class.

## A turn onto the same page

On the home page, clicking the site title turned the home page over onto itself. A link to the page already open is still a navigation, so the page turn ran from a leaf to the same leaf. The script now compares the URL of the page revealed with that of the page left, using the Navigation API's `activation`. When they are the same, it calls `skipTransition()`. A link to an anchor on the same page does not reload it, so it never starts a turn.

## Tests

- [Leaving a page](https://github.com/ShortArrow/hugo-theme-bestiary/blob/cdbbde4ed5cde497a169e0ee6963fe5b338e4929/tests/visual/leaf.spec.mjs#L63) checks on `pageswap` that the flap is hidden on the page being left. Before the fix it was `visible`.
- [Following the site title on the home page](https://github.com/ShortArrow/hugo-theme-bestiary/blob/cdbbde4ed5cde497a169e0ee6963fe5b338e4929/tests/visual/leaf.spec.mjs#L52) checks that the page is revealed again with no turn. Before the fix it turned.

author: phanlipo
body:
## Was

Der Markdown-Editor kann eine Datei jetzt direkt dort speichern, wo sie liegt (Chrome/Edge am Computer). Bisher hat jedes Speichern eine neue Kopie heruntergeladen.

- **Datei öffnen …** nutzt `showOpenFilePicker`. Die geöffnete Datei bleibt mit der App verknüpft.
- **Speichern:** Der Knopf oben wird zur Diskette und schreibt mit `createWritable()` in dieselbe Datei zurück. Beim ersten Speichern fragt der Browser um Schreib-Erlaubnis. Ein Punkt am Knopf zeigt ungespeicherte Änderungen.
- **Speichern unter …** (im Menü) nutzt `showSaveFilePicker`. Das Dokument übernimmt den gewählten Dateinamen.
- **Strg/Cmd+S** speichert in die verknüpfte Datei. Ist keine verknüpft: „Speichern unter“, ohne die API ein Download.
- **„Öffnen mit“** (installierte App): Neu ist `Tools.fileHandle(file)` in `common.js`. Es liefert den Handle aus `launchQueue`, den die App bisher verworfen hat. So lässt sich auch dorthin zurückspeichern.
- **Gleiche Datei nochmal öffnen:** Die App wechselt zum vorhandenen Dokument, statt es doppelt anzulegen.
- **Ohne die API** (iPhone, Safari, Firefox) ändert sich nichts: weiter Download und `<input type=file>`.

Die Handles liegen nur im Speicher, bis die App geschlossen wird. Den Speicher-Standard (nur `localStorage`, keine IndexedDB) habe ich nicht angefasst. Der Text bleibt wie bisher im Browser gespeichert. Hilfe (DE/EN), Diagnose (`fileAccess`, `linkedFiles`, …) und AGENTS.md sind ergänzt.

## Tests

- Neu in `tests/markdown-editor.spec.mjs`: `mockFileAccess` ersetzt die Dateiauswahl und die Handles, denn Playwright kann den Picker nicht bedienen. Geprüft werden Öffnen, Zurückspeichern (Text- und Ansicht-Modus), der Punkt für ungespeicherte Änderungen, Speichern unter, Strg+S, Abbrechen, verweigerte Erlaubnis, „Öffnen mit“, erneutes Öffnen und die englischen Texte.
- Der bisherige Öffnen-Test prüft jetzt den Ausweichweg ohne API.
- `npm test` lokal: 1992 bestanden, 1 übersprungen (inkl. WebKit/Firefox).

author: maro114510
body:
# Merge Overview

The Design Doc now says oe wait and the board make one light read every 2 minutes, read every child Issue only on a change or a time-based deadline, and wait out a rate limit instead of failing. The implementation tasks in this Epic start from this.

## Background

All tokens of one user share one hourly GraphQL bucket across every machine. Today oe wait re-reads every child Issue on each poll and oe ready pages through every open PR in the repository, so the cost grows with the number of Epics, children, and open PRs, and a drained bucket stops the run. The Epic writes the target state into the Design Doc first, and the scripts follow in later Issues.

Closes #614

## Implementation Details

- The rules live once, as the Polling, Open PRs, and Rate limit rows under Decisions, and oe wait and Board refresh point to them, because review found the same rule stated in three places read as three rules.
- A time-based deadline, such as a head with no checks for 10 minutes, also triggers the full read, because some rows change an action with nothing changing on GitHub.
- Only oe wait waits out a rate limit. oe ready still exits with an error on any failed read, so the invariant that a failed read decides nothing holds.

## Changes

### Waiting and the board
- oe wait reads GitHub as Polling and Rate limit say, and the board refreshes as Polling says instead of every 3 minutes.

### Decisions
- Polling: one light read every 2 minutes, and every child Issue is read only on a change to it, its PR, or its checks, or at a deadline.
- Open PRs: oe ready reads only the PRs of the child Issues' branches.
- Rate limit: oe wait waits until the reset time, and any other failure still ends it.

## Impact

Documentation only. The scripts still poll the old way until the follow-up Issues implement these rows.

## Concerns

- The doc already said a board refresh adds no GitHub reads while a Runner holds the lock, but `oe status --watch` still runs oe ready on every refresh. The follow-up Issue that applies Polling to the board should close that gap.

## Test Plan

- Searched the doc for a 60-second poll and a 3-minute refresh: neither remains.
- `claude plugin validate .`: passed with warnings.
- A separate-context self-review of the first commit raised only that the scripts do not yet match the doc, which is this Epic's planned order.

author: kratosdatagod
body:
Part of the redactor consolidation (EA-028).

## What
The best practices check runs in a Fabric notebook, where the app's modules aren't installed. Until now it scrubbed the error it saves with a short pattern list of its own, covering a Bearer header, a JWT, SAS query values and a URL's user:password. It wrote `[redacted]`.

Now the notebook gets a copy of `redact.secrets`' patterns, flags and replacements, written in as a literal when the app builds the notebook (`model_bpa._secret_patterns`). The error file in the lakehouse is redacted just as the app redacts, with `[removed]`, and it picks up any pattern added to `redact.secrets` later. The app still redacts the error again when it reads it back (`model_bpa.error`).

A change to the patterns changes the generated notebook, so the app republishes it on the next check, as it does for any other notebook change.

## Tests
- New: `test_the_check_cell_redacts_with_the_apps_own_patterns` runs the generated cell and checks that the error it saves equals `redact.secrets` of the original. The original holds a GitHub token, an AWS key, a connection-string password and a Teams webhook, none of which the old list knew.
- The existing cell tests pass unchanged: Bearer, JWT, SAS and user:password are still removed. The model_bpa tests, `test_rpc_surface`, silent_except, ruff, py_compile and the mypy ratchet all pass.
