author: michielmanalytics
body: ## Summary I work on [boxd](https://boxd.sh/?ref=sheprd). boxd runs full Linux microVMs (KVM) with a persistent disk that start in about a second, and can be hibernated, snapshotted and forked. This PR adds boxd as a cloud device provider, behind its own `boxd` Cargo feature and shaped like Sprites: an API key, and this app as the exec relay, so there is no SSH key to set up. **Since the first review:** three `fix(cloud)` commits on top address the review. The relay now runs under the config folder the app resolved (including a login shell's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` adopted after a desktop launch), an exec reply whose body ends without a gRPC status fails instead of waiting, and the boxd tab shows its errors in the chosen language. Each has tests. The Sprites and OpenSandbox relays build their command the same way as boxd's did; I left them alone to keep this PR to boxd. What it adds: - `crates/sheprd-remote/src/boxd/`: the provider (settings, credential store, API calls, readiness, setup jobs, the relay) and a `[boxd]` config table. One row in `cloud/providers.rs`. - The `Boxd` variant in `sheprd-client`, the feature forwarded from `sheprd-gpui` (on by default, like the other providers), a Settings > Cloud devices > boxd tab copied from the Sprites tab, the Add Device rail entry, error localization, `assets/icons/cloud/boxd.svg`, and the per-provider match arms in tests. - Docs: a "boxd (experimental)" section in the crate README, `[boxd]` in `config-gpui.example.toml`, the provider lists in `docs/cli.md`, and a row in `docs/sandbox.md`'s evaluated providers table. **Transport, and why no Tokio.** boxd has no Rust SDK and its API is gRPC. `sheprd-remote-control`'s Cargo.toml says Tokio should never reach the GUI, so I didn't use tonic. boxd's API port also serves grpc-web over HTTP/1.1, and it runs bidirectional streams full duplex there. So: - Unary calls (`CreateVm`, `GetVm`, `ListVms`, `StartVm`/`ResumeVm`/`WakeVm`, `DestroyVm`) go through ureq with the same bounds as the other REST clients (size cap, no redirects, sensitive bearer header, one short line of the error). The few protobuf fields are encoded by hand in `boxd/wire.rs`; unknown reply fields are skipped. - `Exec` runs over one blocking TLS connection: stdin is a chunked request body that ends when stdin ends, and the reply's chunks carry stdout, stderr, the exit code and the gRPC status. `sheprd __boxd-exec ACCOUNT MACHINE COMMAND...` relays it the way `ssh` would, so Herdr's bridge, the installer, Teleport's scripts and `cloud exec` work unchanged. I split `cloud::socket::connect` out of `socket::open` to reuse its TLS setup; Sprites and OpenSandbox behave the same. - New dependency: `httparse` (already in the lockfile through tungstenite), optional, only with the `boxd` feature. **A separate fix in the first commit.** The relay helpers return from `app::run` before it set the config loader, so any relay that reads its provider's table failed with "Sheprd's config is not available to cloud providers." That includes Sprites and OpenSandbox today: `sheprd __sprites-exec https://api.sprites.dev x true` prints that error on `main`. The fix moves `set_loader` above the helpers. It is also open on its own as #1136. Once that lands, I'll rebase this PR and drop the commit here. ### How it maps onto the cloud provider table | Sheprd | boxd | | --- | --- | | account | the API URL, `https://boxd.sh:9443` (a region is `https://.boxd.sh:9443`); the API key is in the credential store, `HERDR_BOXD_API_KEY` takes precedence | | device ID | the machine's UUID, so a rename at boxd doesn't break the device; the name is shown | | create (Settings, `cloud create`, dispatch) | `CreateVm` with a generated `sheprd-` name, boxd's default Ubuntu 24.04 image, the label `sheprd=device` plus any `[boxd] labels` | | install Herdr | Herdr's installer through the relay, on approval, as for Sprites | | connect | `GetVm`; `StartVm` if stopped, `ResumeVm` if in standby, `WakeVm` if hibernated; then the bridge through the relay | | account line in Settings | `ListVms` with `sheprd=device` ("the API key sees N machines made here") | | Remove device (delete) | `DestroyVm` after the unpushed-work search; a machine already gone counts as deleted | | failed create | the machine is deleted again | ### Where boxd does not map cleanly 1. **Long-lived exec streams.** A connected device's bridge is one exec stream that stays open for as long as the device is connected. I left a connected device idle for 38 minutes and the same relay process held the connection the whole time, with no reconnect in the log. If the stream ever drops, Sheprd reconnects as for any dropped remote host. 2. **Sleeping machines.** boxd machines hibernate after 4 idle hours by default, and an organization can also turn on standby after a shorter idle time. Idle means no network traffic, and a connected bridge is traffic (the machine above stayed `running`). Connecting brings a sleeping machine back: 0.9 s from hibernation and 2 s from stopped in my runs; boxd keeps processes across standby and hibernation, and Herdr's server comes back on the next bridge after a stop. Sheprd doesn't change these timeouts; users who want a machine never to sleep set that in boxd. 3. **Images.** boxd machines can start from snapshots, not from Dockerfiles, so `image` is `None` and `spec.image` is ignored, like Sprites. A boxd snapshot setting could come later. 4. **Machine names are global.** boxd names are DNS labels under `boxd.sh`, so a generated name can in theory collide; the create then fails with boxd's message and nothing is saved. 5. **No orphan adoption.** A crash between `CreateVm` and saving the device leaves the machine unlisted, as for Sprites. It carries `sheprd=device`, so it is findable in boxd; adopting it back could follow the Container card's pattern later. 6. **Windows.** Unavailable, like every cloud device (`cloud::unavailable()`). 7. **Wire format by hand.** I encode the few fields instead of generating code from boxd's proto, to avoid a protobuf toolchain in the build. Field numbers follow boxd's public `api.proto`; replies with unknown fields still decode. If you'd rather have `prost` for this, I can switch. ## Validation Re-run after the review fixes, on head `e8508137`: - [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - [x] `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `--no-default-features`: clean - [x] `scripts/check-file-size.sh`, `scripts/check-sorted.py`, `scripts/check-i18n.py` (5606 messages valid and used), `assets/icons/test_artwork.py`, `git diff --check`, `scripts/release/check-commit-messages.py range`: pass - [x] `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features`: 8734 passed, 0 failed, 34 ignored. `cargo test --locked --workspace` (default features): 8687 passed, 0 failed, 25 ignored. Both ran with `-j 2 -- --test-threads=2` on a 16 GB machine. - [x] Unit tests for the provider (37 in `sheprd-remote` besides the 2 live ones, 6 in `sheprd-gpui`): protobuf encoding and decoding including malformed and oversized input, the reply decoder on a reply captured from the live service and the same reply fed one byte at a time, trailers-only refusals, HTTP failures, broken chunking, chunked and `Content-Length` bodies that end without a status (whole and byte by byte, output before the end kept), settings validation (origin only, labels), the relay command's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, a loopback grpc-web API (create with labels, list by label, wake a hibernated machine once, start a stopped one, cancellation, typed errors), the relay against a loopback server that answers while the request body is still open (200 KB of every byte value both ways, stderr, exit codes, empty stdin, a failed call, and a reply without a statu

author: nikolagorannaumovski
body:
## CLA

- [x] I have signed the [Stream CLA](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFKsKkAJI7mhCr7K9rEIOpqIDThrWxuvxnwUq2XkHyG154vQ/viewform) (required).
- [x] Code changes are tested

## Description of the changes, What, Why and How?

Ticket: https://linear.app/stream/issue/REACT-1376
Docs: [Query Channels – active member count](https://getstream.io/chat/docs/javascript/query-channels/#active-member-count)
v9 counterpart: #2002
React v15: https://github.com/GetStream/stream-chat-react/pull/3413

Query Channels returns `active_member_count` for each channel when the request has `include_active_member_count: true`. v10's generated client already has both fields. This PR exposes the count in `channel.state` and keeps it through later channel updates.

### State

- `ChannelState` has a new `activeMemberCount` slice (in `MembersState`). It is `undefined` until a response carries `active_member_count`.
- The `channel.data` setter publishes `activeMemberCount` with `data`, `memberCount` and `ownCapabilities` in one update.

### Carrying the count

Only Query Channels returns `active_member_count`. Other responses and events that replace `channel.data` (watch, update, `channel.updated`, …) don't have it. When the new data omits it and the previous data had it:
- the previous count is carried onto a copy of the new data, as `member_count` and `own_capabilities` already are;
- it moves by the change in `member_count`, and stays between 0 and `member_count`. For example, a member removed between two queries lowers it by one.

When the new data has `active_member_count`, it is used as is.

`ai-docs/v10-breaking-changes.md` mentions the new slice and the carry rule.

### Tests

- `test/unit/channel_state.test.js` covers the initial value, the carry, a new count from the server, moving with `member_count`, a `channel.updated` event, the bounds, and clearing `channel.data`.
- `test/unit/client.test.js` checks that a queried channel keeps its count after a channel query that omits it.

## Changelog

- Add `channel.state` `activeMemberCount`, filled from Query Channels with `include_active_member_count`.

author: minimalnl
body: ## Why Universal Everything follows the per-token LSP4 override. On all 7 minted tokens that override is still `icon` = the 600px file and `images` = the 2400px file, so both the enlarged view and “Open image in new tab” stay on `N-600.png`. There is no separate original/download control. This changes the existing owner-only **Fix images for UE** tool so both `icon` and `images` are the 2400px file (`.png`). The 600px PNGs on the site are left as they are. Mint price, supply, claim, contract address, and ownership are unchanged. `tokenMetadataJSON()` is the contract’s immutable computed metadata (empty icon, and both 2400 and 600 in `images`). It does not change. A new mint still gets that computed metadata until the owner runs the button again. The button does not promise to fix future mints by itself. ## What the button does For each minted token it reads `getDataForTokenId` (the override UE uses). If that override is already icon + images = the 2400 original, it skips the token. Otherwise it copies the stored LSP4 JSON and replaces only `icon` and `images`, keeping name, description, links, assets, and attributes (including Seed). Each update is simulated with `eth_call` before the owner is asked to sign. Cancel or a failed token stops the run; a later click skips tokens that already stored the 2400 override. The note no longer says `icon=600`. It says both fields point at the 2400px file, and that new mints keep the computed metadata until the button is run again. ## Tests `node --test scripts/gg-ue-fix.test.mjs` — **12 passed, 0 failed** (with `ethers@6.13.5` and `@noble/hashes@1.3.3`, not committed): - LSP4 key is 32 bytes and equals `keccak256("LSP4Metadata")` - selectors match `ethers.id` for `setDataForTokenId(bytes32,bytes32,bytes)`, `getDataForTokenId(bytes32,bytes32)`, `tokenMetadataJSON(uint256)`, `imageBaseURI()` - produced calldata matches `ethers` ABI encoding - VerifiableURI prefix `00008019f9b10020`, hash is keccak256 of the UTF-8 JSON (noble and ethers agree), data URL base64 round-trips, including a non-ASCII description - patched icon and images are the same 2400 object; no 600 in those fields; other LSP4 fields kept - the current 600-icon override and the computed JSON are not treated as done - cancel/retry: updated tokens are skipped on the next pass - owner guard accepts `0x5222…` and rejects `0x7070…` - simulation report: all 7 skipped passes; mixed updated+skipped passes; the old status string `skip` and a failed `eth_call` fail the report `node --check` passed for `grid-ad.js` and the scripts. ## Read-only mainnet simulation `node scripts/gg-ue-fix.simulate.mjs` against `https://rpc.mainnet.lukso.network`, contract `0x33Dd4D3da812e2cc1B3692456470DFDD99659e62`. No wallet, no `eth_sendTransaction`. Exit 0. - minted: **7** - owner: `0x52224e802F722A3F3f1de8b2157597ae7fEfffD1` (not `0x7070…`) - image base: `https://minimalnl.github.io/stille-feed/gg/42/` - `updated: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]`, `skipped: []` (every override is still icon 600 / images 2400) - exact calldata (noble keccak, same bytes as the `ethers` encoder) `eth_call` from that owner returned `0x` for every token - each `N.png` is HTTP 206 and a real **2400×2400** PNG - attributes and name were preserved in the prepared JSON The script used to store `ethCall: "skip"` while `report.ok` only accepted `"skipped"`. An all-skipped or mixed rerun after the owner updates would have exited 1. Skip rows are now `"skipped"`, and that case is covered by the unit test above. The button code is unchanged. ## After an approved merge The owner connects `0x5222…` and clicks **Fix images for UE**. With the chain as simulated, that is **7 signatures**, one `setDataForTokenId` per token, each dry-run first. Tokens that already store the 2400 override are not submitted. Cancelling midway is safe to retry. ## Not verified UE’s enlarged view and “Open image” still show the 600px file until those overrides are actually written, and UE may cache the old metadata after that. This PR does not send transactions, merge, or deploy. The public page was loaded locally before this follow-up: Generative Square still renders (`#8 of 1000`, the next mint), the fix and claim buttons stay hidden for a visitor, and the page context exposes the new note and the owner guard. No console exception. This follow-up did not repeat that browser check.

**Décision attendue** : aucune.

**Ce qui change** : `chaine.ts:noterReponse` écarte les notations `calibration_jeu_or` et `arbitrage_jeu_or` avant `decider`. Il réutilise `separerCalibration` de `file-humaine.ts`. C'est conforme au §7 : la règle de décision ne lit que les juges, l'échantillon de 10 % et les humains appelés, et le jeu d'or ne sert qu'au kappa.

**Bug corrigé** : sur un pilote, relancer la chaîne sur une réponse du jeu d'or calibrée et encore sans verdict levait `NotationsIncoherentes`. Les tests reproduisent l'échec sur `main` avant le correctif.

**Ce qui pourrait casser** : un futur motif humain sans rôle dans la décision doit passer par `separerCalibration`, sinon le même échec reviendra. L'empreinte figée des verdicts du run simulé devra être relevée à chaque changement voulu de la règle de décision.

**Comment c'est testé** : 6 tests dans `tests/notation/chaine-jeu-or.test.ts` (calibration, arbitrage, humain qui tranche, run mensuel inchangé, verdicts identiques octet pour octet au code d'avant). `pnpm check` vert, 1 210 tests de notation verts après la fusion de `main`.

Global tablolardır: `TenantId` ve RLS yok, `TableInventoryTests` muaf listesine gerekçeyle eklendi. Bir tarihte yürürlükteki sürüm, o günü geçmemiş en yeni olandır. Sürüm değiştirilmez; yanlışsa silinip yeniden yüklenir (kayıtlar koda göre başvurduğundan silme tenant verisini bozmaz).
- **`IGtipCatalog`** (`Core.Contracts`, modüllerin okuma sözleşmesi): `CheckAsync` → `Found`, `PrefixOnly` (kod katalogdaki daha uzun kodların başı, ör. 6 haneli alt pozisyon), `NotFound` (uyarı), `NoCatalog` (yürürlükte sürüm yok, uyarı üretilmez). Hiçbiri kaydı engellemez (K9). `SearchAsync` kod ön eki ya da tanım içinde öneri verir.
- **`IGtipCatalogAdmin`** (`Core`): sürüm oluşturma (2000'lik parçalarla, tek işlemde; sürüm başına en çok 200 000 satır; boş liste, yinelenen kod, aynı yürürlük tarihi reddedilir), silme, sürüm listesi, satır arama. Her yazma platform denetim kaydındadır.
- **`GtipRules`** (biçim kuralı: yalnızca rakam, 6–14 hane) depo modülünden `Core.Contracts`'a taşındı; katalog ve stok kartı aynı kuralı kullanır.
- **Uç noktalar:** platform `GET /api/platform/gtip/versions`, `GET .../versions/{id}/entries`, `DELETE .../versions/{id}` (rol: Operasyon, `PlatformAccessRules`); tenant `GET /api/gtip/check`, `GET /api/gtip/search` (depo modülü açık ve `warehouse.stockitems.read`). Katalog ürün standardı verisidir, tenant verisi değildir.
- ADR-0032 uygulama durumu ve README güncellendi.

## Test

Yerelde (Release, SQL Server ayakta), yalnızca ilgili alanlar:
- `GtipCatalogTests` (yeni, 4 test): mutlu yol (sürüm, satır araması, ayraçlı giriş, `PrefixOnly`, `NotFound`, yürürlük tarihine göre iki sürüm, öneri, denetim kaydı), silme (satırlar gider, `NoCatalog`), doğrulama (boş liste, yinelenen kod, boş ad, aynı tarihli ikinci sürüm çakışır ve ilkini bozmaz, bozuk kod 400, bilinmeyen sürüm 404), paylaşım ve yetki (iki tenant aynı kataloğu görür, modülü kapalı tenant ve tesis izinli kullanıcı 403, tenant kullanıcısı platform uçlarında 403, oturumsuz 401) — geçti. Testler birbirini etkilemesin diye kendi yüzyıl aralığında rastgele yürürlük tarihi kullanır ve sürümlerini siler.
- `GtipCatalogRulesTests` (Core, 11 durum), `Modulix.Modules.Warehouse.Tests` (23), mimari testler (56) — geçti.
- `PlatformAdministrationTests` (platform rol tablosu dahil) ve `SectorCatalogApiTests` — geçti.
- `TableInventoryTests` yalnızca `platform.LicensePolicies` için kırılıyor: yerel veritabanı başka bir daldan kalan tabloyu içeriyor (benim değişikliğim değil); GTİP tabloları muaf listesinde. CI'da temiz veritabanında doğrulanır.

**Doğrulanmadı:** Tam entegrasyon seti ve CI çalışmadı. Dosya yükleme ve arayüz bu PR'da yok. Gerçek Bakanlık cetveli ile deneme yapılmadı; GTİP uzunluklarının mevzuat doğruluğu doğrulanmadı.

author: vegardw
body:
Fixes #183.

### Summary

`mkc clean` fails when removing `built` or `pxt_modules` on Node.js 25 and later because Node removed the `recursive` option from `fs.rmdir`.

The Node host now uses `fs.promises.rm` for recursive directory removal when that API is available. It checks that the path is a directory before calling `rm`, preserving the existing behavior of rejecting plain files. Older Node versions and nonrecursive calls still use `rmdir`.

### Verification

I built the CLI from this branch and tested it locally on Node.js v26.13.0.

- In a temporary directory, I created `built` and `pxt_modules` with nested files. I ran `mkc clean` and confirmed that it removed both directories and their contents. I ran it again and confirmed it exited successfully with both directories absent.
- I also ran `mkc clean` in an actual Arcade project and confirmed it succeeded.

author: marukome0743
body:
## Summary

Main was slower than v0.11.0 for every guest instruction. #321 grew `execute` past what the compiler inlines by itself, so `execute_decoded` makes one more call per instruction. This adds `#[inline(always)]` on `execute`, whose only non-test caller is `execute_decoded`. The wasm grows by 3,115 bytes.

Found while checking a report from formicarium on jj's speed.

## Measurements

`jj status` and `jj root` on a one-file repository, wasm build, Node 26.13 on an Arm Mac, no JIT, in rotating order. The difference is the median of paired runs against v0.11.0 built locally.

| Build | `status` (21 runs) | `root` (21 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| v0.11.0 | 1774 ms, min 1288 | 500 ms, min 472 |
| main | 1630 ms, min 1363, **+4.4%** | 537 ms, min 487, **+6.1%** |
| this change | 1496 ms, min 1307, **+1.1%** | 513 ms, min 478, **+1.4%** |

The medians in the `status` column are not in order because other work loaded the machine (load average 4 to 9). The paired differences and minimums are the reliable part.

By commit, against v0.11.0, 15 pairs each: #318 +1.0%, #321 +4.7%, #322 +4.5%, #323 +5.1%, #324 +4.6%, #325 +5.2%, main +3.7%. `execute` first appears as its own function in #321.

## Not done or not verified

- About 1% is left. It is about what #318 (the iced-x86 update) showed, but I did not establish that as the cause, and the noise is of that size.
- The measured build came from main at `e63587e2` with the same attribute and no comment. The build here has the same size and differs in content, as the comment moves line numbers. I did not measure it again.
- Native builds, browsers and larger repositories were not measured.
- Nothing stops this recurring: no CI check watches the speed or the inlining.
- `#[cold]` on `fxsave`, `fxrstor` and `x87` changed nothing, as they were already separate functions, so it is not included.

`cargo test -p paludarium-cpu`, `cargo clippy -p paludarium-cpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint:all` pass on macOS.

author: espadonne
body:
wolf lsp on PAX: the dev image's language server runs unchanged; a new suite holds it frame for frame to Linux.

Footprint: cross-cutting

(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains the `mpx5-lsp` job; `tools/ci-tiers.map` and `tests/ci-plan` are CI's own planner
and its proof. No kernel change.)

## 1. Forbidden, and what was read

No kernel, firmware or driver source of any system. Read as the program under test: wolf-lang's `crates/wolf_lsp` and
the driver's `lsp` entry at `v0.2.36`, the `lsp-server` 0.10.0 crate's stdio transport, wolf-lsp's `lspconf` scripts
and recorded transcripts at the same compiler pin; sagitta's LSP client and job spawner, for how an editor starts and
watches a server. The LSP 3.17 specification and the man pages. Linux black-box under `strace -f`. `docs/SOURCES.md`
under px99.

## 2. Inputs, verified

- Base: trunk `aba55824` (begun on `37217ba0`; rebased onto `411fc9f5`, then onto `aba55824`, where four files met
  trunk's additions beside them and each kept both: the map's `@net`/`@user`, the README's suites table, SOURCES and
  the CHANGELOG). The second base moves the kernel this suite boots (the network's modules, linked into every
  kernel); the suite uses no network, and its rows at the head are the same. The earlier heads are kept as
  `px99-prerebase` and `px99-prerebase2`.
- `/usr/bin/wolf` sha256 `2df1fb76…ab59`, 16,257,584 bytes, `user/wolf.sums`' bytes for `tools/mkwolf`'s build of
  wolf-lang `v0.2.36` (`5adf3d91`); the std `78b9d3cb` at `/usr/share/wolf/compiler-std`, as the dev image keeps it.
- `user/elf/lspc.c` (C with no libc) by `tools/mklspc`; `kmain_console` at both tiers; QEMU 8.2.2 in an Ubuntu 24.04
  container, KVM and TCG.

## 3. Prediction, scored

Committed first (`523abd49`). Right on every call PAX had to serve: nothing new is asked, no -ENOSYS from `wolf`, no
`refused:` line. Not foreseen: the server sizes a worker pool from `sched_getaffinity` and the cgroup quota (13
threads on the reference's 8 CPUs; fewer on PAX's one), all already served. Frames byte-identical with no
normalisation, as predicted. Time: under 1 ms to the first diagnostics on Linux, 0 to 20 ms on PAX under KVM in
whole 10 ms steps (PAX's monotonic clock is its 100 Hz tick), 110–120 ms under TCG. The table is in the note, §3.

## 4. Evidence index

- **The session** (`tests/mpx5-lsp`, four runs a boot, nothing typed): `initialize`, `didOpen` of a file with one type
  error (E0401 published, its range the literal, its related location the annotation), an unsaved `didChange` that
  fixes it (cleared 110 ms later, after the server's 100 ms debounce), `shutdown`, `exit`, status 0, one SIGCHLD; and
  a server slowed by the compiler's own test hook, killed by its process group after 3 s (signal 9, one SIGCHLD), then
  a write to it answering EPIPE. As root and as `pax`.
- **LSP1:** every transcript byte-identical to the container's on every leg; the one normalisation, named in the
  row, is the client's `time:` lines, left out of both sides.
- **LSP2:** the session's own witness from the repository's files alone (the capabilities wolf-lsp recorded at the
  same pin, the ranges found in `typed.lu`), proved first by 23 mutations of the recorded transcripts. Seen red first:
  with no witness at `1421edf0` (before the rebase), every LSP2 row red by name, LSP1 and LSP3 green
  (`notes/px99/dev2-red-lsp2-1421edf0.txt`). It also caught the suite's own hole: at the first boot LSP2 had passed
  with its witness absent (`notes/px99/dev1-vacuous-lsp2-6014b64a.txt`), fixed in `c1bd9138`.
- **CI wiring, red first:** with the job alone (`e3421f84`), three exact-list rows of `tests/ci-plan` red by name;
  green with the map and rows (`16a2707e`, `89a3b36f`), 328 checks then, 329 at the head.
- **The calls:** `notes/px99/strace-census.txt` and both traces.
- **What yew's client needs** (the note's §4.6): the child's pipes, poll over the terminal and pipes, SIGCHLD through a
  self-pipe, a group kill, EPIPE, all shown working; a timer finer than 10 ms named as a limit (R-px99-2, #299).

### Commits

- `523abd49` notes/px99-wolf-lsp-on-pax.md: the prediction, before any change
- `95f463dc` user/elf/lspc.c: an LSP client with no libc that starts a server on pipes and prints every frame
- `5e75c631` tools/mklspc: build the LSP client static, no libc
- `dedbdd9c` tests/mpx5-lsp.d: a file with one type error, its fix, and the two sessions
- `cc8b7a44` tests/mpx5-lsp: wolf lsp on PAX, held frame for frame to Linux
- `11b010e0` user/elf/lspc.c: ignore SIGPIPE as an editor does, and reap without closing the input
- `de278e98` tests/mpx5-lsp.d/session.py: write once more to the killed server, which answers EPIPE
- `c1bd9138` tests/mpx5-lsp: LSP2 fails when its witness is missing or exits nonzero, and proves itself first
- `1f770fa1` tests/mpx5-lsp.d/test_rows.py: the witness's mutations, from the Linux side's open-fix transcript
- `e3421f84` .github/workflows/ci.yml: the mpx5-lsp job, and the tier job needs it
- `5e475519` tests/mpx5-lsp.d/hung.good: the Linux side's hung-server transcript, for the witness's mutations
- `0a60558e` tests/mpx5-lsp.d/rows.py: the sessions' own witness, from the protocol, typed.lu and wolf-lsp's recorded capabilities
- `16a2707e` tools/ci-tiers.map: mpx5-lsp in @user and @asuser, and the dev compiler's pin and builders reach it
- `89a3b36f` tests/ci-plan: mpx5-lsp among the as users and the compiler pin's readers, and its own paths
- `ab987672` tests/mpx5-lsp.d: the witness and its self-test write no bytecode into the tree
- `bed86e70` README: wolf lsp on PAX, and mpx5-lsp among the suites
- `347593e7` docs/SOURCES.md: what px99 consulted
- `04a1ef09` CHANGELOG.md: wolf lsp on PAX
- `e0c1dfed` notes/px99: the calls wolf lsp makes on Linux, traced black-box, and their census
- `12f69aff` notes/px99: the first boot's empty LSP2 pass, and LSP2 red with no witness
- `370589ce` notes/px99-wolf-lsp-on-pax.md: inputs, the prediction scored, the evidence, yew's needs and the rulings
- `6e22caf6` notes/px99-wolf-lsp-on-pax.md: the runs at the head, under KVM and TCG
- `1f9e1e73` README: link the monotonic clock's issue, pax#299
- `71efcb9b` notes/px99-wolf-lsp-on-pax.md: R-px99-1 ruled A, R-px99-2 filed as pax#299
- `b5ad66af` notes/px99: the excerpts name their fixes by the final base's shas
- `ab3a1827` notes/px99-wolf-lsp-on-pax.md: the second rebase, its shas, and the gauntlet and plant described

### Records

**The green record at the head `ab3a1827`**, recorded by the org's `gauntlet-record.sh` from a clean checkout:
`green-ab3a1827-20261106T100037Z.log`, sha256 `a94421dba7ad8dc24621a12b25728e4c97d7e495c2091c827e428833d2c01fc7`
(read twice, on the host and on the Mac). Every END line and the summary:

```
END locks exit=0 secs=0
END wolf-pin exit=0 secs=0
END dev-wolf exit=0 secs=0
END preflight exit=0 secs=0
END ci-plan exit=0 secs=73
END mpx5-lsp exit=0 secs=468
END mpx5-lsp-tcg exit=0 secs=16
RECORD-END worst=0 steps=7 end=2026-11-06T10:09:55Z
```

Inside it: `PASS LSP1` 20 of 20 runs (16 under KVM on every leg, 4 under TCG), `PASS LSP2` 22 (those runs and both
self-tests), `PASS LSP3` 5 of 5 legs, no `FAIL`.

**The plant** `px99-plant-witness` at `fa56df3e`, one commit, one file, one hunk on the head (`tests/mpx5-lsp.d/rows.py`
expects two diagnostics where `typed.lu` has one), pushed with no pull request: `plant-fa56df3e-20261106T100955Z.log`,
sha256 `a8a4b2b41f64954ccfb917c28c01d657e752eabed2a845fac5adff02b01b00f8`, red by name at LSP2 while LSP1 holds (4
PASS, 0 FAIL), as P8 predicted. Its PLANT, FAIL and END lines and the summary:

```
PLANT base=ab3a182704d3ce8123c8d6651d5ed615a8f1c7e5 branch=px99-plant-witness
PLANT-ROW LSP2
END locks exit=0 secs=0
END wolf-pin exit=0 secs=1
END dev-wolf exit=0 secs=0
END preflight exit=0 secs=0
FAIL LSP2 (self-test): FAIL test_rows open-fix.good: R2 diagnostics: 1 diagnostics, not 2
FAIL LSP2 (self-test): FAIL test_rows open-fix, two diagnostics: not at R2 ([])
FAIL LSP2 (self-test): test_

author: bonguynvan
body:
## Summary

Adds **OtpInput**, a one-time code such as the code of a two-factor sign-in, shown one character per box.

- One `<input autocomplete="one-time-code">` lies over boxes that only show its characters. The code a phone offers from a text message, a paste of the whole code, typing and Backspace all work. Forms submit it by `name`, and screen readers hear one field instead of six unnamed boxes.
- `type`: `'numeric'` by default, which brings up the number pad. `'alphanumeric'` takes letters and digits and uppercases them. Other characters are dropped, so a pasted `123-456` becomes `123456`.
- `oncomplete(value)` runs when the last box is filled: once per code, and again when a different code is pasted over a full one.
- Validation:
  - A code started but shorter than `length` is invalid, with the new `otpIncomplete` locale message ("Enter all 6 characters").
  - `required` refuses an empty code.
  - `rules` run on a complete code.
  - `error`, `validateOn` and form reset work as on TextField.
- The boxes shrink together, so six fit a 320px screen. The box at the caret shows focus and a drawn caret, which stops blinking under reduced motion.
- Docs page at Forms → OtpInput, with an `llms.txt` entry and an e2e test.

## Size

- OtpInput: 2.87 KB gzipped, under a 3 KB limit (the same as Slider).
- `index (everything)`: limit raised from 72.5 KB to 74 KB (73.5 KB measured).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @sveltier/ui test`: browser tests in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, plus SSR
- [x] `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm size`
- [x] Docs e2e (`playwright test`), including the new form test and the 320px responsive check
- [x] Screenshots: typing (light), a refused code (dark), a short code on a 320px phone

body:
## Sammendrag
Erstatter radvis vurdering med direkte overstyring av refusjonsbeløp og perioder.

- Førstegangsoverstyring aktiveres med «Overstyr». Saksbehandleren kan endre månedsbeløp, dele opp perioder, velge årsak og skrive en felles begrunnelse. Eksisterende tilgangsstyring og lesemodus beholdes.
- Tabell og tidslinje viser de samme periodene. Tidslinjevalg åpner riktig rad, valgt zoom beholdes, og inntektsmeldinger åpnes via dokumenttitler.
- Ugyldige perioder og overlappende krav sperrer innsending. Tomt beløp holdes adskilt fra faktisk `0`.
- Mellomlagrede perioder gjenbrukes bare når originalgrunnlaget er uendret. Gjeldende sluttdato bevares når perioder legges til eller slettes, også med usorterte data.

## Kontrakt og gjenstående arbeid
Endrer den offentlige mottakskontrakten til `FordelingGrunnlagDto`, `RefusjonsandelDto` og `RefusjonsperiodeDto`, med flate `fom`/`tom` og `refusjonPrMnd`. Dokumentlisten krever `tittel`. Brukte felter er tilpasset [V2-kontrakten i ft-beregning](https://github.com/navikt/ft-beregning/tree/078f30ad3fa11df8e6672c77215438d0b75e64ac); ubrukte backendfelt er ikke lagt til.

Utgående payload for `OVERSTYR_REFUSJONSKRAV` må fortsatt bekreftes med backend. Innsending samler perioder per arbeidsgiver og blokkerer overlapp mellom kilder, siden kildeprioriteten ikke er avklart. Unikhet per arbeidsgiver/kilde må også bekreftes.

Synkronisering av lokale redigeringer må følges opp: når backend endrer én andel, kan remount av hele skjemaet forkaste ulagrede endringer i uendrede andeler og avslutte aktiv førstegangsoverstyring.

## Aktiv overstyring
Fiktive Storybook-data med endret månedsbeløp, valgt årsak og begrunnelse.

![Aktiv overstyring med endret refusjonsbeløp, valgt årsak og begrunnelse](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a1f842e-8cc2-4159-9778-ad5cd71df416)

## Validering
Refusjonstester og relevante tester for felleskomponentene er kjørt, sammen med knip, lint, typekontroll og bygg. Sjekkene besto.

Erstatter #4515 etter rebase på `main`. Nullbeløpsrettingen i felles `RhfTextField` er allerede merget i #4521 og inngår ikke i denne diffen.

## CLA

- [x] I have signed the [Stream CLA](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScFKsKkAJI7mhCr7K9rEIOpqIDThrWxuvxnwUq2XkHyG154vQ/viewform) (required).
- [ ] Code changes are tested

## Description of the changes, What, Why and How?

Ticket: https://linear.app/stream/issue/REACT-1376
Docs: [Query Channels – active member count](https://getstream.io/chat/docs/javascript/query-channels/#active-member-count)
v10 counterpart: #2001

> [!NOTE]
> Work in progress: this PR has no new tests, and it adds no types. See "Not done yet".

Query Channels returns `active_member_count` for each channel when the request has `include_active_member_count: true`. In v9 the count reaches `channel.data` as is. Any later code that replaces `channel.data` with a response that doesn't have the count drops it. This PR keeps the count, with the same rule as v10.

### Carrying the count (`src/utils/activeMemberCount.ts`)

`withCarriedActiveMemberCount({ next, previous })` returns `next` unchanged when it has `active_member_count`, or when `previous` has no count. Otherwise it returns a copy of `next` with the previous count:
- moved by the change in `member_count`;
- kept between 0 and `member_count`.

It is used wherever `channel.data` is replaced:
- `client.queryChannels`, when it hydrates each channel;
- `channel.updatePartial`, `enableSlowMode`, `disableSlowMode` and `_update` (used by `update`, `addMembers`, …);
- `channel.watch` and `channel.query`;
- the `channel.updated` event handler.

### Not done yet

- **Types:** `active_member_count` on `ChannelResponse` and `include_active_member_count` on `ChannelOptions` are not added. Callers can still pass the option and read the field, untyped.
- **Tests:** none yet for `withCarriedActiveMemberCount` or the call sites. `yarn types` and the existing `channel` / `client` tests pass.

## Changelog

- Keep `channel.data.active_member_count` across channel updates that don't return it.

author: bolichen97
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** `kirocrew status` tells an operator whether the running gateway serves the package selected to run, and if not, which two versions differ and for how long.

A gateway can keep serving an earlier package after a newer one is selected: an in-place upgrade under a running gateway, a desktop update that has not restarted it, or a Dev Fleet cutover not yet restarted into. The gateway still answers, so `kirocrew status` looks the same in both states. `kirocrew doctor`'s `running:` row already compared the gateway with the code the doctor itself imported, but the reporter of #13086 read the status surface and needed a manual process census to see the mismatch.

Builds on #17746 by @chenmingwei23.

## Why it matters

The two states need different action. When the gateway runs the selected package there is nothing to do; when it does not, the operator has to finish the update or restart the gateway before blaming the selected build for anything they see. Without a signal they cannot tell a finished update from a half-applied one.

## Not a goal

- No rows for the desktop app, a gateway daemon or sidecars: none of them publishes a running version `kirocrew status` can read today.
- No diagnostics-bundle row. Inside the gateway the selected package of a side-by-side install (a versioned venv or desktop directory behind a current-version link) cannot be read from the gateway's own files, and a bundle collected by `kirocrew doctor --bundle` has no running gateway version. Both need their own design, so this PR is `Part of` #13086, not its close.
- No warning threshold: skew is reported as soon as the versions differ, with its age, as the reporter proposed. A threshold is a later change.
- No change to update, ownership, restart or recovery behaviour, or to `service.version`.
- Not the dashboard, the diagnostic snapshot or OpenTelemetry attributes.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

`kirocrew status` ends with a new `Version:` line:

| State | Line |
|---|---|
| gateway runs the selected build | `aligned (0.13.0)` |
| it runs another build | `version_skew for at least 2h 0m: the gateway runs 0.13.0.1, 0.13.0.2 is selected; restart the gateway to run it` |
| the gateway gave no version | ``unknown (the gateway did not report its version; try `kirocrew doctor`)`` |
| the selected version is unreadable | `unknown (could not read the selected package's version; check the install)` |

The identity is the string `kirocrew --version` prints, `__version__` plus any `BUILD_VERSION` stamp, as the reporter proposed: it separates two builds of one release, and it reads the same way in packaged and source installs. Two source checkouts at one version read as aligned; that is the accepted tradeoff.

The running side is `/api/status`'s `version`. When token auth answers that request with 401 or 403, the line still prints: it reads the token-exempt `/api/health` version that `kirocrew doctor` reads, through the proxy-free `loopback_urlopen` (so a configured `http_proxy` cannot divert it, for either command), with no age, because that reply carries no `start_time`. No token is read or sent. The selected side comes from a new `live_target.selected_version()` in `service/live_target.py`: the pinned Dev Fleet checkout when one is set, else the package this `kirocrew` runs. Either way it is read from disk, not taken from the process's own `__version__`, so an in-place upgrade under a running gateway shows. The age counts from the later of the gateway's start and the newest change time of the pointer and the version files, so it is a lower bound and never overstates. One known limit, written into the spec: after a git auto-update the gateway re-imports its package, so until its restart lands it reports the new version and the line reads aligned.

`kirocrew doctor`'s `running:` row now reads the same `selected_version()` instead of the version the doctor imported, so the two commands share one definition of "selected" and cannot disagree; before, a pinned checkout at another version made doctor say `restart needed` while the gateway already ran the pin. An unreadable selected version prints `on disk unknown` and is not an issue.

`cli_server.py` prints the line, `doctor_checks/services.py` reads the shared value, and `docs/system-specs/modules/cli.md` documents both.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: `kirocrew status` gains one line at the end; no existing line, key or exit code changes. `kirocrew doctor`'s `running:` row keeps its wording; with a Dev Fleet checkout pinned it now compares against the pin, so it no longer reports a restart that would change nothing.

Removes nothing: the diff only adds output.

## Tests

`test/test_cli_server_version_alignment.py`:

- `selected_version()` reads a pinned checkout's literal plus its `BUILD_VERSION` stamp; unpinned, it reads the installed package's file rather than the imported `__version__`; it returns `(None, None)` for a checkout with no version literal; and an unpin moves its change time.
- `kirocrew status` prints `aligned (0.13.0)` when the gateway runs the selected build.
- Two builds of one release (`0.13.0.1` running, `0.13.0.2` selected) print `version_skew` naming both, aged from the selection's change (persistent skew).
- A gateway that started after the selection changed is aged from its own start (transient skew).
- An unreadable running or selected version prints `unknown`, never `aligned`.
- `_running_gateway_version` reaches a real loopback gateway with `http_proxy` set and `no_proxy=localhost`, and the proxy sees no request (10/10 repeats).
- Each `unknown` line names the side that could not be read.
- Under token auth (a 403 from `/api/status`), `kirocrew status` still prints the `Version:` line from `/api/health`, skew or aligned, with no age.
- `kirocrew doctor` reads the pinned checkout's version, the same value `status` compares, and reports no restart for a gateway that runs it (red on the parent, which compared the imported `__version__`); an unreadable selected version prints `on disk unknown` with no issue.
- `test/test_cli_doctor_gateway_row.py` and the frozen report in `test/test_cli_doctor_refactor_report.py` pin `selected_version()` instead of `_mc_version`.

Determinism: 20/20 runs at `-n0`; 10/10 at `-n 4 --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=2` with `test/test_live_target.py` and `test/test_live_target_pointer_visibility.py` as co-tenants; a shuffled order (seed 20465) green. The age assertions leave a 60-second margin, and the unpin test stamps the pointer an hour ahead with `os.utime` rather than racing the filesystem clock.

## Manual verification

Ran `cli_server._status` from this branch on an isolated data home with the real `selected_version()` and a stubbed `/api/status` payload. A gateway reporting the installed `0.13.0` printed `Version:     aligned (0.13.0)`; one reporting `0.12.0` printed `Version:     version_skew for at least 1h 18m: the gateway runs 0.12.0, 0.13.0 is selected; restart the gateway to run it` (the age is the checkout's own `__init__.py` change time). No live gateway was started.

## Screenshots / video

N/A — no frontend change; the CLI output is shown above.

## Related Issues

Part of #13086

## Sibling sweep

N/A — not a fix PR.

## Pattern harvest

N/A — not a fix PR.

author: rocketman-w
body:
## Why and outcome

Four faults sat on the native write path.

- A game command discarded its session proof after admission, so a request authenticated before logout could still commit after it, including a post that deletes a reply. `setProfile`, `watchRecap`, `block` and `unblock` also skipped the transaction hook.
- The Messages member-action route read its body after authenticating and then appended with no session check, so a revoked or rotated credential could still enter the mailbox.
- Generic server failures rendered as `{error:{code:"INTERNAL_ERROR"}}` with no `retryable` flag. Installed iOS clients default that to false and delete the unsent shot or reply. A storage `fetch failed` TypeError or a bad JSON response was worse: the shared renderer turned it into HTTP 400. Missing storage became `MEDIA_MISSING`.
- A delayed post with a new entry ID silently replaced a live post on the day: the reply is deleted, the entry withdrawn and the retake spent.

Now the session proof reaches every member write transaction through one opener, `commandTransaction`, and a commit-time auth failure returns the native `UNAUTHENTICATED`. The Messages append checks the exact active session row with a conditional update inside its transaction. Everything unexpected after a game write has read its request is reported as retryable, and storage failures are translated at their source, while malformed input, foreign or missing media, bad images and rule refusals stay final. A post may send `expectEmptySlot: true`, checked under the game lock after same-ID replay. It refuses with `SLOT_TAKEN` and is a slot guard, not a day guard, because a capture's opening day is not its posting day. Old clients omit it and keep today's behaviour.

## Product UX

- Effort: Patch. It restores existing promises: a signed-out session writes nothing, and an unsent post survives a server failure.
- Result: Ready
- Walkthrough: A member whose post hits a server failure, on an installed app, now sees Try again instead of losing the post. Signing out during a write now writes nothing and the app's normal sign-in takes over. Closed days, bad images and other final refusals look the same as before. `SLOT_TAKEN` has no visible effect until a later app build sends the field, and its message is written for that build.

## Evidence

- Direct: Real route bytes for shots and replies ran through the real `GameAPIClient.error(status:body:)` and journal decisions extracted from murph-ios `1bc51e46de9c347cf31f3169a9f77b9e24f05309` and compiled with `swiftc`. At base every dumped failure case retired the journal (24 of 24). At head 40 cases give 26 kept, 14 retired, and all 14 are final refusals: malformed JSON, non-object body, oversize body, `DAY_CLOSED`, `SLOT_TAKEN`, a Worker 400 and a bad JPEG. `game-routes.test.ts` keeps a port of those rules on the same real responses so CI holds the contract.
- Direct: `game-api-postgres.test.ts` uses real routes, real auth and PostgreSQL. A real session revocation between admission and commit returns 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` with no row changed, for post, setProfile, watchRecap, block and unblock. A revocation after commit still returns 200. With storage off the real post route returns 503 retryable and writes nothing, and a foreign key is still a final 422.
- Direct: Removing the four branch hooks fails the four matching revocation tests. Removing the route hook fails all five, so those tests reach the transaction rather than passing at admission.
- Direct: `game-replies-postgres.test.ts` proves a guarded post on an occupied slot leaves the entry, its reply, attempts and events identical, same-ID replay still succeeds, an empty slot and an explicit withdraw then retake succeed, and an invalid value is refused. The existing replacement test proves an omitted field keeps today's behaviour.
- Direct: `imessage-mini-app-account-deletion.db.test.ts` drives the real member-actions route. A revocation or a rotation while the body is read returns 401 and leaves no mailbox row. An untouched credential returns 202 and appends once.
- Coverage: focused Vitest on real PostgreSQL passes: 315 tests across the game, push and Messages files, 7 in the Messages database suite, and 202 across the two session concurrency suites and `game-service-postgres`. `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck:prepared` with `MURPH_TSC_WEB_CHECKERS=1`, `pnpm complexity:diff`, `pnpm docs:drift` and the raw-log guard exit 0. Exact-head CI is pending.
- Direct: `game-api-postgres.test.ts` holds a real native recheck open and proves `FOR KEY SHARE` passes while a member update and `FOR UPDATE` time out. That test failed with `55P03` under the earlier lock. A route race runs opposite rematches through the real create route for three rounds.
- Review: A read-only Codex review before ReviewGPT found that a member row held `FOR UPDATE` ahead of the pair or game lock blocks another transaction's foreign-key check, so opposite rematches and chat bootstrap could deadlock. The session recheck now takes `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`.
- Review: ReviewGPT round 1 at `3baec8414f` found no bugs and one Complexity Collapse, accepted: eight transaction sites each ran the same authority hook, and four missing copies were the cause of this bug. `commandTransaction` now opens all eight. CI on that head failed one test, a group HTTP test whose stubbed auth had no session proof. It now stubs the recheck with authentication.
- Review: ReviewGPT round 2 at `df415d8791` returned PASS with no remaining findings.

## Non-obvious affected surfaces

- `assertHostedAuthSessionCurrentTx` is shared by companion, passkey, credential-change and approval routes. Its member lock moves from `FOR UPDATE` to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` for all of them. It still conflicts with every other member lock, row update and delete, so suspension and account deletion serialize as before. Only foreign-key checks now pass. The session row keeps `FOR UPDATE`.
- `push-route` now uses the same assertion, so its commit-time refusal is also `UNAUTHENTICATED`. `game-push-route.test.ts` proves that and that a commit-time suspension passes through unchanged.
- `requireStore` now throws the retryable media error instead of a plain `Error`. Chat photo import catches `putGameMedia` failures as before, and `game-chat-photo.test.ts` proves that with the new error.
- `GameProtoChange` keeps the form open when `retryable` is true. That is the right result for a server failure.

## Hot reply path impact

- Path status: Not applicable — native game commands and Messages member actions are not conversation input reaching a provider turn.
- Database calls: None
- Network/provider calls: None
- Other awaited latency: None
- Before/after proof: Not applicable

## Murph initial provider input impact

Not applicable — no prompt, tool, schema or provider-visible surface changed.

| Runtime | Base input tokens | Head input tokens | Delta | Percent | Base bytes | Head bytes | Byte delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Individual Murph | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| Group Murph | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |

- Assembled instructions: Unchanged
- Tool/schema/generated guidance: Unchanged
- Other provider-visible input: Unchanged
- Measurement method: Not run — no provider-input surface changed

## Risks

- Each native write transaction now runs the existing session assertion: a member row lock, a session row lock and two short reads. Order is member, then pair, then game, matching account deletion. Each transaction stays bounded and database-only.
- A failed recheck compares the whole session row, so a session refresh landing in the same instant returns 401. The app then asks its own sign-in, which keeps a valid session. Native reads do not refresh the row.
- The board sharing route writes in i

## 概述

Paseo 0.15+ 插件：用现有订阅额度（5h/周窗口）把 Taskboard 的 todo 任务分派给 Claude Code、Codex、Kimi Code CLI、Pi 执行，并回写结果。

## 主要变更

- **插件本体**（`integrations/paseo/`）：Paseo 侧栏 Taskboard 入口，内嵌完整看板 + 自动调度页签；调度器读取各账户额度窗口，按标签与剩余额度选择执行模型；独立 worktree、会话绑定、结果回写、等待任务原会话续跑。
- **创建时指定执行目标**：新建议题弹窗可选 Agent 和模型（实时从 Paseo 读取），保存为 `executionTarget`；明确指定后额度不足或未启用时等待，不改派其他 Agent。
- **存储与 API**：SQLite `execution_target` 列、D1 migration 0014、`shared/task-input.mjs`、`cloud/src/index.mjs`、`server/database.mjs`、`cli/taskctl.mjs` 字段贯通。
- 文档：`integrations/paseo/README.md`、`OVERVIEW.md`。

## 实测验证（隔离演示面板 + 真实 Paseo daemon）

- Claude / Codex / Kimi / Pi 各自领取任务 → 独立 worktree 创建并读回目标文件 → 回写 `in_review`：全部通过。
- 周额度触保留线 → 改派其他 Agent：通过。
- 指定 Codex/gpt-6-luna 且额度不足 → 等待不改派：通过。
- 指定 Kimi/kimi-code/k3（覆盖路由默认模型）→ 实际以 k3 执行并回写：通过。
- 插件 typecheck、面板 typecheck、`node --test`（296 pass / 0 fail）通过。

## 边界

- 第一版同机执行；daemon 重启后需打开一次 Taskboard 页面恢复调度；不自动标记 done、不合并、不发布。
- 不支持任务中途自动换 provider；无付费 API 回退。

## 1. Guideline 2.1(a): Sign in with Apple « error »
Measured in production auth logs: three `id_token` sign-ins from Apple's network that afternoon, all `422 signup_disabled`. The reviewer's own Apple ID matches no member, so the app answered « Ce compte n'est relié à aucun membre ». Offering Google on iOS makes Sign in with Apple mandatory (4.8).

author: zhuyue11
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuyue11"} -->
_Requested by **Xing** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MiQnufdRheSxuSeXodHNeA?thread=cmsg_01MiQnufdRheSxuSeXodHNeASdV44qijTnfxK3RQ1nJBJR)_

## What and why

MOTIR-10466 (#3983) fenced the worker's settle writes on `state = 'running' AND claimed_by = <worker>`. That shuts out a late settle over a row another worker claimed, but it cannot tell two claims by the **same** worker apart. A live worker that misses its heartbeats until its lease lapses has the lease reclaimed by its own next `tick()` (`reclaimExpiredLeases` runs before `claimDueRuns`), which can then claim the very run it is still executing. Two things then went wrong:

- the first pass's settle passed the fence and wrote `succeeded` / a reschedule / `failed` over the row the second pass was executing;
- `inFlight`, `parked`, `withdrawals` and `settling` were keyed on the run id, so the first pass's `finally` dropped the second pass from `inFlight`, and the pool and the drain stopped seeing it.

### The fix

- **A fencing token on the row.** `job_queue.claim_token` (`INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, a catalogue-only migration) is incremented by `claimDueRuns` in its claim statement and returned with the row. Nothing lowers it: not a reclaim, a release, a refunded attempt or a settle.
- **Every settle write matches the claim.** `markSucceeded`, `markFailed`, `rescheduleAt` and `isHeldBy` take a `JobQueueClaim { id, workerId, claimToken }` and match all three columns. A stale pass writes nothing and is reported `released`, the same way a release already is, and the dead-letter hook does not run for it.
- **The bookkeeping is per pass.** `inFlight`, `parked`, `withdrawals` and `settling` are keyed on `passKeyOf(run)` (run id + token). Both passes count against the pool until each settles, the drain waits for and withdraws the live pass, and each pass's `finally` removes only itself.
- `docs/decisions/job-queue-foundation.md` **§18.8** records the decision and the options it turned down.

What this does not change: once a lease lapses, two passes of one run can still execute in one process. At-least-once delivery is the contract, and the step ledger makes the second pass resume rather than repeat. The token guarantees that only the live claim's outcome is recorded.

## Reproduction

The card's probe, run with the same worker, `leaseMs: 50`, no heartbeat, two ticks 150 ms apart and both handlers held, then handler 1 released:

| tree | output |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` @ `9ec1c00` (MOTIR-10466 merged) | `PROBE first=1 second=1 handlers=2 mid=running/same afterFirstSettle=succeeded/null inFlight=0` |
| this branch | `PROBE first=1 second=1 handlers=2 mid=running/same afterFirstSettle=running/same inFlight=1` |

The run varied the conditions the card's premise fixes, and each one is a case in `tests/jobs/worker-own-lease-reclaim.test.ts`:

| condition | on main | on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| stale pass succeeds | row overwritten to `succeeded`, inFlight 0 | row stays `running`/`same`, pass `released`, inFlight 1 |
| stale pass yields (`step.sleep`) | row rescheduled under the live pass | unchanged, `released` |
| stale pass defers | row rescheduled under the live pass | unchanged, `released` |
| stale pass fails with budget left | row rescheduled under the live pass | unchanged, `released` |
| stale pass fails terminally | row `failed`, dead-letter hook ran | unchanged, `released`, hook not run |
| live pass settles first, stale pass later | stale settle fenced by state (already correct), inFlight dropped early | live outcome kept, stale `released`, both counted |
| pool capacity with both passes held | one slot freed early | both slots held until each settles |
| drain after the stale pass settled | drain saw 0 in flight, did not wait or withdraw | drain waits, warns "1 run(s) in flight", withdraws, releases |

## Decisions the run made

1. **Fencing token rather than refusing to claim a held run id.** The card offered both. The claim statement has already written the row `running` before the worker could compare ids, so refusing would mean releasing the row again. Another worker would then claim it, so two passes would still run, and only an in-process set would protect the row. §14.1 also keeps `claimDueRuns` free of any predicate over the worker's own set. A token checked where the write lands is the established fix (Kleppmann, *DDIA* ch. 8).
2. **A monotonic integer as the token.** The alternatives were `gen_random_uuid()`, which only supports equality and takes 16 bytes, and `attempts`, which a reclaim refunds. With `attempts`, a reclaim followed by a re-claim would reuse the old value, which is exactly the collision this PR fixes.
3. **Bookkeeping keyed on `passKeyOf(run)`.** The token already makes each claim unique, so the run reuses it rather than adding a second per-pass id.
4. **A new §18.8 rather than an edit to §18.7.** The file keeps one dated amendment per card, and §18.7 already points forward to MOTIR-10500.

## Changed test suites

The settle-write signature change updates three suites that call the repository directly: `tests/jobs/worker-drain-busy-release.test.ts` (its fence `describe`), `tests/jobs/engine-units.test.ts` (`rescheduleAt carries a lastError…`) and `tests/jobs/engine-debounce.test.ts` (the retry-after-claim case). Their assertions are unchanged.

## Fixes ported from main's open PRs (not part of the card)

`main` @ `9ec1c00` was red for two reasons unrelated to this card, both introduced by #3984. Each fix is copied **unchanged** from its own open PR, so this PR merges cleanly whichever lands first:

- `tests/work-items/activity-anchor-walk.test.ts`, `tests/components/activity-all-anchor-walk.test.tsx`: drop a duplicate `checklist` key (TS1117), from #3989 (commit 42c7460).
- `tests/scripts/dataScriptEntry.test.ts`: truncate before the dry-run cases that assert an empty sweep, from #3993 (commit 52b2fe0).

## Checks run locally

- 10 job suites against real Postgres: `worker-own-lease-reclaim`, `worker-drain-busy-release`, `worker-drain-parked-release`, `worker-gate-wait-occupancy`, `worker-fairness-story-gate`, `engine-worker`, `engine-units`, `engine-debounce`, `engine-schema`, `self-rescheduling-supervision-story-gate`. **193 tests passed.**
- `prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema prisma/schema.prisma` is empty, so the schema has no drift.
- `eslint` on the changed files is clean.
- `tsc -b tsconfig.solution.json` is clean once the ported #3989 fix is in (it reported 0 errors).

### Coverage on the changed files

- `lib/jobs/engine/worker.ts`: **97.58 % statements, 95.34 % branches, 97.82 % functions, 98.94 % lines.** The two uncovered lines (602, 800) are older catch-and-log paths.
- `lib/repositories/jobQueueRepository.ts`: every changed function (`heldBy`, `claimDueRuns`, `isHeldBy`, `markSucceeded`, `markFailed`, `rescheduleAt`) is exercised directly by the new file's repository `describe`. The file's overall number in this subset run is lower because its enqueue and debounce methods are covered by other suites.

You need a local Postgres for the test database. No sign-in or seed data is required.

## Why

The 6 November screen sweep (run-1106) found five WS4 defects:

author: lucatescari
body:
## What broke

Since #38, text in Kimbo panes can turn into scrambled fragments of other letters, typically after the Mac sleeps, the window is backgrounded, or memory runs low.

## Why

addon-webgl shares one glyph atlas between all terminals with the same font (`CharAtlasCache.ts`). Each renderer caches, per cell, where its glyph sits in that atlas, and only looks it up again when the cell's content changes.

#38 calls `term.clearTextureAtlas()` after a WebGL context loss. That wipes the **shared** atlas but drops the cached cell data of the one pane that lost its context. Every other pane keeps drawing from coordinates that now hold different glyphs.

## Fix

`clearGlyphAtlasForAllTerminals()` (theme.ts) clears through every registered terminal. The first call wipes the atlas; the rest find it empty and only reset their own model. #38's intent (re-raster after a context loss) is kept.

## Tests

`webgl-shared-atlas.browser.test.ts` uses the **real** WebglAddon and a real `WEBGL_lose_context` loss (headless Chromium has WebGL2). It compares a pane's cached draw with a from-scratch draw of the same pane:

| | PR #38 code | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| other pane intact after context loss | fails 5/5 (~1900 px differ) | passes 5/5 |
| reloaded pane draws its text | passes | passes |

Control: with the clear call removed entirely, the first test passes, so the clear is the cause.

The #38 test stubbed WebglAddon on the claim that headless Chromium has no GL context. That comment is corrected; the stub could only check that the clear was called, not what the screen showed.

Full jsdom (1213) and browser (79) suites pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

body: Version 0.2.0 makes the reference coordinator safe to share as what it is: cooperative exclusion on one Linux or macOS host, not access control and not the full design (no dependency graph, queue, or consent replies). `expectedUntil` stays an estimate. A live holder is never dropped because that estimate passed. ## Review follow-up 1. **Stale-lock takeover.** Confirmed before the fix: 12 trials with 6 waiters after `SIGKILL` of the lock holder granted more than one write lease in 2 trials. A rename-and-restore takeover still double-granted once under CI load (2 grants in trial 5 of 6). The store lock is now `flock`, held by a short-lived Perl helper (`/usr/bin/perl`). The kernel releases it when that helper exits, including when the caller is killed. Test: `killing the lock holder lets only one waiter acquire`. 2. **macOS identity.** `currentProcessIdentity` has a darwin branch: `IOPlatformUUID`, `kern.boottime`, and `ps -o lstart=` (C locale). Machine id and boot id are cached once per process. PID namespace stays required on Linux and is omitted on macOS. A failed probe is `unknown`, never `dead`. The same `decideLiveness` rules are used when judging holders. CI runs Ubuntu and macOS, Node 20 and 22. Ancestor symlinks such as macOS `/var` -> `/private/var` are allowed; only the state directory itself is refused when it is a symlink. 3. **Writer requests.** A repeated refusal from the same process, for the same resource and operation, returns the existing request id and token. Test: `a repeated write refusal reuses the same request`. 4. **Stale uncertain lock error.** The shared `#lastLockState` field is gone with the file-identity lock. A timeout means a live `flock` holder (`lock-timeout`) and does not stick: after that holder exits, the same store can acquire. Test: `a lock timeout does not stick after the holder exits`. 5. **Manual Mac check.** `sh scripts/mac-smoke.sh` acquires, releases, refuses a second writer during `acquire --hold` and during `run`, and checks that killing the holder lets the next acquire through. It passed on Linux here. Run that script on a Mac. ## Confirmed before the first commit Checked against `481a577` by running the module. - In-process `Promise.all` of two writers: **40/40** trials granted both. Read plus write: **40/40** overlapped. - Two real processes, empty directory: **11/20** both received write leases. With 50 extra lease files: **15/15**. - A corrupt lease and a `formatVersion: 99` lease did not block a write. A dangling symlink failed open. - An invalid pid was deleted and replaced. `withdrawRequest("../resources/...")` deleted the resource file. - A lease with `kind: "sideways"` did not block a writer. Preflight threw `TypeError` when `applied` was not an array. - `acquire` without `--hold` exited, and a later process acquired the same write. A past `expectedUntil` still blocked. An interruptible reader still blocked. `docker` write was granted while `db:project` had a reader. ## Audit findings | Id | Result | | --- | --- | | H01 Check-and-acquire is not atomic | **Fixed.** Grants take an OS file lock around check-and-claim. | | H02 Corrupt or unknown-version records fail open | **Fixed.** A missing file is not treated as corruption. | | H03 Lease not tied to the operation | **Fixed.** `withLease` and `run` hold the lease for the work. `setResourceState` requires a live write lease. | | H04 PID-only cleanup | **Fixed** for one Linux or macOS host. Unknown liveness blocks. | | H05 Path traversal | **Fixed.** Ids must be UUIDs. Symlinks are not followed. | | H06 Schema and version checks | **Fixed.** Damaged resource state yields `unknown`. | | H07 Dependency graph | **Confirmed, deferred.** Flat names are the conflict domain. | | M08 FIFO | **Confirmed, deferred.** | | M09 Consent replies | **Confirmed, deferred.** Interruptible readers still block. Urgent requests require a message. | | M10 Request lifetime | **Partly fixed.** Repeated refusals reuse one request. Requests are still not a queue and stay until withdrawn with their token. | | M11 Expiry | **Refuted as a bug.** A reader dated year 2000 still blocks. No foreign-host clock expiry. | | M12 Real preflight | **Confirmed, deferred.** Demo JSON only. | | M13 Preflight exit status | **Fixed compatibly.** Default exit 0. `--strict` exits 2 unless the outcome is `match`. | | M14 CLI arguments | **Fixed.** | | M15 Permissions and tokens | **Largely fixed.** Windows ACLs are not implemented. | | M16 Profiles and activation | **Confirmed, deferred.** | | M17 Event trail; status mutates | **Partly fixed.** `status` does not reclaim. No event log. | | H18 Tests and CI | **Fixed.** Actions runs Ubuntu and macOS, Node 20 and 22. | | L19 Package metadata | **Partly fixed.** No publish. | | L20 Durability | **Partly fixed.** No power-loss guarantee. | | L21 README matrix | **Fixed.** Scope is one Linux or macOS host. | ## Breaking changes (0.1.0 → 0.2.0) - On-disk `formatVersion` is 2. Older or invalid holder files block and are not deleted. - `status` / `listLeases` omit tokens. `listLeases()` defaults to `{ clean: false }`. - `release` and `withdrawRequest` require the token. - `setResourceState` requires a live write lease. Demo setup is `seedResourceState` / `resource seed`. - The CLI rejects unknown options and missing values. `--wait` errors. `preflight --strict` exits 2 unless the outcome is `match`. - `init` tightens the state directory to mode `0700` and refuses a symlink as the directory itself. - Omitting `isAlive` uses process identity. `false` means positively dead. `"unknown"` fails closed. - The supported host is one Linux or macOS machine. Identity includes `platform` and `startId`. Linux records a PID namespace; macOS leaves it empty. A failed liveness probe is unknown, not dead. - The store lock needs Perl (`/usr/bin/perl` or `perl` on `PATH`) for `flock`.

author: catpawprint
body:
## What and why

Pokémon Friends (`010008C01E742000`, update 1.1.5, SDK 19.3.11, Unity 2022.3.62f1 IL2CPP; no profile in the repository yet, run from the NSP script's provisional one) crashed a few seconds after the player confirmed a name and birthday: `CRASH sig=11` at `main+0x5b64f8`, `lr=main+0x3f1b8cc`, on an IL2CPP thread-pool worker. Il2CppDumper's table names the caller `nn.account.AsyncContext$$Finalize`. `main+0x5b64f0` is `if (p) p->vtable[1](p)`, and the object's vtable word held stray bytes (`0xffffd256` in one run, `0x15600000128` in another).

`nn::account::AsyncContext` is polymorphic. The SDK's constructor (19.3.11: `sdk+0x1ad6c8`) writes the class's vtable and nulls the three words after it, the IPC object pointer at +0x18 among them, and sends nothing. `hle_account.c` took the constructor over with one that wrote no memory, so the vtable word kept what the allocator left there. The game's C# binding deletes the native context from the managed finalizer through the virtual deleting destructor, inlined in `main`, which the `AsyncContextD1Ev` takeover never sees.

The change stops taking the constructor over, so the SDK's own runs. No host interface sets the IPC pointer, so the SDK's destructor, reached through the vtable, finds no session to close. `friends::AsyncContext` and `account::NintendoAccountAuthorizationRequestContext` have no vtable (their SDK constructors write none) and keep their takeovers.

Reference entry: "An account AsyncContext needs its SDK constructor" in `docs/reference/services.md`.

## Checked

- Tests: `python3 dm/tools/tests/test_docs.py` passes. No host test covers the account calls.
- Games run: Pokémon Friends 1.1.5 on the Mac. A scripted run on a fresh save (`DM_KBD`, `DM_KEYS`) crashed at the same pc on every boot before the change; after it the game goes on past the birthday entry, and it was then played by hand past the onboarding.
- `scripts/regress.py check --baseline origin/main --games 0100000000010000`: REGRESSION by the screenshot rule only: the screenshots at 70 s and 95 s differ (dHash 32 / 30 bits; one baseline run, so no noise figure). Shaders 27984/27984 on both, 0 newly failing, 0 new `[RED]`, fps p50 59.9 → 59.9, frame p99 17.25 → 17.99 ms, peak 3243 → 3243 MB. Both screenshots render correctly with Mario in different places: the route drifted (the Mac was in use and both runs report their window covered at times). Whether the route reaches the constructor was not measured. Of the local games, Super Mario Odyssey, LEGO Voyagers and Sumikkogurashi: Create a Wonderful Sumikko Island! import the constructor; only Super Mario Odyssey has a smoke route here, and the other two were not run.
- Devices and OS: M5 Max, macOS 27.2.

## Docs

- [x] The finding is in its `docs/reference/services.md` entry, and `python3 dm/tools/docs_symptoms.py` was run (the symptom index)
- [x] No game files, keys or data extracted from a game in the change or the attachments

author: lingelo
body:
## Summary

Security fix for the guard (hook) that keeps vault domains sealed.

- **Case-insensitive volumes (macOS APFS, NTFS)**: paths such as `WIKI/other/x.md` were not recognized as another domain, so a session could read or write another domain's wiki (and other closed zones) by changing the case of a path. The guard now resolves paths the way the OS opens them: `realpathSync.native` segment by segment, symlinks followed (dangling included), `~` / `$HOME` / `${HOME}` expanded, on-disk case. Bash, Grep and Glob zone rules also match case-insensitively on such volumes (volume probed once).
- **Guard failing open**: when `node` was missing from Claude Code's PATH, the hook exited 127 and Claude Code treated it as non-blocking, so the session ran unguarded. The plugin hook now fails closed (`|| exit 2`). `kioku init --guard-hook` pins the absolute Node path; `kioku doctor` and the launcher check that the hook interpreter resolves.

## Behavior change to note

A crash of the guard now blocks the session instead of letting it run. Paths the guard cannot resolve (EACCES, ELOOP) are refused.

## Known limits

- A volume mounted under the vault with a different case sensitivity is not probed.
- Windows shell behavior for the `|| exit 2` fallback is not verified.
- Existing vaults created with `--guard-hook` are not migrated automatically; `kioku doctor` prints the command.

## Tests

9 new guard tests fail on `main` and pass here. `npm test`: 581 tests, 0 failures (1 pre-existing skip). The case test skips cleanly on case-sensitive volumes.

body:
## What's new

- **Transcript parser** (`livestorm_app/record/transcript.py`, `parse_transcript`). Reads a stored Gladia transcript for the v1 Report:
  - Utterances get stable ids (`U0001`, ordered by start, then end, then payload order).
  - Each word gets its utterance's id. Words come from `result.transcription.words` when Gladia sent a non-empty list there; otherwise from inside each utterance, so an empty list never hides them.
  - Long transcripts saved before the merge fix kept their later chunks' words on the chunk's own clock. For those transcripts only, the parser moves these words onto their utterances in memory. Nothing is written back.
  - Sentences are read in every known shape.
- **Speech events** (`record/clock.speech_events`). Place each utterance on the session clock once the recording is aligned with the session, for the speaking lanes.
- **Transcript health** (`record/transcript_health.py`, `build_transcript_health`):
  - word-level mean confidence and the share of unclear words;
  - speech coverage, counted once when people talk over each other;
  - substantial speakers against the people on stage, and the split risk;
  - the detected language against the event's language;
  - the stretches of unclear words, cited by utterance id.
  
  It gives a state (`ok`, `degraded`, `poor`, `unavailable`) with its reasons, and gates for pace and speaker shares. Speech in which diarization found no speaker is degraded (`no_speakers`), so the state never reads ok without saying so. Speaker shares need at least one substantial speaker. Thresholds are provisional and versioned (`HEALTH_VERSION`).
- **The v1 record route** gains `record.transcriptHealth` (record version 4) and the measure `m.transcript_health` (metrics version 4; after #26's grouped measures in the registry). They carry counts and utterance ids only: never a word, transcript text or speaker label. The transcript is parsed once per record build and read only on a cache miss. The health version is part of the cache key.
- Docs: `product.md` §13 "Transcript health (v1 Report)" and the measure's section, plus `api.md`, `architecture.md`, `data-model.md`, `security.md`, `livestorm_app/CLAUDE.md` and the changelog.

## What users will notice

Nothing yet. The classic app, its transcript view, tables and charts are unchanged, and the classic workspace snapshot is byte-identical. No page uses the new block yet. The v1 Report's transcript health chip and its data-quality lines will consume it.

## How it was tested

- `make check`: ruff, ESLint, 1247 pytest tests with the compose Postgres and Redis, 80 Vitest tests, and the frontend build.
- `tests/test_transcript_health.py` runs on synthetic Gladia payloads in three shapes: one chunk, a long recording merged today, and a long recording merged the way it was before the fix. It covers:
  - stable ids;
  - the words fallback;
  - re-basing, only for old chunked transcripts and only past 1 second;
  - word-to-utterance matching when utterances overlap;
  - each state and reason (speech without any speaker included), the speaker thresholds, the gates, the language fallbacks and the cluster merging.
- Mutation testing on the parser and the health module: every mutant tried is killed.
- `tests/test_record_route.py` and `tests/test_performance.py`: the route's response and what it never carries, the frontend fixture, and the transcript parsed once per build and never kept in the cache. `frontend/tests/fixtures/record-v1.json` was regenerated from `tests/synthetic_session.py`.
- `make bench`: the v1 record of the 2-hour session takes 4 ms (median of 7). The first, uncached request takes about 105 ms, as it parses the transcript once; the workspace routes don't change. Measured after rebasing on #26.
- A read-only check over the local development database's transcripts (counts only): health builds for all of them, the gate change moves none, and none reads `no_speakers`.

## Problem
In a Stage 8 Reading Lab run the level path went Stretch ✓, Stretch ✗, Core ✓, Core ✗, Challenge ✓, Challenge ✓. Each Stage 8 unit has only 2 questions per level in each mission (6 in total), so a 6-question run uses every question. The student stayed on Stretch the whole time, but once the 2 Stretch questions were used, `nextLabItem` fell back to Core, and once Core was used it fell back to Challenge. The last two questions were always Challenge, whatever the student did.

- `nextLabItem` (js/lab.js) now tries easier levels before harder ones when the wanted level is empty, so it never moves a student up because the easier questions ran out. This also applies to the Listening Lab and Grammar Lab.
- The Reading Lab passes the same mission's questions from the student's other open units as spares. They are used at the same level before the level changes, so the level stays right.

author: sharmask7777
body:
## Summary

Fixes the issue where non-avian photographic genres (scenery, landscape, portrait, architecture) failed to match properly in real photo archives like `/Users/shaleensharma/Pictures/leh`, falling back to 0 matches across the new categories.

### Root Causes
1. **Human Portraits Not Detected**: YOLO animal detection previously excluded COCO `person` (class ID 0). Human portrait shots like `IMG_3088` had no detected bounding boxes and fell back to general detection.
2. **Scenery Centroid Dilution in Anchor Similarity**: Global category anchor vectors averaged diverse landscape archetypes (e.g., desert dunes, mountain valleys, ocean waterfalls), dampening cosine similarity against specific scenery images like `IMG_3077` below the threshold.
3. **Proper-Noun Bias in BioCLIP Architecture Textures**: Specific architectural monument labels (e.g. `Taj Mahal`) caused barren rocky mountain valley textures to score as architecture due to visual similarity with stone/monuments.
4. **Rust Category Resolution Substring Matching**: `AssetCategory::from_slug` strictly expected prefix matching (`starts_with("portrait")`), causing slugs like `Cultural_Street_Portrait` to fall back.

### Key Changes
- **Detector Person Routing**: Added COCO `person` (class 0) to detection classes in `scripts/infer.py`, directly targeting `AssetCategory::Portrait` with cropped face/subject inference.
- **Top-2 Candidate Pooling for Non-Animal Genres**: Replaced single anchor gating with top-2 similarity pooling over non-animal categories (`Scenery`, `Architecture`, `Botanical`, `Abstract`), eliminating centroid dilution.
- **Curated Taxonomy Clean-up**: Generalized architectural prompts (`Monumental Architecture`, `Historic Stone Temple`) and added `Arid Mountain Valley` (`scen_valley`) to `models/taxonomy.json` and embeddings.
- **Rust Domain Parsing**: Enhanced `AssetCategory::from_slug` in `src/types.rs` to inspect substring markers (`contains("portrait")`, `contains("monument")`, `contains("temple")`).
- **Comprehensive Testing**: Added Python unit tests for YOLO person routing & landscape fallbacks, and Rust unit tests in `test_catalog.rs`.

### Validation on Real Archive (`/Users/shaleensharma/Pictures/leh`)
All target images verified in `catalog.html`:
- `IMG_3066.jpg` -> **Scenery** (`_Needs_Review/Waterfall`, score 0.51)
- `IMG_3077.jpg` -> **Scenery** (`Scenery/Arid_Mountain_Valley`, score 0.97)
- `IMG_3088.jpg` -> **Portrait** (`_Needs_Review/Cultural_Street_Portrait`, score 0.58)
