author: irony42
body:
Three e2e specs that passed only on retry in two local full runs (CI=1, 2 workers, desktop + mobile).

## Causes and fixes (tests only, no assertion weakened)

- **forgot-password.spec.ts:25**: `toHaveURL(/password/forgot)` passes while the sign-in page is still on screen (the route is a lazy chunk and the router keeps the old page until it loads). The test typed the address into the sign-in page's own field; the forgot form then opened empty, submit gave "invalid address", and the "check your inbox" heading never came. Fix: wait for the forgot page heading before typing. Reproduced deterministically on webkit-mobile (5/5 red before, 5/5 green after).
- **photo-book.spec.ts:14**: the test hard-coded the cover title `Camille & Sacha`, but `seedEvent` numbers the name when the slug is taken (`mariage` is used by several specs on a worker's server): `Camille & Sacha 2`. Reproduced with `best-of.spec.ts` then `photo-book.spec.ts` on one worker. Fix: assert the name the server returned (`event.name`).
- **print-kit.spec.ts:62** (also hit the two sibling QR tests): the QR screenshot is ~3.5 px per module with a fractional origin, anti-aliased differently per link (port and join code vary), and zxing lost the finder patterns about one run in ten (3/20 red). Fix: paint the element at 4x (`zoom`) and read it resampled to a few pixels per module, trying several sizes; the decoded text must still equal `joinUrl`.

## Proof (CI=1, --retries=0)

- print-kit: 120/120 (3 tests x 40, chromium-desktop; it skips on mobile). Before: 3/20 red.
- forgot-password:25 and photo-book:14: 80/80 on chromium-desktop + chromium-mobile (20 each, 6 workers); best-of then photo-book on one worker green on both.
- Mutations: cover title not defaulted to the event name -> photo-book red; QR encodes `joinUrl + "x"` -> print-kit red (decoder returns `...000001x`); forgot-password without the wait -> red on webkit-mobile. Product files restored.
- prettier, eslint, typecheck clean.

The branch includes a merge of `test/e2e-seed-no-429` (#385), which is not on main yet.

author: eco-eric
body:
Before: RhoeFlow only runs in a phone's browser. There is no app to install, the PDF download does nothing special on a phone, and there are no privacy or account-deletion pages, which Google Play requires.

After: an Android app (`apps/android`) that installs from Google Play and opens the live app at app.rhoeflow.pro. In the app, "Save or share PDF" opens the phone's share sheet, sign-in and invite emails open in the app once Play's fingerprints are set, and a "No connection" screen shows when there's no signal. Public `/privacy` and `/delete-account` pages exist for the Play listing, and Settings > Profile links to deletion.

The web app can't be bundled inside the app (Next.js with server routes on Workers, ADR-036), so the shell loads the live site. Web fixes reach phones without a Play upload; only `apps/android` changes need a new build. Decision recorded as ADR-046, following ADR-032.

**How**
- `apps/android`: Capacitor 8.6, package `pro.rhoeflow.app` (permanent once uploaded), `server.url` https://app.rhoeflow.pro, only that host loads inside the app, `www/offline.html` as `errorPath`, App Links intent filter (`autoVerify`) for app.rhoeflow.pro, `allowBackup=false`, file sharing limited to the cache folder, release signing from a git-ignored `keystore.properties`, RhoeFlow icons and splash. Only the INTERNET permission (the compass needs none; camera comes with the photo screen).
- `apps/web` (inert in a browser): `components/pdf-download-link.tsx` + `lib/native.ts` (fetch PDF with the session, write to cache, share sheet); `components/native-shell.tsx` + `lib/app-link.ts` (follow the launch link once, same-origin https only); `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` from Worker var `ANDROID_CERT_FINGERPRINTS` (404 while empty, so merging changes nothing until it's filled); `/privacy`, `/delete-account` (deletion by emailed request to info@rhoeflow.com, within 30 days); privacy link on the sign-in pages.
- CI: new `android` job builds a debug APK on every PR and uploads it as `rhoeflow-android-debug`.
- Docs: ADR-046, license inventory, `apps/android/README.md` (build, upload key, Play Console steps, data-safety answers).

author: ant-champ
body:
openDNA now builds for macOS and Linux as well as Windows, and the front page links to all of them.

## What the release workflow builds

| Platform | File | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `oDNA_beta.exe`, `oDNA_beta-folder.zip` (unchanged) | windows-latest |
| macOS 14+, Apple Silicon | `oDNA_beta-macos-arm64.zip` (openDNA.app) | macos-15 |
| macOS 14+, Intel | `oDNA_beta-macos-x86_64.zip` (openDNA.app) | macos-15-intel |
| Linux x86-64, glibc 2.35+ | `oDNA_beta-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (folder) | ubuntu-22.04 |

Each file gets its `.sha256`; one final job makes the **draft** release from all of them (it never publishes). A manual run can untick *release* to build and test only. The macos-14 and macos-13 runners are not offered to this account, so macOS builds on macos-15.

## Changes

- `packaging/openDNA.spec`: an `openDNA.app` on macOS (icon from the 256 px logo, Info.plist from `app/project.py`, macOS 14 minimum as PySide6 6.12 needs), a folder on Linux (Qt as plain files, so it can be replaced, as on the Windows folder build). Windows builds what it built before.
- `scripts/build_unix.sh` builds, smoke-tests and packs; `scripts/smoke_unix.py` starts the built program headless with a demo file and checks it stays alive, shows the file and finds every bundled data file (the program reports this when `OPENDNA_SMOKE_REPORT` is set). On Linux the X11 helper libraries Qt needs (libxcb-cursor0 and others) are installed on the runner so they are bundled.
- `app/updater.py`: only the Windows one-file exe replaces itself; a Mac or Linux build would otherwise have downloaded the Windows exe. They now say where to download the new version.
- README Downloads: macOS (both) and Linux links beside the Windows ones; SECURITY.md and the user guide say how the unsigned builds are opened and checked.

## Tested

Build-only run [42218960683](https://github.com/OpenDNA-project/openDNA/actions/runs/42218960683): all four builds passed their smoke test (each opened `demo_vector.gb`, 1,834 bp, on Qt 6.12). The full test suite also runs on macOS and Linux, for information only: two macOS failures are tests expecting the Windows shortcut text (`Ctrl+C` where macOS shows `⌘C`), one Linux failure is a timing test, and `test_view_edges.py` fails on fonts as before; a font-dependent check in my new `test_feature_groups.py` is fixed here.

Not tested by hand on a real Mac or Linux desktop yet: the smoke test runs without a display.

author: michael-herwig
body:
## Summary

The extension now supports grim's experimental `settings` kind, which ships in [grimoire-rs/grimoire#318](https://github.com/grimoire-rs/grimoire/pull/318).

- **Display.** A settings package gets a badge, a codicon, a tint, a Settings filter chip and a details label, and its CONTENTS tab shows its JSON. Each client is listed once on a settings row.
- **Held-back explanations.** A settings row that grim holds back says why, in grim's own words. It reads "not applied" while no value is on disk, and "held back" once values are written, since a gate never removes them. It reads "needs attention" when grim applied it but still warns. A note on its own never reads as held back.
- **Prompts.** A project whose settings packages are held back gets the same prompts hooks get: Enable settings when the flag is off, and Allow when the workspace is not consented. The consent prompt names every pinned hook and settings package that `grim hook allow` covers. Each gate is asked once per session for each kind it holds back.
- **Consent re-check.** Allow re-reads `grim status` before it consents, because a toast can stay open while the lock changes. If the workspace now pins a package the prompt did not name, or a named one now comes from another repository, Allow records nothing, says so in the Grimoire output, and asks again. A failed status check, a status that does not report its rows, or a failed Allow step also leaves the consent gate free to ask again.
- **Overwrite confirmation.** For a refused settings value, it names each refused piece (package, client, file, JSON pointer and set element), never the value itself.
- **Hardening.** Untrusted names and grim's messages are flattened before they reach a dialog or a toast, so they cannot reorder text or forge a line, a link or an icon.
- **Docs.** The README describes the kind, its two gates and the prompts. `docs/manual-testing.md` walks through it on grim's manual rig.

## Dependencies

- [grimoire-rs/grimoire#318](https://github.com/grimoire-rs/grimoire/pull/318) is merged as [c5e3824](https://github.com/grimoire-rs/grimoire/commit/c5e3824ec2c934d2384d2a8a6b3720c6133347c9). This change still needs a grim release that carries the settings kind (the latest release is v0.15.1). It resolves [grimoire-rs/grimoire#272](https://github.com/grimoire-rs/grimoire/issues/272).
- **Fixtures.** The recorded grim output was captured from [ef2f133](https://github.com/grimoire-rs/grimoire/commit/ef2f133b851bc3f459e66999c29847943d44a25b), the PR's final head, whose tree `main` carries unchanged as c5e3824. The binary reports 0.15.1, since no release has the kind yet. It ran in a sandbox: a fake `HOME`, a private `GRIM_HOME` and a loopback registry. Re-record it once grim releases the kind.
- **No release.** There is no version or changelog change; the extension's release pairs with grim's.

## Commits

13 commits, one concern each, on `main` c210f4e. Every commit passes lint, type check, build and the plain mocha suites, which rise from 954 to 1049 passing tests.

## Verification

- **Release gate** on the final tree (cf8af8f), run fresh in the `grim-vscode-gate:local` image, clean build, no host `HOME`: `npm ci` then `task --force verify` (that is, `npm run check` and `npm run test:headless`), with the live-grim suite on. It exited 0 with 1605 passing and 2 pending.
- **Live-grim suite:** 5 passing against grim built from `main` c5e3824 (it reports 0.15.1). The 2 pending tests need `GRIM_LIVE_ANNOTATED_REF` and `GRIM_LIVE_NETWORK`. The binary links glibc 2.39 and the image has 2.36, so it ran unmodified under the host's glibc 2.39 loader and libraries, mounted read-only beside it.
- **Per commit:** all 13 trees checked one by one, as listed under Commits.
- **Earlier gates:** 1564, 1578 and 1584 passing with the live suite off (7 pending); 1601 passing and 2 pending in the closing round's own run and again on its head (b3adf83).

## Review

One adversarial review of the whole branch diff ran with five seats: spec, correctness and quality, security, docs and test coverage. Two fix passes followed, each re-reviewed.

- **Round 1** found one Block: rows read "not applied" while their values stayed on disk.
- **Re-review 1** found one Block: the shared failure toast and the stale-lock toast showed grim's raw message.
- **Fixes:** both Blocks and every security finding are fixed in this series, along with the Warns on test coverage, prompt stacking and per-kind session memory.
- **Re-review 2** approved with no Block, and left 3 Warns and 6 Suggests.

### Closing round

- **Cross-model pass (codex).** It ran read-only, from a throwaway worktree with the repository's instruction, hook and credential files removed.
  - **Run 1** (shallow) found a High: the consent toast's list can go stale before the click. It also found a Warn: no test accepts Enable or Allow. Both are fixed, by the consent re-check and by new Enable and Allow tests.
  - **Run 2** (high effort) found the same High, and two items that are declined:
    - "Unpinned declarations are not named." `grim hook allow` consents only to keys in the lock, so a row the lock does not pin is never consented.
    - "A consent No should store every kind it names." Storing only the kinds the gate holds back is deliberate: a kind named only because its flag is off gets its own question once the flag is on.
  - **Delta pass:** no findings. Its sandbox could not read the checkout, so it reviewed the diff embedded in its prompt.
- **Re-review 2's open items** are all fixed:

  | Item | Fix |
  |---|---|
  | Warn: the `src/views/hookPrompt.ts` header describes the old "No" | rewritten to the current behaviour, the Allow re-check included |
  | Warn: the `offerLock` toast fix has no regression test | a test pins the flattened toast and the verbatim output channel |
  | Warn: the re-offer test does not prove the newest snapshot is offered | the test offers an older snapshot, then a newer one while busy, and asserts the toast shows the newer |
  | Suggest: doc text at `src/webview/model.ts` (`unarmedVerdicts`, `settingsHold`), `README.md` (the gate paragraph) and `src/gatePrompt.ts` (`hookPromptFor`) | corrected |
  | Suggest: a test title in `src/test/grim.test.ts` | now says what the test checks |
  | Suggest: the toast stub's restore order | the stub closes, settles pending toasts and waits a tick before the original returns |

- **Re-review of the closing round:** the security, quality and incremental passes approved with no Block or High. The security seat found that a failed status check silenced consent for the rest of the session; it is fixed. Lock entries that have no status row stay invisible to the re-check, which the `newlyCovered` doc comment records as a residual. Declined: re-checking workspace trust at the click, since VS Code reloads the window when trust is revoked.
- **Tests that bite:** three planted defects were each caught by the matching new test: skipping the coverage check, re-offering the first snapshot, and removing the flattening in `offerLock`.

### Final delta review

An independent reviewer, who had not seen the work before, reviewed the closing round's whole delta against grim's code at c5e3824. It approved with no Block, and 15 of 16 planted defects were caught. It reported:

- **Fixed:** a missing test that a hook and a settings package with the same name and repository are different consent keys (the one surviving mutant).
- **Fixed:** a status reply without its rows counted as no rows. It is now treated as a failed check, so consent fails closed.
- **Fixed:** a failed `grim hook allow`, or a failed install after it, silenced the consent gate until the window reloaded. One case: no lock, so Allow records an empty set and install exits 79. Both failures now leave the gate free to ask again, as a failed status check already did.
- **Follow-up:** lock entries that `grim status` does not show stay invisible to the re-check (item 5 below).

The same

author: almostintuitive
body:
## Why

Today's scheduled `web-domain-map` run [failed](https://github.com/aperiodic-io/atlas/actions/runs/42217139981) at the large-change guard: 83 losses against a limit of max(20, 2% of 4032) ≈ 80. Nothing is wrong with the network. The run detected its homepage outage and discounted it, and only about 2 losses are new since yesterday's proposal (#66). The count is inflated in three ways:

1. **Stale override keys.** Between 10-14 and 10-30, Atlas symbology minted new IDs for eight assets that `atlas/data/web/overrides.json` names: `HKD`→`USDHKD`, `KRW`→`USDKRW`, `NZD`→`NZDUSD`, `SEK`→`USDSEK`, `NIFTY`→`NIFTY.NIFTY_50_DERIVATIVES`, `RELIANCE`→`RELIANCE.RELIANCE_INDUSTRIES_LTD_DERIVATIVES`, `SOXX`→`SOXX.EQUITY` and `SPACEX.PRE_MARKET`→`SPCX`. The old keys matched nothing. The currencies, NIFTY, Reliance and SpaceX quietly left the map, and #66 would remove them on merge. The only signal was the "override X is not an asset of the map's universe" line under Warnings.
2. **Renames counted as losses.** When a Robinhood or xStock token takes a bare ticker ID, the underlying equity becomes `<T>.EQUITY`: `LULU`, `BA`, `CLSK`, `INTU`, `VRTX`, `MXL`. `report.losses` counted the old key as lost even though the same domain is still mapped under the new key.
3. **The guard compares against `main`.** #66 has been open since 11-05 with about 77 losses, so the daily runs had little headroom left.

## What changes

- **Overrides**: the 8 entries are re-keyed to the new IDs. The `USDHKD`, `USDKRW` and `USDSEK` aliases are removed, since Atlas now resolves those rows itself and the aliases pointed at the old keys. The SPCX reason is updated.
- **`report.losses`**: an old entry whose key is gone is *carried over*, not lost, when an **added** entry has the same domain and Wikipedia article and shares at least one `atlas_symbols` contract. A lost domain is still a loss.
- **New test**: every committed override must name an asset of the universe. It runs in `tests.yaml` but not in the bot's `validate-map` step, so a stale key fails the next human PR without blocking the daily bot run.
- **CLI**: the `%` in `--accept-large-change`'s help is escaped. On Python 3.14, argparse rejects a bare `%`, so `python -m integrations.web` would not start locally (CI pins 3.12).

## Effect

Offline rebuild using the bot branch's caches (`--offline`), main vs. this branch:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Guard losses | 79 | 67 |
| "override … not in the universe" warnings | 8 | 0 |
| USDHKD, USDKRW, NZDUSD, USDSEK, NIFTY, RELIANCE, SPCX mapped | no | yes (via override) |

The remaining ~67 losses are real: domains unreachable two days in a row, parked or hijacked sites, and tokenised-stock symbols. They are the same set #66 already proposes.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests fail before the fix and pass after (`test_a_renamed_key_is_not_a_loss`, `test_every_committed_override_names_an_asset_of_the_universe`, `test_the_cli_help_renders` on 3.14)
- [x] `tests/test_web*.py` pass on Python 3.12 and 3.14 (163)
- [x] `ruff==0.14.1 check .` and `format --check` clean
- [ ] Full CI here will fail on `test_delisted_usd_perpetuals_are_identified_or_known` until the OMNI symbology PR merges. That test already fails on `main` and isn't related to this change.

## After merging

Re-run `web-domain-map` with `workflow_dispatch` (mode `resolve`) to refresh #66 with the restored entries, then review #66.

body:
**In short:** Convert results now list each lost element with its path, reason and severity, where the server would otherwise refuse them on the new SDK, and validate accepts the national formats.

`@beliq/sdk` 0.6.0 hands on the entries of `x-lost-elements` as the API sends them: objects with `path`, `value`, `reason`, `severity` and `acceptableLoss` ([LostElement schema](https://docs.beliq.eu/api-reference/convert/#lostelement-schema)), or one `{ truncated: true, reason }` entry when the list would pass the API's 6 KB header cap, with `lostElementsCount` still the exact count. Up to 0.5.2 the SDK turned every entry into the text `[object Object]`.

## What changes

- The convert tool's output schema took `lostElements` as a list of strings, so on 0.6.0 the server would refuse every convert result with a loss. It now takes the documented entries and the truncation entry. The tool description and README say what the truncation entry means.
- The validate tool's `format` enum follows the SDK's `LIVE_VALIDATE_FORMATS`, which gains `fatturapa`, `facturae`, `eslog` and `poland_ksef_fa3`. The skill and README no longer say it takes only `auto`, `cii` or `ubl`.
- The lockfile pins the registry copy of 0.6.0; no other entry moves.

## Checked

Run locally against the registry copy of 0.6.0: `npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`, `scrub:check`.

author: ivohofland
body:
## Why

`import 'server-only'` fails the browser bundle, but only when a route is **built**: by `next build` in CI's `docker-build`, or by loading the page in `next dev`. Typecheck, lint and the unit and component suites all run in Node, where that import is harmless. So a client component that reaches server-only code passes all of them.

#969 hit this. `now-timeline.tsx → now-line.ts → finish-window.ts → degradation.ts` showed up as a broken `/schedule` in the dev server, and only the e2e screenshot run caught it locally. Production was never at risk, because CI's build would have stopped it. This test moves the catch from a ~3-minute CI build to a 2-second unit run, and prints the whole chain where Next's error names only the two ends.

## What

- `src/lib/client-server-boundary.test.ts`: for every `'use client'` module under `src/`, walks its value imports (type-only imports are skipped, because they are erased) and fails on each chain that reaches a module with `import 'server-only'`. A second case guards against passing vacuously if the directive match ever breaks.
- `src/lib/import-walk.ts`: the BFS import walker, moved out of `loading-coverage.test.ts` so both boundary tests share one copy (`chainsTo(start, isTarget)`). `loading-coverage.test.ts` now calls it. The behaviour is unchanged and its 9 tests stay green.

## Proof it can fail

I reintroduced #969's bug (`now-line.ts` importing `formatClockInZone` from `finish-window`) and watched the test fail:

```
+   "components/schedule/now-timeline.tsx → lib/now-line.ts → lib/finish-window.ts → lib/log.ts",
+   "components/schedule/now-timeline.tsx → lib/now-line.ts → lib/finish-window.ts → lib/degradation.ts",
```

Then I reverted it. Unit and component suites are green (9,257), as are typecheck and lint.

## Not covered

Only this repo's own specifiers (`@/…`, `./…`) are followed. A server-only npm package imported straight from a client module is still caught only by the build.

author: guidone
body: ## Description GraphQL Explorer lets you run GraphQL APIs from Raycast, without opening a browser playground. Save the queries and mutations you use often, attach each one to an environment such as local, staging or production, and run it from Raycast's search bar. - **Environments**: an environment is an endpoint URL plus the headers sent with every request, such as an `Authorization` token. You can run a saved query against a different environment with one shortcut. - **Saved queries**: queries and mutations, each with its own icon and color. Search them by name and filter them by environment. - **Variables**: when a query declares variables, the extension asks for them in a form. If the server allows introspection, the form lists enum values and pre-fills input objects with their required fields. - **Responses**: pretty-printed JSON with the HTTP status, timing, size and number of GraphQL errors. You can also copy the request as a curl command. The extension runs on macOS and Windows. Environments, queries and variables are stored in Raycast's local storage. The only network requests go to the endpoints you configure. ## Screencast ## Checklist - [x] I read the [extension guidelines](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store) - [x] I read the [documentation about publishing](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/publish-an-extension) - [x] I ran `npm run build` and [tested this distribution build in Raycast](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store#metadata-and-configuration) - [x] I checked that files in the `assets` folder are used by the extension itself - [x] I checked that assets used by the `README` are placed outside of the `metadata` folder

author: jobucaldas
body:
## Problem
- A failed or cancelled download kept its files. The downloader sizes every file to full length before fetching chunks, so a cancelled 3.1 GB download kept ~3 GB allocated (free space 4094 → 916 MB), and every later download failed "Not enough free space".
- Slime Rancher (433340) downloaded both Windows depots, 433341 (32-bit) and 433342 (64-bit). They share file paths, so it needed 2337 MB and the two builds overwrote each other.

## Change
- `installs.h`: a fresh install writes `dl_<appid>.partial` before creating files. `discard_partial` removes the folder on failure or cancel. `sweep_partials` runs at launcher start, holding the download/delete lock, and cleans up after a crash or power loss. The folder is kept when a finished install of the same app owns it (a failed update), when another installed app shares it, or when it isn't a downloader-shaped folder (`steam\` etc., same rule as Delete).
- `depot_select.h` (new, portable): Windows/neutral depots only, no DLC, no non-English language depots, no low-violence depots, and skip `osarch=32` when a 64-bit Windows depot exists.
- `steamdl.h`: uses both of the above. The free-space check now counts bytes already on disk for the install, so a resumed download isn't refused because of its own files. A `.done` marker that can't be written is now a failure instead of being ignored.
- Version 0.5.223.0.

## Evidence (console, 0.5.223.0)
- Startup sweep removed the leftover `puyopuyotetris2` and `slime_rancher` folders: free space 916 → 5198 MB.
- Slime Rancher: `depot 433341 skipped (32-bit build (64-bit build present))`, `433342 selected`, 1174 MB, 596 files SHA1-verified in 34 s; detail page shows "Installed - 1.15 GB".
- Cancel (B) mid-download of Puyo Puyo Tetris 2: `folder removed, 1242 files removed, 0 left`; page shows "Cancelled: cancelled (partial files removed)".
- Force-kill mid-download of Terraria, relaunch: `unfinished download of appid 105600 (LocalState\terraria) from an earlier run: folder removed`.

## Tests
- `tests/depot_select_test.cpp` (new, native, in CI): DEPOT-SELECT PASS
- `tests/game_library_test.cpp`: `.partial` marker parsing
- `tests/game-delete.sh` (Wine, real filesystem): fresh/failed-update/shared/launcher-owned cases plus the startup sweep. GAME-DELETE PASS

Note: Slime Rancher now downloads, but its Unity player renders through OpenGL, which Play doesn't support yet, so it isn't playable in this PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches install/delete paths and depot choice; wrong guards could remove or keep the wrong folders, but logic reuses existing deletable/shared checks and adds regression tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Summary:** Adds a portable `depot_select` layer so the downloader follows Steam-like rules for 64-bit English Windows: Windows or OS-neutral depots only, skips DLC, non-English, low-violence, and no-public-manifest depots, and **drops 32-bit Windows depots when a 64-bit one exists** so overlapping installs (e.g. Slime Rancher) are not fetched twice.
> 
> **Partial installs and disk:** Fresh installs **write `dl_<appid>.partial` before files exist**. On failure or cancel, **`discard_partial`** removes the install folder when safe (same deletable/shared rules as game delete); finished installs, shared folders, and launcher paths are preserved. **`sweep_partials`** runs at download-thread startup (under the download lock) to clean crash/power-loss leftovers. **`download_app`** now records partial state, **computes required free space from bytes not already on disk** (better resume), **writes `dl_<appid>.done` via a temp file + replace** (no half-written marker), and **cleans partial data on success**. `marker_appid` gains an optional suffix so `.partial` markers are recognized.
> 
> **Tests and release:** CI runs **`depot_select_test.cpp`**; **`game-delete`** and **`game_library`** tests cover partial markers and sweep behavior. **Appx manifest** bumps to **0.5.224.0**.
>

body:
## Problem

CI fails on every branch at "Install Playwright Chromium". Example: https://github.com/werb-dev/werb/actions/runs/42220515324

```
BEWARE: your OS is not officially supported by Playwright; installing dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 as a fallback.
Cannot install dependencies for ubuntu26.04-x64 with Playwright 1.60.0!
Error: ERROR: Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64
```

`ubuntu-latest` now points to Ubuntu 26.04. Playwright 1.60.0 has no Chromium build or dependency list for it, so the job stops before any test runs.

## Fix

Bump `@playwright/test` to `^1.64.1`. The lockfile resolves to 1.64.1, released 2026-10-14. Playwright supports `ubuntu26.04-x64` from 1.63.

1.65.0 came out yesterday, so this PR stays on 1.64.1. The other option was pinning the runner to `ubuntu-24.04`, but that only postpones the problem.

## Tests

The full e2e suite passes locally on 1.64.1 (36 passed). This PR's CI is the real check on the 26.04 runner.

author: kammeph
body:
## Bug

The `ColorInput` dropdown renders the `ColorPicker` saturation, hue and alpha sliders with `role="slider"`, but `ColorInput` does not accept `saturationLabel`, `hueLabel` and `alphaLabel`. The sliders therefore have no accessible name, and axe reports `aria-input-field-name` for them. The ColorPicker docs already recommend these props for screen readers, but there is no way to set them through `ColorInput`.

## Fix

Move `saturationLabel`, `hueLabel` and `alphaLabel` from `ColorPickerProps` to `__ColorPickerProps`, the props `ColorInput` shares with `ColorPicker`, and pass them from `ColorInput` to `ColorPicker`. This follows the approach `fullWidth` took in #9061. The `ColorPicker` API does not change.

The ColorInput docs page gets a short note with an example after the accessibility section, in the same form as the clear button note on the Select page.

## Testing

- `ColorInput.test.tsx`: `passes slider labels to ColorPicker` opens the dropdown with `format="rgba"` and looks up all three sliders by name. It fails on master (no slider named `test-saturation`) and passes with the fix.
- `ColorInput` and `ColorPicker` suites: 116 passed.
- `npm test` passes. The only failure in the full run was `Tour.test.tsx` (`animates the tooltip position only while moving to another step target`), which passes when run on its own and does not touch these components.

author: beliq-eu
body:
**In short:** Convert Invoice now returns each lost element as a line item with its path, reason and severity instead of the text [object Object], and Validate offers the national formats.

`@beliq/sdk` 0.6.0 hands on the entries of `x-lost-elements` as the API sends them: objects with `path`, `value`, `reason`, `severity` and `acceptableLoss` ([LostElement schema](https://docs.beliq.eu/api-reference/convert/#lostelement-schema)), or one `{ truncated: true, reason }` entry when the list would pass the API's 6 KB header cap, with `lostElementsCount` still the exact count. Up to 0.5.2 the SDK turned every entry into the text `[object Object]`.

## What changes

- Convert Invoice returns the entries as Zapier line items. The sample and tests use the documented entries. The README and the `Unreleased` CHANGELOG section say what the truncation entry means, and that the list holds only the losses the engine recorded.
- The Validate Format dropdown gains the four national formats 0.6.0 offers, with a label for `poland_ksef_fa3`; a test fails when an offered format has no label. Its help text no longer says auto-detect picks only CII or UBL.
- The README no longer says the dropdowns carry every format the API accepts: they leave out what the SDK leaves out, and the SDK states why.

author: faresharrazi
body:
## What's new

- **Refusals are their own error.** When the model declines (Anthropic `stop_reason: "refusal"`; OpenAI `message.refusal` or `content_filter`), `llm_client` raises `LLMRefused` at once. It is never retried, and any partial text is dropped. The content-repurposing loop stops after its one paid call. The usage row is kept, with the outcome `refused` and Anthropic's refusal category when it gives one; the message users see never names the category.
- **Structured outputs for the v1 jobs.** `llm_client.generate_json(kind, schema, …)` and `generate_text(kind, …)` take the model and budget from the job registry and send no `temperature`. Like `call_llm`, they check the org's daily budget before each send, the truncation retry included. They check the stop in this order: refusal, then the token limit, then the schema. A JSON step sends a strict schema (Anthropic `output_config.format`, OpenAI strict `response_format`) and validates the answer against the full Pydantic model. An answer that fails raises `LLMInvalidOutput` and is recorded as `invalid_output`. The error never names the answer's content.
- **Schemas** are Pydantic models registered in `ai/schemas.py`. They are turned at import into a subset of JSON Schema that both providers accept: closed objects, every field required, nested models written out in place, no recursion. Bounds outside the subset are checked by Pydantic on the answer.
- **Truncation per job** (`JobSpec.truncation_retry`). The classic outputs keep their one retry at double the budget. The v1 jobs fail at once when cut off.
- Nothing calls the v1 entry points yet. Classic request bodies don't change.

## What users will notice

When the model declines a session, a classic output now fails with "The model declined this session. Nothing was saved." It used to say the model returned an empty output. The message is the same whatever the model's reason. Nothing is saved, and content repurposing no longer makes three paid attempts on a refusal.

## How it was tested

- New `tests/test_llm_responses.py`, on synthetic provider responses only:
  - the strict schemas and their lint, including a schema that fails the lint never being registered;
  - what each provider is sent, and the answer read from text blocks only (thinking and fallback blocks ignored);
  - refusals on both providers, for classic and v1 calls: the same neutral message whatever the category, the category kept on the exception and in the usage row, and the message surviving arq's stored result;
  - truncation per job, including the retry cap at the model's own limit and an unknown job kind;
  - answers that fail their schema, and unexpected stops;
  - the daily budget on `generate_text` and `generate_json`, the truncation retry included.
- `tests/test_data_integrity.py` on local Postgres: a refusal saves nothing but its usage row, and an invalid structured answer is recorded and not returned.
- Each new test was checked against a deliberate break of the code it covers, and fails on it.
- `make check` passes: ruff, ESLint, pytest (1310), Vitest (80) and the frontend build.

author: blackviperxiii-ui
body:
## Summary

Before: while a reply was being spoken, tapping the mic left voice mode, and talking did nothing until the reply finished. The mic wasn't listening during playback, so a long answer had to be sat through.

After: tap the mic while a reply plays and it stops and listens (the tooltip says "Stop and listen"). If the reply is still being written, a tap stops the talking and says no more of it, and listening resumes when it ends. You can also just start talking over a reply: the mic listens during playback and only sustained speech above the reply's own sound counts, so its echo, a cough or an "mm-hm" doesn't stop it.

How: the open mic gains a `playing` flag the app sets while a written reply plays. It drives the detector's existing echo-aware barge-in (`set_playing`, 400 ms of speech within 600 ms well above the learned echo) and resets the quiet clock so a long reply isn't a quiet minute or a check-in. While playing, blocks are held back from the speech stream (about 1.1 s kept) and only flushed when a barge-in starts, so the reply's own sound isn't sent to be transcribed. `poll_voice_hold` starts a listen over a playing reply; the listen's `Heard::Started` now arrives as `JobOut::VoiceHeard`, which stops the reply. `SpokenReply::hush` stops playback and drops the rest of a reply still streaming in, while still signalling done so the loop carries on.

## Proof of work

- `cargo test --locked -q -p grokhub-app`: 1905 passed (new: `voice_mic` talking over a reply / long reply not a quiet minute; `stream_tests` tap while playing, talking over, tap while still being written).
- `cargo clippy --locked -q -p grokhub-core -p grokhub-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --locked -q -p grokhub-app --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `bash scripts/ci-guards.sh` and `python3 scripts/pii-guard/pii_guard.py`: clean.

## Skipped / not verified

- No real speakers and mic: barge-in over a real echo depends on how loud the reply is at the mic. The test echo is about -34 dBFS, matching the detector's own tests; a much louder echo needs louder speech to cut in, and the tap always works.
- Talking over a reply works once the reply is fully written (usually well before it finishes playing); while it is still being written, the tap is the way in.
- Windows path type-checked only.

author: weicheng59
body:
## Summary
- **Strip retry-delay fields (`headers.retry-after`, `headers.retry-after-ms`, `retry_after`, `retry_after_ms`, `resets_at`, `resets_in_seconds`) in `sanitizeOpenAICapacityShedErrorCodeForClient`:** When OpenAI upstream emits a capacity-shed event (`server_is_overloaded` / `slow_down` / `"Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later."`), it often attaches `"headers":{"retry-after":"326","retry-after-ms":"326000"}`. Even after rewriting `error.code` to `"server_error"` (#6409 / #6417), clients such as Codex CLI parse `error.headers["retry-after"]` / `error.headers["retry-after-ms"]` and replace their millisecond-level exponential reconnect backoff with a multi-minute (e.g., 326s) sleep. Stripping these retry-delay fields on capacity-shed errors (including when an upstream relay hop already rewrote `code` to `"server_error"`) restores fast client backoff while leaving `rate_limit_exceeded` retry delays untouched.
- **Cover `ws_mode=passthrough` in `openAIWSClientFrameConn.WriteFrame`:** Apply `sanitizeOpenAICapacityShedErrorCodeForClient` when writing text frames to the downstream WebSocket client in `ws_mode=passthrough`, matching `ctx_pool` (`openai_ws_forwarder_ingress.go`), `http_bridge` (`openai_ws_http_bridge.go`), and HTTP SSE (`openai_gateway_response_handling.go`).
- **Avoid leaking `Retry-After` HTTP headers on exhausted capacity-shed failover & allow `RequestScopedTransient` in `waitForWSSameAccountRetry`:** Skip `copyFailoverRetryAfter` in `handleFailoverExhausted` when `failoverErr.IsOpenAICapacityShed()`, and allow `failoverErr.RequestScopedTransient` in `waitForWSSameAccountRetry`.

## Test Plan
- `go test -tags unit ./internal/service -run "TestSanitizeOpenAICapacityShedErrorCodeForClient|TestPassthroughLifecycle_CapacityShedSanitizesErrorCodeAndStripsRetryAfter"`
- `go test -tags unit ./internal/handler -run "TestOpenAIGatewayHandler.*CapacityShed|TestOpenAIGatewayHandler.*Failover|TestOpenAIGatewayHandler.*WebSocket"`

author: febose-ui
body:
## What
Makes account import read the archive's file headers in large chunks instead of a few bytes at a time, so a big export starts importing in about a second instead of about twenty.

## Why
The nested-zip import reader checks every entry's local header before importing. It did that with two separate file reads per entry, so an archive at the 100,000-entry limit spent about twenty seconds in system calls before importing anything. The reader's own test of that limit timed out on a busy machine.

## Changes
- Local headers and data descriptors are read through one 1 MiB window that moves forward through the file. Headers are already checked in file order, so the window is refilled only when a read falls outside it.
- Bounds are unchanged: a read past the end of the file is still a format error.

## Tested
The zip reader and importer unit tests pass, and the 100,000-entry case went from about 20 seconds to about 1 second. The real-Postgres account-import suite passes against a local database. API typecheck and Biome are clean.

body:
## Summary

Shorten `ui-capture` by extracting native regression work into four independent Windows runner jobs: sidebar/appearance, Devices, history/discovery, and Tools/build identity. All jobs download the same published payload; desktop automation never competes on one runner.

Closes #197

Task #197 is a verified native child of Epic #164, as selected by @iricigor. Changes are limited to CI orchestration, its dispatch/gate tests, and directly related documentation. No application storage logic or native history/discovery fixtures changed.

## Coverage and failure behavior

- Preserve all existing suites/assertions and the existing DeviceDetails condition for history/discovery; no reduced-frequency or change-aware suite skipping added.
- Preserve Windows PowerShell for sidebar and PowerShell Core for other suites.
- Keep the existing required `ui-ux-review` check and gate screenshot publication on capture, the full regression matrix, installer, tests, and build. Failed/cancelled/missing/unexpectedly skipped required stages cannot pass.
- Retain per-suite transcripts, captures/plans and available diagnostics in unique artifacts, with matrix fail-fast disabled.
- Bound regression jobs/steps to 20/15 minutes and capture job/smoke step to 10/7 minutes. Report elapsed times in logs and summaries.

## Validation and observed timings

Final revision: `1892578ce9d8203e3cd7cdf7e99a6fdfe60ba202`.

- Local `PrValidation.Tests.ps1`, `UiReviewScenarios.Tests.ps1`, and `git diff --check` passed. Dispatch tests use synthetic script stubs, including Windows PowerShell with a multi-scenario plan; no user-desktop automation.
- [Final PR CI](https://github.com/iricigor/fingvibe/actions/runs/42222296690): every required check passed, including screenshot publication and security. `ui-capture`: **3m 04s**; full CI job span: approximately **6m 46s**.
- [Final manual DeviceDetails run](https://github.com/iricigor/fingvibe/actions/runs/42222287567): all four real native suites, two required captures, installer, Core tests, and aggregate validation passed. `ui-capture`: **1m 47s**, with smoke/capture work **80.4s**. History/discovery job: **6m 10s**; sidebar: **3m 39s**; Devices: **3m 15s**; Tools: **3m 23s**. Full CI job span: approximately **8m 35s**. PR comment/publication jobs intentionally skip manual events.
- All four suite diagnostic artifacts and the capture artifact were uploaded and verified.

The previously investigated run spent approximately 15 minutes in `ui-capture`. These are observed runs with different revisions/scenario plans, not a controlled benchmark or guaranteed speed threshold. Parallel runners can increase billed minutes and queue/startup overhead.

## Implementation corrections

GitHub rejected a dynamic shell expression; fixed shell steps now preserve each suite's original host. Real manual CI exposed Windows PowerShell's multi-scenario JSON-array behavior; only the PowerShell Core history suite now reads the capture plan, and a synthetic Windows PowerShell regression covers sidebar dispatch. Final-revision CI passed after both corrections.

## Zusammenfassung

- **Olis Adventskalender:** Vom 1. bis 24. Dezember kommt jeden Tag ein Brief von Oli mit einem kleinen Geschenk (Kekse, Glitzerstein, Samen …), Gutscheinen oder Liebeszetteln. Dabei sind auch Rezeptkarten für **Bratapfel** und **Zimtsterne** (am Herd oder bei Jens). Im 24. Türchen steckt eine **Schneekugel mit Lina, Oli & Winston**. Falls Lina an Heiligabend nicht spielt, kommt sie noch bis Silvester.
- **Schneemann bauen:** Von Dezember bis Februar liegen jeden Tag Schneebälle auf der Wiese. Aus 3 Schneebällen und 2 Ästen baut Lina an der Werkbank einen Schneemann für den Garten (mit Karottennase, Schal und Zylinder). Außerhalb des Winters ist er getaut: Übrig bleiben Mütze, Nase, Äste und eine Pfütze.
- **Wintermöbel** (nur Dezember bis Februar im Katalog, Stil „Winterzauber“): Weihnachtsbaum, Adventskranz, Kaminofen, Lebkuchenhaus, Nussknacker, Schneeflocken-Teppich, Lichtervorhang (Wand), Weihnachtsstrumpf (Wand), Holzschlitten (Garten). Dazu gibt es eine Schneeflocken-Tapete.
- **Punschstand** neben dem Weihnachtsbaum am Dorfplatz (1.–26. Dezember, 15–22 Uhr): Kinderpunsch, heißer Kakao oder Glühwein für ein paar Sternchen.
- **Kleine Winterfreuden:**
  - Fußspuren im Schnee, auch Winstons Pfoten

- **Fehler behoben:** Sparschwein, Weihnachtsstern und Kuscheldecke (Weihnachtsgeschenke) hatten kein 3D-Modell und erschienen als rosa Würfel.

Kein neues Spielstand-Format: Türchen laufen über die Post, Schneebälle über die täglichen Funde.

Ich habe `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (211 Tests, darunter neue in `game/winter.test.ts`) und `npm run build` laufen lassen, alle grün. Im Headless-Browser habe ich Dorfplatz, Punschstand, Schneemann, Atemwölkchen und die Möbel-Vorschaubilder angeschaut.

author: lhotari
body:
### Motivation

A subscription update received from a remote cluster moves the local mark-delete position through a cumulative ack, without any ack from the local consumers. On a Shared or Key_Shared subscription, those consumers can still hold entries at or before the new position.

Before #25592, the pending acks sweep in `readMoreEntries` released these entries. #25592 moved the cleanup to `Dispatcher#markDeletePositionMoveForward`, and only expiry, skip and clear-backlog call that hook, with #25624 later adding backlog quota eviction. The replicated subscription path doesn't call it, so these entries stay in `pendingAcks` until the consumer acks them, disconnects or gets a redelivery. Until then, the consumer's unacked count stays inflated and, on Key_Shared, its draining hashes can stay held.

### Modifications

- Call `markDeletePositionMoveForward()` after a replicated subscription ack succeeds in `PersistentSubscription#acknowledgeReplicatedSubscriptionMessage`.
- Attach the call outside the subscription monitor. The ack can complete synchronously, and the hook takes the dispatcher's lock.
- Don't call it for a rejected update or a failed ack. `ReplicatedSubscriptionsController` retries a failed update, so the cleanup runs when the retry succeeds.
- Update the `Dispatcher#markDeletePositionMoveForward` javadoc to include this path.

### Verifying this change

- [ ] Make sure that the change passes the CI checks.

This change added tests and can be verified as follows:

- Added `ReplicatedSubscriptionTest#testSubscriptionUpdateReleasesLocalPendingAcks`, which runs on two clusters with Shared and Key_Shared subscriptions. r1 acks every message and r2 never acks. Without the fix, r2's mark-delete position moves past entries that stay in its consumer's `pendingAcks`, and the test fails.
- Added `PersistentSubscriptionTest` cases for the hook running outside the subscription monitor when the ack completes synchronously, and for it not running when the mark-delete fails or the update is rejected. Moving the hook inside the monitor makes the monitor and rejected-update cases fail.

- [ ] Dependencies (add or upgrade a dependency)
- [ ] The public API
- [ ] The schema
- [ ] The default values of configurations

author: enzotrevisandev
body:
## Problem

On a fresh v0.3.0 install, 226 of 345 batches failed in 30 min:

```
batch submission failed ... retry exhausted after 1 attempts: The operation was cancelled - Timeout expired
```

Two problems on the agent side:

1. **Timeouts were never retried.** tonic reports its own client timeout as `Code::Cancelled` with the message "Timeout expired". `is_retryable_code` only accepted `Unavailable` and `DeadlineExceeded`, so `retry_max: 3` never applied.
2. **The defaults had no margin.** A 500-envelope batch with a 5s deadline doesn't fit now that the ingestor waits for a full-ISR ack per batch (dodo_ingestor#14). The root-cause fix is in dodo_ingestor#15.

## Changes

- `retry.rs`: `Cancelled("Timeout expired")` is retryable. Any other `Cancelled`, such as a shutdown, is still final. New test case added.
- Defaults: `max_batch_size` 500 → 200 and `timeout_ms` 5000 → 15000, in `agent-config`, `BatcherConfig`, `TransportConfig`, `config/agent.yaml` and the server config generated by `get.sh`. Dev mode keeps `max_batch_size: 100`.

## Tests

`cargo test --features linux --all`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `tests/test-installer.sh` all pass.

Follow-up: the aegis-agent chart configmap hardcodes `timeout_ms: 5000` / `max_batch_size: 500`. That change goes in a separate PR in dodo_helm_charts.

author: sjoelund
body:
The OPC UA server had nodes only for Real and Boolean variables. All nodes had the data type BaseDataType and the access level None, thus clients could not see the type or which nodes they can write.

- Add nodes for the Integer variables (Int64) and for the Real, Integer and Boolean parameters. Parameters are read-only.
- Set DataType (Double, Int64 or Boolean) and AccessLevel on all nodes. Inputs and states are writable. A write to another node gives BadNotWritable instead of BadWriteNotSupported.
- An alias of a state was writable only if the index of the alias was less than the number of states, not the index of the state. Now all aliases of states are writable and other aliases are not.
- Make a node for each element of an array variable, with the name from printArrayElementName. The server used the scalar index on the array variable data.
- A write of the current value of an input does not cause an event.
- Start the server thread after all nodes are added.
- OMEdit: in an interactive simulation, a variable is editable only if the server can write it. Before, a tunable parameter (now in the tree) was editable, but the server ignored the change.

Integer, Boolean and Real inputs (#8704, #8705) can be written on master. The CTest test now writes all three.

Fixes #8318
Fixes #9655
Fixes #11342

author: fuji18
body:
## 概要

GitHub Projects v2 の board を**チケットの進行状況ダッシュボード**にする層を追加した。Issue / PR のイベントで board の Status を更新し、board 自体は**表示専用**に留める。

**board を判定の入力にしていない。** `autopilot-next.sh` は REST 限定のまま 1 行も変えていない(Claude Code on the web で GraphQL が 403 になるため)。board が壊れても止まっても、チケット消化の自動進行には影響しない。

### 入れたもの

| ファイル | 役割 |
| --- | --- |
| `.claude/scripts/project-sync.sh` | 同期の単一経路。`sync-issue` / `sync-pr` / `backfill [--all]` / `--check` / `--resolve-status` |
| `.claude/project-sync.json` | ラベル名と Status / Priority の名前候補(manifest 上は `merge`) |
| `.github/workflows/project-sync.yml` | `issues` / `pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch`。未設定なら何もせず `exit 0` |
| `.claude/scripts/test-project-sync.sh` + `ci.yml` | Status 4 分岐と fork 除外のフィクスチャテスト(20 件) |
| `.claude/docs/project-sync-guide.html` | 人間向け**しくみ**の解説(図 4 点 + FAQ) |
| `.claude/docs/project-sync-setup.html` | 人間向け**操作手順**。画面名とボタン名まで書いた作業用(図 2 点) |

### 設計上の要点

- **Status は Issue の「現在の状態」から毎回決め直す。** イベントの種類からは導かない。このため**すでに進行中のプロジェクトへ後から入れても過去のイベントを再生する必要がない**
- **`addProjectV2ItemById` は冪等**(既にあれば既存 item ID が返る)。`backfill` を何度流し直しても重複しない
- `backfill` は `gh api --paginate` で全ページを辿る。チケットが 100 件を超えても取りこぼさない
- Projects v2 は **GraphQL のみで `GITHUB_TOKEN` からは触れない**。classic PAT(`repo` + `project`)を `PROJECT_SYNC_TOKEN` に入れる前提

## 関連 Issue

なし(テンプレート自体の改修。`ticket` ラベル付き Issue を閉じないため `.harness/decisions.jsonl` の記録対象外)

## ステアリング

`20261104-github-project-sync`

## 検証

- [x] `/check`(lint・型チェック・テスト・フォーマット)がパス
- [x] `--resolve-status` のフィクスチャ 20 件 all passed / `check-shell.sh`(36 ファイル・指摘ゼロ)/ `check-manifest-coverage.sh` / `sync-agents-skills.sh --check` がパス
      ※ ホストに jq・shellcheck が無いため、shell 系はローカル Docker イメージ(shellcheck 0.9.0 / jq 1.6)の結果
- [ ] **実ボードでの動作確認は未実施。** PAT の発行と Project の作成が必要で人間の担当。手順は `.claude/docs/project-sync-setup.html` に画面・ボタン単位で書いた

## レビュアーへ

- `.github/workflows/` `.claude/scripts/` `.claude/*.json` はいずれも**委託禁止領域**のため、Codex には渡さず司令塔が直接書いた
- 手順書 3 枚(`autopilot-guide.html` / `project-sync-guide.html` / `project-sync-setup.html`)は CSS とテーマ切替を流用した別ファイル。**1 枚直したら残り 2 枚にも写す**必要がある(localStorage のキーは 3 枚とも別)。申し送りに記載済み
- SVG に色を直書きしていない(ダークテーマで読めなくなるため `.fig` 配下のクラス経由でテーマ変数に乗せている)

body:
This closes the gaps found after #34: a repository created from the template inherits the template's identity, and nothing noticed.

| Gap | Now |
|---|---|
| A new app's `frame.lock` names no source, so the app could run `frame-sync --lock` and bless its own edited page | `--lock` runs only in UOR-Foundation/template, identified by `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or the `origin` remote. Anywhere else, or where it can't tell, it refuses and points to `--pin`. |
| A new app ships the template's "Template contract" social card until someone runs `og.py` | `og.py` stamps `og.png` with a SHA-256 of the name, purpose, live URL and its own bytes. `page.mjs` recomputes the stamp from `app.json` and refuses any mismatch. |
| The same for the icons (a "T" for Template contract) | `icons.py` stamps every icon the same way, and the renderer checks all four. `icons.py` joins the locked page (13 files). |
| A new app deploys with `app.json` still describing the template | In CI, `page.mjs` refuses an `app.json` whose `repository` isn't the repository being built. |

The template's own card and icons are redrawn with stamps; the icon pixels are unchanged.

**Tested on a copy of the template.** It renders as is, and a new app renders once its card and icons are redrawn. Each of these is refused with its fix named:
- the template's `app.json` in another repository's CI;
- the template's card or icons under a new app's `app.json`;
- a purpose edited after the card was drawn;
- `og.py` changed after drawing;
- an unstamped card from before this change;
- `--lock` run as another repository.

**For existing apps:** prism-luhn, prism-leap-year and prism-legal-chess are unaffected until they next pin. At that pin they redraw their card and icons once.

author: dviejokfs
body:
## Why

A tunnel kept to part of a zone took a subdomain as its domain (`lab.example.com`), so the apps it published were two levels deep: `shop-production.lab.example.com`. Cloudflare's free Universal SSL covers the zone and one level below it (`*.example.com`), so visitors to those names got a certificate error unless the zone had Advanced Certificate Manager (or Total TLS). The console already warned about it, but offered no option that worked on the free plan.

## What

A tunnel can now have a **hostname suffix**. Its domain stays the zone and environments are published as `<label>-<suffix>.<zone>`, for example `shop-production-lab.example.com`. That is one level deep, which the free certificate covers.

**Server**
- Migration `m20261107_000006_ingress_connector_host_suffix` adds a nullable `ingress_connectors.host_suffix` with no backfill. Existing tunnels keep `<label>.<domain>` exactly as before.
- `POST /ingress/connectors` takes an optional `host_suffix`: 1-20 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit. It is refused for a provider with no domain, with a message saying what to change. `ConnectorView` and `EnvironmentHostsResponse` report it, and the create audit entry records it.
- Environment hosts (ADR 068 D3), the reachability plan and the environment address offer all use the suffixed name. A long label is still cut to one DNS label with a short hash, and a taken name still falls back to a hashed name that keeps the suffix and stays one level deep.

**Console**
- *Expose your apps* (guided setup) has a third hostname pattern between the two existing ones: "With a label, one level deep: `<app-name>-lab.example.com`", with the concrete example `shop-lab.example.com` shown next to `shop.lab.example.com`. The two-level option is unchanged and keeps its Advanced Certificate Manager warning.
- The worker's *Set up tunnel* dialog: once a label is entered, it asks whether apps are named `app-lab.example.com` (one level, the default) or `app.lab.example.com` (two levels, which still shows the ACM warning).
- The environment-hosts card shows the pattern the tunnel actually uses (`<environment>-lab.example.com`).
- A tunnel created without a suffix sends exactly the request it sent before.

The suffix is set when a tunnel is created. An existing two-level tunnel keeps working as it is; to move it to one-level names, create a new tunnel with a label.

## Tests

- `temps-ingress`: suffixed hosts stay one label under the zone; a taken suffixed name falls back within one label; a long label plus suffix is cut to one DNS label; suffix validation; the plan offers environment hosts for the suffixed name and not the plain one; create-time suffix checks (normalised, malformed, provider without a domain).
- `temps-migrations`: up/down test on a real database. Existing rows get `NULL`, the column is settable, and down removes it and keeps the row.
- Console: suffix validation and host naming, setup values for both layouts, the guided-setup request (`host_suffix` sent only with a label), the new radio option and its validation message, and the environment-hosts pattern text.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p temps-ingress -p temps-migrations -p temps-entities --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --lib -p temps-ingress -p temps-migrations` (288 + 96 passed)
- `cargo test -p temps-migrations --test migration_tests test_ingress_connector_host_suffix_migration_up_and_down`

body:
## Problem

Automatic typed-answer feedback advanced after a short motion-scaled delay: reduced motion left only 210 ms to read it. The hidden Hold Space pause had no visible equivalent, and timeout/unavailable fallbacks lacked a local explanation (audit L03/L04/I02 and typed-answer I10).

## Change

The existing verdict stays visible until Continue, Space or Enter. A compact Continue/arrow control replaces timed dismissal. Manual grading receives concise timeout, uncertainty or service-state feedback. Existing save/transition guards prevent duplicate answers and permit retry when a save fails.

```text
marked answer → readable feedback → Continue → save once
save fails   → keep feedback → retry Continue
```

## Scope and approval

Standalone PR against `master`, typed-answer feedback only. Authorised by the audit-fix request. No database schema, grading model, backup/import format, sync wire format, credentials or service requests change. Undo and interruption handling remain intact. Written-question service-state presentation is a separate scope. Rollback is a code revert.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with GPT-6.1 Sol. Sol verdict: approved. S1 identified an acceptance latch preventing save-failure retries; the redundant latch was removed and an actual session regression now covers failure, retry and repeated activation. No unresolved findings. Full Stop: keep open and unmerged, without auto-merge or queue entry.

## Verification

Candidate: b6aab76e28d3ee4ffa3561750fd2f2f6159078e6.

- Before: controlled reduced-motion walkthrough auto-advanced after feedback; after: normal and reduced-motion feedback stays readable until explicit continuation.
- Hook/controls: 40 passed; existing session integration suites passed. Final save-failure regression plus hook/full automatic session file: 33 passed. The retry case failed before the S1 fix.
- Intercepted Jev browser suite: 18 passed. Final reading-control alignment checks: 2 passed (normal/reduced motion). No live model requests.
- The final isolated build succeeded; its wrapper encountered a retained preview port. That exact unchanged build was checked on another local port with a matching patch fingerprint. The wrapper is not claimed as a full pass.
- Web typecheck and scoped ESLint passed. Screenshots cover readable feedback and manual timeout fallback; changed browser specs capture hosted evidence.
- Exercised Windows-hosted Chromium at desktop size. Packaged Windows/Linux/macOS were not run locally; hosted checks remain pending.

Created with Codex.

author: kolchurinvv
body:
A dispatch no longer has to cut a branch. **BRANCH** on both dispatch forms is `own branch` (the default, unchanged) or `no branch`. With no branch, the dispatch starts as a **conversation across its product**: nothing is cut in any repo, and the session can read every repo in the product. When the talk arrives somewhere, the conversation becomes a **worker** on a branch of its own, keeping its context, or an **orchestrator** that sends workers out. Recorded in ADR 0028.

## Why

Every dispatch cut a branch and was told "commit as you go, open the PR", including work that only wanted an answer. On the reporting store, three in a row did:
- `review-163`: "only provide the succinct report"
- `byga-integration-sitrep`
- `find-mannequin`

The only other way to a session with no branch was to start one by hand in a shared checkout and adopt it. Every adopted record there sits in a `main` or `dev` checkout.

## What it adds

**Starting as a conversation**
- Pick a repo to start there, or pick the product as a whole: its own row on WHERE, after its repos.
- The session reads each repo's canonical checkout, handed over with `--add-dir`, and is told to change nothing in them.
- It runs in a folder of its own, `branchless/<slug>-<id>`. That folder's `CLAUDE.md` is the brief: every repo, its checkout, what its work merges into, and the two ways into work. claude reloads it, so it survives a long conversation, and Resume puts it back if the folder goes.
- It takes its focus repo's tmux server and toolchain. A whole-product conversation gets a server named for the product.

**Turning into a worker:** `claude-dispatcher worktree --repo <repo> <name>`, from the session's own shell
- Given an existing branch, it goes into that branch's worktree, or cuts one for it. Given anything else, it cuts `<prefix><slug>` from the root, where the repo's layout puts a dispatch's worktree.
- The record becomes a worker's: branch, repo and base set, so PR tracking, provenance and done-means-live come back.
- One branch per conversation, and never the canonical checkout's own.
- Each repo's worktree folder is given beside its checkout, so the session can work in what it cuts without asking.
- Kill and tidy remove a worktree it cut, never one it only went into.

**Turning into an orchestrator:** `claude-dispatcher dispatch --repo <repo> --title … "<brief>"`
- Each worker is an ordinary dispatcher on the conversation's subscription, marked `sent by "<conversation>"` on its row.
- `status --json` has `dispatched_by` for steering them, and `reply` works as usual.
- The worker launches with the session's own variables scrubbed. A pane inherits its client's environment, and `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, the messaging socket and token, and the dispatcher id would otherwise make it the conversation's child.

**On the table**
- While it's still talking: `no branch` on the row, `y` is **mark done**, and it is counted as a ship nowhere (history, velocity, the floor). The steward never wakes for it.
- Once it has taken a branch: a normal worker row.

**Two fixes this needed, useful on their own**
- An empty branch names no PR and no runs. `gh pr list --head ""` lists every PR, so a record with no branch was handed the repo's newest merge and marked done on it.
- Kill keeps a clean worktree whose detached HEAD holds commits no ref does.

## Verification

- Build, vet (Linux and Windows), golangci-lint (0 issues), gofmt and `go test ./... -race` pass locally. Per-file coverage against main: no touched file drops.
- **`--add-dir` placement, measured on claude 2.1.317.** It is variadic: before the prompt, it reads the prompt as a directory. After it, both given dirs were readable (one with a space in its path), and a dir not given was denied.
- **Why our own verbs:** claude's `EnterWorktree` only enters worktrees of the repository a session was launched in, or of one nested inside it. A conversation's folder is neither.
- **The real binary, end to end**, against a scratch HOME, state dir and `TMUX_TMPDIR`, with a stand-in `claude`:
  - a whole-product conversation dispatched from the dx form;
  - `worktree` cut `feature/pricing-fix` inside a folder the session was given, and refused a second branch;
  - the conversation's row turned into a worker row on `api`;
  - `dispatch`, run from a shell carrying a fake session's variables, started a worker whose claude process carried only its own dispatcher id, recorded as sent by the conversation.
- Earlier runs found and fixed:
  - the form opening on the product row;
  - a whole-product session landing on the cockpit's tmux server.
- An independent review of the first version found four defects, each fixed with a failing test first:
  - a done conversation counted as a ship;
  - the contract's mode sentences;
  - folder collisions between conversations whose titles share their first five words;
  - empty repo names in messages.

## Notes for review

- ADR 0028 is numbered after #88's 0027. Nothing else overlaps.
- The design moved twice while this was open, and the ADR records each step:
  - first, a detached checkout of one repo;
  - then a read-only conversation across the product;
  - now a conversation that can turn into a worker or an orchestrator.

author: tvdavies
body:
Part of #766. This PR covers items 1 to 3: disk-only saves, reflinks, and trim before a save. Compression (item 4) is left out for now; the reasoning and measurements are in a comment on the issue.

Rebased onto main after #776 (`snapshot.keep`). Saving a stopped sandbox or a history entry goes through `keepSnapshot` and keeps what the source holds. Nothing in this PR changes that.

## Why

Saved microVM snapshots are 13 to 25 GB. There are three reasons:

- Every save of a running microVM kept its full memory.
- Every disk copy was a full copy.
- Deleted files' blocks were never freed on the host. The guest mounts its disk with `discard`, but Firecracker v1.17 only passes discard through when a drive asks for it (`"discard": true`, Sync engine), and Kantel never asked. So the guest saw no discard support and nothing was trimmed.

On a dev host, one 6 GiB snapshot takes up 4.73 GB on the host, but its file system only uses 186 MB. The rest is deleted data.

## Rollout: trim needs a host-images release

The guest agent ships in the sandbox image (host-images), not in `kantel-host`. Trim before a save starts working only after a host-images release with the new agent, and a bump of the pinned `DEFAULT_HOST_IMAGES` in `packages/hosts/src/http.ts`. Until then:

- A new host talking to an older agent gets a 404 for `POST /disk/trim` straight away. The host treats that as no trim and logs nothing, with no 20 s wait.
- Discard on the drive takes effect on hosts at once, after their one-off template rebuild, so the guest's own online discard (`discard` mount) already frees space.
- Disk-only saves and reflinks don't depend on the image.

## What changed

**Disk-only saves by default**
- `SaveSnapshotBody` and `TakeSnapshotBody` now take `memory` (default false). Compute passes it through `Backend.takeSnapshot(id, { memory })` to the host's `snapshot.save`.
- Without `memory`, the host saves a running microVM's disk alone (`liveDiskSnapshot`):
  - **Sync.** The guest syncs first. If the sync fails, the save fails: no memory is kept, so anything not yet written back would otherwise be lost without a word. The VM keeps running and the incomplete snapshot directory is removed.
  - **Watched copy.** The VM is paused and the disk is copied. Each copy is watched for writes (inotify plus the file's stamp). A write raises its inotify event only as it finishes. So after each copy, and before reading the watch, the host makes a round trip through Firecracker's VMM thread (`Barrier`, a `GET /machine-config`). With the Sync engine, that thread makes every disk write, so when the round trip returns, any write that was still under way has finished and been recorded. The drive config now sets `"io_engine": "Sync"` explicitly rather than relying on Firecracker's default. A copy that overlapped a write, or a failed barrier, means the copy is made again, up to 4 times; if every copy fails the check, the save fails rather than keep a torn copy. The memory snapshot's copy made beside the memory uses the barrier too.
  - **No watch.** If the disk can't be watched (for example, inotify instances are used up), it is only cloned with a reflink, which captures the file at one instant. On a file system without reflinks the save fails. It never relies on the file's stamps alone.
  - **Pause and resume.** If the answer to a pause is lost, the pause may still have applied, so the host resumes the VM anyway. Resuming a running VM is harmless (checked against Firecracker v1.17). Each resume attempt gets its own 10 s, separate from the caller's context, and there are three tries. A VM that still won't resume is stopped, keeping its disk, rather than left frozen while it's reported as running, and the save fails. The memory snapshot path now pauses and resumes the same way.
- With `memory: true`, the existing live snapshot (memory and disk) runs as before.
- Saving a stopped sandbox keeps whatever its stop kept, memory included, whatever `memory` says. `memory` only applies to running sandboxes.
- Everywhere else:
  - CLI: `kantel snapshot save|take --memory`.
  - MCP: `snapshot_save` takes `memory`.
  - Console: the Save snapshot dialog has a "Keep its memory too" checkbox, shown for running microVMs only. Stories are in `Compute/Save snapshot`.
  - Docs: the snapshots pages explain disk-only versus memory.
- Compatibility: an older host ignores `memory` and keeps memory, and says so in its answer. An older control plane talking to a newer host gets disk-only saves.

**Reflinks**
- `copySparse` keeps main's reflink-then-sparse copy from #776. The isolate tier's template copy now uses `cp --reflink=auto --sparse=always`.
- `KeepSnapshot`'s hard links aren't affected: a snapshot's files are never written after they're made, and discard only punches holes in the running VM's own `disk.ext4`.
- The hosts page now recommends XFS (with reflinks) or btrfs for `/var/lib/kantel-host`.

**Discard and trim**
- `fc.BootConfig.Discard` sets `"discard": true` on the writable disk.
- The host turns it on when Firecracker is v1.17 or later (`fc.DiscardSupported`). It's added to the templates' fingerprint, so templates are rebuilt once.
- The guest agent has a new `POST /disk/trim` endpoint (FITRIM on `/dev/vdb`'s mount). Before a live save, the host calls it with a 20 s limit, best effort:
  - These answers each mean no trim, and the host stays quiet about them: an older agent (404), a disk without discard (501), or a trim still running (409).
  - The guest runs one trim at a time. The ioctl isn't cancelled when the host stops waiting, so a hung trim makes later saves skip trimming rather than queue behind it. It holds no lock that a save or a sync needs.
- Live forks don't trim, so they stay fast.

## Tests

- **Go:** `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags vmtest ./...` and `go test ./...` in apps/host all pass. New unit tests:
  - `TestBootDiscard` (now also asserts the Sync engine) and `TestDiscardSupported`.
  - `TestCopyQuietDiskWaitsOutAWriteInFlight`: a write finishes inside the barrier, after the copy. That copy is refused, and the next, which contains the write, is kept. A failing barrier means nothing is kept.
  - `TestSaveSnapshotOfAStoppedSandboxKeepsWhatItsStopKept`: all four combinations of stop-kept-memory and memory-asked.
  - `TestCopySparseFallsBackWithoutReflinks`, `TestCopyQuietDisk` and `TestCopyQuietDiskRefusesADiskBeingWritten`.
  - `TestCopyQuietDiskFailsClosedWithoutAWatch`: watching is forced to fail while writes overlap the copy.
  - `TestLiveDiskSnapshot*` against a fake Firecracker API and guest agent:
    - The normal pause, copy and resume.
    - A failed guest sync: the VM is never paused and no directory is left.
    - A pause applied with its answer dropped: the VM is resumed and the save fails.
    - A resume that always fails: three tries, then the VM is stopped and the save fails.
  - `TestTrimBeforeASaveWithAnAgentThatCantTrim`: 404 from an old agent's mux, 501 and 409 are no trim, take under a second and log nothing; 200 logs the trim.
  - `TestTrimDiskOneAtATime`, in the guest package.
- **VM tests**, run locally as root in a separate network namespace with Firecracker v1.17.0, the host's kernel and image, and a freshly built injected `kantel-guest`:
  - **New `TestDiskOnlySave`**:
    - Resuming a running VM is harmless.
    - Writing a 512 MiB file pushes the disk to 528 MiB on the host. Deleting it brings that to 384 MiB through online discard.
    - A disk-only save while a writer fsyncs all the time took 54 ms and is 22 MiB, because the trim freed the rest. It has no memory file.
    - `e2fsck -fy` on a copy of it is clean.
    - The same save with memory is 2,071 MiB.
    - A sandbox of a different size starts from the disk-only save and has the file written before it.
  - `TestSpooledForkDiskMatchesMemory` (4 forks; the disk never needed a second copy), `TestDeferredDiskGrowth` and `TestGrowDisk` pass, now with discard on as a host has it.
- **TypeScript:**
  - `pnpm

body:
Newsletter sign-ups from a business's own website now land in Business Agent, for any business: each person goes onto **Customers** as a lead from the website with a yes to marketing, and the topics they ticked (for Easy Beans: Coffee tips, Learning Spanish, Learning English, Menu updates, Events, Offers) become tags, so **Campaigns** can send to just the people interested in each one.

## What's in it

**Website & SEO → Newsletter sign-ups** (admins):
- Who's subscribed and for which topic, and the latest sign-ups and unsubscribes.
- The business's own topics, each a tag on Customers with its wording in Spanish and English, whether the form asks for a name or a phone, its own heading, and a live preview of the form.
- Three ways onto a website:
  - a **link** (Instagram bio, a QR code);
  - a **snippet** any website builder takes: an iframe that fits itself to the form and speaks the visitor's language;
  - the website's **own form** posting to `POST /api/site/<business>/signup`.
- A **website key** (shown once, only its hash kept) for a website's server: it skips the per-address limit, can send older sign-ups with their date, and can tell us about unsubscribes (`POST /api/site/<business>/unsubscribe`).
- **Bring in your list**: a CSV from another newsletter service or the website's own export. Only people still subscribed come in (an unsubscribed date, a "no" status or no yes in any opt-in column leaves them out), with their topics and the day they signed up.

**Database** (the `newsletter` migration):
- `newsletter`: one row per business, admins only.
- `newsletter_events`: every sign-up and unsubscribe, kept as the GDPR record of each yes, and deleted with the person.
- `newsletter_signup()` / `newsletter_unsubscribe()` for the Worker: one person per email per business; someone already there keeps who they are and gains the topics. Unsubscribing takes the yes back, and signing up again is a new yes.
- Easy Beans is seeded on, with its website's six topic keys.

**Worker** (`worker/newsletter.ts`): the hosted form page, the public sign-up with CORS open, a hidden robot trap and five an hour per address (kept only as an HMAC), the keyed unsubscribe, and the admin key and import routes. It's registered before the menu feed so the sign-up's CORS preflight is answered here.

The contract for websites is in `docs/WEBSITE.md` → *Newsletter sign-ups*.

## Not in this PR
- **Easy Beans' website** (its own repo) still needs to send its sign-ups and unsubscribes here: a small change to its `/api/signup`, competition entry and unsubscribe routes, using a key made on Website & SEO.
- Its **three existing sign-ups** come in from the website's admin export through *Bring in your list*. Of those, two are still subscribed; the third is a test entry with no yes.

## Checks
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test`: 1,254 pass, including the new `shared/newsletter.test.ts` and `worker/newsletter.test.ts`
- `npm run test:db`: all pass, including the new `zz_y_newsletter.test.sql` and the several-businesses checks
- CI on the branch: green, every browser test included
- The hosted form in a real browser, inside another site's page: "All" ticks every topic, a bad email is refused, the right fields are posted, and the frame grows and shrinks to fit.
