author: erdhyernando
body:
Closes #15
Closes #16

Combined into one PR as suggested — both are pure dependency work and share a single lockfile diff.

**`pnpm audit`: 57 → 2 advisories. Critical 1 → 0, high 30 → 0.**

## #15 — React Router

`react-router` 7.5.3 → **7.18.5**; `react-router-dom` **removed**.

In v7 `react-router-dom` is only a compatibility re-export, so the lockfile held two copies (`7.5.3` direct + `7.6.0` pulled through the re-export). All four imports now point at `react-router`:

| File | Import |
|---|---|
| `src/main.jsx:3` | `BrowserRouter, Routes, Route` |
| `src/components/BackButton.jsx:1` | `Link` |
| `src/pages/ClientProjectPage.jsx:1` | `useParams, useNavigate` |
| `src/pages/NotFoundPage.jsx:1` | `Link` |

`pnpm why react-router` → single version.

On the advisories themselves — refreshed from the advisory text, unchanged from the audit: **9 of the 11 state verbatim that declarative mode (`<BrowserRouter>`) is not affected**, and the 2 open-redirect ones require untrusted paths reaching `navigate()`/`<Link>`, which this app never does. Upgraded anyway because it is patch-level and it clears the Socket P0 score penalty.

## #16 — Toolchain

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `eslint` | 9.26.0 | **10.14.0** |
| `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` | 5.2.0 | **7.1.1** |
| `eslint-plugin-react-refresh` | 0.4.20 | **0.5.7** |
| `@eslint/js` / `globals` | 9.26 / 16 | **10.0.1 / 17.14.0** |
| `react` / `react-dom` | 19.1.0 | **19.3.1** |
| `three` | 0.176.0 | **0.187.0** |
| `@react-three/fiber` | 9.1.x | **9.8.2** |
| `@react-three/drei` | 10.0.x | **10.7.9** |
| `gsap` / `react-hot-toast` / `react-icons` | 3.12.7 / 2.5.2 / 5.5.0 | **3.15.1 / 2.6.1 / 5.7.0** |
| `react-helmet-async` | 2.0.5 | **`@dr.pogodin/react-helmet` 3.3.2** |
| `tailwindcss`, `@tailwindcss/vite` | `dependencies` | **`devDependencies`** |

### Why eslint 10 is the big one

`eslint@9.26` added a **direct** dependency on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, which pulled in `express@5` and its entire middleware chain. That single edge produced `proxy-addr` (critical), `body-parser`, `qs`, `path-to-regexp`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` itself — roughly 30 advisories, all of it dead weight for a project that only lints JSX. `eslint@10` no longer depends on it. Whole cluster gone, and the `critical` count finally reaches 0.

### The React Compiler rules needed a decision

`eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7` turns on the React Compiler rules by default, which surfaced **7 pre-existing violations** this repo has always had:

```
react-hooks/purity        ×3  Gallery.jsx: Math.random() inside useMemo
react-hooks/refs          ×3  GradientBackground3D.jsx, Interface.jsx: refs read during render
react-hooks/set-state-in-effect ×1  App.jsx: setState in effect on section change
```

I did **not** fix these here — they are real behavioural changes, not dependency work, and #18/#19 already own them. Instead the three rules are set to `warn` in `eslint.config.js` with an inline comment naming the files and the tracking issues, so this upgrade does not gate `pnpm lint`.

Result: `1 error, 8 warnings` (was `1 error, 1 warning`). **The 1 error is `no-unused-vars` for `actions` in `NamlapanStudio.jsx:14` and it is pre-existing on `master`** — lint was already exiting non-zero before this PR. Left alone; say the word and I'll remove the unused destructure in a follow-up.

### `react-helmet-async` → `@dr.pogodin/react-helmet`

Per your decision. The old package declares `peerDependencies.react: "^16.6.0 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0"` — it never claimed React 19 — and its maintainer has publicly declared it unmaintained. `3.0.0` of the original only adds the peer while turning `HelmetProvider` into a passthrough with an open duplicate-`<title>` regression, so it was the worse option.

The fork is a drop-in: `HelmetProvider` and `Helmet` keep the same API, 5 import lines changed, zero behavioural change.

### `pnpm.overrides` for source-map-js

`@tailwindcss/node@4.3.4` pins `source-map-js` **exactly at `1.2.1`**, so pnpm could not dedupe onto the patched `1.2.2` and the high-severity `CVE-2026-93749` survived even after the Vite 8 bump. A one-line override resolves it; `1.2.1 → 1.2.2` is a patch with an identical API.

## Verification — master build vs this build, real Chromium

Four routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/project/BNI`, and `/nope-404`. Both builds served with SPA fallback, `Math.random` stubbed to a constant so the gallery layout is call-count-independent.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `document.title` | identical, all 4 routes |
| `<title>` tag count | **1 in every case** — no duplicate-title regression |
| `<link rel=canonical>` | identical |
| JSON-LD `<script type=application/ld+json>` | still in `<head>` on `/` |
| `meta[name]`/`meta[property]` sets | **byte-identical** — 12 / 10 / 10 / 2 |
| Screenshot diff, `/pricing` | **0 differing pixels** |
| Screenshot diff, `/nope-404` | **0 differing pixels** |
| Screenshot diff, `/` | 0.05%, bounding box inside the WebGL canvas |
| Screenshot diff, `/project/BNI` | 5.6%, bounding box `787x477+653+236` — **exactly the YouTube iframe**; two page loads serve different video frames |
| Console errors / page errors | 0 / 0 |

Also: `pnpm dev` (Vite 8.3.6, ready in 271 ms, deep link `/pricing` → 200), `pnpm build` (1286 modules, sitemap + robots emitted), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` clean.

## Numbers

```
advisories      57 → 2     (critical 1→0, high 30→0, moderate 22→2)
lockfile       366 → 253 packages
bundle         1,433.34 → 1,558.00 kB   (417.16 → 451.11 kB gzip)
```

**The bundle grew ~125 kB.** I measured it per-module rather than guessing:

| package | Δ kB (rendered) |
|---|---|
| `@react-three/fiber` | +202 |
| `react-reconciler` | −308 |
| `react-dom` | +93 |
| `three` | +80 |
| `@dr.pogodin/react-helmet` (+ −`react-helmet-async`) | +7 net |
| `react-router` | +13 |

fiber 9.8 now bundles `react-reconciler` instead of importing it as a separate module, which nets −106. The real growth is `three` 0.187 and `react-dom` 19.3. Not a regression from anything done here, but worth knowing — #19's motion-stack work is the natural place to claw some of it back.

## Remaining, deliberately

```
[moderate] fflate@0.6.10   via @react-three/drei > three-stdlib   (no untrusted ZIPs here)
[moderate] minimatch@10.2.6 via eslint                            (eslint pins ^10.2.6; forcing 11 is a semver-major)
```

Both dev/build-time only. Forcing either would mean overriding a semver-major contract of an upstream package — not worth it. This satisfies the umbrella's "0 critical, 0 high" bar in #12.

## Pre-existing peer warnings, unchanged

pnpm still reports these two — both are exactly what #19 removes:

```
framer-motion@10.12.16   ✕ unmet peer react@^18.0.0        (found 19.3.1)
framer-motion-3d@12.4.13 ✕ unmet peer @react-three/fiber@8.2.2 (found 9.8.2)
```

author: balsoft
body:
Currently, sending multi-paragraph messages is broken - the markdown
fallback is sent correctly, but the rich text blocks are not; the result
is that paragraph breaks disappear on send.

E.g.
```markdown
hello

world
```

Turns into
```markdown
helloworld
```

The actual bug is that slk assumes that each slack RichTextSection is
automatically a new paragraph, whereas this is not the case.

The commit simply adds a newline at the end of each RichTextSection
coming from goldmark's Paragraph AST node, keeping the markdown
representation the same as before.

Note that the case with multiple consecutive paragraph breaks is (still) not
handled correctly due to the way goldmark parses paragraphs. It is more
involved and left as a future bugfix, as it is used much less often.

body:
Third of six layered PRs, and it builds on #2.

## Why

The page, its nav and `check-brand` each kept their own list of sections, and they had drifted apart: `check-brand` failed on a section nobody rendered. Shared components also had Okonkwo's own words typed into them.

author: rchillyard
body:
Closes #108, closes #109, closes #110, closes #111.

## What

- **`TopN`** (core `util`): an immutable accumulator of the n greatest (`TopN.greatest`) or least (`TopN.least`) values by an `Ordering`, built on Visitor's `PrioQueue` (a binary heap). It holds at most n values; a value no better than the worst kept is ignored, so each costs O(log n) at most.
- **`Table.topN` / `Table.bottomN`**, beside `sort`, keeping the header.
- **Streams:** `IOTable.topN` / `bottomN` (fs2 `Pipe`s) and `ZIOTable.topN` / `bottomN` (`ZPipeline`s) emit the n best rows once the stream ends, holding only n rows, so a stream far too big for memory can be ranked.

## Dependency

core now depends on **Visitor 1.7.0** (`PrioQueue`), excluding Visitor's runtime `logback-classic` so users still choose their SLF4J backend. The generated POM carries the exclusion; core's runtime classpath gains only `visitor_3` and `slf4j-api`.

## Docs and tests

- README: Table methods, Streaming section, 2.4.0 release notes; streaming, Kafka and JSON docs (#110). Raw predicate (#109) and the setter fix (#111): see the third commit. #112 (encrypted parser setters) is not fixed here.
- New `TopNSpec` (12 tests, including agreement with sorting on random data), one `TableSpec` test, two stream tests each for fs2 and ZIO (one ranks a 100,000-row stream as it is parsed).
- Locally: `sbt clean test unidoc` passes.

Version 2.4.0.

author: xyhstruggler
body:
## Summary

A scheduled result can update its source Chat while the next message is being prepared. The client then used an older revision and the server correctly rejected the message, leaving the draft unsent. This was reproduced during both attachment uploads and the actual attachment-free Full Access scope read.

Finish preparation before binding the first request to the latest accepted record for the same Chat and unchanged authority/context. Release definitively undispatched preparation failures without discarding concurrent preparations or uncertain requests. Web Canvas, Web Desktop and Web Mobile use the shared Web helper; Electron Desktop uses the same guarded tracker with its current accepted record.

## Dependency

Stacked above Draft #3194, exact parent `f0a7985b0cd78ce37c6b6b91030cc0f4741096ff`. Reuses the existing routine persistence, result publication, scheduler, approval and cancellation paths; no backend rewrite.

Exact head: `6ea9a385bb9ec3d211a1cd95d8666ae74d71b2e2`; tree: `fa59cd7496541fb0f76a25255ce2021978e3a876`.

## Tests

**191 tests pass across 12 files, zero skipped:** 188 client regressions and 3 real pooled-Postgres writer/notification/Web-hook/CAS tests. Meaningful Red covers attachment and actual attachment-free scope-read races, plus preparation tracker exhaustion at the 101st distinct undispatched failure. Existing unknown-receipt and concurrent-preparation tests pass. Setup errors are excluded from qualification.

Affected UI/Web/Electron renderer source types and new-test types pass; ESLint has zero errors and two inherited warnings. Pattern checks have zero violations and the same two baseline warning categories; whitespace checks pass. The isolated database was audited clean and restored stopped. These are local isolated checks; the separate bounded live-account evidence is below. They do not establish full CI.

## Invariants

- Source of truth: committed canonical Chat state on the server; the client uses only an already accepted same-Chat record with unchanged owner, lifecycle, selection, provider binding, active Run and project context.
- Lock/transaction scope: server CAS and existing transactional receipt publication remain unchanged. Routine-control revisions in command text are never rewritten.
- Acceptable orphan states: an unsent draft remains visible after a concurrent conflict. Preparation references are released only before any possible dispatch; bound or unknown requests remain immutable and are never automatically replayed.
- Auth source of truth: existing captured browser/native authority and trusted host context. This adds no endpoint, identity claim, permission, scheduler, Settings switch or general background consent.
- Deferred scope: a commit after the first transport invocation can still cause a legitimate CAS conflict. Full CI, independent C signoff, comprehensive affected-surface UI checks and production reliability remain separate gates.

## Review / Monitoring

Independent review found and fixed pre-dispatch preparation retention, including a concurrent-preparation guard. Main verified the final seven reviewed source/test hashes before commit. Keep this PR Draft. No merge or release-channel promotion is requested. Public guide changes remain in FinnaAI/matrix-os-site#319.

## Matching-version live acceptance

A separate, bounded Dev test ran this exact host-bundle source with the matching isolated Electron QA bridge, actual Claude 2.1.317 source process and the existing ChatGPT subscription. Official bundle-only build/register execution [42235707409](https://github.com/HamedMP/matrix-os/actions/runs/42235707409) produced `v2026.11.06-pr3198-42235707409-1-6ea9a38`, SHA256 `0418d75401b12fe5b2fa16bb76fdf8b92b1f31b9ec7d72911e5683797bdc15ff`. Only the owner-selected Dev Computer was updated; installed, running and release source matched. No channel, fleet or shared Platform rollout was performed for this build.

- A real Claude CLI proposal produced the independent approval card in its original Chat. The primary assistant performed owner-browser confirmation and activation under the owner's explicit delegation; the harness did not approve itself. The activation POST completed in 16.002 seconds, exercising the inherited 30-second response budget. The 30-minute owner-decision window is a separate deadline.
- Eight scheduled occurrences completed, each with one attempt. Initial and post-resume results appeared in that same source Chat, executed by the existing canonical Matrix Bot. No new Bot or per-harness durable scheduler was created.
- A real CLI pause was followed by 401.404 seconds between independent paused reads with the same four fire IDs across multiple due times. A separately requested resume selected a future slot; no paused backlog was replayed.
- Five actual native tool-call/result correlations verified that the known-applied duplicate returned an identical full envelope and original saved receipt, while a new stale-revision request returned `revision_conflict`. The final native show was paused at revision 6. A stale JSON block copied into the model's prose was excluded from acceptance.
- Actual CLI archive advanced the test to archived revision 12. Independent owner reads and a separately correlated actual CLI show retained all eight completed entries, untruncated, after the previous next-due time. Archive was not an owner-management cleanup substitute. `execution.stop=unconfirmed` remains truthful; there is no physical worker-stop claim.
- An ordinary one-time reminder with Persistent task off used actual native `CronCreate` with `recurring=false`, delivered its exact marker back into the original Chat at the later scheduled time, and then actual `CronList` returned no jobs. The native intent did not attest Matrix creation. This closes the bounded native-default coexistence check without creating a duplicate durable routine.

Full Access composer mode was retained during command testing, but the expired source lease was not extended. This case used the normal per-operation owner confirmations under delegation; it is not proof of unattended Full Access source-lease renewal. Scheduling capability requires no Settings grant. Source authority, task activation, model consent and integration permissions stayed separate; the general background model authorization remained false in the observed account read.

Some browser Chat/Schedules/status reads timed out during the session and recovered through ordinary read refresh. The bounded lifecycle above does not establish a sole cause or general UI/network reliability fix. Earlier failed/uncertain test histories remain preserved separately and were not replayed or counted among these eight occurrences. Missing-permission, cross-owner/Chat/Bot, changed-payload and cancellation/unknown guard cases retain their isolated-test evidence; no fresh real cross-account or deliberately uncertain side-effect experiment was run here. The English demonstration is an edited presentation of the real evidence, not additional runtime coverage.

author: luketobrien
body:
Diagram text was always white, so it was close to unreadable on light fills. Each box now works out its text colour from its own fill.

## Contrast on the real Jetty themes

Lowest text-on-box contrast on the theme's own fills, measured with `jetty/themes/*.css` and the built bundle:

| Theme | Before | After | Text now |
|---|---|---|---|
| dusk | 1.44:1 | 14.56:1 | black |
| cinema | 1.6:1 | 12.88:1 | black |
| dark | 2.6:1 | 8.06:1 | black |
| plain | 4.47:1 | 4.47:1 | white, unchanged |
| report | 5.17:1 | 5.17:1 | white, unchanged |

The "before" figures for cinema and dark come from the Sue walk report (2026-11-05). The others are from this run.

## The rule

- White text, or black once white would fall under 4:1. This is CIE lightness 53, written in CSS with relative colours (`lch(from var(--node-fill) …)`).
- The bar isn't WCAG's 4.5:1 because plain's indigo gets 4.47:1 with white, and its white text is worth keeping. So 4:1 is the floor.
- It's CSS rather than script, so it follows a change of theme, a brand or a dark slide with no redraw, and it works on a colour in any format.
- A browser without relative colours gets white, as before.

## Behaviour changes to check

- A page's `--chart-on-fill` still wins on the page's own fills, but not on a node's own `colour`, because the page didn't choose its token for that colour.
- A node's own colour now wins on a flowchart decision or start/end shape. It used to lose on specificity.
- A timeline card with its own colour now gets readable text instead of the page's ink. Its date stays in the ink because it sits on the page.
- Depth 6 and below now gets the third colour. It used to have no rule, so it fell back to black.

## Tests

- Three new tests in `tests/e2e/diagram.spec.ts`: the themes' accents plus a sweep of 64 colours and non-hex formats, each box working out its own text, and the token's precedence. All three failed on the old build.
- Jest 615 passed. The diagram and diagram-editor specs pass, 11 in all. The rest of the browser suite is left to CI.
- `print` emulation computes the same colour and a PDF is written, but nobody has looked at that PDF (no renderer on this machine).
- Not run in the app, the Player or on a tablet. Older browsers' white fallback isn't exercised.

## After merging

Jetty and Logbook bundle this from source, so rebuild them, then vendor into jollify and release. The Logbook half is a separate PR that drops its `--chart-on-fill` override: Jollify-Software/logbook, branch `diagram-readable-text`.

**1. Project snapshots accept a required `kicad-packages3D`** (`3a2814d`)

CopperReview compiles `.copper` project folders through the source snapshot (`copper_lang::snapshot`). The snapshot checks each locked module's `source` against the plain git forms (`git:` / `replace:git:` / `replace:<path>`). KiCad's 3D library is a sparse module, locked as `sparse-git:https://…` or, behind the GitLab replacement from `docs/3d-models.md`, `replace:sparse-git:https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D.git@10.0.8`. So any project that requires it was rejected:

```
WEB_PROJECT: locked source differs for github.com/KiCad/kicad-packages3D
```

The module holds no `.copper` sources, and the snapshot is an electrical-review boundary that loads no physical assets. It is now skipped (via `packages::is_sparse_module`); every other module is checked as before.

Examples on the root manifest now export KiCad's own 3D models instead of generated bodies. `copper lock` was run for every such example board. author: matheusgomessouza
body:
## What changed

The API now sends a password reset link and sets a new password from that link.

- Add `POST /admin-users/password-reset/request`. It returns `202` for every valid email.
- Add `GET /admin-users/password-reset/validate`. It checks the token.
- Add `POST /admin-users/password-reset/confirm`. It sets the new password.
- Store only the SHA-256 hash of the token in `AdminPasswordResetToken`. The token expires after 30 minutes and works once.
- Send the email with Nodemailer through the new `SMTP_*` variables.
- Revoke the refresh tokens of the user after a successful reset.
- Limit the three endpoints per IP address.
- Add 24 tests for the flow.

## Why

The admin panel had no way to recover a forgotten password. The reset token is a random 256-bit value, so an attacker cannot guess it. The database never stores the raw token. The request response is always the same, so the endpoint does not reveal whether an email exists.

## How to test

1. Run `npm install`.
2. Set `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_FROM`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, and `SMTP_PORT` in `.env.local`. Leave `SMTP_HOST` empty to print the link in the server console.
3. Run `npm run start:dev`.
4. Call `POST /admin-users/password-reset/request` with `{"email":"admin@example.com"}`.
5. Copy the link from the email or the server console.
6. Call `GET /admin-users/password-reset/validate?token=<token>`.
7. Call `POST /admin-users/password-reset/confirm` with `{"token":"<token>","password":"new-password"}`.
8. Call `POST /admin-users/authenticate` with the new password.
9. Call the validate endpoint again with the same token.

Expected result: Step 6 returns `200`. Step 8 returns `200`. Step 9 returns `400`.

## Risks

- A duplicated `AdminUser.email` fails closed. A duplicated email receives no link until the data is clean. Add a unique index after the cleanup.
- Production does not start without `SMTP_HOST` and `SMTP_FROM`. Set both before the deploy.
- The rate limiter keys by IP address. Behind a reverse proxy, set `trust proxy` to keep one limit per client.
- The refresh-token store is an in-memory `Map`. The revocation does not survive a restart. This is a pre-existing limit.

## Out of scope

- `POST /admin-users` is public. This PR does not change it.
- `AdminUser.email` is not unique. This PR does not change the schema for it.
- The access token stays valid for up to 15 minutes after the reset. This PR records `passwordChangedAt` but does not check it.
- The manual end-to-end test did not run. No PostgreSQL client and no Docker daemon were available.

author: bielweed
body:
## O que muda para quem usa (versão 1.5.140)

- **Busca:** quem digita no singular acha o plural (anel acha Anéis, cartão acha Cartões); a caixa diz que está carregando em vez de "nenhum produto"; termo longo não estoura.
- **Fotos do produto:** escolher só a cor mostra a foto daquela cor; capa vale quando a lista de fotos está vazia; foto que falha tenta de novo.
- **Cupom (dinheiro):** aceita código com acento ou espaço (tenta como digitado primeiro); aviso de conexão lenta claro; lista de cupons relida depois de recusa; porcentagem com vírgula no painel. Nenhum cálculo de desconto mudou.
- **Carrinho guardado:** avisa quando um produto saiu da venda.
- **Visitante:** pedido consultado sem conta some em 60 min; lembrete do carrinho não fica atrás do convite de avisos.
- **Rastreio do pedido (autenticação por código):** colar com espaço ou traço funciona; a tela avisa quando o código foi bloqueado. Sem mudança de banco.
- **Prévia do link (todas as lojas):** descrição sem Markdown, preço com ponto de milhar.
- **Painel, Pedidos (dinheiro):** o cancelamento confere se o pedido mudou; a etiqueta some depois de cancelar.
- **Teclado do celular:** campos de preço abrem o teclado numérico; Enter no número do endereço vai ao complemento.
- **Textos:** plural no singular, "Não informado" no lugar de "N/A", termos únicos.

Cada lote é um commit (reverter um só é possível). Revisões: Opus em S (prévia do link, contrato do deploy), W (cupom), Y (código do rastreio) e Z (cancelamento); Sonnet em T, U, V, X, AA, AB. Revisão final Opus do conjunto no topo deste PR. Sem migration. Tetos: cliente 617 kB (mede 616,35), painel 509 kB (mede 508,79).

body:
本 PR 当前修订由 dsh-superagent 自动更新，使用 SummerSec 账号；不是用户本人发言。原始实现的自动生成说明保留于提交历史。

Refs #951。仅交付完成失败诊断，不改变完成协议、Job 终态或恢复权限，不关闭整单。

## 实现

- 实际 `executeReal` 的运行器异常、最终语义/runner 错误及本地缺 done 路径，在已有 normalized evidence stream 追加一条版本化 `run.completion_diagnostic`，再完成原归档/失败。正常接纳完成不写缺完成诊断。
- 缺 done 使用稳定 `AGENT_COMPLETION_UNOBSERVED`；不把缺响应推断为“Agent 故意跳过”，原运行器异常对象和现有错误分类不替换。
- 记录 Job/Attempt、最后已持久化工具名称/类别/游标、宿主拒绝码及受权限保护的 Job/evidence/原完成回执引用。没有工具参数、返回正文、summary、transcript 尾部或公开原始日志。
- 只读查询按同 Job/Attempt 的 source_event_id 统计可归属 Artifact 版本/Finding/Fact；历史 Attempt 隔离。不可归属 Artifact 单列；报告表没有 Attempt 身份，`reports=null`，不假造零报告。
- 回执按 Job/Attempt/snapshot digest/内核 receipt identity 校验，仅投影 key/revision/status/code。区分未观察到持久回执、拒绝、接纳待结算、done 事件持久化与未知；持久 done 事件不等于 Job 成功。读取/写入失败均明确 unavailable。

## 测试与文档

扩展已接线 `executor-real.test.ts`、`executor-real-terminal-race.test.ts`/fixture 及 `job-rerun.integration.test.ts`：真实 executor 失败保持和正常完成不误报；隔离 PostgreSQL 的两 Attempt 产出分离、原拒绝回执保留、新 accepted receipt 与 done 事件分别观察、Job/Attempt 不变。单元负例覆盖外来/损坏回执、读取/归档不可用和不回显敏感输入。原 test 脚本 `ci:unit:executor-real` 与 `ci:integration:recovery` 已在 Ready gate 调用，不增加未接线测试。

同步 DESIGN、生命周期专题、接口/运行时视图、现有 FR-CTRL-005 追溯行和索引；无 schema、采纳 ADR、OpenAPI 输入或新 UI/配置变更。

后续补修 `6b447934` 调整真实 REA 验收的诊断顺序：先确认已有完成运行的 Attempt，再检查 token 清理。未启动的 provision 失败会直接显示终态原因，不再混淆为令牌撤销失败；原运行、模型/Control token、沙箱与共享卷门禁全部保留。这不是 Egress 启动根因修复。

## 验证口径

- 已执行：静态阅读、调用链与 diff 审查、`git diff --check`。
- **未执行任何本机测试、构建、typecheck 或主动 LSP 检查。全部测试只使用 GitHub Actions。** 工具自动附带的旧/缺依赖诊断不作为候选验收。
- 当前已为 Ready；最终 head 的完整核心与全部适用专项仍以 Checks 和最新证据评论为准，不能用旧候选或 Draft 快检顶替。

## 安全与未交付范围

author: matheusgomessouza
body:
## What changed

The admin web app now has a request screen and a reset screen.

- Add `/forgot-password`. The form sends the email and shows one generic message.
- Add `/reset-password`. The page checks the token and asks for the new password.
- Add a "Forgot password?" link to the sign-in form.
- Add `ForgotPasswordSchema` and `ResetPasswordSchema`.
- Add the `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` header to `/reset-password`.
- Upgrade `eslint-config-next` from `0.2.4` to `14.2.5`, so `next lint` runs.
- Add the implementation plan under `docs/superpowers/plans`.

## Why

The admin panel had no way to recover a forgotten password. The reset link carries a secret token in the URL. The `no-referrer` header stops the token from leaking to other sites through the `Referer` header.

## How to test

1. Run `npm install`.
2. Start the API from the `feat/password-reset` branch of `community-cares-server`.
3. Run `npm run dev`.
4. Open `/forgot-password` and send a reset link.
5. Open the link from the email.
6. Type the new password twice and submit.
7. Sign in with the new password.
8. Open the same link again.

Expected result: The app goes to `/` after the reset, the new password works, and the same link shows "This link is invalid or expired."

## Risks

- This PR needs the backend PR. Merge the backend first.
- The sign-in form stores the access token in a JavaScript-readable cookie. This PR does not change it.
- The reset page needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_API`. A wrong value breaks both screens.

## Out of scope

- The token stays in the browser history until the redirect. This PR does not clear it.
- The reset page shows no success message. This PR redirects to the sign-in screen.
- The manual end-to-end test did not run. No PostgreSQL client and no Docker daemon were available.

body:
Closes #30（Claude C：モンスター図鑑の全敵データ対応）。仕様：`docs/ai-tasks/CLAUDE_C_COMPENDIUM_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

詳細は `docs/specs/monster-compendium/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md` にまとめました。

## 対象の敵（27種）
| 分類 | ID | 対象 |
|---|---|---|
| ステージボス（5） | `boss-1`〜`boss-5` | スライム／ゴブリン／オオカミ／ドラゴン／魔王（`enemyData`） |
| 隠しボス（1） | `hidden-boss` | 混沌の幻影（`hiddenBossData`） |
| 迷宮の通常敵（10） | `field:<ID>` | はぐれスライム、キノコもどき、森ゴブリン、ゴブリンの斥候、霧コウモリ、森オオカミ、火トカゲ、溶岩ゴーレム、魔王軍の騎士、さまよう亡霊 |
| FOE（5） | `field:<ID>` | 森の暴れ熊、ゴブリン親衛隊長、霧纏いの大鹿、灼熱のサラマンダー、黒騎士団長 |
| 亜種（6） | `variant:<variantId>` | 毒スライム、炎スライム、ゴブリンアーチャー、ゴブリンシャーマン、大コウモリ、大蜘蛛 |

対象の一覧は、既存データ（`enemyData`・`FIELD_ENEMIES`・`EXT_ENEMY_VARIANTS`）から実行時に作ります。能力値を図鑑用にコピーしていないので、敵データを追加・変更すれば図鑑にもそのまま反映されます。

## 遭遇・討伐の記録方式
- `monsterRecords[id] = {encountered, defeated, encounters, defeats}` に、表示名ではなく敵 ID を主キーにして記録します。
- **遭遇**：`beginStageCore()` で、既存の `registerEncounter()` の直後に記録します。中断した戦闘の再開では、遭遇回数を増やしません。
- **討伐**：`finishStage()`（勝利時だけ呼ばれる）の先頭で記録します。雑魚戦・FOE 戦も、`fieldFinishEncounter()` に分かれる前にここを通るので、**`field.js` は変更していません**。
- **二重登録の防止**：敵オブジェクトに印を付け、1回の戦闘で2回数えないようにしています。
- **表示**：未遭遇は「？？？？」。遭遇すると名前と遭遇・討伐回数が見えます。討伐すると、画像・能力値・属性・弱点・耐性・説明（主な行動と出現場所。既存データから自動で作成）が見えます。FOE と通常敵は別の分類で表示します。

## 既存の図鑑・隠しボス条件
- 名前キーの `compendium`、`registerEncounter`／`registerDefeat`、`hiddenBossUnlocked()`、実績 `compendium_80` は**変更していません**。ボス5種のカードも、従来どおり名前キーの記録で表示します。
- 隠しステージの文言「通常モンスター図鑑80%以上」は、迷宮の通常敵と紛らわしいため「ステージボス図鑑（5種）80%以上」に変えました（判定の内容は同じです）。
- 隠しボスの能力値が、図鑑（HP 4500 …）と戦闘（HP 7200 …）で食い違っていました。`data/enemies.js` の `hiddenBossData` に一本化し、戦闘の値はそのまま使っています。

## 旧セーブ互換性
- 新しいセーブ項目は `monsterRecords` だけです（`saveVersion` は変えていません）。
- `monsterRecords` がない旧セーブは、全敵を未遭遇として初期化するので、ロードエラーにはなりません。そのうえで、次の情報だけ引き継ぎます。
  - 旧 `compendium` に記録されたボスの遭遇・討伐
  - 迷宮の敵の遭遇回数（`field.enemyEncounters`）
- 迷宮の敵の討伐や、亜種の記録は、旧セーブに情報がないため未記録から始まります。

## 変更ファイル
- `monster-compendium.js`（新規）
- `script.js`：`// [COMPENDIUM]` の印を付けた呼び出しの追加、`renderCompendium` の委譲、`createEnemy` の隠しボスの参照先の変更。**編成処理と `level.js` には触れていません。**
- `data/enemies.js`：`hiddenBossData` を追加
- `css/02-screens-and-shell.css`：分類の見出しとラベル（最小限）
- `index.html`：新しいファイルの読み込み、`?v=20261106-19` への更新（PR #26・#27 が使う `-17`・`-18` と重ならない番号にしました）
- `docs/specs/monster-compendium/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md`（新規）

## 確認
仕様どおり、網羅的な検証は今回の対象外です。ヘッドレス Chromium で最低限の確認だけ行いました。
- JS エラーがないこと
- 対象が27種であること
- 雑魚戦・FOE 戦・亜種戦の記録
- 討伐が二重に数えられないこと
- セーブへの保存と、旧セーブからの引き継ぎ

**未確認**：実際に迷宮を歩いて遭遇した場合の流れ、隠しボス戦、スマホ幅の表示、実機、Claude A・B と GPT の変更との組み合わせ。

## 他の担当との関係
- `field.js`・`data/field-maps.js`（Claude B）と、編成・`level.js`（GPT）は編集していません。
- `script.js` には数行の追加と、セーブ項目 `monsterRecords` の追加があります。セーブ構造を整理するときは、この項目を残してください。

author: dpage
body:
## Summary

The Cluster scope in the create and schedule blackout dialogs was disabled for auto-detected clusters and their servers, because the client only recognised a database-backed cluster by a `cluster-{id}` topology ID; auto-detected clusters use transient IDs (`server-{id}`, `cluster-spock-{prefix}`) even though they have a `clusters` row.

- The topology response now carries a read-only `db_cluster_id` on each cluster that has a `clusters` row (`attachDBClusterIDs`, fed by the ID now returned from the cluster overrides query). The OpenAPI schema and `openapi.json` are updated.
- The client threads it through as `dbClusterId` on server and cluster selections; both dialogs now share `utils/blackoutScope.ts` to decide availability and the ID to send, so Cluster is offered for any cluster with a row and `cluster_id` is that row's ID.
- The navigator's cluster blackout indicator and the blackout banner for a selected cluster, or for a server in it, now match on that ID, so they light up for auto-detected clusters too (the banner never matched cluster blackouts before).
- A selected auto-detected cluster stays selected when a refresh changes its topology ID, because the re-sync falls back to matching on `db_cluster_id`; a selection with no match is kept, as before.
- `GetClusterTopology` now fails the request if the cluster overrides query fails, instead of carrying on with an empty map; that map now supplies `db_cluster_id`, so swallowing the error would silently remove the Cluster scope for every auto-detected cluster. The dismissed-key lookup on the same table already failed hard.
- Standalone servers still do not offer Cluster scope.

## Security

Authorisation and input handling are unchanged. The only API change is a new read-only response field. Blackout creation still goes through the existing endpoints and RBAC checks, and both the RBAC check (`GetConnectionIDsForCluster`) and the alerter's `IsBlackoutActive` already resolve cluster members through `connections.cluster_id`, so a cluster blackout created with the new ID suppresses alerts end to end with no alerter change.

## Other changes

- Adding a field took `TopologyCluster` to 128 bytes, which tripped gocritic `rangeValCopy` in several loops in `internal/database`; those loops now index rather than copy, with no change in behaviour.
- `scopeLabel` uses a per-scope lookup table rather than a branch chain, to stay under Codacy's complexity limit.
- Coverage floors: the server `COVERAGE_MIN` is pinned at the CI matrix minimum of 93.8% (PostgreSQL 14 and 15), and the client thresholds keep a little headroom for run-to-run variance; all remain above `main`.
- Coverage: new integration tests for the `GetClusterTopology` error paths and the overrides query, unit tests for `attachDBClusterIDs`, and real-render tests for `BlackoutDialog`, `BlackoutScheduleDialog` and the `ClusterNavigator` handlers, bringing each touched unit to 90% or more.

## Test plan

- Server: `go test -race -p=1 ./...` in `server/src`, golangci-lint clean.
- Client: lint, typecheck and `vitest run --coverage`.

Closes #809

* **New Features**
  * Auto-detected clusters now provide a database cluster ID for cluster-scoped actions. Blackout dialogs offer cluster scope for eligible auto-detected clusters; standalone servers remain ineligible.

* **Bug Fixes**

author: aamnanaveed
body:
This PR addresses Issue #939 regarding intermittent `HTTP 400 Bad Request` crashes when using `tax_name()` or `get_uid()` with large lists of species names.

As noted in the issue, these random crashes are likely caused by temporary rate-limiting or server overload on the NCBI E-utilities API. Previously, the `repeat_until_it_works` helper function only retried on complete connection failures (e.g., "Could not resolve host"), causing the package to crash immediately upon receiving an HTTP 400 or 500 error.

This PR updates `repeat_until_it_works` in `R/get_uid.R` to check the HTTP status code. If the API returns a `status_code >= 400`, the function now waits and retries (up to `max_tries`) instead of passing the error downstream and crashing the user's script.

I have:
- Modified the `repeat_until_it_works` function to handle HTTP 4xx/5xx errors gracefully.
- Locally tested `get_uid()` and `tax_name()` with single and multiple species to ensure the normal request flow remains completely unaffected.
- Verified that the package loads and functions correctly via `devtools::load_all()`.

This small change significantly improves the robustness of `taxize` for users processing large taxonomic datasets. Let me know if any adjustments are needed!

author: jalez
body:
Part of Jalez/kehikko#268

The person can now write skills for a kehikko in Kehikot. This module loads them into every session it starts on that kehikko.

- `hostPlace` reads `kehikkoSkills` from the host's answer (`kehikkoSkillsOf`, protocol `kehikkoSkillsSchema`).
- A session start asks the host once for its doors and the kehikko's skills (`startPlace` in live.ts). This covers both the background start and the attached start.
- `sessionPlugin` puts each kehikko skill into the session's plugin before any module's skill, with the text exactly as the host handed it. A module skill with the same name is left out with one log line, because the person's skill wins. Each kehikko skill is added to `held-skills.json`, so the notes never claim one the session lacks.
- context.ts passes `kehikkoSkills` to the protocol's `sessionNotes`, which lists them at the start under "Skills of this kehikko…". The told record keeps each skill's mark.
- **Running sessions:** this module does not hot-reload the plugin. A skill added or changed while a session runs is told at its next prompt; an added one is marked as not loaded and pointed to `kehikko_skills` on the host's door to read it. It loads as a skill when the session starts again.

## Tests

- test/live.test.ts: a session started with a stand-in pty and a stand-in host gets the kehikko's skill in its plugin and in its held list. Its start notes list the skill. A skill added later is told at the next prompt as not loaded, with `kehikko_skills`.
- test/session-skills.test.ts: the plugin takes kehikko skills as handed, leaves out one that does not parse, and the person's name wins over a module's skill.

Full suite, queued from inside the worktree: 737 pass, 0 fail. tsc is clean.

Version 1.28.0, with notes in notes/1.28.0.md.

**Protocol pin:** this PR pins protocol branch commit `4cb91f1` (Jalez/kehikko-protocol#104). The pin must become tag `v2.53.0` before merge. Release after the host that answers `kehikkoSkills`. An older host leaves the field out, and this module then loads and says nothing about kehikko skills.

author: marcosanti
body:
A successful `rmdir` on a CAPIO directory returned 1 instead of 0. The server answers an rmdir request with `delete_from_files_location`'s code: 1 when it removed the directory, 2 when it had none. `capio_rmdir` turned 2 into ENOENT but passed any other answer through as the syscall's result.

`unlinkat(..., AT_REMOVEDIR)` sends the same request, but `capio_unlink_abs` only treated -1 as a failure. It returned 1 on success, and 2 for a missing directory, instead of -1 with ENOENT.

Both now return 0 on success and fail with ENOENT for a missing directory. An excluded path is still handed to the kernel.

| change | where |
|---|---|
| map the server's answer to 0 or ENOENT | `posix/handlers/mkdir.hpp` (`capio_rmdir`), `posix/handlers/unlink.hpp` (`capio_unlink_abs`) |
| tests that check the returned values, which the existing ones did not (they only checked `!= -1`) | `tests/unit/syscall/src/directory.cpp` |

#269's `TestDirectoryEntriesHaveTheirOwnType` fails on this (`rmdir` returns 1 at `listing.cpp:48`), which stops its CI run. This PR is meant to be merged before #269.

body:
## Why this change is needed

The public source still identified itself as r7 while enhanced r8 monitoring lived in a separate private source tree and subsequent configuration work accumulated separately. This candidate brings those runtime changes together under the distinct **AoTT-8311-v2r9** identity so they can be built and qualified as one firmware revision.

## What this candidate includes

- An **89-file runtime overlay** combining optional UDP/TCP syslog, protected external metrics, durable monitoring restoration and HTTPS private-key permission status.
- Seven manual administrator Configuration readback panels covering all **54 existing GUI fields**, including redacted identity and credential status. Stored/configured evidence remains distinct from independently observed runtime effects.
- The enhanced r8 collector restrictions and credential format, with no credential reset caused by the r9 display-version change.
- Mandatory runtime integrity records for the 15 new readback files, while retaining the inherited monitoring and vendor S11/S12 boot-link requirements.
- Current source development and deterministic concurrency tests, including the latest configuration transaction work. Unfinished history, certificate, firewall and native VLAN write adapters remain outside the installed overlay.
- Vendor boot-restoration scenarios using private configuration/staging directories and genuine vendor MIPS UCI, without mount namespaces or chroot privileges.
- Portable preservation tests using exact, hash-pinned vendor CSS, sysctl, syslog and pre-monitoring r7 initializer references when the execution-only runtime omits those files. Complete supplied references remain preferred, assertions remain in place, and the HTTPS adapter fixture uses an explicit private OpenSSL configuration.

**The final combined regression passed all 1,304 tests, with zero failures, errors or skips.**

| Acceptance group | Passed | Failures | Errors | Skips |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Configuration | 335 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Integration | 969 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The run includes **131 real Chromium browser cases**, genuine vendor-MIPS execution and the isolated monitoring, HTTPS and boot-restoration checks. The independent verifier confirmed every expected test ID exactly once in the expected order, no missing or unexpected cases, controller exit 0 and no remaining service processes. It rehashed all **428 source files**. Elapsed time was **466.972 seconds**.

- Public source commit: `6865d9bf347fc3ac96329c6e1bd51374cc4441e9`.
- Tested local commit: `ed227423ba25e8768f7994c5f5490693f706ee50`.

- Source-manifest, disclosure and whitespace checks passed. Test portability fixes leave the **89-file runtime overlay and its manifest unchanged**.

The final independent image audit verified all **1,411 payload files**, all **89 overlay files** and **184 runtime integrity records**, and passed **7 of 7 genuine vendor-MIPS Lua cases**. Kernel and bootcore retain their qualified identities. Firmware binaries and operator data remain private.

author: 0xiamthebest
body:
## Summary

Fixes from an end-to-end smoke test of every module (`--app` mode and the full 31-module pipeline) run inside the Docker image against a throwaway local lab target seeded with known artifacts. After these changes, both modes exit 0, every planted artifact is discovered, and every remaining warning is accurate.

### Hangs / silently empty output
- **asn_discovery:** without a valid PDCP key, asnmap prints an interactive `Enter PDCP API Key` prompt on stdout and reads stdin. Unattended, the prompt text was written into `asn_ip_ranges.txt` and CloudRecon hung indefinitely on it. Interactively (`docker run -it`), the prompt blocked the run. asnmap now gets no stdin, output is filtered to CIDRs, and a warning is recorded.
- **xnLinkFinder:** the tool ignores `-i` whenever stdin isn't a TTY, so every unattended run produced empty xnLinkFinder output, which in turn starved `extract_params`. Added a `run_xnlinkfinder` helper that passes the input on stdin, and used it at all 3 call sites.
- **subdomain_enum:** the supplied domain is now always included in `subdomains.txt`. Previously it was only probed if a passive source returned it, so with no passive hits the entire web chain ran on empty input.
- **extract_inline_scripts:** now recurses into katana's per-host response store. It previously never saw a crawled page.
- **`--dry-run`:** no longer clears checkpoints when combined with `--replay-from` or `--fresh`.

### Tool error text ending up in result files
- **subdomain_enum:** `_clean_hostnames` skipped the replace when *no* line was valid, so error strings such as `invalid API key` stayed in `subdomains.txt`.
- **ip_discovery:** godigger error lines were saved as IPs. Only IP-address lines are kept now.
- **shodan_search / credential_intel:** a bad key (HTML 401, `{"error": ...}`) looked identical to "no results". Each now records a warning with the reason.

### Incorrect summary / output
- **run_summary:** read the uniq-URL files from the wrong directory (counts were always 0), counted trufflehog banner lines as findings, and reported itself as `in_progress`.
- **wordpress_scan:** removes sites WPScan identifies as not WordPress, so the seeded `--app` target is no longer reported as a WordPress site. wpscan and graphql-cop now also run with `</dev/null` inside `while read` loops.
- **api_docs_probe:** saved specs no longer get a doubled extension (`*.json.json`).

body:
Summary:
The FIPS module version was not actually pinned. bcpkix-fips and bctls-fips depend on
bcutil-fips by version range, and bcutil-fips depends on bc-fips by range, so a plain
declaration loses to the range: build.sbt declared bc-fips 2.1.0 while the resolved classpath
carried bc-fips 2.1.3. Verified with Compile/dependencyClasspathAsJars before this change. The
version would have kept climbing on its own with each BouncyCastle release.

That matters here because bc-fips is the FIPS 140-3 validated module itself, and 2.1.3 carries
no validation. The last certified build is 2.1.1, CMVP certificate #4943, validated 17 Jan 2025,
sunset 16 Jan 2027. The one before it is #4743 for 2.0.0, validated 21 Oct 2024, sunset 28 Jul
2029. A newer BC-FJA submission is on the CMVP modules-in-process list at "Review (9/4/2026)"
but has no certificate yet.

So bc-fips moves 2.1.0 -> 2.1.1: the newest build with a certificate, rather than the newest
build. The companions are outside the validated boundary and go to latest:

  bc-fips      2.1.0    -> 2.1.1     (CMVP #4943)
  bcutil-fips  (implicit, 2.1.7) -> 2.1.7 declared
  bcpkix-fips  2.1.9    -> 2.1.12
  bctls-fips   2.1.20   -> 2.1.24

All four are declared, and the two reachable through a range - bc-fips and bcutil-fips - also
get dependencyOverrides, which is what actually fixes them; the declaration alone still resolved
2.1.3. Their versions live in vals so the declaration and the override cannot drift apart.

Worth checking separately: released builds that claim FIPS validation may have shipped 2.1.2 or
2.1.3 through this same range.

If the policy is longest-lived validation rather than newest certified, 2.0.0 (#4743) runs three
years longer than 2.1.1 and this pin is a one-line change.

Original commit: a6c03b2dd871dc40a60d315b6e4301cfe8c2875c / #35027

Test Plan:
sbt "show Compile/dependencyClasspathAsJars" - resolves bc-fips 2.1.1, bcutil-fips 2.1.7,
bcpkix-fips 2.1.12, bctls-fips 2.1.24. Before the change the same command showed bc-fips 2.1.3.

sbt "testOnly com.yugabyte.yw.common.certmgmt.CertificateHelperTest
  com.yugabyte.yw.common.certmgmt.VaultPKITest
  com.yugabyte.yw.common.certmgmt.EncryptionInTransitUtilTest
  com.yugabyte.yw.controllers.CertificateControllerTest
  com.yugabyte.yw.controllers.JWTVerifierTest"

These cover the paths that go through the provider: CertificateHelper generates and signs with
BouncyCastleFipsProvider, and MainModule registers it plus the JSSE provider from bctls-fips.

Not covered here: an approved-only run (yb.fips.enabled / org.bouncycastle.fips.approved_only)
against a real FIPS deployment.

Reviewers: anijhawan, nsingh, dshubin

Reviewed By: nsingh

Subscribers: yugaware

Differential Revision: https://phorge.dev.yugabyte.com/D58021

- `managed/build.sbt` (version vals): kept the branch's `flywayVersion` and added `bouncyCastleFipsVersion` / `bouncyCastleUtilFipsVersion` next to it.
- `managed/build.sbt` (`dependencyOverrides` block): context-only conflict with the `yb-client` / `ybc-client` lines, which differ between master and this branch. Kept this branch's client versions and added the two overrides above them.

author: antontranelis
body:
## shared-connect 0.1 on registry Trust Tasks

The shared connection ceremony across apps, as agreed with Consensual (Geb, NAOMS) and Keyring this week: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1034 (revision of 5 November) and trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#86 (Brendan Miller, 4 and 6 November). Two registry tasks (`vrc/relationships/propose/0.1`, `vrc/relationships/issue/0.1`), one ceremony definition, a VTI trigger link whose `_from` is a per-encounter `did:peer:2` carrying the inviter's relays. The responder proposes (its challenge is the propose `id` and the `threadId`); `ceremony.enactment` is the link's `_id` on every step. Draft: the registry entries are proposed, not registered. The encounter ceremony is unchanged.

### Library (`lib/src/shared-connect.ts`, exported as the namespace `sharedConnect`)

- `peer2Of` / `parsePeer2`: did:peer:2 numalgo 2, local resolution, keys listed under `authentication`/`assertionMethod` (`#key-1`) and `keyAgreement` (`#key-2`), both TSP service spellings read (`TSPTransport` with a string, `tsp` with `{uri}`).
- `sharedConnectLink` / `readSharedConnectLink`: the link with `_from`, `_id`, `_exp`, `_type` and the proposed `_label` (display only; dropped, not truncated, when too long or carrying control/bidi/zero-width characters). Checks in the order of VTI-LNK-020 as far as they apply.
- `propose` / `accept` / `credential` / `issue` / `receipt`: the five documents and the receipts. Step proofs under `authentication` by the issuer's `#key-1`; credentials by the pairwise `did:key` under `assertionMethod`, `@context` repeated in the proof. Document ids are caller-supplied (the Entropy port rule).
- `checkPropose` / `checkAccept` / `checkIssue`: what each receiving side refuses, with a typed reason.
- `binding`: RLTP-ENC-5330 under the ceremony URI. `backCodeOf` / `proposeFromBackCode`: the offline path, the propose in reconstruction form (466 characters in the vector).

### Vectors

- `vectors/shared-connect.json` (new): one enactment from fixed seeds; link 380 characters with two relays and a label. Verified by `lib/test/shared-connect-vector.test.mjs`, reproduced by `scripts/gen-shared-connect-vector.mjs --check` (in `check:generators:lib`).
- `vectors/shared-connect-binding.json`: a row for the `shared-connect/0.1` ceremony URI (Naonatus, #1034).

### Binding (dev only, `RLTP_LIVE_MEDIATOR=1`)

`shared-connect-invite.mjs` (our inviter), `shared-connect-respond.mjs` (our scanner side), `shared-connect-loopback.mjs` (both sides over real TSP frames, no network). Documents travel as TSP 1.0 `direct` messages inside the registry's TSP binding envelope. **Live run on 6 November against `mediator.web-of-trust.de`: login under two never-seen `did:peer:2`, XRFI answered with XRFA, five documents and two receipts, complete in six seconds; no mediator change needed.** The binding lockfile now pins vti-didcomm-js 0.13.0 and vti-tsp-js 0.4.0, which the README named already.

### Checks

`lib`: build, 929 tests green (8 new); `node scripts/validate.mjs`; `conformance/runner.mjs` (1910 claims); both simulator freezes refrozen and identical; `check-code-samples`; both generators in `--check` mode.

### For review

- The reconstruction rule of the back-code (`backCodeOf` / `proposeFromBackCode`): what the inviter rebuilds from its own state, and that a propose with `expiresAt` is refused as a back-code.
- `readSharedConnectLink`: the `_type` comparison (path form on the link's own host, absolute otherwise) and the `_label` rules.
- `checkIssue`: profile checks apply only to members that are present, so credentials of other profiles (Consensual's `binding`, Keyring's) pass the envelope checks.

Normative paths (`vectors/`) are touched: human merge.

author: wcpos-mini[bot]
body:
## What

Fixes the two Codex threads from the 11:36 re-review of the promote PR (#69). It lands on `next` first, then `next` merges into `promote/2.0` and the draft is rebuilt.

**Device refund (thread 4492015777).** #73 fixed an unanswered refund on the cloud provider only. The Bluetooth device provider still handed back whatever the client returned, and SumUp's own `call()` flattened a throw first, so a timed-out refund could withdraw its allocation while SumUp may have paid it. That was my miss on #73. `SumUp_Device_Provider::refund()` now reads the answer the same way:

- `true`: succeeded.
- SumUp's own 4xx (`Refund_Client::refused()`): the refusal, returned as is.
- A throw, a timeout, a 5xx, anything else: `sumup_refund_unanswered`, `indeterminate => true`, status 502. Free's ledger strands that and keeps the reservation.

The two providers now share `Refund_Client::refused()` and `UNANSWERED_MESSAGE`.

**Reader grace (thread 4492015787).** `reader_finished()` read an idle reader as finished as soon as its activity was newer than the checkout start. With no terminate delivery reported, the grace was counted from the checkout's age, so a tap that had only just ended could read as abandoned. The reader's last activity must now be older than `TERMINATE_GRACE_SECONDS` (10 s) unless a terminate delivery was reported.

The conformance fake's `expired` scenario ages the reader's activity as well as the checkout marker, because the sweep now reads it.

Part of wcpos/roadmap#546. Thread replies go on #69 after this merges and folds.

## Disclosures

- **#73 missed this path.** The same defect sat in the device provider when I called the refund fix done.
- **The grace does not cover a listing slower than 10 s** after the reader's last activity. A SumUp transaction that takes longer than that to appear can still be missed by this check.
- **`last_activity` behaviour is not proved live.** If SumUp refreshes it while the reader sits idle, the leg stays pending until its deadline. That is the safe direction: no false cancel, only a slower one.
- **The `$grace - 1` test cases** depend on a one-second boundary, only if a tick falls between the set-up and the read. Negligible, not impossible.
- **`includes/Services/*.php` sit outside the phpcs command CI runs.** I ran phpcs on `RefundClient.php` by name; CI will not. Unchanged here.

author: hk9890
body:
## Summary

`challenge:grill` now writes every question for a **cold reader**: a user who comes back from other sessions and remembers none of this one. Before this change, every question went through `AskUserQuestion`, whose 12-character header and one-line options left no room for background. Users followed the recommendation without knowing why.

- A question is **simple** when a cold reader can decide it from the picker alone and its effect stays inside what is being grilled. Simple questions go through `AskUserQuestion`. Every option says what it commits us to, and the recommended one adds why, what it costs, and what would change the agent's mind.
- Every other question is **complex** and goes out as prose:

  ```
  **Q<n>: <the decision, in one line>**
  <background: the facts it rests on, and the decisions that hang on it>
  - **<option>**: what it commits us to, what it costs, what it rules out later
  **Recommendation: <one option's label>.** Why, what it costs us, what would change your mind.
  ```
- Until the user confirms, each message holds only questions. Facts go inside the question that rests on them, each with its source.
- A request for more ("why", "explain", "let's discuss") is not an answer: the agent asks the same question again with more background. "Your call" settles a question on the recommendation. The user ends the discussion.
- A question about the user's own goal is always prose and ends on a **Best read** line: the agent's guess, with its source, and what each answer would change.
- The agent recomputes what to ask after each answer, so a later question can use the latest decision.

`NOTICE.md` now says the prose shape grows from upstream's chat-prose template, and that the cold-reader rules are locally authored.

## Evidence

- **Gate:** `bash tests/run-all.sh`: passed, 27 suites, 0 failed, at `e77c1b1`.
- **Gate:** `mise run check-consistency`: passed, all checks, at `e77c1b1`.
- **Gate:** `claude plugin validate plugins/challenge`: passed at `e77c1b1`. `plugin-dev:plugin-validator` on `challenge` at `936d511`: 0 errors, 1 warning (no icon). Later commits change only `SKILL.md` text.
- **Gate:** Docs-Route-Check and Shell-Lint: skipped, because no doc or shell script changed.
- **Driven:** A/B test, four rounds. Each round ran the first round of the old and the new skill headless on 5 real topics from this repo (`claude -p --plugin-dir <old|new> "/challenge:grill <topic>"`). Blind cold-reader judges scored each pair on 6 criteria, 1 to 5. `AskUserQuestion` is not available headless, so both variants printed the picker JSON instead.

  | Round | New skill | Old skill | Topics won by new |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 (`e69c274`) | 130 | 80 | 5 of 5 |
  | 2 (`4b7f799`) | 117 | 86 | 4 of 5 (the loss was a harness defect: only the last message was judged) |
  | 3 (`ad4ebc2`) | 117 | 89 | 5 of 5 |
  | 4 (`d466e3b`) | 131 | 84 | 4 of 5 |
  | 5 (`e77c1b1`) | 129 | 85 | 5 of 5 |

  The largest gains are "why the recommendation wins" (20 against 13 in round 5) and "what it costs" (21 against 11). In round 5 no goal question used the picker. After each round, an auditor checked the new outputs against the skill's own rules, and its findings went into the next commit.
- **Driven:** round 4 includes the tasks design-page topic: the run opened with the question, and the goal question carried a best read with its source. One earlier run at `732e3e7` sent two short progress notes before the first question; the model narrates between tool calls, and the skill text does not fully stop it.
- **Known gaps from the round 5 audit:** a raw sub-agent report can still reach the user as its own message; some options hide a second choice; some goal options give no cost.
- **Not driven:** a live multi-turn session. The rule that a request for more is not an answer needs a real user. Check it in use.
- **Review:** `project-review-change --fix`: 3 fixes applied (background inside the re-ask, positive rules for message content, one home for the source rule), 3 open questions answered by the user (recompute after each answer, goal questions always in prose with a Best read line, premise rule moved to the question-writing section); suggested rule additions: none; `code-review xhigh`: 13 applied in a consolidated rewrite (one scoped message rule, one simple-question test, picker before prose, a commitment on the recommended option, options as real choices, prose where the picker is missing, delegation settles on the recommendation, re-ask only the questions a report changes, short headers allowed, positive phrasing, no duplicates, no patch sediment), 2 answered by the user as above (round pacing, the best-read format), through `e77c1b1c21b5c6ab51e19b321fdc5c8d880ec7de`

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** consumers

Every `/challenge:grill` user gets longer prose questions for hard decisions, and fewer pickers.

## Summary

This plan is slice S5 of the trusted plan executor (Decision 238). Today `terraform-github-plan.yml` runs from the PR's own workflow text, under the planner's PR session, with the plan App key in a repository secret. After this plan, main's copy runs on `pull_request_target` in `tf-trusted-plan`, the way S3 did for terraform/personal:
- the PR's terraform/github files are screened before any credential exists, and main.tf and the lockfile always come from main;

author: konradhe14
body:
Closes #1564

**Gate PR: the owner merges.** It changes the `Makefile` and `.claude/settings.json`. `gh api` stays outside the allow list.

## What and why

US-DEV-13, US-DEV-02. Fewer permission dialogs, as the owner decided on 2026-11-06. Agents used `gh api` for PR and issue reads because `gh pr view` and `gh issue view` spend the shared GraphQL budget, and a rule cannot tell a `gh api` read from a write. Four plain targets replace it: `make pr-state`, `make issue-read`, `make pr-text`, `make issue-comment` (`app/tools/workflow/actions/issue/rest-cli.mjs`, REST only). Seven allow rules cover them and `grep`, `rg` and `sed -n`.

## For the reviewer

- **The allow rules are wider than "read only".** A prefix rule cannot express that. `Bash(sed -n:*)` also matches `sed -n -i …` and `sed -n '1w file'`, which write. `Bash(rg:*)` also matches `rg --pre <command>`, which runs a program. This PR adds no deny rules for them; the owner decides. Deny rules for those forms would catch the common spellings, not all of them.
- **`make pr-text` and `make issue-comment` write without a dialog once this is merged,** like `make pr` already does.
- **User input never enters a recipe.** The first version put `TITLE`, `PR` and `BODY` in the recipe text, so a backtick in a title ran as a command, on a target going on the allow list. The Makefile now exports them raw (`export REST_TITLE := $(value TITLE)`), and `rest-cli.mjs` reads only the environment. Newlines and `#` in values are not tested.
- **The make-level tests run through `bash -c`,** the idiom of `check-ci-drift.test.mjs`. Spawning `make` directly fails knip as an unlisted binary, and adding an exception would have loosened a gate.
- `pagedKey` of `ci-wait.mjs` is now exported, so it is reused. The module sits in `actions/issue` because that was the only directory with a free unit.

## Test evidence

- Live on GitHub, by the orchestrator: `make pr-state` and `make issue-read` return the real data; `make issue-read` on a PR number refuses and names `make pr-state`; a missing PR fails with a non-zero exit. This text was written with `make pr-text`, after a title with a backtick command reached GitHub unchanged and ran nothing.
- `rest-cli.test.mjs`: 19 of 19 pass with a fake `gh`, reported by the implementer. Against the old recipes, rebuilt in a scratch copy, the three make-level tests fail for the right reason.
- `make gates`: 24 steps, 0 failed, no knip exception, also in the pre-push hook.
- Read by the orchestrator: `rest-cli.mjs` (first version, before the environment change), the Makefile and settings diffs. The test file was not read in full.
- Not run: `make ci`, e2e. The rules themselves can only be seen working once the sessions have this merged.

## Definition of Done (FR-QG-10)

- [x] Story and acceptance criteria exist; the code traces back to a criterion
- [x] Tests derived from the criteria (happy path, edge cases, error cases, security paths) with the story ID in the name
- [x] Errors handled (stable `error_code`), nothing swallowed silently (P-10)
- [x] Input validated, no secrets in code
- [x] Module boundaries respected, no magic strings
- [ ] View, flow or control changed? Not applicable: no UI change
- [ ] `feat:`/`fix:` PR: not applicable, this is `chore:`
- [ ] Spec status and counters in `docs/specs/product/readme.md` updated in this PR: not applicable, no status changes
- [x] New routes and operations named: the targets are in `docs/guides/reference/app.md` and spec 19
- [ ] `make ci` green locally: not run, see above

## AI involvement

Written by a Claude Haiku implementer. Claude Opus orchestrated, found the shell injection in review, sent it back twice, ran the live checks and wrote this text. No human has reviewed it yet.

- [x] No gate, threshold or exception list was loosened, or the justification is above: the allow list grows on the owner's decision

body:
Fixes DOTOBRD-636

## Proposed Changes

* In the entrepreneur flow, the create-site step ignores the domain and site URL stored in the onboard store, so the server generates the trial site's address.

## Why are these changes being made?

* The onboard store keeps the selected domain in localStorage. A free subdomain picked in an earlier signup reaches the entrepreneur flow's site creation and is sent as the exact blog name, which fails with `blog_name_exists: Sorry, that site already exists!`.
* The flow only clears the store when the URL has no step, so entering on a localized URL (`/setup/entrepreneur/es`) or a step URL keeps the old domain. The flow never asks for a domain, so it should not use one.

## Testing Instructions

* Go to `/setup/onboarding`, pick the free `.wordpress.com` subdomain and the free plan, and let the site finish provisioning.
* In the same browser, go to `/setup/entrepreneur/es`, choose "A new store for myself" and start the Commerce trial.
* Before: "We've hit a snag" with `blog_name_exists`.
* After: the trial store is created with a new address.

## Pre-merge Checklist

- [ ] Has the general commit checklist been followed? (PCYsg-hS-p2)
- [ ] [Have you written new tests](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/docs/testing/index.md) for your changes?
- [ ] Have you tested the feature in Simple (P9HQHe-k8-p2), Atomic (P9HQHe-jW-p2), and self-hosted Jetpack sites (PCYsg-g6b-p2)?
- [ ] Have you checked for TypeScript, React or other console errors?
- [ ] For UI changes, have you tested the affected components in [dark mode](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/docs/dark-mode.md)?
- [ ] Have you tested accessibility for your changes? Ensure the feature remains usable with various user agents (e.g., browsers), interfaces (e.g., keyboard navigation), and assistive technologies (e.g., screen readers) (PCYsg-S3g-p2).
- [ ] Have you used memoizing on expensive computations? More info in [Memoizing with create-selector](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/packages/state-utils/src/create-selector/README.md) and [Using memoizing selectors](https://react-redux.js.org/api/hooks#using-memoizing-selectors) and [Our Approach to Data](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/docs/our-approach-to-data.md)
- [ ] Have we added the "[Status] String Freeze" label as soon as any new strings were ready for translation (p4TIVU-5Jq-p2)?
    - [ ] For UI changes, have we tested the change in various languages (for example, ES, PT, FR, or DE)? The length of text and words vary significantly between languages. 
- [ ] For changes affecting Jetpack: Have we added the "[Status] Needs Privacy Updates" label if this pull request changes what data or activity we track or use (p4TIVU-aUh-p2)?

author: vladastos
body:
Stacked on #561 (base `docs/rfc-0219-copy-qualifier`); retarget to `main` after it merges.

Records the language owner's decision of 2026-11-06: **a type's class is declared and checked against its fields, never inferred.**

- `linear` is the must-call spelling and a declared class keyword (struct, enum, named record, closure prefix, function type). A struct, record, enum or closure that holds a linear value must itself be declared `linear`; the error suggests the keyword. `linear` may also be written with no linear field (a capability token, a must-call callback). `linear` implies `once`; `copy` and `linear` are mutually exclusive.
- **No `affine` keyword.** Affine is the default and is never written; `Copy` and `Linear` are declared only in a declaration, so nothing can change a type's class elsewhere.
- Generic types: the keyword states a capability (`linear struct Pair<T>` is linear exactly when a field is; without it, parameters must satisfy `Discard`). Types with no declaration site (tuples, arrays, anonymous records) are linear when a component is, by a compiler rule.
- `Linear` becomes a `declared` aspect: no structural `auto` derivation, no `!Linear` opt-out, no `extend X: Linear {}`.

Amended: RFC-0089 (sections 1, 2, 2.1, open questions), RFC-0194 (explicit `linear`, must-call spelling resolved), RFC-0207 section 3, RFC-0206, RFC-0212 (`Linear` leaves the `auto` list), RFC-0219 (question 4 resolved), RFC-0215 and RFC-0162 notes, the spec text for ownership classes, the overview report and INDEX. `rfc.py check`: no problems.

author: blankmeadow
body:
## Why
In the Doris end-to-end run (main 78a1986), the first submit was rejected with `SQL_NOT_READ_ONLY` for a query dataset using `DATEDIFF`. `DATEDIFF` only reads; it was missing from the whitelist in `services/dataset_sql.py`, and every unknown construct was reported as a write, which misleads the agent and cost one of three repair rounds.

## What
- Allow `DateDiff`, `TimestampDiff`, `DatetimeDiff` (and their unit argument, e.g. `TIMESTAMPDIFF(DAY, …)`).
- Writes and DDL inside a query (Insert/Update/Delete/Merge/Create/Drop/Alter/Command) keep `SQL_NOT_READ_ONLY`; any other unknown construct is `SQL_UNSUPPORTED` with a message saying it is not supported yet.

## Tests
- New `tests/test_dataset_sql_functions.py` (Doris/MySQL DATEDIFF, TIMESTAMPDIFF, unknown function → SQL_UNSUPPORTED, DELETE → SQL_NOT_READ_ONLY).
- `apps/api`: 1286 passed, 18 skipped; ruff 15 = main baseline.

author: uglygameface
body:
Polymarket's price is the default forecast for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP at 5m, 15m and 60m. A model can supply a qualified call or ping only after passing the same prospective, source-specific contest as every other model. The main menu and persistent DM panel now share the same renderer and qualification result.

The earlier implementation compared pooled forecasts with older opening quotes, reran an iid test on rolling data, and left a separate early-call notification path active. This change replaces those paths with one immutable checkpoint and one qualification authority.

- All available contestants use the first verified book at 20% elapsed (20-second capture window). One transaction freezes contract/condition identity, source/payoff, normalized midpoint benchmark, actual ten-share ask-depth costs with the market's published fee schedule, probabilities and artifact hashes. WAIT/missing candidates cannot be replaced with a later favorable entry. Existing research ledgers remain preserved and cannot qualify as new contest evidence.
- Qualification uses disjoint 28-day prospective batches, enrollment before batch start, at least 300 contracts, 21 UTC days, 80% expected-window/cost coverage and 150 predetermined paper entries. Daily Newey-West Brier and stressed net-return tests must both pass; Holm covers models, all 12 markets and settlement scopes, with summable alpha spending across batches. These tests depend on statistical assumptions and do not guarantee future profit.
- Reviewed challengers include d2 GBM/EWMA, an empirical Merton jump mixture and queue-weighted microprice. Chainlink/USD contracts use a fresh median from at least three of Coinbase, Bitstamp, Gemini and Bitfinex, with a published strike preferred over a labeled opening-price proxy. TWAP distribution calculations are explicitly approximations.
- Hourly Binance contracts instead require Binance **spot/USDT** prices, closed minute bars and the exact hourly opening value. USD medians, futures and a forming hourly close cannot substitute. Provider denial enters cooldown and leaves the formula absent while other contestants continue.
- Frozen pooled artifacts remain available through nightly retraining (bounded current/previous batch rosters). Formula-only rounds feed the existing authoritative settlement worker. The selected qualifying model can serve; old early-call/formula unlock modules and the unused Coinbase-only reader are retired.

Without a winner the card says **“No model beats Polymarket's price here.”** Every prediction ping additionally requires the exact condition/source, a fresh book, known current costs and sufficient estimated edge after stress. No model has been manually promoted and no orders, wallets or credentials are introduced.

Validation:
- Full local regression evidence: **1,924 passed, 120 skipped**; subsequent shared-menu regressions **40 passed**.
- Ruff, Python 3.11 syntax, final diff/reference checks pass.
- Final commit PostgreSQL 16/full CI: **2,043 passed, 1 skipped**, plus 43 source/causality/LLM repair checks. [Final commit checks](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/commit/7526999d4f3de4700c0dc6a959d2640dcfcff2f3/checks) are authoritative for the completed patch.
- Read-only live probes verified actual Polymarket v1 fee metadata and available CLOB bid/depth costs, three-source quorum for all four USD coins, and a complete BTC four-source/opening-proxy snapshot. Binance spot was denied on this runner and correctly abstained; this is not Discloud runtime proof.
- Production worker behavior and genuinely new completed forward batches remain separate acceptance requirements. Issues #6, #138, #151 and #299 stay open.

Policy, assumptions and primary sources: [docs/POLYMARKET_MODEL_CONTEST.md](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/blob/7526999d4f3de4700c0dc6a959d2640dcfcff2f3/docs/POLYMARKET_MODEL_CONTEST.md).

Post-release receipts on main `3299bf5f6cd1e71ae82fc24442d840b4ea08fef8`:
- [Main CI](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/actions/runs/42247960984), [Discloud release](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/actions/runs/42248507736), [host learning receipt](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/actions/runs/42248636505) and [persisted LFM3 receipt](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/actions/runs/42248636460) passed. The host reported fresh forecasts and learning; the LFM3 record advanced 89→90 with a valid evidence hash. These receipts do not prove the new models' predictive edge.
- The scheduled LFM3 edge audit initially returned `production_audit_unavailable`. One read-only rerun after the fresh host receipts [completed successfully](https://github.com/UglyGameFace/RivaL/actions/runs/42248527558); after-cost edge remains unverified.
- The existing verified retirement workflow retired `feat/model-league`; its remote ref now returns 404. Local merged content was independently matched before local retirement; the workspace is clean on main.
- No model was promoted. The new contest still requires its own completed prospective batches.

author: skifahrer
body:
#81 showed no build. A pull request opened by the workflow's own token starts no workflows, so `upstream` dispatches `terrain-ios` itself, but only when the head has no `terrain-ios` status. #81's head `157e1fe` already had a pass from 2026-11-05, earned merged into master `d8ab262`. Master has since moved (to `725e6d0`, with #80's symbol heights), and nothing built #81 on it.

- `terrain-ios`: a dispatched pull request's status now names the master it was merged into, e.g. "Build and simulator tests: success, merged into master 725e6d0". Push and pull-request runs read as before.
- `upstream`: each night it asks for a run again when the head's status names another master or none, as well as when there's no status or a pending one with no run left. So an upstream pull request is tested again after master moves, at most once a night.

I started a run for #81 on today's master by hand: https://github.com/skifahrer/maplibre-native/actions/runs/42235202795

Checked here: both files load as YAML, every `run:` block passes `bash -n`, and the jq expression reads the old status (no master), the new one, and none. Not run: the workflows themselves. They act on master, so the next nightly `upstream` after this merges is their first run. Its log says "testing #N at … on master …".

body:
**Symptom.** With `StreamTarget` in chunked mode, finalizing a file whose data comes as one big contiguous write fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when the chunk size is small. For example, an in-memory fast start MP4 (`fastStart: 'in-memory'` writes the whole file at the end) of about 20 MB with `{ chunked: true, chunkSize: 1024 }` throws from `finalize()`. The threshold depends on the stack left at that point: in a busier call stack, a 5 MB file already failed. Same on bug-fix-mania. Realism: plausible but unusual — a chunked stream target with a small chunk size (e.g. for uploads) and a large in-memory MP4 or a big fragment; at the 16 MiB default nothing happens.

**Repro.** `test/node/target.test.ts` › "StreamTarget in chunked mode handles a write spanning many chunks": one 32 MiB write into a chunked `StreamTarget` with `chunkSize: 1024`. Expected the stream to receive the data in chunks of at most 1024 bytes; main throws the RangeError.

**Cause.** `_writeDataIntoChunks` writes the part of the data that fits into the current chunk and then recurses with the rest, one stack frame per chunk, so a write spanning tens of thousands of chunks recurses that deep.

**Fix.** Write chunk by chunk in a loop: the body becomes `_writeDataIntoChunk`, which returns how many bytes it wrote, and `_writeDataIntoChunks` loops over the data. Same writes, same order.

Found by the round-trip fuzzing lane.

_Written by an AI agent (Claude) auditing Mediabunny on behalf of @vjeux._

author: immakermatty
body:
## What

Release 0.1.1 of the template (draft): Lazurio runs the **built version** from `main` instead of the development server, and the adoption guide's first checks work as written.

The review of the first adoption (LazurioExampleOrganization/presentations#1) found that `app/v1/package.json` declared neither `start_script` nor `build_output`, so Lazurio ran the development path from `main`. That is a defect of the template release 0.1.0, fixed here.

### Built version (Module Standard, "The built version from `main`")

- `lazurio.runtime` declares `start_script: start` and `build_output: dist` beside `build_script: build`, as `LazurioTemplates/mission-control` does.
- From `main` Lazurio builds the client (`build` → `dist`) and starts `start` with `NODE_ENV=production`; the server serves the installed build from `LAZURIO_RUNTIME_BUILD_OUTPUT` (the package's own `dist/` in a local production run, `src/static.ts`).
- A development run (`dev`) lets Bun bundle the client (HTML import with hot reload) and serves `public/` beside it, so it needs no prior build. One process in both runs.
- The preparation is separate from the build: `check:prepared` only checks the installed dependencies, `prepare:app` is gone, the first-slide preview check runs in `build`.
- Health is `/api/health`, answered by the server in both runs (it refuses a foreign Host).
- `planModuleRuntime` and `parsePreparationDeclaration` of LazurioPlatform `main` (7ccf1fc8) accept the declaration: a server App with `start_script` and a build with output `dist`.

### Issue #3

`docs/adoption.md` step 1: the name check reads the `full_name` GitHub answers with (a moved repository redirects, so a 200 alone is no collision); the release check compares the tag with the recorded commit, because the registry records no artifact digest yet (`null`, not verified by Lazurio); the module is created with `--teams` and a dry run first; LazurioPlatform v0.1.11 or newer is named for the built version. `docs/release.md` and `docs/marketplace.md` no longer promise a digest. Closes #3 when merged.

### CHANGELOG

`0.1.1 — proposed, not released`, with what an adopted module does when it merges the tag.

## Verification

- `bun run check` in `app/v1` with Bun 1.4.4: typecheck, Biome, 31 tests. New: the start contract for `dev` and `start` (exit 2 without the listener, health 200, foreign Host 403, SIGTERM exit 0), `build_script` writing `build_output` and `start_script` serving an installed copy outside the checkout (a marker file proves it, SPA fallback, immutable assets, no escape), the static handler and the runtime declaration.
- CI (`Check`, Ubuntu, Bun 1.4.4) green on `14323fa`: 31 tests.
- Browser, in the Environment's browser on loopback: the **built version** (`build`, the output copied outside the checkout, `start` with `NODE_ENV=production` and `LAZURIO_RUNTIME_BUILD_OUTPUT`) shows the library with the starter's first-slide preview, the detail drawer, and playback of the deck (arrow key to 2/4, "Tisk / PDF", "Zpět do knihovny"); Inter Tight loads from the build. The **development run** (`dev`, no build) shows the same library with the fonts bundled by Bun.

## Audit

The two new commits (`ae731f1`, `14323fa`) and the tree at the head: authors and committers only the GitHub noreply address; no credentials, tokens, client or colleague names, internal hostnames or private e-mail addresses.

## Review

`agentrozjedemeai` cannot be requested here: GitHub answers 422 "Reviews may only be requested from collaborators" (in `LazurioTemplates/mission-control` the account is a read collaborator; here it is not). Access is not added without the owner's instruction.

Not done here: no tag, no release, no registry change.
