author: hherb
body:
Fixes #19.

## What was wrong
- **Word readings lost their syllable boundaries.** `prepare_data` deleted the spaces between source syllables ("nán guò" became "nánguò"), so the splitter had to guess where each syllable ended.
- **About 130 words were split wrongly.** Examples: 全国 as quáng|uó, 晚安 as wǎ|nān, 然而 as rá|nér.
- **131 words could not be split at all.** Examples: 女儿 nǚér, 可爱 kěài, 第二 dìèr, and erhua words.
- **Ten readings carried a literal `r5`.**
- **Composed readings were run together.** `lookup_text` joined them with nothing in between, so 很爱 split as hě|nài and 我爱你 could not be split.

## What changed
- **Readings follow dictionary orthography.** They now carry an apostrophe only where the spelling requires one, before a non-initial syllable starting with a/o/e: `nǚ'ér`, `kě'ài`, `wǎn'ān`. Erhua is written `zhèr`. A new `pinyin::join_syllables` builds readings this way, and `prepare_data` uses it, while also cleaning CC-CEDICT markup (`r5`, `u:` to `ü`, the `˙` dot). `lookup_text` uses it too: 很爱 becomes `hěn'ài`, 我爱你 becomes `wǒ'àinǐ`, and 你好 stays `nǐhǎo`.
- **Splitter rules:**
  - an unmarked `ng` followed by a vowel splits as `n|g`, as the orthography implies;
  - `'` is a hard boundary;
  - a trailing erhua `r` stays on the syllable before it;
  - capitals split the same way as lower case (ZHONGGUO becomes ZHONG|GUO).
- **Search tries both splits when an apostrophe is left out.** Learners often type `pingan`, so character search adds both readings of each untyped n|g boundary (pin+gan and ping+an). An explicit `pin'gan` is left alone.
- **Coloured pinyin shows the apostrophe.** `TonedPinyin` now prints the text that lies between aligned syllables (`syllableGaps`), so `kě'ài` and `Tiān'ānmén` keep their apostrophes, where before they rendered run together.
- **Docs:** the module docs, `Word.pinyin` and HANDOVER are updated.

## The artifact (`crates/hanzi-core/data/hanzi.bin.gz`): regenerated and checked
- **Upstream hasn't drifted.** No source revisions are recorded in the repo (see #38), so the four inputs were fetched from the current upstream heads: makemeahanzi `bddc96d4`, hanziDB.csv `3e9f908d`, complete-hsk-vocabulary `7ac65bf1`. Run through the **unchanged** pipeline, they rebuild the committed artifact **byte for byte**.
- **The new artifact differs only in word readings.** Decoded and compared with the old one:
  - all 9,574 characters are identical;
  - every word's text, meaning, HSK level and rank is identical;
  - only `pinyin` changed, for 127 words: 106 gained an apostrophe, 10 lost `r5`, and 11 had `u:` written as `ü` (one of them also lost `˙`).
  
  The independent review reproduced both builds byte for byte and read all 127 changes.
- **Effect:**
  - Readings that don't divide into one syllable per character fell from 131 to 57, and those 57 are all erhua words (儿 is not a syllable of its own).
  - 100 words that were split wrongly are now split correctly.
  - No word that used to divide is now refused.
  - Tone targets went from 9,312 to 9,386.
- **Character search across the full HSK list:** each word's toneless reading was typed into `search_characters`, counting words where any character was missing from the results. That count fell from 459 on `main` to 382, and no word is worse than before.

## Known limits
- **The 57 erhua words still have no tone target.** The target and transcript code assume one syllable per character; HANDOVER records the design question.
- **Older vocabulary entries without the apostrophe** (e.g. `píngān`) now align as pín|gān. The tones are the same; only which syllable the `g` is coloured with changes. No migration is needed.
- **Upstream sources are still unpinned (#38).** The new artifact tests (erhua count pinned at 57, no stray markup, apostrophe placement) would catch drift on the next refresh.

## Tests
- **Splitter:** the `ng`+vowel words (全国, 见过, 难过, 参观, 办公室, 人工); the apostrophe words (晚安, 然而, 女儿, 可爱, 第二); erhua; capitals; `join_syllables`; a join-then-split round trip.
- **`lookup_text`:** 很爱, 我爱你, 你饿, 你好.
- **`prepare_data` readings:** spaced input, `r5`, `u:`/`˙`.
- **Search:** `pingan` finds 平 and 安, `quanguo` finds 全 and 国, and `pin'gan` does not find 平.
- **New `tests/words_artifact.rs`, against the committed artifact:**
  - every reading divides one syllable per character, with erhua exempt;
  - no misplaced boundaries;
  - no stray markup;
  - apostrophes only where the orthography wants them;
  - the issue's own examples.
- **vitest:** `syllableGaps`, and the rendered apostrophe.

Each fails on the code before it; four of the five artifact tests fail on the old artifact.

Run locally:
- `cargo test -p hanzi-core --features prepare -p hanzi-tutor`: 461 passed, 0 failed. hanzi-say and tone-trainer pass too.
- `cargo clippy -p hanzi-core --features prepare --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `npx vitest run`: 271 passed. `svelte-check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

An independent review was done before opening; its findings (apostrophe display, search without apostrophes, capitals) are addressed in the second commit.

**CI note:** `audit` is red on `main` for unrelated reasons (see #46).

author: kirankigi5
body:
## Summary

Addresses correctness issues identified during review of the Week 1 data/audio pipeline after it was merged into `main`.

### Fixes

#### 1. Prevent REFRAMED test-selection leakage

The held-out REFRAMED test sample is now selected using only non-target metadata and a fixed seed.

- No professional AD contents or AD density are used to choose test clips.
- No subtitle contents are used to choose test clips.
- The fixed sample contains 30 clips, three per movie.
- Validation/pilot selection behavior and K-rate derivation remain unchanged.
- Legacy test-selection configs that used annotation-dependent criteria are rejected.

#### 2. Preserve the fixed-K design for Audio selector A

Long non-speech gaps can now contribute multiple candidate timestamps.

- Candidates remain inside usable VAD gaps.
- The shared 2-second minimum temporal separation is enforced.
- Selection is deterministic.
- A returns K moments whenever at least K feasible non-speech timestamps exist.
- Genuine shortfalls are reported only when the available non-speech capacity is insufficient.
- Existing acoustic gap scoring is retained, with deterministic earlier-time tie breaking.

#### 3. Missing audio no longer aborts a run

A video without audio features now:

- produces zero A moments,
- records the requested-K shortfall,
- and allows processing of the remaining videos to continue.

#### 4. Make word budgets consistent with available gap duration

Word budgets now use:

`min(30, floor(max(0, gap_seconds) * 3))`

There is no artificial minimum word count.

- Zero-word moments are not sent to generation.
- They are recorded as `not_safely_speakable` in the moment-build `.report.json`.
- Generation rejects an explicit zero-word budget instead of replacing it with the default 15-word limit.
- Proposal/spec documentation has been updated to match the implementation.

### Testing

Added 17 tests covering:

- annotation-independent REFRAMED test selection,
- long silent gaps supporting multiple A timestamps,
- multiple short gaps,
- genuine K shortfalls,
- deterministic tie behavior,
- 2-second minimum separation,
- exclusion of speech-overlapping timestamps,
- mixed batches with missing audio,
- zero-word budget handling,
- selector capacity against an exhaustive small-case oracle.

Full suite:

```text
Ran 158 tests
OK (skipped=1)
```

The remaining skip is the existing optional librosa-dependent test in the local macOS environment.

### Unchanged

The following evaluation behavior is unchanged:

- temporal matching,
- Temporal Precision / Recall / F1,
- BERTScore,
- sentence cosine similarity,
- evaluation aggregation.

### Remaining environment validation

Real-data/HPC validation is still required for:

- CUDA/Linux dependency installation,
- real Silero VAD + librosa extraction,
- real MTG-AD downloads,
- GPU VLM generation.

The PyTorch source configuration and `uv.lock` are intentionally unchanged in this PR.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Fixes #6903

Follow-up to #6836. Its reflog guard counts only the kept branch and its
reflog as reachability roots, so any commit the worktree's HEAD ever
visited outside that history blocks the prune until the leaf reflog
expires — including commits that are safe on another ref.

## Regression evidence (this commit: tests only)

`go test ./session/git/ -run TestVerifyWorktreeHeadReflogReachableFromBranch`
on master's implementation:

- `a_detached_checkout_of_another_branch_is_not_refused` — FAILS:
  names `main`'s tip as "the kept branch af/p does not contain"
- `a_detached_commit_kept_by_a_tag_is_not_refused` — FAILS
- `an_aborted_rebase_onto_another_branch_is_not_refused` — FAILS
- `autosquash_intermediates_are_still_refused` — passes (must keep
  refusing; see below)

## Fix (next commit)

Roots for the verdict are now everything that survives the leaf's
deletion: **every ref in the repository** (`--all`: branches incl. the
kept branch's tip, tags, remote-tracking refs, other `refs/` entries —
prune deletes no ref) **plus every value the kept branch's reflog has
recorded** (the branch ref survives, and its reflog with it). The verdict
becomes a single bounded `git rev-list <leaf shas> --not --all <reflog
roots>`: it prints exactly the leaf-reflog commits no root reaches, so
the cost is proportional to the commits that are actually unrecoverable
rather than enumerating the branch's whole reachable history into a set.

Issue properties:

1. A leaf-reflog commit blocks the prune only when no surviving root
   reaches it — (a) and (b) prune; a true leaf-only commit still refuses.
2. Case (c) keeps refusing: the autosquash intermediates are genuinely
   unreachable from every ref and the branch reflog — they exist only in
   the leaf reflog, so they fail closed exactly as #6836 intends.
3. `rev-list <shas> --not <roots>` prints only the unrecoverable
   commits.
4. #6836's tests stay green; each of (a)–(c) has a test (the daemon
   test's asserted substrings `reflog`/`does not contain` are
   preserved).

Linear: FDY-176 (BL-10). Dependency "BL-05 merged" met by PR #20 (2026-11-06).

## What this is
`docs/ops/refresh-jobs.md` — the three refresh jobs, one per tier, each with **schedule, inputs, output status, rollback step, failure alert**:

| Job | Cadence | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `briefing-refresh-deep` | monthly (`0 6 1 * *`, proposed) | schedule |
| `briefing-refresh-standard` | quarterly (`0 6 1 1,4,7,10 *`, proposed) | schedule, chunked 25/invocation |
| `briefing-refresh-profile` | on signal | **daily sweep** (`30 6 * * *`, proposed) over new `signals` (`company_tags ? company_id`) / `company_facts` rows since the brief's watermark, ≥3 new signals, 14-day cooldown — config rows, not code |

**No schedule is enabled.** Nothing in this PR runs. Enabling is §6 of the doc: merge → apply the migration → tier the rows → generator hand-off → registry grants → schedule with `cron_http_post` + Vault `cron_caller_token` (FAR-344).

## The two locked rules, and how they are enforced rather than promised
- **Every run writes `status = 'draft'`, never `'published'`.** A run never touches the live `briefings` row. It writes a staged `briefings_versions` row with `kind='draft'`, and that table carries `CHECK (kind <> 'draft' OR status = 'draft')`. A published brief stays on the shelf, unchanged, until Myke promotes the staged version; publishing is a separate explicit UPDATE and stays human.
- **Rollback from `briefings.version`.** `briefings.version` is an integer and cannot restore content on its own, so the companion migration `supabase/migrations/20261106220000_bl10_briefings_versions.sql` (**NOT applied**) adds `briefings_versions` (every editorial column, unique on `(briefing_id, version, kind)`, deny-all RLS), a per-job `briefing_refresh_config` row, and three service-role functions: `briefings_version_snapshot`, `briefings_version_promote` (snapshots first; never changes `status`), `briefings_version_restore` (snapshots first; a restore is a new version so history stays append-only). Until applied, the doc gives the manual rollback.

## Flags for Myke
1. **All 436 `briefings` rows have `tier = NULL` and `last_refreshed = NULL`** (measured 2026-11-06). Every job selects on `tier`, so every candidate set is empty today. Tiering the rows is editorial work that precedes the first run.
2. The Profile trigger is a daily sweep, not a row-level trigger on `signals` — a per-row trigger would call a generator inside a transaction, the jobid-227 pattern this estate has retired.
3. The migration is proposed, not applied; the three AUTO ids are not self-assigned (registry grants pending).

author: kylemyers001
body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

Two Dependabot alerts were still open in build and dev tooling: glob 10/13 (GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4, alert 1452) and minimatch 9/10 (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, alert 1457). The packages pinning them have no release that moves to the fixed majors: Expo 58's CLI, Metro config and fingerprint, cacache, app-builder-lib, @electron/universal and pi-coding-agent 0.84. Separately, `google-auth-library` 10.6.1 pinned `gaxios` 7.1.3, which still pulls `rimraf` 5 and, through it, glob 10 and minimatch 9.

**Stacked on #16.** After #16 merges, retarget this PR to `main`.

## What changed

- Root `package.json` `pnpm.overrides`:
  - `glob@>=9.0.0 <14.0.2` → `^14.0.2`
  - `minimatch@>=7.0.0 <11.0.1` → `^11.0.1`
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: refreshed `google-auth-library` 10.6.1 → 10.9.1, which is inside `@google/genai`'s `^10.3.0` range. It brings `gaxios` 7.3.1, which no longer depends on `rimraf`. No direct dependency or package manifest changes.

Resolved versions after the change:

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| glob | 7.2.3, 10.5.0, 13.0.6, 14.0.4 | 7.2.3, 14.0.4 |
| minimatch | 3.1.5, 5.1.9, 9.0.9, 10.2.5, 10.2.6, 11.0.5 | 3.1.5, 5.1.9, 11.0.5 |

glob 14.0.4 and minimatch 11.0.5 were already in the tree through rimraf 6.1.4.

glob 7 and minimatch 3/5 are outside both advisories' vulnerable ranges.

**API compatibility.** I read each consumer's call sites against the new majors. The breaking changes in glob 14 and minimatch 11 are removal of `makeRe`, `.regexp`, `matchOne`, `debug` and the `AST` class, plus changed partial `**` matching. None of the consumers use the removed APIs:

| Consumer | APIs used |
|---|---|
| app-builder-lib | `new Minimatch(p, { dot: true })`, `.negate`, `.match(path, partial)`, `.set` (read by `hasMagic`; in v11 its elements are Matcher objects instead of RegExp, and `hasMagic` still returns the same results) |
| @expo/fingerprint | `Minimatch`, `.negate`, `.pattern`, `glob.glob` |
| @electron/universal | `minimatch(file, pat, { matchBase: true })` |
| @expo/cli | `glob`, `globStream`, `sync` |
| @expo/metro-config | `globSync` |
| cacache | `glob` |
| pi-coding-agent | `globSync`, `minimatch` |

minimatch 11 needs Node 20 or ≥22, and glob 14 inherits that through it. Foundry requires Node ≥22.19, and Electron 44 bundles Node 24.

No wire, CLI, or documentation changes.

**Not covered:** the packaged desktop app ships npm 11.16.0, which bundles its own glob 13.0.6 and minimatch 10.2.5 in `app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/npm/node_modules`. pnpm overrides can't rewrite an npm package's bundled dependencies, and Dependabot only scans `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so it won't flag these copies. No npm release fixes this yet: npm@latest (12.2.2) still depends on glob ^13.0.6 and minimatch ^10.2.5. Once npm moves to glob ≥14.0.2 and minimatch ≥11.0.1, bump the `npm` pin in `packages/bb-app`.

**Follow-up:** remove both overrides once Expo, electron-builder/@electron/universal, cacache and pi-coding-agent require the fixed majors themselves. Until then, a new dependency that asks for glob 9–14.0.1 or minimatch 7–11.0.0 will be forced onto the new major without any warning.

## How you verified

- Confirmed each consumer above resolves glob 14.0.4 and minimatch 11.0.5 in `node_modules/.pnpm`.
- **Desktop packaging**, the riskiest consumer because app-builder-lib uses partial matching. I ran `pnpm run package` in `apps/desktop` on #16's head and on this branch, then listed every file in `Foundry.app`, including the `app.asar` contents. Ignoring code-signature files, both builds contain the same 24,534 files.
- `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck --filter=@bb/desktop --filter=@bb/mobile --filter=@bb/app --filter=bb-plugin-provider-pi` — 9/9 tasks passed.
- `pnpm exec turbo run test --filter=@bb/desktop --filter=bb-plugin-provider-pi`:
  - desktop: 59 files, 564 tests passed
  - provider-pi: 35 files, 327 tests passed
- `apps/app` `react-compiler-cache` test (cacache → glob) — 4/4 passed.
- `apps/mobile`:
  - `expo config --type prebuild` resolves 10 plugins plus the ios and android mods.
  - `@expo/fingerprint` `createFingerprintAsync` completes. The mobile config sets no fingerprint `runtimeVersion` policy, so the hash isn't used.
- Independent review (`review-fix-loop`, passed in round 1, no findings at risk 5 or above):
  - Compared minimatch 10.2.6 with 11.0.5 on 5,520 cases. They differ only for the path `.`, empty paths, and partial matches on dot segments without `dot: true`. app-builder-lib always passes `dot: true`.
  - Ran app-builder-lib's own file matcher under both minimatch versions against the desktop electron-builder config: 42,691 entries in darwin, win32 and linux modes, 0 differences.
  - Compared glob 13 and 14 on 16 Expo, Metro and pi cases: identical results.
  - `@expo/fingerprint` produces the same hash under the old and new versions.
  - Windows packaging itself wasn't run; only the win32-mode matcher comparison covers it.

body:
Lane: sim-static (prohibitions with a condition, per the lead's split with sim-grammar). Attack and block restrictions gated by a condition (`mtgsim/cx_static_combat.py`).

**Grammar:** `[<label> — ]~ can't attack | block | attack or block unless <condition>.` (creatures only). The condition is any `cx_condlib` phrase, read from the creature itself, so "another" excludes it. With two players, "defending player" and "attacking player" are the opponent. "a Goblin or Orc" and "another Wolf or Werewolf" carry the determiner to the second noun. Stored as `advanced_rules["cx_combat_unless"]` = ((attack|block|both, code), ...), and checked by one line each in `Permanent.can_attack` and `can_block`. The parser hook shares the late line with `cx_static_cost`, so "can't attack or block unless" lines the older `cx_conditions` reader takes are untouched.

**Left unparsed on purpose:** prices ("unless you pay {N}", "sacrifice a land", "return an enchantment", "tap an untapped creature"), "a creature with greater power also attacks", "at least two other creatures attack", "there are N Islands on the battlefield", max speed, monarch, soulbond pairing, exile counts and "an opponent has been dealt damage this turn".

**Newly read (all full in a local parse):** Chained Throatseeker, Chief Warg's Company, Deep-Sea Terror, Desperate Castaways, Felhide Brawler, Goblin Cohort, Goblin Goon, Howlpack Wolf, Lambholt Pacifist, Lurking Green Dragon, Marauding Boneslasher, Mindless Null, Mogg Conscripts, Mogg Toady, Monstrous Hound, Mouser Mark III, Olog-hai Crusher, River Serpent, Silburlind Snapper, Steelclad Serpent, Vantress Gargoyle, War Falcon, Warden of the Chained, Whimwader. author: maihwe
body:
## What this changes

The production container selected development dependencies, could hide failed static collection, copied the full build context, and used a readiness curl that could accept an HTTPS redirect. The entrypoint was also non-executable in source. Prepares a production-shaped staging image with a pinned Python digest, a hashed production lock that includes the base app, explicit executable startup, build-context exclusions, root-owned source/non-root runtime, build-only static settings and WhiteNoise serving. The loopback readiness probe requires a real ready response; Gunicorn accepts the platform PORT and omits query strings from access logs.

Adds a Container workflow that builds the image, applies migrations explicitly against PostgreSQL 16, validates deployment settings and image boundaries, serves admin assets, and verifies a Redis outage fails readiness while liveness remains available. The dependency-audit gate now also scans the production lock. Adds a staging environment template/guide and updates the saved handover.

GitHub's staging environment was created with protected-branch deployment restrictions. Hosting/domain/database/Redis access and real delivery providers are still pending; this PR does not claim a hosted deployment or completed registration/group walkthrough.

## Self-review (11 §3.3)

**1. What could this break that the tests do not cover?**

Real hosting proxy/header behavior, resource limits, persistent secrets, external delivery providers and production-sized migrations require the target deployment. Local Docker access is unavailable, so the added Container workflow validates the actual image in GitHub CI. Readiness regressions cover redirects, proxy variables, dependency failures, invalid JSON, liveness confusion and invalid host/port/URL configuration.

**2. Is there a path where money moves without a ledger entry, or a ledger entry without an audit record?**

Not applicable — no financial module or money movement in this slice.

**3. What did I assume about the caller that the code does not enforce?**

The hosting operator must provide the actual hostname, trusted TLS proxy, database/Redis connectivity, stable staging keys and delivery adapter. Docker ignores local environment/credential artifacts; build-only settings do not import runtime secrets. CI verifies the non-root user, immutable source, executable entrypoint and excluded context canary. Django runtime configuration still fails closed when required settings are missing.

**4. If this is wrong in production, how will I know — and before a member does?**

Container image validation, explicit deployment checks, readiness and static-asset smoke checks detect packaging/startup failures before deployment. Centralized logging/alerts and real-provider walkthroughs remain unfinished operational work; this PR does not establish member-before-incident detection for those integrations.

Additional workflow questions: a build fails instead of hiding collectstatic errors; migrations remain a discrete transactional release command, not implicit startup work; no money can move twice here; the deployment operator controls secrets and the staging host, while app permissions are unchanged; the provider-specific walkthrough is not run because its target/access and real delivery integration have not been supplied.

## Slice and scope

- Slice: Phase 1 staging preparation and deployment validation.
- Requirement context: NFR-OPS-001, NFR-QUAL-001, SEC-SEC-001, SEC-DATA-001, DEP-LOG-003, 11 §6 and 12 §§1–7.
- Test obligations: container readiness distinction and packaging/secret-boundary checks; no financial obligation closure claimed.

body: ## Summary v1.14.1 `atomic_json` publishes `lua-inbox.json` with one `os.replace`. body:
Second L1 PR: every `react-hooks/refs` violation (47 at the recount, 45 on this main) is fixed at its cause, and the rule is on as an error. Only `set-state-in-effect` (53) is left off, for the next PR. Based on main with B1 (#131) merged, so AgentDetail is included.

## What changed

**"Latest value" refs (30 sites).** These are refs that follow a prop or callback so that a listener set up once calls the current one. They were written during render with `ref.current = value`. They now use `useKeepCurrent(ref, value)` from `src/hooks/useKeepCurrent.ts`, which writes the ref in a layout effect, so the ref is current before any effect or event runs. Sites: Dropdown (3), Popover, SidePeek, PrefilledExpenseModal, useConnectionSetup, GraphView, WorkloadTable (3), useNewItem, useReceiptDrop (2), useUnsavedChangesWarning, UsageTab (2), CalendarPage, ClientDetailPage, InvoiceFormPage (3), QuoteFormPage (3), WikiPage (3), AgentDetail (2).

In four places a cleanup reads the ref: SidePeek, useConnectionSetup, the WikiPage editor and the AgentDetail images. There the layout effect is written out in place, because `exhaustive-deps` only treats a ref as ours when it sees the assignment in the component.

**Focus return (Modal, ContextMenu).**
- Modal still captures the trigger at render time, on the closed→open transition, because autoFocus children take focus during commit. The capture now lives in state, adjusted during render (React's documented pattern), instead of in two refs written during render.
- The StrictMode re-capture branch now uses the captured element.
- ContextMenu captures the trigger once, with a `useState` initializer.
- Shared helper: `src/components/ui/focusedElement.ts`.

**OptionsEditor.** The stable row keys move from a ref read and written during render into state. Adds and removes update the state in the same batch as `onChange`. A change of count from outside still gives fresh keys.

**GraphView.**
- The settled layout and the live drag positions move into state. Before, a positions ref was read during render, and a frame counter state forced the re-render.
- A change of graph lays out again from the last positions, as before. Dragging sets the positions in state once per frame, the same number of renders as the counter caused.

**Wiki graph saved view.** WikiPage passed `graphViewRef.current` as a prop during render. It now passes the ref itself, and GraphView reads it once, in its `useState` initializer, when it mounts. The prop is renamed from `initialView` to `savedView` and only WikiGraph uses it.

## Behaviour
No intended change. Things to check by hand:
- **Modal and ContextMenu:** focus still returns to the button that opened them, with the keyboard and the mouse.
- **OptionsEditor:** keep typing in a field after removing an earlier option.
- **Wiki graph:** drag a dot; switch away from the graph and back, and the zoom and pan should be kept.

No eslint-disable lines were added.

## Checks
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `npm run lint`: clean (0 problems)
- `npx vitest run`: 253 files, 1944 tests passed (adds `src/hooks/useKeepCurrent.test.ts`)

author: atomicdeploy
body:
# Standalone peer discovery and update exchange

One peer catalogue describes boards and controller applications. A board does
not need a connected controller, and an application does not need a connected
board. Existing board controls, APK installer and firmware maintenance owners
remain authoritative; finding a peer never starts a game, changes the selected
device, installs an app or reboots a board.

## Independent policies

- Public identity and descriptive releases remain readable through
  `GET /api/peer/info`, regardless of automatic checking or release enforcement.
- Automatic checking, artifact sharing and accepting an offer are separate
  controls. An enabled caller can query a passive peer whose automatic checks
  are disabled. A disabled check is not permission to bypass authentication,
  change the remote policy, accept an unsupported command or replay a write.
- A peer with a newer compatible artifact may offer it. An offer is a bounded,
  expiring suggestion, never an installation grant. A recipient requests the
  bytes and owns staging, cancellation, validation and explicit apply.
- Different artifact families remain visible but cannot update one another:
  table firmware is not key-game firmware; Android APKs are not desktop apps.
  Equal SemVer with different SHA/build metadata is not assumed newer.

## Additive metadata

Identity retains the existing product/application, board or instance identity,
session/boot, hostname, descriptive version, capabilities and compatibility
policy. `exchange` describes actual sharing/check/listener state. `artifacts`
describes only available packages with family, version, byte length, SHA-256,
relative download path and readiness/progress. Never publish credentials,
private settings, raw flash, an unavailable package or an invented checksum.

Board firmware exchange uses its running application partition and existing
inactive-slot staging/journal/apply pipeline. A LAN transfer pins source board,
boot, hostname, verified private IP, exact download path, image family, size
and whole-image SHA-256. It does not enable arbitrary HTTP firmware downloads.
The existing image/header/chip/partition checks and post-boot verification still
apply. Saved scenes, correction rules and settings are not part of the image.

Controller apps combine discovered boards and application peers in a dedicated
peer workspace. Read details without connecting a board; explicitly open the
selected board's existing controls or an advertised app-management capability.
Unreachable/auth-required/unsupported/stale peers retain distinct states.

## Acceptance (not claimed complete by this design)

- Firmware-only two-node discovery, newer/older offer and verified staging.
- App-only discovery and supported package exchange without a board.
- Mixed parties, separate application/artifact identities and management.
- Automatic checks disabled independently at either end, both release-policy
  build settings, authentication, malformed/equal/incompatible artifacts.
- No implicit flash, reboot, device selection or uncertain-write replay.
- Actual Flutter/Rust controls and deterministic transport/transfer tests;
  SDK builds and installed-device acceptance recorded separately.

## Implemented candidate endpoints and ownership

Tracked by [issue 58](https://github.com/atomicdeploy/PakarController/issues/58).
This is source-candidate documentation, not a claim of deployed acceptance.

| Operation | Endpoint | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public identity and available artifacts | `GET /api/peer/info` | No selection or installation; readable with checks disabled |
| Board-owned catalogue | `GET /api/peers/discovered` | Bounded eight peers, age and stale state |
| Explicit discovery | `POST /api/peers/discover` | Runs the bounded SDK/network worker, never on the game loop |
| Independent board policies | `POST /api/peers/policy` | Persist `automatic_check`, `accept_offers`, `sharing` booleans with readback/rename |
| Advisory incoming offer | `POST /api/peer/offer` | One expiring suggestion, bound to actual private-LAN TCP source; never fetch/apply |
| Receiver-owned staging | `POST /api/peers/update` | Validate source and download to the inactive slot; never selects boot partition |
| Existing progress/apply/cancel | `/api/firmware/remote`, `/api/firmware/apply`, `/api/firmware/cancel` | Same journal, exact job/boot/hash ownership and explicit apply |

Discovery checks default on at a 60-second interval; turning them off does not
disable public identity, backup reads, explicit discovery or incoming offers.
Sharing off removes advertised artifacts and outgoing offers, not the existing
authenticated backup API. Source authentication is explicit, origin-pinned,
memory-only and cleared on completion/cancel/failure. No recipient credentials
are forwarded to a peer. General remote firmware HTTPS policy is unchanged.

For staging, send `source` with `hostname`, verified private `address`,
`board_id`, `boot_id` and one advertised `artifact`; optional `authorization`
is for that source alone. The running-image family is generated from MCU/FQBN,
role, pin map and compiled capabilities, not installation hostname, release,
initial box mask or an arbitrary Git hash. Validate the retained family marker
inside the complete SHA-verified image as well as the HTTP identity headers.
The retained release marker must also match the advertised release; a valid
hash of an old/different binary is not a newer firmware candidate.
Different families are visible but cannot replace one another. A same-release
image is not automatically considered newer just because its digest differs.

The eight-entry firmware catalogue retains compact identity/artifact metadata,
not complete app hardware reports. Full information remains at each endpoint.
Catalogue pages fit the existing USB response budget: follow `next_offset` via
the HTTP `offset` query or WS/USB `offset` field until null. Age/stale information
belongs to each observation; a saved index is not control or update authority.
Staging refuses to overlap an active discovery worker to avoid concurrent
network/maintenance allocation pressure.

The USB general API has the same catalogue, policy and staging operations.
WebSocket/MQTT use existing peer-fenced commands `peer-catalogue`,
`peer-discover` and `peer-update-stage`; no numeric wire opcode was added.

Flutter exposes Peers from Devices independently of a connection, with app APK
receive/offer actions using its existing signed-package transaction. Rust adds
a dockable Peers panel available disconnected and a separately configurable
passive identity listener; disabling API bridging still blocks WebSocket and
board/control/export calls. Opening a peer's controls uses the existing draft
guard, explicit connection and credential flow, not discovery authority.

Windows x64 apps also share only their running, hashed executable through
`GET/HEAD /api/peer/package`. Package preparation is asynchronous; unavailable
packages are never advertised. `peer_package_sharing` is separate from API
bridging and automatic update checks. Receivers re-probe the exact app/session,
pin its actual TCP address while retaining Host/TLS identity, validate family,
platform, release/build, byte length and complete SHA-256, then use the existing
managed candidate/rollback installer. Peer reception never inherits automatic
apply; Apply and restart binds the exact verified hash and still waits for all
drafts/operations to finish. Cached verified candidates are not re-streamed.
Other native platforms remain discovery/control peers but do not advertise a
Windows installer; their managed replacement adapters are explicitly absent.

Both peer views offer newer same-role board firmware to the currently selected
receiver. Source credentials are entered separately and kept transient; the
receiving board verifies the exact family and source identity. Flutter uses
the same fenced general API over network or USB

author: dave356w
body:
Owner's request (2026-11-06): fix Fit model's totals step, which stalled on the throttled NBA report server ([run 42297144065](https://github.com/Dave356w/nba-matchups/actions/runs/42297144065), cancelled) and committed nothing. No model, rule, tag or record change.

## Cause
`totals.py fit` re-derived the injury-report stage's per-game terms (av_o, av_d, av_m) from NBA report PDFs on every run: four completed seasons at the 300-minute lead. The report server throttles GitHub runners' parallel fetches, the step never finished, and the job's failure also discarded the margin-model refit and the partly filled report cache.

## Fix
- **Stored terms** (`totals.report_terms`, `model/totals_report_terms.csv`, 4,923 games, 2022-23 .. 2025-26). Completed seasons are read from the file; a season that is missing, or whose fingerprint (lead, that lead's play-rate table, report parser version) changed, is recomputed from the reports and stored, season by season. The current season is never stored.
- **Reproduces the deployed model:** a fit from the reports equals `model/totals.json` exactly; a fit from the stored terms equals it to ~15 significant digits (the CSV float round trip).
- **`fit-model.yml`:** the totals step gets a 45-minute limit and `continue-on-error`, so the other refits are still committed (and `model/totals.json` stays as it was); fetched reports are cached even on failure; a failed totals fit leaves a warning in the run.
- Fit model was not dispatched from this branch: it pushes to `main`.

## Checks
- `python validate_data_files.py`: OK
- `python -m pytest tests/ -q`: 532 passed (new `tests/test_totals_terms_cache.py`: computed once then read, current season never stored, changed inputs recompute, committed file matches the deployed play rates)
- No page changes.

author: farq-tech
body:
## كاميرات رصد السرعة (ساهر)

طبقة على الخريطة + تنبيه صوتي قبل الكاميرا أثناء التوجيه + زر بلاغ من المستخدمين لبناء قاعدتنا الخاصة. العمل **إضافي بالكامل** ولا يلمس `NavSession` / `SaryVoice` / `NavMapLayer` / `PlaceSearch` / `FarqTiles` / `LiveOutingScreen` (قراءة فقط).

### ١) الـAPI
- **ترحيل 018** (`018_sary_speed_cameras.sql`، إضافي فقط): جدول `sary.speed_cameras` (النقاط العامة التي يرسمها التطبيق ويُنبّه عليها، upsert عديم التكرار على `source+source_id`) وجدول `sary.camera_reports` (بلاغات السائقين الخام). RLS مفعّل بلا سياسات مثل بقية المخطط، وREVOKE عن `anon`/`authenticated`.
- **الخصوصية**: هوية المبلّغ لا تعبر أبدًا إلى الجدول العام. `GET /api/cameras` يقرأ `speed_cameras` فقط ولا يختار أي عمود هوية. `user_id` يُحفظ فقط لمنع تكرار نفس الشخص، ويُنسى مع حذف الحساب (`ON DELETE SET NULL`).
- **lib/cameras.js**: قراءة bbox، استيراد GeoJSON idempotent، ترقية البلاغ (٣ مبلّغين مختلفين خلال ٥٠م → كاميرا مصدرها `user`؛ بلاغ عند كاميرا موجودة يرفع ثقتها بدل تكرارها)، و`confirm`/`dismiss`.
- **routes/cameras.js**:
  - `GET /api/cameras?bbox=west,south,east,north` — الطبقة (قابلة للتخزين المؤقت، بلا هوية).
  - `POST /api/cameras/report` — `{lat, lon, kind, client_id}`. المصادقة اختيارية؛ توكن Bearer يربط البلاغ بمستخدم **على الخادم فقط** لإزالة التكرار، ولا يُعاد أبدًا.
  - `POST /api/cameras/:id/confirm` و`/:id/dismiss`.

#### كيف يُستورد ملف الكاميرات
```
node apps/api/scripts/import-cameras.js [مسار/cameras.geojson]
```
المسار من الوسيط، وإلا من `CAMERAS_GEOJSON_PATH`، وإلا `~/code/map-wt/cameras/cameras.geojson` (حيث يكتبه وكيل البحث). **idempotent**: upsert على `source+source_id`، لا يكرّر ولا يمسّ بلاغات المستخدمين. اختُبر بعيّنة صغيرة (٣ كاميرات) وتأكّد عدم التكرار عند إعادة التشغيل.

### ٢) التنبيه الصوتي (قراءة فقط — بلا مساس بجدولة التنبيهات)
- مزوّد منفصل `CameraHazardProvider` (في `Sources/Cameras/`) يُسقِط الكاميرات على المسار (ممر جانبي + فحص اتجاه فلا تُنبّه كاميرا تواجه الاتجاه الآخر)، ويجد أقرب كاميرا أمام السائق، ويُطلق **تنبيهًا واحدًا على الأكثر لكل مستوى لكل كاميرا — دون تكرار**، ويحترم الكتم، ويصمت تحت حدّ ثقة.
- **لا يُولَّد أي صوت هنا.** المزوّد يُصدِر النص فقط؛ التسجيل بـ«صوت سرى» لاحقًا.

#### النصوص الصوتية العربية المقترحة للاعتماد
- اقتراب (٥٠٠م): **«انتبه، كاميرا رصد على بُعد ٥٠٠ متر»** (المسافة مُدوّرة؛ أرقام هندية).
- وشيك (~١٢٠م): **«كاميرا رصد قدّامك»**، وللإشارة: **«كاميرا إشارة قدّامك»**.
- لا نذكر رقم حد السرعة بصوت إلا إذا كنا واثقين منه (`speakLimitMinConfidence`).

### ٣) الطبقة والزر
- `CameraMapLayer` — مصدر/طبقة Mapbox مستقلّان (رمز كاميرا بسيط على قرص ملوّن، أخفت عند الثقة المنخفضة، **بلا أي شعار تجاري**). مُعرّفات خاصة به، جاهز للربط.
- `CameraReportButton` — زر «كاميرا هنا» داخل الأدوات/القائمة (ليس ضمن الأزرار الظاهرة دائمًا)، يفتح منتقي نوع ثم يرسل بلاغًا بموقع السائق الحالي فقط.

### الإثبات
- **اختبارات API** (تنجح على Postgres محلي): `lib/cameras.test.js` (استيراد idempotent + upsert، bbox بلا هوية، ترقية ٣ مبلّغين، عدم ترقية نفس المبلّغ، البلاغ عند كاميرا موجودة، confirm/dismiss)، و`lib/cameras-route.test.js` (نقاط HTTP + 503 عند غياب الخدمة). الترحيل 018 يُطبّق ضمن 001–018.
- **اختبار وحدة iOS** `Tests/CameraHazardTests.swift`: الإسقاط، أقرب كاميرا أمامك، قاعدة تنبيه واحد لكل مستوى بلا تكرار، حجب الثقة المنخفضة، الكتم — **`** TEST SUCCEEDED **` على المحاكي**.
- **لقطات من المحاكي** (عبر `-SaryCamerasDemo`): شريط «انتبه، كاميرا رصد على بُعد ٥٠٠ متر»، شريط «كاميرا إشارة قدّامك» (أحمر)، وحوار زر البلاغ بالأنواع الأربعة ورسالة الخصوصية. *(رموز الطبقة على الخريطة لم تُصوَّر لأن توكن Mapbox خارج git عمدًا؛ الكود مبنيّ ومُجمَّع ضمن التطبيق.)*

### ملاحظات للدمج (shared files — إضافية وموثّقة)
- `outings-migrations.test.js` و`outings-integration.test.js` يؤكّدان قائمة الترحيل الدقيقة، فأُضيف `018_sary_speed_cameras.sql` بعد 017. (حُلّ تعارض الـrebase مع 017 يدويًا؛ القوائم الآن …016، 017، 018.)
- `SaryAlbarqApp.swift`: سطر واحد إضافي `.saryCamerasDemoIfRequested()` (DEBUG + `-SaryCamerasDemo` فقط، مطفأ افتراضيًا) على نمط خطافي Showcase/CarPlay الموجودين.
- للربط الحيّ لاحقًا دون مفاجأة للوكلاء الملّاك: ينادي منسّق الخريطة `CameraMapLayer.ensure/update`، وتقرأ جهة التوجيه `CameraHazardProvider.latestAlert.text` (قراءة فقط). لم يُجرَ هذا التعديل هنا.

author: fueroberther
body:
## What & why

An attack chip looked the same whatever reached its roll, so a Poisoned attack read as a normal one until you read the cue above it. A chip now wears each condition that reaches its roll, in that condition's own hue, with one signature that loops at rest. This is the design system's one named exception to its motion rule, chosen on purpose over the rounds on the design canvas. The source of truth is the [spec](https://claude.ai/artifact/QZpJecqnrzhmMnooCAppyx).

Attack chips only, on the Play and Spells tabs. Settings gets "Animate condition effects", on by default; off, and under reduced motion, a chip keeps its colours and marks and holds still.

| Dark | Light |
| --- | --- |
| ![Every condition on a chip, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FueRobertHer/cast-guidance/f5b95dc384bfbbe77dae4c8aaf70faf27ad6ac74/docs/pr-shots/condition-chips/every-condition-dark.png) | ![Every condition on a chip, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FueRobertHer/cast-guidance/f5b95dc384bfbbe77dae4c8aaf70faf27ad6ac74/docs/pr-shots/condition-chips/every-condition-light.png) |
| ![Attacks on the Play tab, Poisoned and Prone, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FueRobertHer/cast-guidance/f5b95dc384bfbbe77dae4c8aaf70faf27ad6ac74/docs/pr-shots/condition-chips/play-dark.png) | ![Attacks on the Play tab, Poisoned and Prone, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FueRobertHer/cast-guidance/f5b95dc384bfbbe77dae4c8aaf70faf27ad6ac74/docs/pr-shots/condition-chips/play-light.png) |
| ![The Settings switch, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FueRobertHer/cast-guidance/f5b95dc384bfbbe77dae4c8aaf70faf27ad6ac74/docs/pr-shots/condition-chips/settings-dark.png) | ![The Settings switch, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FueRobertHer/cast-guidance/f5b95dc384bfbbe77dae4c8aaf70faf27ad6ac74/docs/pr-shots/condition-chips/settings-light.png) |

Each chip is one frame of its loop. The images are pinned to a commit that a later commit removes, so a squash merge leaves none in main.

## How it was verified

- [x] `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (through `bun run check`: 255 files, 3845 tests passed)
- [x] `bun run build`, then `bun run bundle:budget`: "All metrics are within budget." CSS 72,288 B of 79,000 B, precache 1,358,289 B of 1,475,000 B
- [x] `bun run notices:check`: "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is current."
- [x] `bunx playwright test e2e/a11y/reduced-motion.spec.ts --project=a11y`: 5 passed, including chips moving by default, holding still with the switch off, and holding still under reduced motion
- [x] `bunx playwright test --project=axe --project=a11y --project=flows`: 95 passed, 13 failed. All 13 fail on this machine without this change too: 11 in `a11y/layout` need the DejaVu font, plus `manifest` and `offline-reload`
- [x] Manual/browser check: real data at phone width, both themes, no console errors. Arrival held under a sheet, roll flash, Ignore once, removal, the Settings switch, concentrating rows at the top and bottom of a list
- [ ] **Real phone: not done.** The spec asks for several Paralyzed chips on a mid-range phone before merge

The review fixes were each broken in turn, and a test failed all 10 times. Contrast is now a test: the number holds 4.5:1 over each condition's strongest layer, lowest Prone at 4.63 (dark) and Frightened at 4.66 (light).

## Notes for the reviewer

**CI is the first real run of the layout spec on this change**, since this machine lacks DejaVu. A scratch copy using Verdana passed 19 of 19 before the review fixes, which moved no layout.

**Budget.** The stylesheet takes both over: CSS from 63,000 to 79,000, and precache from 1,341,000 to 1,475,000, the owner's decision so that the next updates do not each need a raise. `FUTURE_WORK.md` has the measurements.

**Changes from the boards**, all in the spec:

- Two conditions keep to their own sides of the chip. Stacked as on the boards, the number dropped to 2.9:1.
- Paralyzed's bolts park at the chip's edges when held still. Behind the number they left it at 1.5:1, for exactly the people who turned motion off.
- The attack list and the two spell lists on the Spells tab no longer clip, because they cut off Unconscious's Z's. They give their first and last rows the card's corners, for a concentrating row's tint.
- Contrast became a test, as above.

**Behaviour to look at:**

- Prone falls only when it is the newest condition. A Prone that is not newest tilts straight away when a chip comes back from Ignore once, rather than falling.
- Under reduced motion with the switch on, a change made under a sheet still appears about 300ms after the sheet closes. Nothing animates, it just lands then.
- A change under a condition sheet waits until the sheet clears. A tap cannot reach a chip in that 300ms, because the sheet's overlay is still over it, so a roll during the hold is not handled.

**Design system.** Colour and Motion in the brand book name the exception, and RollChip says what a chip wears. Those are already published.

author: drehtuer
body:
## What
A new `spamhaus` textfile collector, run hourly, reports whether this host is listed. A listing does nothing to the host itself, so the first sign would otherwise be other servers refusing its mail.

| Checked | Lists |
|---|---|
| `ip_v4`, `ip_v6` | ZEN, AuthBL |
| `domain`, `domain_aliases` | DBL, ZRD |

That's ten lookups a run with the two test records, about 240 a day against the free limit of 100,000.

| Alert | Severity | Fires when |
|---|---|---|
| `SpamhausListed` | critical | A target is listed, for 5m |
| `SpamhausChecksFailing` | warning | A test record or lookup fails, for 3h. This is what catches a dead key |
| `SpamhausCollectorStale` | warning | The result is over 3h old, for 30m |

A failed lookup or a Spamhaus error code emits no `spamhaus_listed`, because a zero would claim the target is clean.

## The key
It's in a `0600` file written by a `no_log` task, because collector scripts are `0755` and appear in `--diff`. It reaches `dig` through a file descriptor, so it stays off the command line. The collector only runs where `spam_dqs_key` is set, so only on production.

## Testing
- `invoke lint` and `invoke test-static` pass.

author: d-fankhauser
body:
## What
A hub can name its operation when it rejects a participant of another operation, so that an application can offer "join this operation?" to its user (#27).

- `Hub(..., announce_operation=True, operation_name="...")`: the `REJECT` with code `wrong_operation` carries the optional keys `operation` (identifier) and `operation_name` (1-100 characters, checked like participant names).
- The participant exposes them as `rejected.operation` and `rejected.operation_name` (`None` otherwise). It never switches on its own: the application asks its user and greets again.
- The frame check validates the keys when present (identifier, length). Older peers ignore them because unknown keys are already allowed. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is unchanged.
- Spec 14.5 (decided, added 2026-11-06), spec 11 (security note), `docs/decisions.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased).

## Deviation from the issue
The issue proposed "default on". This PR makes it **off by default**: anyone who reaches the hub would learn the operation identifier. The identifier alone grants nothing, but an application should turn it on deliberately (e.g. in closed networks or with TLS).

## Tests
- New `tests/test_announce.py` (14 tests):
  - off by default
  - with and without a name
  - only for `wrong_operation`, not for `unknown_participant`
  - greeting again with the announced operation is welcomed
  - valid and invalid frames
  - invalid operation name rejected by the hub
- Full suite: 192 passed, 5 skipped (soak is opt-in, the TLS tests need the `openssl` CLI). pyflakes clean.

No release yet.

Refs #27

body:
Named class expressions could hide unrelated rule diagnostics outside their private scope. A local iterator alias called `Array` could also be flagged as an eager array pipeline, and a mapped key named like an outer generic could be misclassified as `unknown`.

Fix those three lexical evidence defects while preserving rule names, options and public exports. For example, `const C = class Promise {}; function read(): Promise<unknown> { throw 0; }` now reports the unknown return; `type Dict<T> = { [T in string]: T }; type Safe = Dict<unknown>` correctly remains accepted.

Validation:
- Independent whole-repository review confirmed findings and implementation, with no remaining substantive objections.
- New CI step runs nine focused fixtures against the pre-audit sources and verifies five behavioral failures and four controls before restoring fixes and running all existing checks.
- Add the user-requested real tester-army `e2e@0.23.0`, pinned in the lockfile. Its documented engine-free target and fixture support runs the compiled plugin through native Oxlint: reject defective consumer source, repair it, and accept the resulting iterator/domain contracts. No UI, credentials or model calls are used. The dependency was selected for this explicitly requested regression framework.
- CI uploads baseline JSON and e2e evidence. Tests/builds run exclusively in CI; local work was static inspection, lint and typecheck.

Audit inventory, triggers, rejected hypotheses and applicability: `docs/reliability-audit.md`.

author: bld75
body:
Depuis le 06/11 vers 10:00, l'API des événements du site de la mairie de Saint-Paul (`wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events`) répond 404, et rundata.re sert une copie de son agenda datée du 05/11. Le site, lui, marche : la page `/evenements/` répond 200 avec le plugin The Events Calendar, et son export iCal `?ical=1` donne les événements à venir.

## Ce qui change

- Quand l'API d'un agenda The Events Calendar répond 404, et seulement dans ce cas, l'agenda lit l'export iCal de sa page, avec le lecteur iCal déjà utilisé pour d'autres agendas. Il lit les heures comme la mairie les tape, malgré le `TZID=Europe/Paris` de son site.
- Seul Saint-Paul a ce repli (`https://www.mairie-saintpaul.re/evenements/`).
- L'API reste lue d'abord, puisqu'elle peut revenir : elle donne en plus les événements commencés avant aujourd'hui et la position des lieux.
- Toute autre panne de l'API (503, délai dépassé) se passe comme avant : la copie est gardée, et l'export n'est pas lu.
- Chaque lecture de l'export est notée dans le journal, avec le nombre d'événements lus.
- La copie lue par l'export porte l'heure où elle a été lue. Si l'export tombe à son tour, la copie servie garde cette heure.

## Vérifié sur le site (lecteur cadencé, une page par minute, 07/11 de 02:11 à 02:16)

- `robots.txt` répond 200, inchangé depuis 2021. Il ne ferme ni `/evenements/` ni `?ical=1`.
- `wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events?per_page=1` répond 404, avec une page HTML.
- `/evenements/` répond 200 et porte 6 événements en JSON-LD. Le JSON-LD n'est pas retenu : il donne des heures en `+01:00` alors que la mairie les tape à l'heure de La Réunion, et seulement la première page de la liste.
- `/evenements/?ical=1` répond 200 (`text/calendar`), avec 8 événements du 07/11 au 05/12.

## Tests

Le test se fait sur l'échantillon enregistré de l'export de Saint-Paul (`test/fixtures/agenda/ics_saint-paul.ics`) :
- API en 404 : l'export est lu, et ses 5 événements sortent avec l'heure de lecture de la copie.
- Un jour après, export en 503 : la copie est servie, toujours datée de sa lecture, et marquée ancienne.
- API en 503 : l'export n'est pas lu.

## Copies

`agenda` passe de 36 à 37 dans revisions.ts : les pages d'événements se reconstruisent à la mise en ligne, avec Saint-Paul.

## Vérifications

- tsc : 0
- suite complète : 270 fichiers, 2 963 tests, tout passe

author: marcodotio
body: ## Problem Every completed Codex web search lists its query twice. The repo's own recorded fixture (`testkit/fixtures/web_search/codex_transcript.ndjson`) ends with a row whose detail reads "FIFA World Cup 2026 ticket prices official, FIFA World Cup 2026 ticket prices official". An opened page shows its URL twice. A multi-query search adds Codex's summary ("a ..."), and a find-in-page adds "'pattern' in url". Codex sets a web search item's `query` from its action (`codex-rs/core/src/event_mapping.rs` calls `web_search_action_detail(action)`). `webSearchPatterns` in `CodexAdapterV2.ts` added that `query` to the action's own query, URL or pattern. Path: Codex `item/completed` (`webSearch`) → `buildWebSearchArtifacts` → `web_search` turn item `patterns`. These are joined with ", " for the work-log detail on web (`session-logic.ts`) and mobile (`threadActivity.ts`), one per line in the item inspector, and returned as-is by the orchestrator MCP item read (`OrchestratorMcpService.ts`). ## Change `webSearchPatterns` now takes its values from the action and removes duplicates. It falls back to `item.query` only when the action gives nothing: no action yet (`item/started`), or `other`. ## Scope and approval This is a small fix for an obvious bug in one function, with no issue. The bug shows in the repo's own recorded Codex transcript. The change is limited to how the Codex adapter builds web search `patterns`. Other providers and the clients are unchanged. ## Verification - New `CodexAdapterV2.test.ts` test: "lists each Codex web search target once beside the query Codex derives from it". It replays `item/completed` web searches for each action type, with `query` set the way Codex derives it. On `upstream/main` it fails: ``` - Expected + Received [ [ "codex changelog", + "codex changelog" ], [ "codex changelog", "codex 0.160", + "codex changelog ..." ], [ + "https://developers.openai.com/codex", "https://developers.openai.com/codex" ], [ "sandbox", "https://developers.openai.com/codex", + "'sandbox' in https://developers.openai.com/codex" ], ] ``` It passes with the fix. - The `web_search` Codex replay fixture's assertion is now `assert.deepEqual(patterns, [WEB_SEARCH_QUERY])` instead of `assert.include`. On `upstream/main` it fails: `expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]`. It passes with the fix. - `vp test run` for `CodexAdapterV2.test.ts` and `CodexReplayFixtures.integration.test.ts`: 172 passed. Targeted `vp lint` and `vp fmt --check` pass. `effect-tsgo tsrs --noEmit` in `apps/server`: 0 errors. ### Web client, before and after A real Codex turn in a web dev server (empty state, a scratch repo), asking Codex to search the web for "FIFA World Cup 2026 ticket prices official". The "before" turn ran with the fix reverted, the "after" turn with it applied. The expanded **Web search** row lists the stored `patterns`. **Before:** the query twice (stored `patterns` were `["site.fifa.com World Cup 2026 tickets official prices USD 60", "site.fifa.com World Cup 2026 tickets official prices USD 60"]`). **After:** the query once. Not checked: mobile (it joins the same `patterns`, unchanged client code), and the open-page and find-in-page action types in a live turn (covered by the test). Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved Created with Claude Opus 5.5 in the Claude Code desktop app. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: punk6529
body:
## Issue

The owner approved a terminology change on 2026-11-06. Users should see **decision(s)** wherever the app said **competition(s)**. The scheduled winner-selection moment, previously called a "decision", is now a **result**.

## Fix

Only what users see changes. Internal identifiers stay as they are: component, hook and file names (`components/competitions/`, `useCompetition…`), i18n keys (`competitions.*`) and `{competition}` placeholders, API paths, `ApiCompetition*` models, `openapi.yaml` and `generated/`.

### Copy (commit 1)

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Competitions (tab, heading, region) | Decisions |
| + Competition / New competition / Add competition | + Decision / New decision / Add decision |
| Competition name / Competition type | Decision name / Decision type |
| Manage competition / Edit competition (rules, details) | Manage decision / Edit decision (rules, details) |
| Archive and stop competition | Archive and stop decision |
| All competitions / Loading competition… | All decisions / Loading decision… |
| Competition \| Waves / Competitions \| Waves (page titles) | Decision \| Waves / Decisions \| Waves |
| Competition published / ended / cancelled / updated | Decision published / ended / cancelled / updated |
| Competition entry disqualified / New competition results | Decision entry disqualified / New decision results |
| Competition decisions paused / resumed | Decision results paused / resumed |
| Pause decisions / Resume decisions | Pause results / Resume results |
| Decisions have not been paused. | Results have not been paused. |
| Decisions are paused. Entries and voting continue… | Results are paused. Entries and voting continue… |
| Next decision: {date} / rules label Next decision | Next result: {date} / Next result |
| Decision Timeline / Toggle decision timeline | Results timeline / Toggle results timeline |
| Next decision after {date} / No decision scheduled | Next result after {date} / No result scheduled |
| Discovery: Next decision {date} | Next result {date} |
| Home: Next decision today / tomorrow / {date} at {time}. | Next result today / tomorrow / {date} at {time}. |
| Checking its competition entry… / …to this competition yet. | Checking its decision entry… / …to this decision yet. |
| View this participant's / winner's competition entries in {wave} | …decision entries in {wave} |
| Projected vote count at decision time | Projected vote count at result time |
| Wave rules: First decision / Decision cadence / Single decision | First result / Result cadence / Single result |
| API tools page: PARTICIPATORY → a competition entry | PARTICIPATORY → a decision entry |

All of the roughly 55 visible strings in `i18n/messages/competitions.ts` now use the new terms. Articles and possessives were adjusted ("this decision's terms", "a decision"). The en-GB, es-ES, fr-FR and de-DE timeline strings now use resultado / résultat / Ergebnis. The fr/es/de submission-discovery strings now use décision / decisión / Entscheidung. The phase label "Deciding winners" is unchanged.

Review follow-up: the Decisions tab label and the vote-progress tooltips now resolve through `t(locale, …)` with existing keys (`competitions.title`, `waves.myVotes.projectedAtDecision`, `waves.myVotes.votesGivenNow`). The `/tools/api` glossary, the wave-rules result rows and the Memes voting FAQ phases still hard-code English. They are recorded in `ops/workstreams/i18n-fallbacks/decisions-rename-english-copy.md`.

These were left alone because the word has another meaning there: "competitive", the Open Metaverse essay, moderation's "content decision", "Community decisions powered by TDH", Museum governance decisions, and the About FAQ's general "decisions".

### URLs (commit 2)

- The routes moved from `app/waves/[wave]/competitions/...` to `/waves/[wave]/decisions` and `/waves/[wave]/decisions/[decision]`. The page files are still thin.
- `getCompetitionsRoute`, `getCompetitionRoute` and `getCompetitionDropRoute` build `/decisions` URLs. Notification inbox links, push deep links and in-app navigation all go through these helpers.
- `isCompetitionPathname`, `getCompetitionIdFromPathname`, the wave tab shell (`helpers/waves/wave-tab-shell.ts`) and the proxy wave-id policy (`lib/proxy/waveRoutes.ts`) accept both `/decisions` and the legacy `/competitions` segment.
- **Redirect:** a permanent `next.config` redirect sends `/waves/:wave/competitions/:path*` to `/waves/:wave/decisions/:path*`. `:path*` also matches the bare collection route, and the query string carries over. This is the repo's existing mechanism (`config/nextConfig.ts` `redirects()`, as used for Safe Collecting). It runs before `proxy.ts`, so the malformed-wave-id check sees the canonical path. App Router client navigations follow it too, through the redirected RSC fetch.
- `tests/routes.manifest.json` and the PR CI planner's native-competition path filter now point at the new route directory.

### Help corpus and docs (commit 3)

- `ops/help/help-index.json`: decision/result wording throughout. **"competition" and "competitions" stay as aliases and keywords**, with decision versions added beside them. The main record says that competitions are now called decisions, and the route fact names the redirect. `public/help-index.json` was regenerated with `6529 run help-index:sync`. `agent-files:sync` ran cleanly; `public/llms.txt` and `public/glossary.json` contain neither term and are unchanged.
- `ops/docs/` (48 files): user-facing wording now uses the new terms. File paths and link targets are unchanged. The main competitions doc and its README note that decisions were formerly called competitions, and `shared/feature-legacy-route-redirects.md` documents the new 308 redirect.

### Tests (commit 4)

- Jest assertions and Playwright selectors that use the changed copy or app URLs are updated. API paths (`v3/waves/.../competitions`) are unchanged.
- New: `__tests__/config/decisionsRedirects.test.ts` checks the redirect targets and query preservation with `unstable_getResponseFromNextConfig`. It also checks that `/decisions` routes are not redirected.
- New: `__tests__/helpers/competition-routes.test.ts` covers route builders, pathname parsing of both URL forms, and wave tab shell transitions from legacy URLs.
- `__tests__/lib/proxy/waveRoutes.test.ts` runs the wave-id policy cases for both segments.

## Validation

**Why test expectations changed.** The owner requested two changes: the copy rename (competition → decision, old-sense decision → result) and the route move (`/competitions` → `/decisions`). Every changed assertion or selector swaps an old visible string or app URL for its new value; what each test checks is unchanged. Negative assertions (`toHaveCount(0)`, `not.toContainText`, `queryBy… toBeNull`) were updated to the new copy so they still guard the real label. The navigation-continuity monitor (`tests/support/waveNavigationContinuity.ts`) now flags a visible "Decisions" detour instead of the label that no longer renders. API paths (`v3/waves/.../competitions`) stay unchanged in mocks and route interceptors.

**New coverage:**
- `__tests__/config/decisionsRedirects.test.ts`: the 308 targets for `/waves/<id>/competitions`, `/competitions/new` and `/competitions/<id>`, with the query preserved; `/decisions` routes are not redirected.
- `__tests__/helpers/competition-routes.test.ts`: route builders, parsing of both URL forms, and wave tab shell transitions from legacy URLs.
- `__tests__/lib/proxy/waveRoutes.test.ts`: the wave-id policy cases for both segments.
- `tests/social/native-competition-sandbox.spec.ts`, "redirects a former competition link to its decision with the query intact": a real-browser check that the legacy URL lands on `/decisions/alpha?tab=leaderboard`.
- `__tests__/scripts/app-pr-ci-effective-plan.test.ts`: both new route files select native-competition browser evidence.

**Run locally:**
- Jest on the 99 affected suites: 1,860 tests, all passing after one st

author: 0bmario
body:
Fixes #77.

## Summary

`${TMPDIR:?}` only catches an unset `TMPDIR`, not one that the same command reassigns. Recursive `rm` of `"${TMPDIR:?}/name"` now counts as disposable only when the command can't have rebound `TMPDIR`. The rule lives in one place in `guard.ts`, next to `DISPOSABLE`. It adds prompts and allows nothing new.

```diff
 classify(command)
+  tmpdirUnsafe = tmpdirMayChange(command)   // raw command, before messages/heredocs are dropped
   ...
   recursive rm: every target is DISPOSABLE and has no `..`
+    and (target isn't ${TMPDIR:?}/… or !tmpdirUnsafe)

+tmpdirMayChange(command)
+  rest = command without every literal ${TMPDIR:?}
+  ask if rest has anything but plain chars [\w\s/.,:@%+&|;>"-]
+      (any $, `, =, (, {, *, ', \, <, # …: covers assignments, expansions, arithmetic, braces, escapes, sh -c '…')
+  or, with quotes removed (TMP""DIR, TMP''DIR), rest contains TMP or DIR,
+      or a word env|sudo|doas|su|runuser|pkexec|export|unset|set|source|declare|local|typeset|readonly|read|readarray|mapfile|printf|getopts|eval|let|builtin|enable|exec|select|trap|alias|fc|history,
+      or `.` at a command start not continued by a path (`. v`, `.>/dev/null v`, `.>>x v`, `.>|x v`)
```

The check is broad on purpose and fails closed. It matches anywhere in the command, not just at command starts, so full paths (`/usr/bin/env`), `\export`, and `builtin export` are all caught. Some prompts are false, e.g. `rm -rf ${TMPDIR:?}/x/*`, which has a glob.

## Evidence

`classify` on each form, comparing `origin/main` (7abdfac) with this branch:

| command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TMPDIR=/ rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/Users"` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `export TMPDIR=/; rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/Users"` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `\export TMPDIR=/; …` / `builtin export TMPDIR=/; …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `declare -x` / `local` / `typeset` / `read TMPDIR <<< /` / `printf -v TMPDIR /` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `export TMP''DIR=/; …` / `export TMP""DIR=/; …` / `declare -x TM"P"DIR=/; …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `env TMPDIR=/ …` / `/usr/bin/env TMPDIR=/ …` / `env -i …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `sudo …` / `/usr/bin/sudo …` / `doas true; …` / `su -l x; …` / `runuser -u x true; …` / `pkexec true; …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `unset TMPDIR; …` / `set -a; . ./vars; …` / `source ./vars; …` / `. ./vars; …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `.>/dev/null ./v; …` / `.>>x ./v; …` / `.>|x ./v; …` (`.` then a redirect still sources) | allowed | recursive rm |
| `bash -c 'TMPDIR=/; rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/Users"'` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `z=TMP; z+=DIR=/; ((z)); …` / `e{xport,} TMP{DIR,}=/; …` / `$x TMPDIR=/; …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `git commit -m "x" <<< "$(export TMPDIR=/)"; …` | allowed | recursive rm |
| `rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/x"` | allowed | allowed |
| `cd /tmp/x && rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/x"` | allowed | allowed |
| contract scratch cleanup `rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/repro"` | allowed | allowed (`classify` and `workerRisk`, `test/delegate-worker.test.ts`) |

- **Before:** the 37 new ask rows in `test/guard.test.ts`, run against `origin/main`'s `guard.ts`, give 0 of 37 asking. `node --test test/guard.test.ts` fails at `TMPDIR=/ rm -rf "${TMPDIR:?}/Users"`.
  **After:** all 37 ask, and `npm run check --prefix extensions` passes (316/316 tests, lint, typecheck, install smoke test).
- **No new allows:** I ran 47 prefixes × 3 `rm` spellings × 18 targets × 8 suffixes = **20,304 generated commands** (including dot-redirect, `./build.sh &&` and `cd ../x &&` prefixes) through `classify` on both versions:

  ```text
  main asks: 10152, fix asks: 15354
  main asks, fix allows (new allows): 0
  main allows, fix asks (new asks): 5202
  ```

  All new asks are on `${TMPDIR:?}` targets.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The change only adds prompts, so reverting it is safe.

**Blast Radius:** prompts

Recursive `rm` of `${TMPDIR:?}/…` now asks in more commands. Examples are an inline glob, a `$var`, a command substitution, or any command that mentions `env`/`set`/`read`/`printf` elsewhere. In print mode (no UI), those commands are blocked. The plain cleanup the implement contract teaches still passes. Out of scope, left for #78: `doas`/`su`/`runuser`/`pkexec` aren't in `AT_COMMAND`'s wrapper list, so `doas rm -rf /` is still allowed on main and on this branch. Redirects with `&`/`|` hiding later targets, and symlinked temp paths, are pre-existing and tracked in #88.

## What changes
- **Game hall** (drawer → 小游戏, the discovery card, capabilities page, `?game=hall`): games still going at the top ("轮到你了" / "等 TA"), category tabs, each game with a one-line pitch, a "how to play" list, and its stats.

- **五子棋**: 15x15, tap to pick then tap/“落子” to place, five in a row wins (winning line ringed), resign, play again with black alternating.
- **你画我猜**: drawer sees the word (with "another word"), draws on a pad (6 inks, 3 widths, undo, clear); the guesser sees the drawing replayed, a hint (kind + length) and has 3 guesses; then roles swap. Words exist in zh/en/es so each sees and guesses in their own language. Cooperative score.
- 二选一 / 默契问答 / 真心话 are listed under Questions and still play as cards in Us.

## Built to add more games
`server/matches/index.mjs` documents the module shape (`start / act / turn / finished / view / stats`); a game is a module there plus a screen and a catalog entry (`src/features/games/catalog.tsx`, which also holds the categories: board, drawing, questions, puzzles, just for fun — shown once they have a game).

## Privacy and delivery
- Matches are a shared `matches` collection (`relationship_matches`), kept out of the home graph and snapshots; the drawer's word is removed from the guesser's view server-side.
- Moves are checked on the server (turn, bounds, occupied, game over).
- Partner gets a push ("轮到你了", "画好了，来猜猜", "结束了") only when it becomes their move or the game ends, not while they have the app open, following their messages switch and quiet night, at most once per game every 3 minutes.

## Summary

The journal hook (`.claude/hooks/bitacora.ps1`) now removes the blocks that Claude Code and its hosts wrap around the
user's text before it builds the 160-character excerpt and the tags: `<browser_instruction>`, `<system-reminder>`,
`<ide_opened_file>`, `<ide_selection>` and `<pasted_content>`. Until now a block at the start of a prompt ate the user's
words: four entries (15-10, 16-10 and 30-10) kept only the start of a system block.

- Each opening tag pairs with the nearest closing tag of the same name, so text between blocks is kept.
- An unclosed tag removes nothing, except `<pasted_content>`: from it to the end of the prompt everything becomes
  `[pegado]`, because pasted text is not the user's own words and the journal is public.
- Pasted content becomes `[pegado]`, and a prompt made only of blocks reads `(solo bloques del sistema)`.

author: willyldx
body:
Lot 5 de la Mission 003 : remises, corrections, annulations et réexamen des obligations. Décision : [0022](docs/decisions/0022-ajustements-et-reexamen.md).

**Aucune de ces opérations n'est un encaissement. `SETTLED` et `SETTLEMENT` n'existent pas.** Aucun déploiement, paiement réel ni interface. NestJS et Android ne sont pas modifiés.

## Ce qui change

- **Trois opérations distinctes, plus la contrepassée.** `DISCOUNT`, `CORRECTION`, `CANCELLATION` et `REVERSAL` sont des écritures séparées. Un dû nul garde son sens : `WAIVED`, `CORRECTED` ou `CANCELLED`.
- **Un contrôle proportionné.** Une opération dont le cumul reste dans le seuil s'applique aussitôt, avec motif. Une opération sensible devient une demande, qui ne change pas le dû tant qu'une seconde personne ne l'a pas confirmée.
- **Sensible** : annulation, dû amené à zéro, cumul au-delà de 50 % du montant émis, année clôturée, contrepassée d'une écriture confirmée.
- **Imposé par PostgreSQL** : la seconde personne pour tout dû amené à zéro, annulation complète, contrepassée exacte, demande figée après décision, journal et décisions immuables.
- **Réexamen déduit de la réalité** : `GET .../billing/reviews` signale les écarts de tarif et les retraits, sans rien modifier. La différence est signée, sans présumer de supplément ni de remboursement. `POST .../billing/reviews/decisions` enregistre une décision motivée, et une situation nouvelle redevient visible.
- **Permissions** : `BILLING_ADJUST` et `BILLING_APPROVE`, pour l'administrateur et le comptable, qui se confirment mutuellement.

La migration `V6` renomme `ADJUSTMENT` en `CORRECTION`. Aucune route n'écrivait cette valeur avant ce lot, et rien n'est déployé.

## Vérification

Sur `94dec6e`, sur GitHub Actions et PostgreSQL 18.6 réel. Les commits suivants ne modifient que la documentation.

- [Campagne concluante](https://github.com/SPX-tech/ScolaPay/actions/runs/42315265001) : 97 défauts détectés sur 97, 3 contrôles verts sur 3, 294 tests.
- [Première campagne](https://github.com/SPX-tech/ScolaPay/actions/runs/42307031300), sur `0e0f433` : 95 sur 97. Les deux survivants ont conduit à deux nouveaux tests.
- Sur les 46 défauts du lot 4 : 41 rejoués à l'identique, dont ceux de la clé d'unicité, 3 redéfinis sur `V6`, 2 remplacés par des défauts plus fins et non rejoués tels quels.

Détails : [journal de validation](docs/mission-003-validation.md#lot-5-en-détail).

**Non vérifié** : le volume du réexamen, recalculé sur toute l'année à chaque lecture et à chaque décision.

## Décisions ouvertes pour le propriétaire

1. **Le seuil de 50 %** : la valeur, et son réglage global ou par établissement.
2. **Qui confirme** : un établissement avec une seule personne habilitée ne peut ni annuler ni amener un dû à zéro.
3. **La visibilité des motifs** : le caissier et l'auditeur voient aujourd'hui les motifs de bourses et de remises.
4. **L'expiration des demandes** : une demande attend indéfiniment et bloque toute autre demande sur cette obligation.
5. **Les catégories de remise** : le motif reste un texte libre pour l'instant.

Le lot 6 ne démarre pas avant cette revue.

author: marcodotio
body: ## Problem A setup script's output line in the worktree setup card can show a replacement character (`�`) instead of an emoji. This happens at the end of a line longer than 400 characters, or at the start of a line that follows more than 4096 characters of output with no newline. Call path: `ProjectSetupScriptRunner` reads the setup terminal's output and passes each line to `onOutputLine`. In `ThreadLaunchService` that callback is `WorktreeSetupTracker.appendTail`, and the tracker's snapshot goes to the setup card on web, desktop and mobile (`WorktreeSetupCard.tsx`, `worktree-setup-card.tsx`). The runner cuts each line with `cleaned.slice(0, 400)`. It also keeps only `lineBuffer.slice(-4096)` of output with no newline. Both cuts count UTF-16 units. When a cut falls between the two halves of an emoji, one lone surrogate stays in the line, and clients show it as `�`. To reproduce, give a project a setup action that runs on worktree creation and waits for it to finish, with the command `node -e 'process.stdout.write("🙂".repeat(2100) + "x"); setTimeout(() => process.stdout.write("\n"), 500)' && sleep 90`. Start a new thread in a new worktree. The setup card's output line starts with `�`. The end-of-line cut has the same split, but on web the card truncates a 400-unit line with an ellipsis long before its end, so only the start-of-line case is visible there. The lone surrogate is still in the line's text either way. ## Change Each cut moves by one unit when it would split a pair. The head cut stops before a trailing high surrogate. The 4096-unit tail starts after a leading low surrogate. The code is inline, like the other merged emoji-cut fixes in the server (#29647, #29633, #29844). The repo has no shared helper for this. The shared `truncate` trims the text and adds `...`, so it does not fit here. The change is two small edits in `apps/server/src/project/ProjectSetupScriptRunner.ts` and two tests. ## Scope and approval This is a small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so CONTRIBUTING lets it go in without an issue. It belongs to the same family as #26070, #24255 and #29647: a length cap leaves half an emoji. Both cuts affect the same output line on the same path, so they are one problem. Open PR #31882 edits `stripTerminalControl` in the same file. That is a different line, and the two PRs do not conflict. User-visible surfaces: the setup card output on web (app.t3.codes and `npx t3`), desktop and mobile. Only the stray `�` goes away. A line can now be one unit shorter (399), and the layout stays the same. ## Verification `vp test run apps/server/src/project/ProjectSetupScriptRunner.test.ts`, with two new cases: - "keeps an emoji whole where a long output line is cut": emits `x` followed by 250 `🙂` and expects `x` followed by 199 `🙂`. - "keeps an emoji whole where newline-free output is bounded": emits 2100 `🙂` and `x` with no newline, then a newline. It expects 200 `🙂`. On `main` with only the test changes, both fail: ``` × keeps an emoji whole where a long output line is cut × keeps an emoji whole where newline-free output is bounded Received: "x🙂🙂…🙂�" / "�🙂🙂…🙂�" Tests 2 failed | 8 passed (10) ``` With the fix: ``` Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 10 passed (10) ``` `vp lint` and `vp fmt --check` on `apps/server/src/project` pass. `effect-tsgo tsrs --noEmit` in `apps/server` reports 0 errors. ### Web client, before and after Web dev server (empty state) with a scratch repo whose Setup action is the reproduction command above, set to run on worktree creation and wait for it to finish. Each shot is a new thread in a new worktree; "before" ran with the fix reverted. The zoomed shots are the same screen at 200% page zoom. **Before:** the third output line starts with `�`. In the DOM the line is 400 units, starting with `U+DE42` (a lone low surrogate) and ending with `U+D83D` (a lone high surrogate). **After:** the line starts with a whole emoji; in the DOM it starts and ends with `U+1F642`. Not checked: desktop and mobile setup cards (they show the same tracker snapshot). `WorktreeSetupTracker.clampText` has the same kind of cut for stage details and launch errors. It does not affect these output lines, because the runner already limits them to the tracker's 400-unit cap. This PR does not change it. Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved Created with Claude Opus 5.5 in the Claude Code desktop app. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
