author: claude-aethon
body:
Implements the release-branch and manual-hosting design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-release-branch-and-manual-site-design.md`, following the plan in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-06-release-branch-and-manual-site.md`.

## Releases
- **`release.yml` publishes only on pushes to `release`.** Pushes to `main` and PRs build and smoke-test without publishing. The path filters now live in `.github/release-filters.yml`, and the leg logic is in `scripts/release/legs.sh`. On `release` pushes, the paths-filter diffs against the previous `release` tip. The `recut-bases` job is removed.
- **The release PR is kept open from `main` to `release`.** `release-pr.yml` maintains it, and `scripts/release/pr-body.sh` writes its description:
  - what changes for users: the manual's changes, with links to the **Next** version
  - which parts it rebuilds
  - the merged PRs

  The workflow ignores fork PRs, and skips cleanly until `release` exists.
- **`gate` runs on `release` too.** It also runs the manual tests and builds the customer manual, so a leak fails the required check.
- **`AGENTS.md`:** agents merge to `main` when `gate` is green and the review has passed. Only the user merges into `release`.

## The manual
- **Version names come from the branch:** `release` → **Released** (the default), `main` → **Next**, `goal` → **Goal**. `manual/antora.yml` no longer names a version.
- **Content can be marked internal:**
  - `[.internal]` on a block, a section or a phrase
  - `ifdef::internal[]`
  - `:page-internal:` for a whole page
  - `ext.internal.modules` for whole areas
  - The customer build drops all of it. It fails on any leftover internal markup, any link to dropped content, or an internal start page.
- **The team manual deploys to Cloudflare Pages** (`aethons-tools-jam`) from `manual-site.yml`.
- **The customer manual is built into jam** at `/app/manual/`, for members and admins.

## Review
Each task had a spec-and-quality review with fix rounds. A final whole-branch review found 6 issues, all fixed and re-reviewed:
- an in-page link leak
- a way a fork PR could take over the release PR
- the gate not building the customer manual
- wrong ruleset docs
- missing first-time setup docs
- the list of internal areas being split across playbooks

Tests: manual extensions 8/8, `pr-body` 19/0, `legs` 5/0, `jam-image` 54/0, `go test` for `internal/jam`, actionlint, shellcheck.

## After merge
- `release-pr` and `manual-site` run for real for the first time.
- `goal` needs `main` merged into it. Resolve `manual/antora.yml` to `main`'s version, with no `version:` key.

author: mrballistic
body:
Merges recordstoreday.co.uk's release list into each season as a `regions` field on every release, plus the UK exclusives as new releases. Contract notes for the apps: `docs/uk-regions.md`; each app repo has `docs/data-contract/uk-regions.md`.

**Merging changes no live data.** Regions and UK exclusives appear only once a season has `releases/<season>/uk.json`, which only `watch-uk` or a manual `ingest-uk` creates. No live data file is changed by this PR. Plan: merge, disable `watch-uk` right away, and enable it and run it by hand once the iOS build with region support is live in the App Store (the Play Store build already handles it).

## What's in it
- **Parse and merge** (`scripts/uk/parse.ts`, `scripts/uk/merge.ts`): reads the UK four-column PDF, fuzzy-matches rows to US releases one-to-one, and tags `regions` as `["us"]`, `["us","uk"]` or `["uk"]`. `uk-overrides.json` pins or rejects matches. Every US publish re-applies `uk.json`, so watcher revisions keep the regions and exclusives.
- **Hydrate UK exclusives** (`scripts/uk/site.ts`): finds each release's recordstoreday.co.uk page through `sitemap.xml` and accepts it only when its schema.org `MusicAlbum` JSON-LD matches artist, title and season date. Fills description, tracklist (split out of the description), `rsdUrl`, and the cover, into empty slots only.
- **Watcher** (`watch-uk.yml`, `scripts/watch-uk.ts`, daily 15:00 UTC): finds the PDF linked from `/black-friday` or `/record-store-day` and merges it when its URL or ETag changes. It waits quietly for the US list, for a link, and while the page still links last year's list (under 30% overlap with the US list). Real failures open one issue per season.
- **Manual path**: `ingest-uk` workflow and script; with no URL it re-merges after you edit overrides.
- **Safety**: the gate, site repair and daily site enrichment see only US releases, and Discogs overrides apply to UK exclusives too.

## Measured on 2026 Black Friday
151 UK rows: 111 shared, 75 US-only, 40 UK exclusives. All 40 matched a verified UK page (description, link, cover; covers checked by eye), and 4 have tracklists. The real merge is `docs/samples/2026-november-releases-with-uk.json` (an app fixture; not served to the apps).

## Checks
472 tests pass, plus typecheck, lint, `validate.ts` and `actionlint`.

body:
## 📌 Feature / Sub-task: HU-27 Incoming Orders Real-Time Integration

### 📑 Summary
Implemented the operator interface view (`PedidosEntrantes.jsx`) to display incoming orders awaiting approval (HU-27). Replaced period polling with a live WebSocket event stream to keep the order lifecycle synchronized automatically in real time.

---

### 🚀 Key Changes
- **Initial Hydration:** Added HTTP `GET /api/pedidos/entrantes/` call to populate the initial list of orders sorted from oldest to newest.
- **WebSocket Lifecycle Management:** Replaced `setInterval` with a managed `useEffect` hook connecting to `ws://127.0.0.1:8000/ws/pedidos/entrantes/?token=<access>`.
- **Real-Time Event Stream:**
  - `pedido_nuevo`: Appends incoming orders to the list.
  - `pedido_actualizado`: Removes orders from the list once their state moves out of `pendiente_aprobacion` (approved or canceled) or updates existing item details.
- **Error Handling & Auto-Reconnect:**
  - Handled custom closure codes (`4401` for expired/invalid token, `4403` for missing store/permissions).
  - Added visual connection status indicator (connecting, connected, disconnected).
  - Implemented automatic retry reconnect logic on unexpected closures.
- **Approval Endpoint Fix:** Updated approval action to execute `PATCH /api/pedidos/:id/aprobar/` (matching HU-28 backend specification).

---

### 🧪 How to Test
1. Log in with an **Operator** account assigned to a store.
2. Navigate to the **Incoming Orders** page:
   - Verify initial order list loads correctly (`200 OK`).
   - Verify WebSocket connection status changes to **Connected** green dot.
3. Place a new order from a **Client** account in another browser session:
   - Verify the new order instantly appears at the end of the operator's list without manual refresh.
4. Click **Aprobar pedido**:
   - Verify request sends `PATCH /api/pedidos/:id/aprobar/`.
   - Verify `pedido_actualizado` WebSocket event automatically removes the approved order from the view.

author: jsaldias39
body:
> **Depende de #135 (v4.2.96): mergear #135 primero.** Esta rama ya contiene la de #135 (merge `c289e0b`), así que el manifiesto final es v4.2.97 = v4.2.96 + guion y FAQ. Una vez mergeado #135, el diff de este PR contra `dev` queda solo con lo de v4.2.97.

## Qué

Agrega el modelo de datos de dos funciones nuevas del médico: **Script de preguntas** (un guion ordenado de preguntas que usa durante la atención) y **Preguntas y respuestas frecuentes** (FAQ que publica para sus pacientes). Son tres tablas en el esquema **`forms`** (módulo 09, REC 09.1 y 09.2):

| Tabla | Columnas clave |
|---|---|
| `forms.question_scripts` | `owner_practitioner_id` NOT NULL → `profiles.health_practitioner_profiles(profile_id)`, `title` 1..160, `description`, `specialty_code` (texto, sin FK), `status` `active`\|`archived` DEFAULT `'active'` |
| `forms.question_script_items` | `script_id` → `question_scripts(id)` **ON DELETE CASCADE**, `position`, `question_text` 1..500, `help_text`, `answer_type` (`free_text`, `yes_no`, `single_choice`, `multiple_choice`, `number`, `date`), `options` jsonb, `required` DEFAULT false |
| `forms.faq_entries` | `owner_practitioner_id` (la misma FK), `question` 1..300, `answer` 1..4000, `category`, `position`, `is_published` DEFAULT false |

Las tres tablas llevan `created_at`/`updated_at` con DEFAULT `now()`, `created_by_user_id`/`updated_by_user_id`, y `row_version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` para la concurrencia optimista (la convención del repo; no hay columna `version`).

- **`options`** tiene que ser un arreglo JSON de textos no vacíos. En `single_choice` y `multiple_choice` es obligatorio y lleva 2 o más opciones (`ck_question_script_items_options`).
- **`position`** no se repite dentro de cada lista: `uq_question_script_items_script_position (script_id, position)` y `uq_faq_entries_owner_position (owner_practitioner_id, position)`. Los dos UNIQUE son `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE` para poder reordenar. Reordenar en una sola sentencia funciona tal cual. En varias sentencias, la API hace `SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED`. Un duplicado sigue dando 23505. Limitación: un UNIQUE diferible no sirve para `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`.
- **Índices:** `ix_question_scripts_owner_practitioner_id (owner_practitioner_id, status, updated_at DESC)`, `ix_faq_entries_owner_practitioner_id`, `ix_faq_entries_owner_published (owner_practitioner_id, position) WHERE is_published`, más los de `created_by`/`updated_by`.
- **RLS:** ninguna. Las tablas no tienen `tenant_id`, igual que `dynamic_field_definitions` y las demás tablas de `forms` sin tenant, así que `tenant_isolation` no las alcanza. Que el médico solo edite lo suyo y que fuera de su panel solo se lean las FAQ publicadas lo controla la API. El parche da `GRANT` DML a `mantra_app`.

## Cómo

- Se declara en `diagram_09_forms.puml` (tablas, aristas, índices) y en `diagram_33_integrity.puml` (CHECK_SQL).
- **Cambio en el generador:** `gen_integrity.py` suma `UNIQUE_SQL : <nombre> | <columnas> [| DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE|DEFERRED]`, porque un índice único de un INDEX_SET no se puede diferir. Las declaraciones se validan: nombre, columnas entre comillas y solo esas dos frases de diferimiento. El cambio tiene pruebas.
- El SQL se generó con `gen_ddl` + `gen_integrity` + `gen_apply`, como diferencia entre dev y la rama en el mismo entorno, porque la bóveda local no reproduce byte a byte el SQL de dev. Sale el primer `SQL/09_forms/05_constraints.sql` y `apply_all.sql` lo aplica.
- El parche `SQL/patches/2026-11-06_v4297_forms_guion_preguntas_y_faq.sql` es idempotente y corre en una sola transacción. Se copió del DDL generado y suma `COMMENT ON` y `GRANT`.
- También quedan al día el catálogo de datos (más las 3 justificaciones de tabla), el manifiesto, el README, `physical-materialization.md`, `_generation_report.md`, `integrity-matrix.md` y `SHA256SUMS` (`sha256sum -c` OK).
- **Versión v4.2.97:** la v4.2.96 es la del PR #135, que ahora esta rama incluye.

## Evidencia (salida real, PostgreSQL 16.15 local)

- **Base nueva desde la rama:** `apply_all.sql` y `apply_deferred.sql` terminan sin errores.
- **Base desde `origin/dev` con `tenant_rls` y el parche:** dos corridas, las dos con rc=0. La segunda solo da NOTICE «already exists».
- **Deriva:** `pg_dump -s` de las tres tablas da lo mismo en la base nueva y en la base de dev con el parche. Solo cambian los tokens `\restrict`.
- **Casos probados en las dos bases** (17 casos más los de defaults):
  - CHECK de título, status, answer_type, options (sin opciones, 1 opción, no arreglo, número, texto vacío), largos y position negativa → 23514.
  - FK con dueño inexistente → 23503.
  - position repetida en el guion y en las FAQ → 23505.
  - Reordenar en una sentencia y con `SET CONSTRAINTS … DEFERRED` funciona.
  - Borrar el guion borra sus ítems (0 ítems quedan).
- **Constraints por tabla nueva:** 9 CHECK, 9 FK, 3 PK y 2 UNIQUE diferibles (`condeferrable = t`).
- **Los 165 parches ×2 sobre la base nueva:** 164 OK. `v407_nullable_embedding_model_versions` falla porque necesita el esquema NoSQL `vector_rag`; ya pasaba antes y no tiene que ver con este cambio.

body:

Current best score: 355.987558956258. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5.5
Harness: Claude Code

# The 64-set PMULL switch on the four-tile tree, with longer recombination chunks and a word-at-a-time commitment encoder

Effort: xhigh

## Summary

This candidate starts from the current record, `e5248328` by jungjipdo (355.99 ms official), and makes three independent changes.

1. It restores the field switch of `4ff98b58` by fkiene (357.59 ms official): dadon's 64-set prefix switch with register-resident PMULL products for `B128`. The record was prepared from `d7b8a098` before that switch landed, so the two latest records carry separate gains and neither contains the other's. Their changes touch different phases.
2. It raises the commitment's reconstruction chunk from 224 to 256 elements, which reduces the inverse transforms from 115 to 97 per column.
3. It replaces the byte-slice encoder of the commitment with one that writes a whole word per coefficient.

The modulus `Q = 9721 * 55 * 2^16`, the transcript, the proof format (13,958,612 bytes) and the verifier are unchanged. For a given seed and table the proof bytes equal the record's, except for what a statistical reconstruction failure would change, which is covered below.

## Where the time goes

Phase timers on the `0e4884e7` tree, on two development hosts that are not the official runner, split the commitment as follows. Sums of the parts match the phase time of the same tree without timers.

| part of the commitment | fast core, ms | slow core, ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| index construction | 8.7 | 24.1 |
| table-fed levels | 18.0 | 59.5 |
| radix-3 levels 4 and 5 | 34.3 | 124.8 |
| radix-3 level 6 | 18.4 | 68.6 |
| accumulation | 32 | 82 |
| narrowing, inverse, recombination, clearing | 8 | 29 |
| final reconstruction | 0.4 | 1 |
| encoding of the commitment | 1 | 3.5 |

The slow core runs at 2.8 GHz, the official clock, with fewer vector units than the official core; the fast core is much wider. Neither is a Neoverse V2. The table shows that nothing is hidden in the commitment outside these parts and that the part after the accumulators is about 7% of it, which is what changes 2 and 3 address.

## What changes

Against `e5248328`:

- `solution-arm/labinius/crates/pcs/src/fields/lean.rs`, `neon.rs` and `scalar.rs` become the versions of `4ff98b58`, byte for byte.
- `solution-arm/proof_generate/src/ntt_sms.rs`: `CHUNK` goes from 224 to 256, and `MAX_COLUMN_FAILURE` from 1e-9 to 1e-7. The certificate code is unchanged.
- `solution-arm/proof_generate/src/rq.rs`: `pack_ring_elements` writes one unaligned little-endian `u64` per coefficient into a buffer eight bytes longer than the result, instead of `extend_from_slice` of a five-byte slice. The bytes above the coefficient width are zero and are overwritten by the next coefficient. Moduli wider than eight bytes keep the old path.

No crate is added and both `Cargo.lock` files are unchanged.

## Why the changes compose

- The switch runs after the commitment and reads only the packed table and the transcript's switch challenges. It shares no source file with the commitment and only the eight cores with it.
- The chunk is a multiple of the four-tile sweep of 32 elements, so the sweep of the parent still fits a chunk exactly, and 4096 elements divide into exactly 16 chunks.
- Each chunk costs six inverse transforms, their narrowing and their recombination. The base row costs one inverse per column regardless. So 18.3 chunks of 224 elements become 16 chunks of 256.

## Reconstruction bound

`CHUNK` 256 with encoder search 512 gives, as printed by `build.rs` from the public matrix: smallest margin 7.530 standard deviations; Hoeffding union bound 4.666e-8 per column and 4.778e-5 per 1024-column proof, so at most 2.4e-4 per five-run benchmark. `MIN_MARGIN` stays 7.5. `MAX_COLUMN_FAILURE` moves from 1e-9 to 1e-7. The record's values are 8.039 standard deviations and 9.05e-7 per proof.

The bound assumes fresh pseudorandom tables, as the earlier certificates do, and it does not hold for a crafted table. A reconstruction failure gives a wrong commitment, which the verifier rejects, so the risk is a failed run and never an accepted wrong proof. This is a deliberate trade against the record's tighter bound. Hoeffding's inequality is an upper bound, and the sum of independent bits is close to Gaussian in the tails, so the true probability is smaller.

## Correctness

- `cargo test --release` in `proof_generate` on an AArch64 development host with Neoverse V2 code generation: 35 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, including the SMS commitment against the reference on the SVE path.
- One test added by the parent did not compile on this tree because of a `usize` seed. It is fixed with a cast; no production code is involved.
- End to end, five fresh-seed proofs on each development host were accepted by a checker built from the unmodified verifier against this tree's library: modulus 35,039,150,080, 13,958,612 bytes.
- The library's `fields` tests were not rerun: the three files are byte for byte those of `4ff98b58`, whose proofs passed the official verifier.
- Not run: the pinned x86 verifier, which the official evaluation applies.

## Measurements

Slow development host, five fresh seeds, eight cores, not the official runner:

| tree | median ms | commitment | switch | fold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `e5248328` | 514 | 400 | 50 | 49 |
| this tree | 492 | 389 | 40 | 48 |

That host exaggerates the switch: earlier trees show about 12 ms there for a change that gained about 1 ms officially on the prefix-5 tree, and 13 ms officially on the prefix-4 tree. The expected official gain is therefore a few milliseconds.

On the fast development host the four-tile parent shows irregular commitment times, 214 to 294 ms against 119 ms for the two-tile tree, and this tree does the same, so those runs are not used here. The official score of the parent does not show this. The cause is not established.

Only the hosted evaluation is a ranked measurement.

## Experiment configuration

- The prover is built in release mode with the repository's own profile, for Neoverse V2 code generation with `aes`, `sha2`, `sha3` and `sve2`.
- Eight cores of one type per run, 16 GB, fresh seed and table for each proof, verification outside the timer, nothing dropped.
- The hosts are development machines, not the official runner.

## Reproduction

```sh
bash .yukon/setup.sh --track arm
bash .yukon/benchmark.sh --track arm
```

## Packaging

Only `solution-arm/` differs from the base tree. `.yukon/`, `verifier/`, `.github/` and `benchmark.json` are untouched.

## Credits

- jungjipdo: the record, its four-tile sink and lane reconstruction (`e5248328`, `4381e86b`).
- fkiene: the PMULL product and the switch tree (`4ff98b58`, `76616f9f`).
- dadon: the 64-set prefix switch (`fec7683c`).
- e-man07: the commitment line and the published port data (`0e4884e7`, `d7b8a098`).
- i34-9: the longer chunk against the certificate (`d73d6cfd`).

## Limitations

- The gain of each change is small and close to the official noise of about 3 ms on one tree.
- Phase shares on the development hosts do not transfer to the official runner as absolute numbers.
- A chunk of 256 is the longest one the build's minimum margin admits; a further step would need a better digit encoder.

author: elliotchance
body:
A pull request now runs every job, like a tag does, instead of only Linux x86-64. That way a change that breaks macOS or Windows is caught before it's merged. pr.yml and tag.yml are one workflow again (ci.yml). The Linux job is written out instead of being called from another workflow, so its check keeps the exact name the main ruleset requires ("Linux (x86-64)"). On a pull request the Release job still builds and tests the amalgamation, but it only publishes on a tag. docker.yml is unchanged.

Every tag since v1.4.0 has failed, for two reasons.

**macOS ARM64: the server dropped idle clients.** The server's client connections kept V's default read timeout of 30 seconds. A client that didn't send anything for 30 seconds was disconnected, including a psql session left idle:

```
$ psql ... (VALUES 1; wait 35 seconds; VALUES 2;)
server closed the connection unexpectedly
```

The slower macOS ARM64 runner hit this in the server tests. A test's other connections can sit idle that long while it runs, and a long statement made the test client's own 30 second timeout fail ("net: op timed out", or an empty error when the server had already closed the connection). The server now sets no read timeout on a client, the same as PostgreSQL, and test_server_idle_client checks that. The test client waits up to 10 minutes for a result. An error from a test (rather than a failed assertion) now names the file, line and mode, instead of ending the whole run with a bare "op timed out".

**Linux x86-64: the app test for cancelling an import was flaky.** After Cancel, the page read the tab (still marked as importing a file) before the import finished, then asked whether it was importing after it had finished. So it showed "The import of big.sql was interrupted because the app was stopped" and no result, and nothing reloaded it. The page is now made again if an import starts or finishes while it's being made. Locally the two cancel tests failed 6 times in 12 before, and passed 15 times in 15 after; all 181 app tests pass.

**Windows: V master doesn't build there.** V master at e140fd7 fails to build on Windows (errors in vlib/os/execute_capture_nix.h), while 95a0d51 before it builds fine. That's a V problem, not a vsql one. When V master can't be set up after the retry, the Windows jobs now run .github/workflows/earlier-v.sh. It builds the newest of the 20 commits before V master that builds on Windows, puts it on the PATH, and adds a warning annotation that names both commits.

Checked locally: the psql idle session from above now works, and `make sql-test` passes (66/66, 100% coverage), along with `make fmt-verify` and the -prod check. The workflow and the Windows fallback can only be tested by CI, which this PR runs in full.

body:
Closing a model could leave its weights allocated after the worker thread exited. Eredu now cleans up completed model resources automatically, without a special call from the app.

Thread shutdown waits for in-flight work to finish safely instead of abandoning its resources. A device that never finishes can therefore prevent thread shutdown.

Checked with a real Metal model, including generation and panic cleanup, plus the session recovery tests.

These workflows follow the mcp-gateway pattern:

body:
Task 6 of `.drafts/MINDS-TASKS-2026-11-05.md`, first step: the Lean witness checker is complete on its fragment. `witness_sound` proved that `accepts` implies `Settled`. The converse was only argued in the witness README ("This is argued below, not proved"). It is now a theorem: on the fragment, the checker decides `Settled`.

## What is proved (`proofs/Vars1/WitnessComplete.lean`)

- **`prove`** builds a derivation from the store alone:
  - stand lines for the decision and for every verdict that counts (ATTESTED, empty witness slot, judges and attests it, meets the stand conditions down its `relies`);
  - an endorse line for every key of the evaluator policy with a seal on such a verdict, under a scope of the chain, by a key of that scope's roster;
  - the settle line.
- **`witness_complete`**: if the model holds the decision `Settled`, `accepts S (prove S n d) d`.
- **`accepts_iff_settled`**: with `witness_sound`, the checker accepts the prover's derivation exactly when the model holds the decision `Settled`.
- **`stale_complete`** discharges one new hypothesis for Pass 2 `Stale`.
- **Axioms**: `#print axioms` gives `propext` and `Quot.sound` only. Lean core's `List.length_erase_of_mem` and `List.mem_erase_of_ne` rest on `Classical.choice`, so the file proves the two lemmas over its own `drop1`.

**The fragment (`Fragment`)** is where the checker's syntactic rules read as the model's:
- no computation;
- no INVALID verdict judges the decision (the model withdraws only the keys that seal one under the verdict's verifier id; the checker refuses any);
- the live cone (the decision, the verdicts of `W_max`, and what they rely on) holds local cells that supersede nothing and that no cell invalidates, retires or supersedes.

**What completeness assumes beyond `Pin` (`PinComplete`)**: the decode must be complete, not only faithful.
- what a live cell relies on is live (`stale_complete` proves it of `Stale`, where `active` is decidable);
- the store holds a seal for every cumulative endorser of a local cell;
- a policy meets its quorum with threshold many distinct keys of it;
- the decision's evaluator policy is decoded.

There is also a rank on `relies` that bounds the depth.

## Running it

- **`vars1witness --prove`** reads a store line and checks `prove S (cells + 1) d` instead of a derivation.
- **`check.py --lean --prove`** writes that line: every seal that verifies on a verdict of the decision, and no derivation.
- **Witness test 14:**
  - On both generated histories, before the failure and after it, `--prove` accepts exactly the decisions whose `prove.py` term is HELD.
  - On every decision of the live chain at `7c6899b7`, it accepts exactly those the lens settles: 34 of 47 (3.9 s for all 47).
  - Outside the fragment (a withdrawn notice in the cone; an INVALID verdict that withdraws one key) it does not accept decisions the lens settles. Completeness is not claimed there.
- **Mutant `m-prove-seals`** (the prover's line carries no seals) is killed by test 14. A second mutant that I tried, dropping the empty-derivation return, would survive by design (`--prove` does not read the line's derivation), so it is not in the list.

## Claims

- New claim `assurance.witness-complete` (proved): `lean:witness_complete`, `lean:accepts_iff_settled`, `lean:stale_complete`, witness test 14, `m-prove-seals`.
- New ASSURANCE.md row; the section's text names the converse.
- The theorem table in `proofs/README.md`, and the witness README's opening, Lean checker section, evidence table and mutant count, are updated.

## Local runs (`MINDS_REQUIRE_LEAN=1 MINDS_REQUIRE_CHAIN=1`, sigma-glyph 1.0.1)

- `lake build`: built (27 jobs), `vars1witness` built.
- `experiments/witness/test_witness.py`: 14 OK (141 s).
- `test_vars1.py`: 128 OK (799 s).
- `tools/check_claims.py`: 195 claims, 421 mutants, OK.
- Witness mutants: only `m-prove-seals` was run locally (killed on its assertion); CI's mutants job runs all 45.

## Not here

- **The next step of task 6:** edges that do not count (stratified negation), so that a withdrawn notice and an unauthorized edge enter the fragment. Test 14's two outside cases are where it would start.
- **`check.py`'s completeness**, which stays argued and tested.

body:
## What this does

**Watcher, twice a day (06:00 and 18:00 Pacific standard time).** Reads three sources for everything in `watch/watchlist.json` (WordPress, PHP 8.2–8.5, 22 plugins, 4 themes, seeded from Glyn Dwfn's site plus widely used plugins):

1. **The official CVE list** (CVEProject/cvelistV5). WordPress plugin CVEs name the exact wordpress.org plugin and the affected versions, so this is a first-class source, not just a headline feed.
2. **WPVulnerability**, which adds Wordfence/Patchstack/WPScan entries. Example from this week: Wordfence marks the WPForms Lite 2.0.3 bug as usable *without a login*; the CVE record doesn't say.
3. **WordPress core's own security advisories** (core releases often have no CVE).

New problems are grouped per product and drafted into `site/bulletins.json` in one open PR titled **"Bulletin drafts …"** (**"URGENT: …"** when usable without a login, rated critical, or being exploited). **Merging publishes. Nothing publishes without a merge.**

**Health check, daily.** Runs a real check of a sample site against the live services and checks the CVE list is still updating. A failed run gets a GitHub failure email.

## How it remembers

What the watcher has seen lives on the unpublished `watch-state` branch (baseline pushed today: 1,087 known ids, CVE list read to 2026-11-06 21:58 UTC). Closing a drafts PR without merging doesn't bring its items back. Products added to the watchlist start quietly: only problems found after they're added become drafts.

## Also in this PR

- Bulletins for this week's **WPForms Lite** (usable without a login; fixed after 2.0.3) and **Elementor** (two cross-site scripting bugs; fixed after 4.3.5).
- About section explains how bulletins are made and that a person reviews each one.

## Checked

- 33 tests pass, including the CVE fixtures for The Events Calendar, WPForms, WordPress core and PHP.
- Live dry runs: last week's CVE list → 8 matches across 4 products, drafted correctly; with today's baseline → nothing new, nothing drafted; a simulated open drafts PR keeps its pending (edited) draft.
- `watch/health.mjs` passes against the live services.
- Independent `/code-review` (medium): 10 findings, all fixed in the second commit with tests (prefix-matching CVE ids, through/fixedIn scoping, per-branch core fixes, retrying failed CVE downloads, isolating source outages, stale/leftover drafts branch).

## Needs one setting before it can open PRs

Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → **"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"**: https://github.com/BaronyOfGlynDwfn/site-check/settings/actions

After merging, the first scheduled run is at the next 02:00 or 14:00 UTC; it can also be started by hand from the Actions tab ("Watch for new vulnerabilities" → Run workflow).

author: itsomidkarami
body:
The sub-agent contract test (`tests/test_logs_claude_e2e.py`, from #1243) was written against claude 2.1.316. Its docstring now records two things a reader would otherwise go looking for:

- **No nested case.** A `general-purpose` sub-agent has no Agent tool of its own in a headless run. Asked to start one, it says so and does the work itself (`subagent_stats.spawned_by_subagents: 0`), so this test has no depth-2 case. The CLI does count nested spawns and a depth limit, so a custom agent given the tool may nest; that stays unmeasured.
- **No background check.** A prompt that asks to wait gets a foreground sub-agent (`is_backgrounded: false`). Kraft's tagging and sub-agent list never read that field, and the background-job check skips every `local_agent` task, so both kinds read the same.

Both were seen on claude 2.1.319, where the test's assertions still hold. The test skips without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so its command was run by hand with the same assertions. Three probe logs (one background run on 2.1.316, two foreground runs on 2.1.319) were also read through `logs.Tail` and `subagents.Fold`: every sub-agent row tagged, the right status, tokens and answer, and no false background job.

The cost: nesting stays unpinned. If a later CLI, or a repo's custom agent, gives sub-agents the Agent tool, this test will not notice.

author: robbertbos
body:
Niets bewaakte of een element dat focus krijgt ook zichtbaar verandert. axe en HTML_CodeSniffer kijken niet naar de focusstijl, dus een `outline: none` die ergens terugsluipt komt door elke gate heen. In deze sessie kwam dat twee keer langs: in #320 (focus in het zoekveld) en in #326 (de melding die focus bedekte).

De toets tabt echt door elke pagina. Dat moet, want `:focus-visible` matcht niet betrouwbaar bij focus vanuit een script, en het is meteen de enige meting die klopt met wat een toetsenbordgebruiker krijgt.

Per element wordt de rusttoestand vergeleken met de toestand met focus: omlijning, schaduw, achtergrond, tekstkleur, rand, onderstreping, filter, doorzichtigheid en de pseudo-elementen, op het element zelf en op zijn ouder. Dat laatste omdat een wrapper de ring kan dragen, zoals bij een invoerveld.

Alleen wat iets toont telt mee. Dat bleek nodig: de site zet bij focus ook `outline-offset: 2px`, en mijn eerste versie keurde daarmee elke pagina goed terwijl de omlijning zelf was uitgezet. Een offset zonder omlijning verschuift niets, een randkleur bij 0px breedte is onzichtbaar.

Gemeten op de gebouwde site:

| Toestand | Uitslag |
|---|---|
| Zoals de site nu is | nul bevindingen op 95 pagina's |
| Met `outline: none !important` op links en knoppen | 405 elementen op 95 pagina's |

Die tweede regel is de proef dat de toets echt iets vangt. Hij draait in ongeveer tien seconden over de hele site en hangt aan `npm run a11y`, dus aan `just a11y` en `just checks`.

Presentaties vallen af; die hebben hun eigen toets in `presentaties.js`. Zes unit-tests dekken de randgevallen: een eigen focusstijl zonder omlijning, een ring op de ouder, en een onderstreping die bij focus verschijnt. 208 tests groen, 102 URL's zonder bevindingen in de toegankelijkheidstoets.

author: mathiasbourgoin
body:
Stacked on #533 (8-bit wmma, base `feat/ptx-wmma-int8`); no commit here touches that branch. **Not to be merged before it; the CUDA paths need NVIDIA execution and a performance check.**

## What

CUDA/C and CUDA/PTX trapped on a cooperative-matrix load or store whose address is not 32-byte aligned or whose stride is not a multiple of 16 bytes, although `CM_load` / `CM_store` promise any index and stride. They now compute the interpreter's answer, and a launch whose arguments are aligned pays nothing for it.

What the other backends do (investigated): **HIP gfx11 has no precondition** (bit-identical to the interpreter at index 400 / stride 48), Metal and Vulkan emit no check. Only CUDA/C and PTX trapped, so they are the only ones changed.

## Design: three levels

1. **Static proof** (`spoc/ir/Sarek_ir_coopmat_align.ml`). A power-of-two *factor* of the index and stride expressions (constants, `a +- b`, `a * b`, `a << c`, immutable `let`-bound variables; parameters, loop and mutable variables are 1; lexical scoping; sound under wrapping int32). Proven: the bare `wmma` instruction, no check, no buffer.
2. **Launch-time variant** (aligned / staged / checked). For accesses that depend on kernel parameters (a GEMM's `k`, `n`), `derive` reduces "every access of the kernel is aligned" to a **predicate over the kernel's int32 parameters** (a disjunction of conjunctions of "p is a multiple of n"; products are split over every divisor, implied atoms absorbed). For `Sarek_gemm.Coopmat` it is `k` and `n` multiples of 8. At launch `Execute` (`Coopmat_variant`, CUDA/C and CUDA/PTX only) evaluates it on the actual scalar arguments:
   - **satisfied**: the kernel marked with `mark_aligned` (a body pragma the generators read; CUDA-C does not print it) is generated and run: bare `wmma`, **no check, no buffer, no trap**, identical to the proven path;
   - **not satisfied**, or no predicate derivable (an index the rules cannot reduce, a coopmat statement in a helper): the staged variant below.
   The marked kernel is a distinct IR value built once per kernel, so `Execute`'s source memo (keyed on the IR's physical identity and the block) holds one source per variant and block and each is compiled once. `Execute.coopmat_variant ~device ir args` exposes the choice without launching; the launch counts it (`Coopmat_variant.counts`) and logs it at debug level.
3. **Staged variant** (block known): a warp-uniform alignment test; misaligned tiles are copied element by element through a 32-byte aligned per-warp `.shared` buffer (1 KiB per warp, declared only in this variant, sized from the block), `wmma` runs on the buffer with a leading dimension of 16; a store scatters only its 256 elements. PTX slow paths are out of line after the final `ret`; CUDA/C uses `sarek_cm_stage_in/out` and `__syncwarp`. **Block unknown at codegen**: the trap stays (documented).

## Footprint

- **Aligned variant: 0 extra shared memory, no check, for every `Sarek_gemm.Coopmat` tiling and both B layouts** (asserted on PTX and CUDA-C by `test_marked_variant`: no `sarek_cm_tiles`, no `trap`, no `.shared`, no `bar.warp.sync`).
- Staged variant, as before: 1 KiB per warp: 1x1/1 warp 1 KiB, 2x1/2 warps 2 KiB, 2x2/2 warps (default) 2 KiB, 4x2/4 warps 4 KiB; PTX has one slow path per access (12 for the default tiling).
- A `.shared` source array on CUDA/C stays unproven even in the aligned variant (that generator does not declare it 32-byte aligned); PTX declares accessed shared arrays `.align 32`.
- Aligned-variant cost: the bare instruction. Staged-variant fast path: the alignment test (about 7 ALU/predicate instructions) plus one not-taken warp-uniform branch. Not measured (no NVIDIA GPU here): **a performance check on NVIDIA is needed**, GEMM on this branch versus #533.
- **Base pointers are checked at launch too.** `Execute.base_alignments` reads the device pointer of each array argument (a vector without a buffer yet gets a fresh allocation, at least 256-byte aligned on CUDA). If any array a coopmat access touches is below 32-byte alignment, the launch runs a third, **checked** variant (`mark_checked`: no static proof, every access tested at run time and staged), so a misaligned base is correct instead of undefined; costs nothing on the device, and the host reads pointers only for coopmat kernels on CUDA (the last kernel is answered without the lock). Sarek's `sub_vector` gives each vector its own device allocation, so a misaligned device base cannot be built through the API; it is tested with fake pointers.

## Tests

- `test_ptx_coopmat` (unit): factor and proof-walk tests; **derived predicates** (GEMM = k, n multiples of 8; parameter-driven f16 and 8-bit tiles; let-bound multiples; shadowing by a loop variable; an unreducible index gives no predicate; a missing argument is false); marked variant of every tiling x layout has no buffer (PTX, CUDA-C) while the unmarked one keeps it; staged snapshots with and without a block; the ptxas gate assembles the staged kernels.
- `test_coopmat_misalign_e2e` (any device offering a configuration, `COOPMAT_MISALIGN_FRAMEWORK` restricts it): host part (no device): `choose` and the generated PTX / CUDA-C of each variant for both CUDA frameworks, GEMM at aligned and misaligned `k`/`n`, parameter-driven tiles for f16 and 8-bit; device part: misaligned index/stride tiles (tile and neighbours vs the interpreter) **and parameter-driven tiles at aligned and misaligned `off`/`ld`, with the variant asserted (and, on CUDA, the launch counters) and the result compared with the interpreter**.
  - **Executed here**: RX 7900 XTX via HIP gfx11 (`ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`, flock): all pass (variant not applicable there; results match for aligned and misaligned parameters), `journalctl -k` clean. Earlier: RADV Vulkan s8/u8 all cases pass (f16 refused by policy), clean.
  - **Not executed**: CUDA/C and CUDA/PTX launches (no NVIDIA GPU).
- Full `dune test` with `SPOC_DISABLE_GPU=1`: only `new_runtime/test_runtime_comparison` ("No devices found": local `CUDA_PATH` with the GPUs disabled), unrelated.

## Launch-path benchmark (HIP, RX 7900 XTX hip:0)

This PR touches the launch path (`Execute.run_jit`), so the existing `sarek-hip/test/bench_launch_overhead` (host microseconds per `Execute.run_vectors` launch of a trivial 3-argument and 10-argument kernel, no synchronisation; "enqueue" and "enqueue+flush") was run on three builds, alternating main (9fde0ea3), #533 head (4e943232) and this head, 9 rounds of 20000 launches, under flock `/tmp/katra-gpu.lock`, with the machine shared with other sessions (load average 10 at the start of the runs, so the absolute numbers are noisy; the comparison is by median over alternating rounds). `journalctl -k` clean afterwards.

- First head tried (be78d23f): HIP 3-arg enqueue medians main 3.57 / #533 3.53 / #535 3.66 us (+2.5 %), 10-arg 4.40 / 4.53 / 4.53 us. The variant choice allocated two closures and a result tuple per launch before finding it had nothing to decide; that is the size of the difference, so it was fixed rather than argued away.
- Fixed head (3fea0055: `Coopmat_variant.relevant` answers first with a string comparison against two names and, for a CUDA kernel, one physical comparison with the last kernel seen; nothing is allocated for a non-coopmat launch). Medians in microseconds per launch (min .. max over 9 rounds):

| kernel, metric | main 9fde0ea3 | #533 4e943232 | this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| HIP 3-arg, enqueue | 3.73 (3.59 .. 4.18) | 3.66 (3.45 .. 4.22) | 3.65 (3.51 .. 4.22) |
| HIP 3-arg, enqueue+flush | 3.57 (3.47 .. 3.72) | 3.55 (3.38 .. 4.34) | 3.55 (3.50 .. 4.25) |
| HIP 10-arg, enqueue | 4.54 (4.44 .. 4.84) | 4.62 (4.34 .. 5.16) | 4.60 (4.47 .. 5.02) |
| HIP 10-arg, enqueue+flush | 4.49 (4.43 .. 4.60) | 4.52 (4.28 .. 5.23) | 4.56 (4.41 .. 4.67) |
| Native 3-arg, enqueue | 73.6 | 74.2 | 74.0 |
| Native 10-arg, enqueue | 80.9 | 77.8 | 77.3 |

No measurable difference for non-coopmat kernels (all within the run-to-run spread

author: lstanden
body:
Since #1583, `pytest_main.py` starts coverage after the `chdir`. coveragepy then writes `SF:` paths for sources under the chdir relative to the CWD (`SF:src/mod.py`). `write_lcov` looks each path up verbatim in `_absfile_mapping`, whose keys are absolute, so those records keep the CWD-relative path instead of the manifest path and no longer name a workspace file.

It only shows up when runfiles are real files, as under remote execution. With local symlinked runfiles, coveragepy resolves the source outside the CWD and keeps it absolute, so the existing lookup still hits. That's why `coverage_pytest_chdir_test` stays green.

The fix resolves each `SF:` path against `coverage.files.relative_directory()` (the directory coverage started in, not the CWD at report time) and normalizes it with `coverage.files.abs_file`, the same normalization used to build the mapping. Absolute paths pass through `os.path.join` unchanged, so the existing symlink case is unaffected.

Repro on 2.0.0-alpha.10 with `chdir` set to a package whose sources sit below it, run with remote execution:

| version | `SF:` |
|---|---|
| 2.0.0-alpha.7 | `SF:<pkg>/src/event/event.py` |
| 2.0.0-alpha.10 | `SF:src/event/event.py` |

### Changes are visible to end-users: yes

- Searched for relevant documentation and updated as needed: yes
- Breaking change (forces users to change their own code or config): no
- Suggested release notes appear below: yes

`bazel coverage` now reports workspace-relative `SF:` paths for `py_pytest_test` targets whose sources sit under their `chdir`.

### Test plan

author: justyannicc
body:
## Problem

A Worker upload failure can leave a release partly activated. Earlier Workers have already changed when a later upload fails, and the resulting mixed release can break sign-in.

## Change

Prepare the complete native Alchemy stack in shadow state and freeze each Worker's actual modules, bindings, compatibility flags and asset policy. Upload every version before activating any Worker. Require immutable version IDs and provider startup evidence at or below 750 ms. Missing evidence, rejection or deployment drift stops activation.

Carry 0370 adds a generic opt-in Alchemy hook at the assembled-request boundary. Basalt owns admission, receipts and activation policy. Activation uses the accepted IDs without rebuilding. Deferred database work starts after admission, and live verification Commands run after activation. A closed Command contract prevents unknown work from bypassing preparation. Existing source-namespace EU readiness is checked without provisioning before uploads and again before activation. Unsupported resource changes, new resources and Durable Object migrations fail closed.

Carry 0372 keeps per-attempt release identity in Commands instead of Worker Config bindings. Production uses one independent, stable `POOL_DEPLOYMENT_KEY` Actions secret, validated as 64 lowercase hex characters. Only PoolWorker and its release verifier receive it. Previews derive their own stable per-PR key.

Exact frozen requests persist privately with mode 0600, outside the safe receipt artifact. Preflight refusals retain the candidate and zero-activation disposition. Recovery records exact baseline IDs, completed calls and uncertain intent. It never silently retries an uncertain write or uses `force=true`. The first release cannot repair historical versions created with random secrets: restoring one may still fail with Cloudflare 10220 and require an explicit recovery decision. Recorded-version recovery restores traffic only; it does not undo database changes or mark the release ledger successful.

Start review at `scripts/release-barrier/deploy-stack.ts`, then `alchemy-plan.ts` and `barrier.ts`. The native-provider proof covers the hook and ordinary provider behavior. Existing backup, headroom, drain and image gates remain in place.

## Scope

This stands alone as the release barrier requested after repeated partial deployments. It must ship in the same b21 batch as the six existing members and the AppPages revert in carry 0374. Do not merge it alone. The merged release workflow and candidate deploy command apply the barrier to that same first release, with no bootstrap release required.

## Verification

The production build, build checks and local startup checks pass. Root, stack, Worker, pool and full upstream typechecks pass. Owned tests report 1,176 passed and 8 skipped; carry/upstream checks report 392 passed and 7 skipped. Fake-provider and real Alchemy graph tests cover late upload rejection, exact-ID activation, metadata/assets preservation, namespace admission and uncertain recovery. The default compiled provider import and ordinary no-hook upload pass. Release checks report 328 passed. Architecture validation, model generation, fitness and workflow lint pass. Independent Input and Standards reviews report zero findings at the final candidate. Batch-preflight and pinned fitness passed immediately before the push. No production calls or release dispatch were used during implementation and review; live acceptance remains with the coordinated release.

Model and harness: gpt-6.1-sol in the Codex harness.

author: bootuz
body:
## What Replaces the hand-drawn "#K" app icon with a radar icon built in Icon Composer.

- **Source:** `mac/Resources/AppIcon.icon` (open in Icon Composer). Background is a slate gradient fill; layers are three ring SVGs (glass), the sweep wedge with the dim blips and glow (flat), and the sweep line, bright blip and center dot (glass). - **Build:** `mac/generate-icon.sh` now runs `actool` on the `.icon` and writes `Assets.car` (layered Liquid Glass icon, macOS 26+) and `AppIcon.icns` (flat fallback for macOS 15). `build-app.sh` and `build-dmg.sh` copy both into the bundle. Both outputs are gitignored. - **Info.plist:** adds `CFBundleIconName` so macOS 26 uses the layered icon; `CFBundleIconFile` stays for macOS 15. - **README:** shows a rendered PNG (`docs/icon.png`) above the title. - `mac/Resources/AppIcon.png` is removed. - **Menubar:** the SF Symbols magnifier is replaced by the radar, drawn in code (`MenuBarIcon.swift`) as an 18 pt template image so macOS tints it. Health states keep their meaning: dot badge when a server update is waiting, dimmed radar when some instances are unhealthy, slashed radar when all are down. - **Web:** a flat radar mark (no tile, no glass; `RadarMark.svelte`) sits next to the name in the sidebar, teal on light and mint on dark. The same drawing is `web/public/favicon.svg`, which `index.html` already linked but which never existed. ## Why The old icon read as "#JC", blurred below 32 px, and filled the whole canvas instead of following the macOS icon grid. ## Testing - Rendered the `.icon` with Icon Composer's renderer in Default, Dark, Clear and Tinted appearances and at 16/32 px. - Compiled with `actool` (Xcode 27.2) and checked Finder shows the radar icon on a bundle laid out like `build-app.sh` makes it. - Menubar: `swift build` and `swift test` in `mac/` pass (160 tests, 4 new in `MenuBarIconTests`); rendered all four variants on light and dark backgrounds. Not yet seen in a live menu bar. - Web: `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass; checked the sidebar mark in light and dark against a local server, and `/favicon.svg` serves as `image/svg+xml`. - Not yet run: a full `build-app.sh` / `build-dmg.sh`, or `actool` under Xcode 26 (what the release workflow uses). Xcode 26 is the first version with `.icon` support, so it should compile there. - Known limit: actool's macOS 15 `.icns` fallback tops out at 256 px, so very large Finder previews on macOS 15 look slightly soft.

author: sbalabanov
body:
## Summary
Provider-cancelled executions cannot be rebuilt. Treat Failed and Cancelled viable paths as exhausted only after dependencies settle, without rewriting cancellation facts or changing user cancellation and successful alternatives.

Add an explicitly queue-scoped, dry-run-default recovery command using normal speculation messages and a stable operator recovery ID. No schema, provider contract, automatic retry, or planner authority changes.

## Test Plan
Repro (performed against isolated MySQL and ordinary orchestrator consumers):
1. Seed queue quiet-cancelled: request 1 processing v1; batch 2 speculating v1 containing it, no dependencies; SHA-256("2") path cancelled at attempt 1; no queued messages.
2. Run ./tool/bazel run //tool/submitqueue/recovercancelledpaths -- --queue quiet-cancelled --recovery-id demo-run --dry-run with MYSQL_DSN configured. Observed affected-head=2 and zero writes. Configure QUEUE_MYSQL_DSN, replace --dry-run with --apply, and repeat: exactly one speculate nudge with ID 2/cancelled-path-recovery/demo-run.
3. Start the ordinary orchestrator on a free local port with fake extension configuration and MQ_TENANTS=quiet-cancelled. Observed batch failed v2, request error v2, path still cancelled/attempt 1, and terminal log "every viable build failed or was cancelled".

TestRun_ProviderCancellationExhaustsHead proves cancellation persistence and conclude ordering; existing shared tests cover CAS/publish fault windows. Focused speculate, sticky, buildsignal and recovery tests passed. Deploy the policy and drain old consumers before applying recovery.

## Revert Plan
Revert this commit and stop applying recovery. Do not reverse terminal outcomes or rewrite Cancelled facts; older consumers may strand heads again.

author: bobliuuu
body:
## What
- `S3Backend::get_stream`: HEAD for length + ETag, then one un-ranged GET with `If-Match: <etag>` whose body is returned as a reader (no buffering, no hash pass; the ETag is the tag).
- Declines (caller reads whole) when the object is small, missing, or replaced between HEAD and GET (412 / different ETag), so a body never mixes versions. A body cut short is an `UnexpectedEof` error, not a short object.
- Time allowance for the streamed GET scales with length like uploads do; bytes_read still counted.
- docs/known-limits.md item 1 updated; trait doc in vcs-remote corrected.
- Tests: in-process fake S3 (HEAD+GET sequence, tag equals whole-get tag, small/missing/swapped-object fallbacks, truncated body) and a MinIO test gated on VCS_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT (CI s3 job).

## Why
PR #578 streamed un-ranged GETs only for the directory backend; an S3-backed server still loaded whole packs into memory per download. Not yet verified: the MinIO test was not run locally (no MinIO on the bench box), and no real-S3 measurement. Note: `cargo clippy --workspace` currently fails on main at crates/vcs-cli/src/main.rs:1685 (unrelated, untouched here); clippy on vcs-store-s3/vcs-remote/vcs-server is clean.
